At the late Eastern Han Dynasty, Zhang Jiao called himself "The Great Teacher" and led the followers of Taiping Taoism to wear yellow turbans on their head, and rebel against the Han Dynasty, which shocked the capital for a while. The imperial court called for the volunteers for support, and all the heroes responded. The talented heroes such as Yuan Shao, Dong Zhuo, Liu Bei, and Cao Cao prologue the beginning of The Three Kingdoms era, during which the rivalry of warlords broke out.

In the first year of Chuping (Emperor Xian's reign), Dong Zhuo took control of the imperial and rioted in Luoyang, which aroused condemnation among the governors and inspectors in the Guandong area, who jointly promoted Yuan Shao as the leader of the "Anti-Dong Zhuo Alliance". Dong Zhuo take Emperor Xian to Chang'an and burned Luoyang, Lu Bu leaded the army to resist the combined forces. The allied forces had different intentions, they want to take this chance to strengthen themselves in this situation...

After the rebellion against Dong Zhuo, all parties vied for the Central Plains, and no one had a clear advantage. Cao Cao held Emperor Xian and occupied Xuchang, Liu Biao seized Jingzhou, Sun Ce captured Jiangdong, Yuan Shu Yu proclaimed himself emperor in Shouchun, Ma Teng stationed in Liangzhou and Yuan Shao won Hebei. The forces of all sides were competing with each other, making the situation in the Central Plains complicated and confusing. It was unknow that who would be the final winner.

Cao Cao controlled the emperor in Xuchang, and captured Yanzhou, Yuzhou, and Xuzhou; Yuan Shao defeated some of the vassals including Gongsun Zan, and dominated Qingzhou, Jizhou, Youzhou, and Bingzhou, seizing all lands of Hebei. Both sides were on the verge of breaking out a war. Yuan Shao intended to occupy the land in the south and led his army to attack Cao Cao, while the other vassals were eager for action, hoping to obtain benefit in the battle between the two powers.

After the Battle of Guandu, Cao Cao controlled all the states of the Central Plains, and the domination of all lands was in sight, so Cao Cao ordered his army to invade southward. Liu Bei sent Zhuge Liang to Jiangdong, lobbying Sun Quan for the alliance. Zhuge Liang and Zhou Yu carried out a common plan to resist Cao Cao's army of a million men at the Red Cliff of the Yangtze River. The survival of Sun and Liu, and the domination of the world for Cao Cao, hung upon this single action.

Liu Bei defeated Liu Zhang to win Yizhou of Shu, with the intention of capturing the Central Plains; Sun Quan based in Jiangdong, attempting to move westward to reclaim Jingzhou; Cao Cao defeated Ma Chao and gained Liangzhou and Yongzhou, and planned to move his troops to Hanzhong. Although the confrontation of the Three Kingdoms are roughly settled, it didn't mean any stabilization for the situation. The war was on the verge of breaking out among the three powers.

After Liu Bei gained Yizhou, he seized Hanzhong and proclaimed himself the King of Hanzhong. The following year Cao Cao died of illness, and his son Cao Pi succeeded to the throne and forced Emperor Xian of Han Dynasty to abdicate, resulting in the collapse of the Han Dynasty. Afterwards, Liu Bei proclaimed himself emperor as well, while Sun Quan changed his reign and named himself the Great Emperor of Wu. Since then, the tripartite confrontation of the three kingdoms mentioned in the Longzhong Plan was settled. The three powers were making preparation for future wars and waited for the chance to break the deadlock.

The tiger finally won and ran away with the dead dragon in its mouth.

A hundred miles to the west of Chengdu in Shu Province is Zhangren Mountain. The mountain is much quiet, green and looks like a city, so it is also called Qingcheng Mountain (Green City Mountain). There are special talents in the mountain who lived a long time.

Ding Feng, a native of Anfeng (Lujiang, Yang Province), is one of the Twelve Tiger Ministers of Jiangdong. His service years in Eastern Wu extends over all four rulers. 
He participated in numerous major battles, notably Red Cliffs, Jiangling, Fancheng and Yiling, and proved his worth. At earlier years, he was the lieutenant under the command of more prominent generals such as Gan Ning, Lu Xun and Pan Zhang. In the Battle of Dongxing, he led an assault with light cavalry regimen to secure a decisive victory against the invading Cao Wei force. 
When Sun Xiu succeeded to the throne, he accepted Zhang Bu's request of cooperation to put Sun Chen to justice. 
It is said that he is skilled at using slings as weapon, and he's given the alias of Master Slinger.

Ding Yuan is a native of Nancheng (Taishan Commandery, Yan Province) He assumed the Administrator of Bing Province, and is known as the foster father of Lu Bu. 
As one of the warlords levied to Luoyang by He Jin, he was against Dong Zhuo's decision of dethroning Emperor Xian, and led Lu Bu to attack Dong Zhuo. Lu was later instigated by Li Su, leading to the assassination of Ding and Dong Zhuo's takeover of Ding's force.

Yu Jin, a native of Juping, Taishan, is one of the notable generals of Cao Wei. He's a leader of discipline and fairness, and so is he, among the Five Elite Generals, the one who Cao Cao held with the highest respect. 
At Zhang Xiu's rebellion, Cao's force was in confusion, save those under Yu's command that also took minimal loss. Cao was impressed of Yu's leadership and stated that "such composure bests even the fabled generals of old times". 
When the rebellion started by his old friend Chang Xi was eliminated, Yu ordered to execute him according to the military justice. 
In the Battle of Fancheng, Yu was forced to surrender to Guan Yu due to the flooding. Later, The stress from Cao Pi's mocking with a wall painting caused Yu to fall ill and eventually die.

Son of Jiaozhi Governor Shi Xie. After the death of his father, he prevented Lu Dai from becoming governor and claimed the post for himself. So Sun Quan ordered Lu Dai to execute Shi Hui and others, Lu Dai tricked Shi Hui into surrendering, and then executed him and sent his head back to Wuchang. 
The Shi family thus declined until the end.

Minister of the Later Han. He was regarded by the people of his time as a learned and knowledgeable person who was good at politics. 
Sun Quan sent Bu Xie to be the governor of Jiaozhou, and Shi Xie led his people to submit and became his subordinate. Later, when Wu and Shu were in dispute, he persuaded a powerful clan in Yizhou, Yongkou, to rebel against Shu and join Wu. 
He once ruled part of Vietnam, because of his spread of Confucianism and the success of local management, he was called "King Shi" by Vietnamese historians, and was highly respected.

With the name "DaQiao" in official history record, she is the elder sister of Qiao Xuan's two foster daughters, the consort of Sun Ce, and the sister of XiaoQiao, Zhou Yu's companion. She's one of the renowned fine ladies in the era of Three Kingdoms. 
Before death Sun Ce bade farewell to DaQiao, and urged her to work with her sister in reminding Zhou Yu to be a good counselor. 
In the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Zhuge Liang revised the clause "communing two bridges on weft, resembling a rainbow on the sky" in Cao Zhi's Rhapsody of Bronze Bird Terrace to "communing the two Qiaos of the southeastern lands to celebrate the glorious triumph" to irritate Zhou Yu, on the false premise of Cao Cao's ambition to take everything into his possession, including the Qiao sisters.

With the name "XiaoQiao" in official history record, she is the younger sister of Qiao Xuan's two foster daughters, the companion of Zhou Yu. She's the sister of DaQiao, Sun Ce's consort. 
She is said to convey the will of Sun Ce to her companion Zhou Yu with his sister DaQiao. In the Romance, she is said to psych Zhou up before major battles. 
In the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Zhuge Liang revised the clause "communing two bridges on weft, resembling a rainbow on the sky" in Cao Zhi's Rhapsody of Bronze Bird Terrace to "communing the two Qiaos of the southeastern lands to celebrate the glorious moment of triumph" to irritate Zhou Yu, on the (understandably) false premise of Cao Cao's ambition to take everything into his possession, including the Qiao sisters.

Gongsun Yuan, a native of Xiangping (Liaodong Commandery), is the grandson of Gongsun Du. 
He leveraged the competition between Wei and Wu, and later claimed to be the King of Yen and launched a major attack on the central land. Cao Rui responded by assigning Sima Yi as the commander. Sima surrounded Gongsun's force at Xiangping Castle. After a long encirclement, Gongsun Yuan sought to surrender by sending messengers or his heir as captive. Sima denied all these offers. Out of the fear of being overwhelmed by the Cao force and the misery following an open surrender, he tried to flee with his son under the cover of night but caught by Sima's force. They were executed, and Gongsun's bloodline and officials shared their fate.

Gongsun Yue, a native of Lingzhi (Liaoxi, You Province), is one of Gongsun Zan's cousins. In the Romance, he is portrayed as Gongsun Zan's biological brother. 
Gongsun Zan ordered Gongsun Yue to assist Yuan Shu and Sun Jian in attacking Zhou Ang. In the Battle of Yangcheng, Gongsun Yue died to stray arrows. Gongsun Zan blamed Yuan Shao for his cousin's death, and their conflict over the dominance of the northern lands began since then.

Gongsun Zan is a native of Lingzhi (Liaoxi, You Province). 
As an imperial officer, he led the "White Horse Fellows" and held off the invaders with less than a hundred elites, this soon spread all over the barbarian tribes. 
As an apprentice of Lu Zhi, he is senior to Liu Bei. In the Romance, he accepted Liu Bei during the coalition. 
After the coalition, he had a grudge with Yuan Shao for Liu Yu's execution. Since assuming the Administrator of You Province, he became preoccupied with self-pity and misplaced his trust. He was eventually surrounded by Yuan's overwhelming force, and had to pull back to Yijing. He tried to convince Zhang Yan to strike Yuan, who learned of the plan and arranged an ambush. Knowing that his fate was sealed, Gongsun set himself aflame in the castle.
Fictional character in Romance of The Three Kingdoms. He was originally from the Yellow Turban Army and later served Cao Cao, later he was killed by Guan Yu during the Thousand League Journey.

Taishi Ci, a native of Huang County (Donglai, Qing Province), served Kong Rong and Liu Yao before swearing fealty to Sun Ce. 
Kong offered hospitality to his mother, and Taishi returned the favor by charging out the Yellow Turbans alone to seek help when Kong was surrounded. While serving Liu Yao, he fought Sun Ce numerous times. After the defeat of Liu, Sun valued Taishi's valor and offered a place to him, and trusted the task of recruiting Liu's force to him. Taishi completed the mission and returned as requested. Also interested in recruiting Taishi, Cao Cao made numerous offers that were ignored. 
Taishi died of illness before the Battle of Red Cliffs, and Sun Quan pitied for his untimely death.

Kong Zhou, a native of Chenliu Commandery, Yan Province, started his service to the dynasty on the endorsement of Fu Rong, a renowned scholar of the time. Though assuming the Administrator of Yu Province by Dong Zhuo to win the heart of people, he also attended the coalition against Dong. Kong died of illness after the coalition, and his position was succeeded by Sun Jian. 
According to historian comments, he is"a master debater lacking military or leadership talent".

Kong Rong, a native of Qu Fu, Lu State, is the descendant of Confucious and one of the Seven Scholars of Jian'an. He is known for the anecdotes of "sharing the pear" and "a prodigy is not necessarily a prominent figure in later years". 
While Dong Zhuo was in office, Kong was sent to Beihai to fight the Yellow Turbans for his advices to Dong. 
After Cao Cao escorted Emperor Xian to Xudu, Kong also irritated Cao with his advices. His vision of restoring imperial authority and "warlords must be far away from His Majesty" pushed Cao to the limit. Cao accused Kong for misbehavior to execute him and his bloodline. 
Other than his unmoving belief, he had no military or political talent, nor did he make anything notable. Still, his uncompromising nature is rare at that time.

Wen Qing, a native of Qiao Commandery, Yu Province, first served Cao Wei, then swore fealty to Eastern Wu. 
He involved in Wei Feng's rebellion and was nearly executed. Cao Cao spared Wen's life for his years of service. 
With Sima Shi came to power and had the late ruler abdicated, Wen started up a rebellion with Guanqiu for their sense of insecurity but eliminated by Deng Ai and Sima Shi. Wen decided to seek shelter in Eastern Wu. 
While serving Eastern Wu, he had grudge with and later murdered by Zhuge Dan. His sons Wen Yang and Wen Hu had no choice but returned to Cao Wei.

Wen Pin, a native of Wan, Jing Province, first served Liu Biao, then joined Cao Cao. 
While serving Liu Biao, he worked with Cai Mao in the assassination of Liu Bei by distracting his close guards Zhao Yun and Wang Wei. 
When Liu Cong surrendered to Cao Cao, he blamed himself for being unable to defend Jing Province and excused himself from Cao's audience. Impressed of Wen's pride as an officer, Cao stated that "Zhongye's loyalty is undeniable". 
He participated in the Battle of Changban and the Battle of Red Cliffs. After the Battle of Red Cliffs, he assumed the Magistrate of Jiangxia for improving the stability in Jin Province. With Yue Jin he held off Guan Yu to save Cao Ren and the defenders in Xiangyang, he later defeated Sun Quan in Shiyang.

Wen Chou is one of the prominent generals of Yuan Shao. In official history records, he was only mentioned in the biography of other more prominent figures, and how his life ended remained a missing piece of history. 
In the Romance, he, Yan Liang, Gao Lan and Zhang He are known as the "Four Generals of Hejian". 
In the expedition against Dong Zuo, Hua Xiong the commander of Sishui Pass halted the advancement of the coalition. Yuan stated that "Hua Xiong would not a really threat if Yan Liang or Wen Chou were here". 
In the Battle of Jieqiao, he tried to chase Gongsun Zan but stopped by Zhao Yun. Before the Battle of Guandu, he sought to avenge Yan Liang by attacking Cao's force. He managed to best Zhang Liao and Xu Huang, but slain by Guan Yu.

Guanqiu Jian, a native of Wenxi, Hedong, has a compound surname"Guanqiu", where "毌" is the archaic form of "貫" (both pronounced as guan4). 
He is an important general of late Cao Wei. With Sima Yi he fought Gongsun Yuan, who claimed to be the King of Yen and waged a war against them. Later he led the expedition against Dongcheon of Goguryeo and nearly fully eliminated the Goguryeo force. With this battle, the territories lost in the later years of the Eastern Han dynasty were reclaimed. 
After the Incident at the Gaoping Tombs, Sima Shi ordered the execution of Guanqiu's friends Xiahou Xuan and Li Feng. This caused his resentment and later rebellion at Shouchun. The rebellion ended in failure and Guanqiu was shot by civilians.

Mao Jie, a native of Pingqiu, served as an imperial official in its ending year. 
Known for impartiality, he sought refuge under Cao Cao's influence. When Emperor Xian went on the run, Cao Cao was in the dilemma. Mao suggested Cao to offer refuge and leverage His influence. Cao then took action. 
Mao also elected talents with moral integrity, reforming the governance. 
Seeing that Cao Cao showing affection to Cao Zhi, Mao suggested Cao to keep a close watch on heir election, which also impressed Cao. 
Before his death, he was accused for defaming Cao Cao and put to jail. Huan Jie and He Qia advised against execution, but his titles were revoked. After his death, Cao Cao paid for his coffin, granted his family with valuables, and his son was granted with the title of Langzhong.

Niu Jin is a general of Cao Wei. 
In the aftermath of the Battle of Red Cliffs, Sun Quan took advantage of the momentum to claim the castles from Cao's influence. Niu worked with Cao Ren and Cao Hong in defending Nan Commandery and Yiling. When Yiling fell and Cao force relocated to Nan Commandery, Niu Jin charged at the baited Zhou Yu, and came to provoke the Wu force that held the line. He raided the camps of Wu force at night but ambushed by Zhou Yu. Niu and Cao force fell back to Xiangyang, and Nan Commandery was taken. 
In an anecdote, he was assassinated by Sima Yi with poisoned wine for the old saying of the cattle ("Niu") would succeed the horse ("Ma").

She was married to Sima Zhao at the age of fifteen and had five sons and one daughter, and was the mother of Sima Yan and Sima You, the Emperor Wu of Jin. Brilliant enough to be able to recite classic texts at the mere age of 8, her grandfather, Wang Lang, despaired that she had not been born a man. She predicted Zhong Hui's rebellion and warned Sima Zhao against him multiple times.

Wang Yun, a native of Qi (Taiyuan, Bing Province), is the Minister of the Masses ("Situ") and Chief Secretary in the early years of Han Emperor Xian. 
In the Romance, he formulated the chain stratagem with DiaoChan to cause abrasion between Dong Zhuo and Lu Bu and Lu's assassination of Dong Zhuo. 
After the death of Dong Zhuo, Wang claimed it to be his merit but this hard-earned trust is well spent when he insisted on executing Cai Yong, and Dong's men were concerned about Wang revoking their military titles. After the death of Niu Fu, Li Jue and Guo Si accepted Jia Xu's plan to take Chang'an. Wang was then executed.

Wang Pin, a native of Dangqu, Baxi Commandery, first served Cao Wei, later surrendered to and served Liu Bei. 
Surrendered to Liu Bei in the Battle of Hanzhong, he was trusted with important duties and became one of the most important generals in the late years of Shu Han. 
He attended numerous northern expedition with Zhuge Liang, and was trusted to support Ma Ji in the Battle of Jieting. Unfortunately, Ma was reluctant to accept suggestion and resulted in the loss of this strategic location. 
Impressed with his deliberation and fidelity, Zhuge Liang stated that Wang is "a man valuing trust and loyalty even over his dear life". 
He was the only general promoted following the Battle of Jieting. His highest title is Zhenbei ("northern expedition") General.

Wang Kang is the Magistrate of Yongchang under Shu rule. 
When Yong Kai, a local noble in Nanzhong, Yi Province started a rebellion, Wang worked with Lu Kai in holding the line until the Shu force arrived. 
Zhuge Liang approved of Wang's credit, and suggested to assign him as the Magistrate of Yongchang. 
Records about him are largely the same in both official history record and the Romance.

Wang Kuang, a native of Taishan Commandery, Yan Province, is the Magistrate of Henei. He was one of the warlords joining the coalition against Dong Zhuo. 
In the official history record, he was a charitable young man until he assumed the official position, by when he even tortured for his own benefits and caused public dissent. He managed to control himself when given the advice, though his tyranny resumed during the expedition against Dong Zuo. 
Lacking military aptitude, Wang Kuang formed an alliance with Zhang Miao after the defeat to Dong Zhuo. 
He eventually died in Cao Cao's expedition against Zhang Miao.

Wang Zhong, a native of Fufeng Commandery, Sili Province, is a general of Cao Wei. 
The tyranny of Dong Zhuo and the conflicts between warlords led to the famine around the imperial capital. Wang had to feed on human flesh to stay alive during this time, this caused general distrust, Cao Pi even picked on him for this matter. 
In the Romance, Wang Zhong and Liu Dai were taken into custody when defeated in the expedition against Liu Bei, who offered them with hospitality and later released them. When Wang and Liu returned, Cao Cao planned to execute them, Kong Rong intervened and their lives were spared.

The statement regarding Wang Wei is scarce in official history record. It is known that he first served Liu Biao, then Liu Cong. 
When Liu Cong surrendered to Cao Cao, Wang suggested to ambush Cao for the best effect. Liu Cong did not accept this suggestion, then he is not seen any of official history records again.

Wang Xiu, a native of Yingling, Beihai Commandery, served Kong Rong, Yuan Shao, Yuan Tan and Cao Cao. 
As an official recommended by Kong Rong, he saved Kong from Yellow Turbans or bandits at numerous occasions. After the death of Yuan Shao, Yuan Tan waged war against Yuan Shang but was defeated. Wang came to the rescue and advised Yuan Tan against taking offensive on siblings. 
In Cao Cao's expedition against Yuan Tan, Wang was unable to offer timely rescue but pleaded to give Yuan a proper burial. Cao approved his request for his fidelity.

Wang Lang, a native of Tan County, Donghai, is an apprentice of Yang Si the Grand Commandant. He was granted the title of Langzhong for his vast understanding of the classics. 
When Emperor Xian succeeded the throne, he assumed the Magistrate of Kuaiji. When Sun Ce conquered Kuaiji, he sent Zhang Zhao to convince Wang to surrender, Wang refused. 
Later, Cao Cao suggested Emperor Xian to relocate Wang back to direct imperial influence. Wang proposed the policies with less punishment and more emphasis on civilian welfare. As with Zhong Yao, he is also known for his juridical profession. 
In the Romance, he died of falling from his horse when lost in a debate against Zhuge Liang on Mt. Qi.

Wang Lei, a native of Guanghan Commandery, Yi Province, is an officer served Liu Zhang. 
When Liu Zhang decided to lead Liu Bei into Yi Province, Wang tried to convince Liu Zhang that the risks outweigh the benefit, if any. He even hang himself upside down on the castle gate and said that he would rather die than accepting the fate. Liu Zhang ignored his advice, and Wang suicided by cutting his own neck. 
His unfortunate death was also noted in the Romance, but said to die of falling from severed rope.

Wang Can, a native of Gaoping County, Shanyang Commandery, is one of the Seven Scholars of Jian'an. He is considered the top of the Scholars. 
However, Cai Yong held Wang Can, who was a teenager at the time, with high regard and considered Wang a more talented scholar. It is said that he had extraordinary memory, and could even remember a whole chess playthrough. 
Wang Can first visited Liu Biao but was rejected. After Liu Cong succeeded Liu Biao's position, Wang offered him to surrender to Cao Cao. 
Wang Can went on the expedition against Wu and died of illness at the age of 41 on the way back to Ye. It is said that his death was caused by leprosy. 
Wang Can mastered the art of literature and mathematics, though regrettably his publications have long lost.

Wang Shuang, a Cao Wei lieutenant under Cao Zhen's command, is nearly untold in official history record. 
In Zhuge Liang's second northern expedition, the siege of Chencang dragged on for weeks. Wang was sent to reinforce Chencang, and numerous Shu generals were defeated. Zhuge Liang ordered Wei Yan to feign inferiority to bait Wang. Shu force then ambushed Wang's headquarters, and Wang was slain by Wei when hurrying back.

Sima Yan, a native of Wen County, Henei Commandery, is the founder of Jin dynasty with the post-humous title of Emperor Wu. 
He dethroned Wei Emperor Yuan and established Jin dynasty. 
He launched policies to facilitate production, leading to a period of prosperity in the years of Taikang. 
As the family of Sima came to power due to Cao Wei not developing an authority system of their family, Sima granted titles to his kin, leading to a new era of warlords. In more than a decade after the death of Jin Emperor Wu, these warlords fought each other for the throne-the War of Eight Princes. 
This war led to the exhaustion of the central lands, and barbarian support sought by these warlords led to the subsequent invasions and rebellions of the five major barbarian tribes.

Sima Zhao, a native of Wen County, Henei Commandery, is the second son of Sima Yi, the brother of Sima Shi, and the father of Sima Yan and Sima You. He was granted with the posthumous title of Jin Emperor Wen after the inauguration of Sima Yan. 
He and his father Sima Yi made major contribution in holding Zhuge Liang's northern expedition, and assumed his brother's position after Sima Shi's death. In the rebellion started by Zhuge Dan, he suggested Cao Mao as the successor. Cao Mao was concerned about Sima's influence, and planned to murder him. This was soon known to Sima Zhao, and Cao Mao was murdered. Cao Huan was elected as the heir. 
Later, he sent Zhong Kuai and Deng Ai to the conquest of Shu, and he was granted with the title of the King of Jin in the next year.

Sima Shi, a native of Wen County, Henei Commandery, is the eldest son of Sima Yi and Zhang Chun Hua, and the brother of Sima Zhao. He was honored as the Emperor Shi after the inauguration of Sima Yan. 
Sima Shi's wit is no inferior to his father, as seen in his composure prior to the Incident at the Gaoping Tombs. He also correctly presumed that the Wu's Hefei expeditionary force would rally at a single spot. He held the ground and sent Wen Qin to cut off enemy's way. This won them a decisive victory. 
The replacement of the heir out of his decision led to a rebellion, and Sima Shi had to command despite being sick. He managed to put the rebellion to an end, but the ambush by Wen Yang, the son of Wen Qin, caused his eye illness to exacerbate and eventual death.

He was a famous scholar and hermit in the late Eastern Han Dynasty, Xiang Lang, Yin Mo and others studied under Sima Hui. Famous scholar and hermit in the late Eastern Han Dynasty, has a good relationship with Pang Tong and recommend him to Liu Bei later.

Sima Yi, a native of Wen County, Henei Commandery, is a famed general of Wei. As the father of Sima Shi and Sima Zhao, he was granted with the posthumous title of Emperor Xuan after Sima Yan's inauguration. 
According to the Book of Jin, Cao Cao noticed Sima Yi's ambition, and told Cao Pi to keep an eye on Sima. and yet Cao Pi trusted him with all his heart. 
When Guan Yu laid the siege, Sima Yi invited Sun Quan to strike Guan Yu. 
After the foundation of Shu Han, Sima Yi played a key role in the defense effort. 
People are more interested in his mind games against Zhuge Liang than his war effort, this is also a major part of the Romance. 
With the next Caos died early, Sima gradually came to power. After the coup d'etat, he paved the way for the abdication.

He was a native of Lujiang County. He claimed to have lived for more than 300 years, and was often said to be an immortal in rural legends. Alchemist in the late Eastern Han Dynasty, often regared as immortal in rural legends. In the feast held by Cao Cao, he performed many fantastic magical feats.
Gan Ning has only one son in the official history. A fictional character, daughter of Gan Ning.

Gan Ning, a native of Linjiang, Ba Commandery, is one of the Twelve Tiger Ministers of Jiangdong. 
He was the representative figure of Jin Fan bandit, but chose the academician path from his twenties. 
He served Liu Biao and Huang Zu, but it was Sun Quan that made him shine. 
While serving Huang Zu, he shot Ling Tong's father Ling Cao to death. They became nemesis until a reconciliation. 
He gave chase after the Battle of Red Cliffs, and showed no fear when Yiling Castle was besieged. 
In the Battle of Ruxu, Gan led his men to ambush Cao Cao's headquarters. Sun Quan was impressed and stated "though Mengde has Zhang, I have Gan". 
After the Battle of Nan Commandery, he held the line with about a thousand men, but Guan Yu didn't brave the river even with five thousand elites.

Tian Kai, a prominent general under Gongsun Zan's command, is the Administrator of Qing Province. He worked with Liu Bei and others in fighting Yuan Shao. 
Tian and Liu went to reinforce when Cao Cao launched offensive on Xu Province, but the operation ended in failure. 
After defeating Gongsun Zan at Yijing, Yuan Shao sent his eldest son Yuan Tan to wrestle the control over Qing Province with Tian. This conflict ended in the victory of Yuan and the demise of Tian. 
In Zizhi Tongjian, it is stated that Yuan defeated Tian before the Battle of Yijing, which is different from the Recordings of the Three Kingdoms chronologically.

Tian Feng, a native of Julu, is a strategist served Yuan Shao. He offered the plan to defeat Gongsun Zan and take Hebei. 
His advice of escorting the Emperor to his range of influence was rejected by Yuan. 
Before the Battle of Guandu, Tian suggested to take Xudu when Cao Cao attacked Liu Bei. Yuan refused with the excuse of children in illness, which frustrated Tian. Due to his direct remark and argument on the plan against Cao Cao, Yuan put him into jail. 
After the defeat in Guandu, Pang Ji accused Tian for humiliating Yuan. Yuan executed Tian later. Before death, as he stated "I would have the chance to survive if our war effort went well, but with the war lost." 
Xun Yu gave a fair and exact statement of Tian for "he's a bold man that challenges his superior".

Yin Mo, a native of Peicheng, Zitong, is a scholar of Shu State. He sought apprenticeship from Sima Hui and Song Zhong. He mastered the profession of classics and history. 
He was one of the subordinates that urged Liu Bei to inaugurate. He was granted with the title of doctor before Zhuge Liang's first northern expedition. 
In official history record, he took the position of the heir's mentor to teach Liu Shan "Chun Chiu Zuo Zhuan".

Yi Ji, a native of Gaoping County (Shanyang, Yan Province), is an official of Shu Han. 
He first served Liu Biao, and sought to join Liu Bei and followed him to Yi Province after Liu Biao's death. 
He is one of the five creators of the "Codes of Shu", the other four are Zhuge Liang, Fa Zheng, Liu Ba and Li Yan. 
Yi Ji is also known for his debate talents. He convinced Sun Quan when on his envoy duty to Eastern Wu.

Quan Cong, a native of Qian Tang County, Wu Commandery, is one of the prominent generals of Eastern Wu. He accepted any talent seeking shelter and provided hospitality, and hence won reputation. He was later given the order by Sun Quan to organize an expedition against Shan Yue, Quan managed to recruit more than ten thousand. Quan suggested that they must not miss the chance when Guan Yu attacked Fancheng and left their back undefended. Sun Quan feigned ignorance to keep it confidential, and the merit was rewarded after the battle. He advised Sun Quan against expeditions across the sea but Sun ignored. The wars resulted in terrible losses, and Sun much regret for the operations. Quan passed away soon after the Conflict between Two Princes.

Xiang Chong, a native of Xiangyang, Yicheng, is a general of Shu Han. He is Xiang Lang's nephew. 
In the expedition against Wu with Liu Bei, Liu was impressed that his force suffered the least losses in the chaos. 
In Chu Shi Biao, Zhuge Liang recommended Xiang as the military counselor for Liu Shan. 
He was later promoted the position of the Commandant of the Central Army, but died in the battle against the barbarian rebellion in Hanjia Commandery.

Cheng Yi is a warlord with his circle of influence in Liang Province. He served Ma Teng, Ma Chao and Han Sui. 
When Cao Cao went on an expedition against Zhang Lu, the warlord of Hanzhong, he, Ma Chao and Han Sui started an uprising with a hundred thousand men. Cao Cao sent Cao Ren and Xu Chu to settle, Cheng was slain in the battle.

Zhu Zhi, a native of Guzhang, Danyang, is a prominent official of Eastern Wu. He is considered one of the founding champions of Wu. 
After the death of Sun Jian, Sun Ce sought to serve Yuan Shu. Zhu noticed Yuan's incompetence. 
Liu Yao feared that Sun-Yuan alliance would be a threat and took Sun's family in Yang Province. Zhu sent men for the escort. After Sun Ce's death, Zhu along with Zhou Yu and Zhang Zhao served Sun Quan. 
When Jin Province surrendered, Sun Quan's cousin Sun Ben planned to send his son as captive. Zhu managed to convince not to do so. 
In Zhu's late years, Sun Quan put even more trust in him. Zhu led a humble life despite his achievements, Sun Quan stated that he's "a man with the wellness of the state at heart that led a life of frugality".

Zhu Huan, a native of Wu County, Wu Commandery, is a prominent general of Sun Wu. 
In the Battle of Ruxu, he feigned weakness for a fire attack. 
In the Battle of Shiting, he offered a plan to capture Cao Xiu alive, take Shouchun and Huainan, Lu Xun didn't approve the plan. A three-pronged assault was taken instead, resulting in a Cao force casualty of ten thousand, and ten thousand animals and vehicles, along with the supplies were seized. 
When Lu Xi, secretary of Lujiang, planned for a rebellion, Zhu and Quan Cong were sent to reinforce as necessary. Later they had to retreat for the plan has been revealed. Li Ying, the Magistrate of Lujiang, intended to ambush when Wu force crossed the river but gave up at the sight of Zhu.

Zhu Yi, a native of Wu County, Wu Commandery, is a prominent general of Sun Wu, and the son of Zhu Huan. 
When Zhuge Dan started a rebellion in Shouchun and sent captive to Eastern Wu to request reinforcement. The operation ended in failure as Hu Lie, a magistrate under Cao Wei rule at the time, ambushed and destroyed their foodstock. 
Zhu Yi refused Sun Chen's order to fight to the last man. Outrageous, Sun had Zhu executed.

Zhu Ran, a native of Danyang Commandery, Yang Province, is a prominent general of Eastern Wu. In early years, he and Sun Quan are classmates. 
After the death of Lu Meng, he and Lu Xun assumed the position of chief military counselors and secured a decisive victory against Liu Bei's spearhead unit. 
In the following years, his mettle as a prominent general won him Sun Quan's respect.

Zhu Bao is a native of Zhuti Commandery, Yi Province. 
When Yong Kai of Nanzhong started a rebellion, Zhu aligned himself to Eastern Wu and joined the fray under Shi Xie's influence. He is no longer seen in history record since then.

Zhu Ling, a native of Shu County, Qinghe State, is a prominent general of Cao Wei. 
First served Han Fu, he joined Yuan Shao when Yuan seized Ji Province. 
When Cao waged war against Tao Qian, Zhu reinforced on Yuan's order, then decided to join Cao. 
Later, he was sent by Cao to stop Yuan Shu. Zhu noticed Liu's thoughts but didn't report. 
In the Battle of Guandu, his reluctance to fight his previous warlord led to his position revoked. 
It was not until the Yuans wiped out was he placed trust again. He participated in numerous battles as the lieutenant, and most of his appearance were in the northwestern theater. 
When Cao Pi came to power, Zhu was trusted and promoted to the General of the Rear, and even provided Zhu with the chance to choose Gaotang County as his fief.

Yang Hu, a native of Nancheng County, Taishan Commandery, is a prominent general of Western Jin. His older sister is the spouse of Sima Shi. 
In the early years of administration in Jin Province, his battles against Lu Kang didn't go well. He took several measures to secure his influence. 
Before passing away from illness, he recommended Du Yu as a good candidate for the expedition against Wu. Later, Du successfully completed this mission. 
The people of Jing and Xiang held Yang with high respect, and a monument was elected in Xiangyang. This stele is also known as the "weeping stele". 
Though also a gifted scholar, most of his works didn't carry on. The old saying "most of a man's life is far from satisfactory" is quoted from him.

He Jin, a native of Wan County, Nanyang, is one of the royal relatives in the ending years of Eastern Han. 
Thanks to his sister elected as the Empress, he was granted with the position of Shizhong. After the Yellow Turban Uprising, he was promoted to marshal, and granted with the title of Shenhou for revealing Yuan Yi's plan. 
The argument over heir selection led the grudge with the eunuchs. He summoned Dong Zhuo to bring men into Luoyang, but this plan was revealed and he was murdered by the Ten Attendants. Dong entered Luoyang as told, and started the era of warlords. 
He Jin sought great achievement but lacked the resolve, Cao Cao stated that "he's just a dim-witted monkey dreaming of dining in the royal hall".

He Yi is a leader of Yellow Turbans. 
With Liu Pi, Huang Shao and He Man, they took Runan, Yingchuan and the vicinity under their control. He sought to join Yuan Shu and Sun Jian, and was eliminated by Cao Cao in the first year of Jian'an. 
In the Romance, on his way to run from the chasing Cao force, Xu Chu trapped him at the Gepi Docks. When Xu Chu surrendered to Cao Cao, Cao executed He Yi and the Yellow Turbans to restore order to the Ru-Yin region.

Leng Bao is a general served Liu Zhang. 
When Liu Bei tried to take Yi Province, Liu Zhang ordered Leng Bao, Liu Gui, Zhang Ren and Deng Xian to defend Luo County. They tried to hold off Liu Bei at Peisui Pass, but was overrun and had to regroup at Mianzhu Pass. When the ownership of Yi Province came to Liu Bei, Leng Bao was executed for his relectance to surrender. 
In the Romance, he's one of Liu Zhang's fierce generals, and appeared in the parts of sword dancing in the feast and the duel against Wei Yan.

Wu Ban, a native of Chenliu, is a general of Shu State. His highest title is the General of Fast Cavalry. 
He made little presence in official history record. It is known that he participated Liu Bei's expedition against Wu as well as Zhuge Liang's northern expedition. 
In the Romance, he first served as Zhang Fei's lieutenant, and led the spearhead in the expedition against Wu. He trapped Sun Huan in Yiling, but had to retreat due to Liu Bei suffering from a decisive defeat. He later participated in Zhuge Liang's northern expedition. In the fifth northern expedition, Wu tried to set the floating bridge on fire to cut the path of chasing Wei force, but was shot by Zhang Hu and Yue Chen from the bank, fell into the water and met his demise.

Wu Lan is a general served Liu Bei. 
In the Battle of Hanzhong, Liu Bei sent Zhang Fei, Ma Chao and Wu Lan to station at Xiabian but took a decisive defeat when attacked by Cao Hong and Zhang Ji. Wu was slain by Qiang Duan, the King of Yinping Di tribe, and his head was sent back to Chang'an.

General for Liu Zhang. His sister is the wife of Liu Zhang's older brother Liu Mao. Cousin of Wu Ban. When Liu Bei invaded Shu, Wu Yi, Liu Xun, Wu Lan, and Lei Tong went to rescue Zhang Ren in Luocheng, but he was captured by Zhao Yun and made into a vassal. When his widow sister became Liu Bei's queen, he would be cordially welcomed as she gave birth to Liu Yong and Liu Li. He participated in Zhuge Liang's northern expedition.

Lu Bu, a native of Jiuyuan, served as the foster son of Ding Yuan then Dong Zhuo. 
He's recognized as fiercest general of the time, there is a saying, "Lu Bu has the best mark for mankind, as with Red Hare for horses". 
Wang Yun came up with a plan to assassinate Dong Zhuo by Lu Bu's hands. Li Jue then summoned Dong's men to take Chang'an. After the defeat, Lu Bu sought to join Yuan Shu and Yuan Shao. 
He attacked Yan Province when Cao was on expedition. After the defeat to Cao, he took Xu Province from Liu Bei. 
He was later defeated by Cao-Liu alliance. Fearing that Lu would help Cao, and still angry about the previous loss, Liu suggested Cao to execute Lu. 
As a man of reputation, the evaluation of Lu Bu had been a topic of debate.

Officer of Wei. When Cao Cao first gained Yanzhou, he recruited Lu Qian to serve in his post and governed the area around Taishan, where he repeatedly put down bandits. He was also a member of the Wei dynasty.

Lu Kai, a native of Buwei County, Yongchang, is a general of Shu Han. 
When Yong Kai surrendered to Eastern Wu, Lu kai and official Wang Kang put up a vigorous struggle, preventing Yong from entry. 
Zhuge Liang promoted Lu Kai to the position of the Magistrate of Yunnan, and planned for further promotion. Unfortunately, Lu was later murdered by barbarian rebels.

Lu Xiang is a native of Dongping, Yan Province. 
He served Yuan Shao and Yuan Shang before surrendering to Cao Cao with Lu Kuang.

Officer of Shu. When he was young, his father, Lu Chang, sent Liu Yan to Shu, but Liu Yan was unable to return to his hometown because Zhang Lu was blocking the transportation. 
After Liu Bei entered Shu, and after the establishment of Shu Han, he served as a local governor, and during his term of office, he was quite successful in governance.

Lu Meng, a native of Fupi, Runan, is a prominent general of Wu. 
After the death of Sun Ce, he served Sun Quan. Excels at both military art and strategies, he participated in battles such as the expedition against Huang Zhu and the Battle of Red Cliffs. 
He is best known for the Battle of Fancheng: He took Gong'an and Jiangling with platoons of elites when Guan Yu was busy attacking, establishing the foundation for reclaiming Jing Province. 
Lu Meng was minimally educated when young, and Sun Quan urged him to read. His dedication in studying from thirties made him a general exceled at both liberal and military arts, for which Lu Su stated that "Lu is no longer the man of mere muscle". The old saying of "with dedication, men change with time" is also quoted from Lu Meng.

Lu Fan, a native of Xiyang, Runan, is a prominent general of Eastern Wu. 
He participated in Sun Ce's conquest of Jiangdong, and continued to serve Sun Quan after Sun Ce's death. He made notable contributions either as a commander or a magistrate. 
In the Romance, he is portrayed as the one inclined to surrender, which is inconsistent with the official history records.

Lu Kuang is a native of Dongping, Yan Province. 
He served Yuan Shao and Yuan Shang before surrendering to Cao Cao with Lu Xiang.

Staff officer of Liu Cong, and scholar. He was invited by Liu Biao to lecture in Jingzhou, and his reputation was second to that of Zheng Xuan in his time. After Liu Biao's death, he presented a surrender letter to Cao Cao on behalf of Liu Zong. 
Later, his son was implicated in the rebellion with Wei Miao, and Song Zhong was executed.
He first served Lu Bu. Song Xian, Wei Xu and Hou Cheng surrendered when Cao Cao trapped Lu Bu at Xiapi, which led to Lu's demise. He is no longer seen in official history record from this incident.

Daughter of the famous minister Li Gu in later Han. Li Xie was dismissed by Li Gu and thought that Li was in trouble, so Li Wen Ji used a scheme to hide Li Xie, and then her father and brother were killed, Li Wen Ji entrusted Li Xie to Wang Cheng, a disciple of Li Gu, after more than ten years, Li Xie was finally rehabilitated and returned to his hometown to observe mourning for Li Gu, and finally reunited with Li Wen Ji, who also warned Li Xie not to have complaints, so as not to be convicted again.

Li Dian, a native of Juyie County, is one of the earliest subordinates, and is one of the few scholarly generals. 
He participated in Cao's expeditions against Lu Bu, Zhang Xiu and Yuan Shao. He assumed the position of lieutenant when Cao Ren attacked Xinye. His night ambush was a terrible failure as Liu Bei's strategist Xu Shu knew it. 
As the lieutenant of Xiahou Dun, he saw the intent of Liu force and advised Xiahou against taking aggression but was ignored. Xiahou was caught in Zhuge Liang's fire attack and managed to escape thanks to Li Dian's rescue. 
After the Battle of Red Cliffs, he defended Hefei with Zhang Liao and Yue Jin. Though in much disagreement with Zhang Liao, he was still able to cooperate with Zhang to fight Sun Quan's force in the Battle of Xiaoyao Ford.

Li Hui, a native of Jianning, Yi Province, is an official of Shu Han. 
He first served Liu Zhang, joined Liu Bei when he entered Shu. Soon he was sent to Hanzhong to escort Ma Chao. 
Li Hui's merit came from eliminating numerous Nanzhong rebellions.

He first served Liu Zhang, then joined Eastern Wu. 
He surrendered to Gan Ning when Liu Bei entered Shu, and participated in numerous battles against Shu with varying result. 
In the Romance, he fought the Shu Han force led by Zhang Bao and Guan Xing around Yidu, and was slain by Guan Xing.

Li Su is a native of Wuyuan, Bing Province. 
Participated in the plot to murder Dong Zhuo, he led just a dozen of elites disguised as close guards. When Dong arrived, Li Su stabbed Dong with halberd. The injured Dong fell from the carriage and slain by Lu Bu. 
After the death of Dong Zhuo, Lu Bu sent Li Su to attack Niu Fu. Li was defeated and later executed by Lu for accountability.

Li Jue, a native of Beidi Commandery, is a warlord of Liang Province. 
After the assassination of Dong Zhuo by Lu Bu and Wang Yun, he rallied Dong's force to defeat Wang and Lu and take Chang'an as suggested by Jia Xu. 
Li Jue managed the imperial affairs with Guo Si and Fan Chou, until he and Guo started to have disagreements over authority and waged war against each other for months. 
After Han Emperor Xian was escorted by Cao Cao to Xudu, Cao started an expedition against Li, and ordered to execute his relatives within three levels. The Emperor hated Li to the core, and ordered to hang his head high to display to the general public.

His family was a local powerful man in Yizhou. 
His father was executed by Liu Yan after Liu Yan first entered Shu to establish his authority. 
After Liu Bei won Yizhou, he was recruited. 
In the play, Zhuge Liang asked Li Fu to tell Liu Chan his last words before he died in Wuzhang Yuan.

The original was a subordinate of Dong Zhuo. 
After Dong Zhuo and Niu Fu were killed, Li Jue was convinced to save his life, and Li Meng and Fan Chou followed suit. 
However, Li Meng was subsequently killed by Li Jue and others who were fighting for power.

Li Ru, a native of Heyang (Zuofengyi, Sili Province), is a respected scholar of the ending years of Eastern Han. 
He poisoned the young emperor on Dong Zhuo's order. Other than this incident, he is not seen in the official history record. 
In the Romance, as the son-in-law and strategist of Dong Zhuo, he offered crafty plots and participated in important plans such as persuading Lu Bu to surrender, the election of the young emperor, and the relocation of imperial capital to Chang'an. 
Wang Yun sent DiaoChan to cast in a bone between Dong Zhuo and Lu Bu. Li knew Wang's intent and advised Dong to grant Diao to Lu but was ignored. Dong was eventually assassinated. 
After Dong's death, Li was executed by Wang.

There are few records in the official history. 
When Cao Cao conquered Yuan Shu, Yuan Shu abandoned his army and fled, leaving Qiao Liao, Li Feng, Liang Gang and Le Jue behind. After the defeat, Li Feng was killed by Cao Cao.

Li Yan, a native of Nanyang Commandery, Jing Province, is a prominent official of Shu Han. 
When he moved to Shu to stay away from the conflicts, Liu Zhang granted him with the Magistrate of Chengdu. Liu Zhang ordered him to hold Liu Bei off, but he surrendered without a fight. 
After Liu Bei took Yi Province, he was granted with the Magistrate of Jianwei, and he focused on infrastructure improvement while in office. After expedition failed, Liu Bei intended to trust his son to Li. Zhuge Liang knew that Li is an arrogant man of ill intent, and took precautions. In Zhuge's expedition, he was demoted to a citizen for finding excuses about the delayed delivery of supplies. After Zhuge's death, Li believed that he would never be offered a position again and fell to depression.

He was a native of Dingling County in Elling County, an official of Cao Wei. 
When he was a governor of Xi'e county, he was promoted by Zhong Cao and served three generations of Cao's father and son, and his reputation was heard even by Zhuge Liang, who even wrote to Sima Yi to ask him about it.

Bu Zhi, a native of Huaiying, Linhuai, is a prominent officer and general of Eastern Wu. His kin Bu Lian Shi is a preferred concubine of Sun Quan. 
Bu Zhi first served as Sun Quan's chief accountant, then left the position to visit the talents in Wuzhong with Zhuge Jin and Yan Jun. He became an official again when he gained a considerable amount of reputation. 
When Liu Bei started an eastern expedition, the minority population around Wuling also sought to join the fray. Sun sent Bu to garrison at Yiyang. The unrest continued until Bu eliminated them. 
Bu garrisoned at Xiling for two decades and the enemies nearby did not bother to mess with him. 
After Lu Xun's death during the Conflict between Two Princes, he assumed the position of prime minister.

After Cao Cao defeated Lu Bu, he was appointed as the governor of Xuzhou. 
Cao Cao sent Liu Bei and Zhu Ling to Xuzhou to intercept Yuan Shu, but Liu Bei took the opportunity to kill Che Zhou and seize Xuzhou.

Xin Pi, a native of Yangdi, Yingchuan, is Xin Ping's younger brother. He first served Yuan Shao, then joined Cao Cao. 
After the death of Yuan Shao, Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang went against each other and fought at Pingyuan. After the defeat, Yuan Tan sent Xin Pi to negotiate for a truce. 
Xin Pi advised Cao Cao to take the chance of the Yuan brothers fighting each other to take Hebei for his own. Cao Cao did as advised and successfully took Hebei. 
Trusted by Cao Cao, Xin Pi served three Cao rulers. He is known for providing direct and practical advices.

Xin Ping, a native of Yangdi, Yingchuan, is Xin Pi's older brother and an official under Yuan Shao's command. 
He first served Han Fu, and won Yuan Shao's interest by convincing Han to grant the position of the Governor of Ji Province to Yuan. 
Though loyal to Yuan Shao, Xin Ping also suggested his sons to fight for dominance, leading to the Yuans being out of the competition.

Xing Dao Rong is a fictitious character in the Romance as he is not seen any of available history record. 
Portrayed as a fierce general under the command of Liu Du, the Magistrate of Lingling, Xing is said to possess the strength to fight ten thousand men. Along with Liu Xian, Liu Du's son, he fought the invading force led by Zhuge Liang. 
Defeated by Zhuge Liang with a plot, Xing offered to cooperate with the invaders, with the true intent to organize an ambush against Liu Bei's force. His true intent was noticed by Zhuge Liang, and later he was slain by Zhao Yun.

A literary man from Wei and one of the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove. 
Lack of decorum and drinking during his parents' death alienated him from Zhong Hui, and political strife as a whole. Committed to Taoism, he wrote several famous books and poems on it. An old Chinese idiom on greeting people civilly is said to come from his warm reception of Ji Kang, who arrived with a harp and alcohol, after a poor reception of his brother, who came to offer condolences.

Dian Wei, a native of Jiwu, Chenliu, is a prominent general under Cao Cao's command. He is said to possess extraordinary strength. In the Romance Cao Cao called him the "Er Lai of the time", suggesting that Dian possesses immense strength. 
As a man of justice and chivalry, Dian first served Zhang Miao. Xiahou Dun later offered an invitation, which Dian accepted. 
When Cao was at mortal danger in Puyang, he led Cao out with armor and shield. 
Since then Dian served as Cao's personal guard. During Zhang Xiu's rebellion, he held the line for Cao to escape. It is said that he still stared menacingly even at his last breath. 
Cao Cao cried his eyes out when he learned of Dian's death, "the loss of both my eldest son and nephew is not as heart-breaking as the death of Dian Wei!"

Zhou Cang is not seen in the official history record, but in the Romance and anecdotes. He is portrayed as a general under Zhang Bao's command. After the downfall of Yellow Turbans, he made a living as a bandit on Mt. Wo Niu until he met Guan Yu and joined his rank. 
He fought Yu Jin and Pang De, and took Pang from water into custody. 
After Guan Yu was defeated in Maicheng and executed by Sun Quan, Zhou Cang cut his neck to follow his commander's fate. 
He is referenced from a guard barking at Lu Su as Lu demanded Guan Yu to return Jing Province.

Zhou Tai, a native of Xiacai (Jiujiang, Yang Province), is one of the Twelve Tiger Ministers of Jiangdong, and served Sun Ce with Jiang Qin. 
When holding against the bandits with Sun Quan in Xuancheng, he took a dozen bad injuries and nearly lost his life. 
He was allocated to the main force in later major battles, including the Ref Cliffs, Hefei and Yiling, and even got Sun Quan and Xu Sheng out of the encirclement. 
When served as the commander in the Battle of Ruxu, Zhu Ran and Xu Sheng were not at all pleased with the assignment. Sun ordered Zhou to take off his armor to show his scars and talk about the bitter battle that caused them, by then Zhu and Xu were convinced.

Zhou Yu, a prominent general of Eastern Wu, is the sworn brother of Sun Ce, a close friend of Lu Su, XiaoQiao's spouse. He is said to be a man of quality and talents. 
He helped Sun Ce take Jiangdong. Before death, Sun Ce ordered Zhou Yu and Zhang Zhao to offer Sun Quan their expertise. 
Zhou is an attractive, considerate man well versed in music and rhythm. He was known as Zhou Lang at his time. 
Cheng Pu was not fond of Zhou, but was still impressed of Zhou's temperament. 
Before the Battle of the Red Cliffs, Zhou insisted on a direct conflict with Cao, and brokered an alliance with Liu. With a fire attack, the battle ended in a decisive victory. 
Zhou mapped out the major plans of Eastern Wu, and proposed to beocme the second super power of the time.

Zhou Fang, a native of Yang Xian, Wu Commandery, is an official of Eastern Wu, and the father of Zhou Chu. 
Before the Battle of Shiting, he feigned surrender to Cao Wei, and baited Cao Xiu's attack. Cao took a terrible defeat and the casualty was claimed to be more than a hundred thousand men and horses combined.

This is a fictional character that does not exist in history. 
Meng Tan was a general under Han Fu, the sheriff of Luoyang, and died under Guan Yu's sword when he was cutting down six generals.

Meng Da, a native of You Fufeng, Sili Province, is a talent served Liu Zhang, Liu Bei and Cao Pi. 
In the 1st year of Jian'an, he served Liu Zhang. Liu Zhang sent Meng Da to bring Liu Bei into Shu, he joined Liu Bei at arrival. After Liu Bei took Shu, he assumed the Magistrate of Yidu. 
In the 24th year of Jian'an, Guan Yu started an expedition, his refusal to reinforce caused Guan to take a bitter defeat at Maicheng. Meng surrendered to Wei. 
During his years of service in Wei, he won Cao Pi's trust and assumed the Magistrate of Xincheng, a key position on the southwestern border. 
As Meng lost his privilege after the death of Cao Pi, Zhuge Liang offered him a chance to rejoin. Sima Yi learned of his intent and attacked him on Shangyong. Meng was caught off guard and executed.

Wu Anguo is a fictitious character in the Romance. 
He is portrayed as a general under the command of Kong, the Magistrate of Beihai. 
After Guan Yu slew Hua Xiong, Lu Bu showed up to fight in person. The warlords sent two generals but were defeated with ease. Wu Anguo challenged Lu with his hammer and lost his hands in about ten exchanged attacks. The coalition provided timely rescue for him to escape from death.

Fa Zheng first served Liu Zhang but was not given much attention. He later joined Liu Bei and became trusted. 
He was one of those to yield Yi Province to Liu Bei, then along with Pang Tong assumed the chief strategists to help Liu take the province. 
He is one of the five creators of the"Codes of Shu. 
For the Battle of Hanzhong, Fa Zheng made the plan to slay Xiahou Yuan. Cao stated that "regrettably, Fa is not among my countless talents!"
As a man obsessed with fairness, Fa Zheng offered great plans and sought to return any favor, with his attempt to shield incoming arrows for Liu being the most notable. 
After the bitter defeat at Yiling, Zhuge stated that "If Fa were alive, he would do anything to stop His Majesty from this expedition, or at least minimizing losses".

Ju Shou is a strategist served Yuan Shao. 
Ju recommended to escort the Emperor. Yuan refused to oblige, giving Cao Cao the chance. 
Ju suggested against Yuan's "fair allocation of territory" but was ignored. After Yuan's death, his sons fought for dominance. 
Ju and Tian recommended Yuan Shao not to press on the people. Yuan ignored and even kept them at arm's length. 
Before the Battle of Guandu, Ju stated that Yan Liang is not the man of choice to lead the troops and was again ignored. Yan were killed in action. 
He suggested that Yuan's force should hold Yanjin and divide a force to Guandu, and was again ignored. Frustrated, Ju claimed that he fell ill and was relieved from military duty. 
After the battle, Cao offered him to join. Ju refused and was executed for escaping.

Jin Xuan, the Magistrate of Wuling at the last years of Eastern Han, is (possibly) a descendant of Jin Mi Di, a duke of Western Han, and the father of Jin Yi. 
The official history records about him is contradictory, with one stating that he surrendered to Liu Bei, and another stating that he died when Liu Bei attacked Wuling. 
In the Romance, Jin ignored his subordinate Gong Zhi's suggestion to surrender the castle and determined to participate in the battle in person. Defeated by Zhang Fei, he tried to return to the castle and found it already taken. Gong scolded him, "you're a stubborn leader that does not follow what the fate leads, but the people and I do, we have surrender to Liu!" He was then shot to death and his head was brought to Zhang Fei.

Hou Cheng is a lieutenant under Lu Bu's command. 
In the official history record, when Cao force trapped Lu Bu in Xiapi, Song Xian, Wei Xu and Hou Cheng betrayed Lu by opening the gate and surrendering to Cao, leading to Lu Bu taken into custody. 
The Romance, Hou's behavior while Cao and Lu stood off at Puyang takes up a considerable part. While Lu Bu was trapped at Xiapi, Hou set up a feast to celebrate for reclaiming the horses taken by bandits, then was given caning as punishment by Lu. Irritated, Hou worked with Wei Xu and Song Xian to formulate a plan to surrender to Cao Cao. They stole Lu's Red Hare and Fang Tian Painted Halberd and went straight to the headquarters of Cao force.

Jiang Wei first served Wei before surrendering to Shu. He assumed the high commander after Fei Yi, and is a prominent general in the late years of Shu. 
Under Jiang's leadership, eleven expeditions were organized without any decisive gain. Some historians stated that Shu "is a minor power of the time that cannot afford wars" and the expeditions led to its earlier end. 
After the end of Shu, Jiang Wei feigned surrender to Zhong Hui and tried to cast in a bone between Zhong Hui and Deng Ai. He died in a mutiny. 
In Romance, he is portrayed as the one to carry on Zhuge Liang's legacy, and hence played a major role.
There is no such person in the official history, it is the daughter of Jiang Wei, who was invented in later times.

Huangfu Song is a prominent general known for his fidelity. 
On imperial order he fought the Yellow Turbans with promising result, notably the capture and execution of Zhang Liang. For these merits he was granted with the General of Chariots and Cavalry and the Governor of Ji Province. 
Huangfu did not take the credit for his own, but claimed it to be Zhu Jun's, and tried to plead innocence for Lu Zhi. Reluctant to bribe the eunuchs, he was relieved from position. 
Huangfu assumed commander numerous times and remained loyal to Han. 
With the influence from his achievements, he tried to interfere with Dong's ambition. 
Huangfu responded to Wang Yun's call to arms against Dong Zhuo by leading his force to Meiwu to eliminate the remnants of Dong's men.

Ji Ling, a ferocious general under Yuan Shu's command, is largely seen in the biography of others. 
In the Romance, he's portrayed as a native of Shandong that wielded a two-edge pike. 
He led an attack on Liu Bei, who was garrisoned at Xiaopei at the time. Lu Bu made an unbelievably accurate shot to convince both sides give up the conflict. This is seen in official history record but not an anecdote in Romance. 
On the northward journey with dishonored Zhongjia, namely his warlord, to seek shelter under Yuan Shao's influence, they encountered Liu Bei's force and Ji was defeated in a duel against Zhang Fei.

Hu Ban, a fictitious character in the Romance, is portrayed to be under the command of Wang Zhi, the Magistrate of Xingyang under Cao Cao's rule. 
When Guan Yu left Cao Cao to take a long journey back to Liu Bei and passed Xingyang, Wang Zhi planned to set up a fire to kill Guan. Hu Ban noticed that Guan was no ordinary man and carried a letter written by his father Hu Hua, and decided to grant him pass. 
Later, Hu went to Jing Province to join Guan Yu. When Liu Bei assumed the Lord of Hanzhong, he entered Chuan with Fei Shi and witnessed Liu receiving the honor.

Hu Zhen, a native of Liang Province, is a general under Dong Zhuo's command. 
When the coalition against Dong, Hu was assigned as the defense commander to lead the generals. Hu is an irritable man without leadership skill that caused the discontent of Lu Bu and other generals. With Dong's force in disarray, Sun Jian launched an offensive and slew Hua Xiong. After Dong's death, he first served Wang Yun then joined Li Jue, a general previously under Dong's command. 
In the Romance, Dong assigned Hua Xiong as the commander, with Hu as his lieutenant, to hold the coalition force attacking HuLao Pass. Hu fought Cheng Pu, a general under Sun Jian's command, and was slain in a few exchanges of attacks.

Officer of Shu. Zhang Fei's subordinate. After the death of Guan Yu, Zhang Fei plans a campaign against Wu. He orders this man to prepare funeral clothes within 3 days. The next day, he and Fan Qiang beg for more time. A furious Zhang Fei has him whipped and threatens him with execution if he is late. To protect himself he stabs a drunken Zhang Fei and takes his head as a gift to Wu. When Liu Bei invades Wu, he is given to Liu Bei, who has him executed.

Ling Tong is a prominent general of Wu and one of the Twelve Tiger Ministers of Jiangdong. 
He served Sun Ce with his father Ling Cao since young. In the battle against Huang Zhu, Gan Ning shot his father dead. Ling then took Gang as his nemesis. 
After the Battle of the Red Cliffs, Gan attacked Yiling on Zhou Yu's order but was encircled by Cao Ren. Ling proposed and insisted on reinforcing and rescuing Gan despite their relationship. The operation hindered Cao's advancement and successfully rescued Gan. 
In the Battle of Xiaoyao Ford, he held the chasing force with his elites to make space for Sun Quan to escape, and was badly injured in the process. 
Ling later volunteered to persuade the Shanyues to give up opposition but unfortunately died of illness during the process.

Ling Cao, a native of Yuhang (Wu Commandery, Yang Province), is the father of Ling Tong and served under Sun Ce's command. 
He answered Sun Ce's call to arms and was a notable contributor of merit. 
In the attack against Huang Zhu, he took the role of spearhead to attack Xiakou and defeated Huang's force, but was killed in action by Gan Ning's shot.

Xiahou He is a son of Xiahou Yuan, a general of Wei, and the brother of Xiahou Ba. 
In the official history record, Zhong Hui started a rebellion soon after the conquest of Shu. Xiahou, the Left Minister of War at the time, was in Chengdu on the envoy mission and ignored the intimidation. After the rebellion was settled, Xiahou was granted with Xianghou for his merit 
In the Romance, when Zhuge Liang launched the northern expedition to attack Wuzhang Plains, Sima Yi promoted Xiahou He to the Marching Minister of War for his insights of tactics and the passion to avenge his father like his brother Xiahou Hui. The brothers managed to grab the supplies at Shangfang Valley to please Sima Yi, unaware that it was an arrangement intentionally made by Zhuge Liang for a later offensive.

Xiahou Shang, a native of Qiao County, Pei State, is the nephew of Xiahou Yuan, a general of Wei. 
He's a man of military talents, as shown by eliminating the rebellion in Dai District, defeating Liu Feng, taking Shangyong, and defeated Zhuge Jing with fire attack. 
Xiahou won Cao Pi's trust and was given the right to "judge the worth of the people", which was later revoked on Jiang Ji's vigorous objection. 
In the Romance, he is portrayed as Xiahou Dun's nephew that lost Mt. Tian Dang to Huang Zhong, assigned to hold Xiangyang with Xu Huang after successfully holding Fancheng. He later attacked Jiangling with Cao Zhen but was defeated by Lu Xun.

Xiahou Wei, a native of Qiao County, Pei State, is a son of Xiahou Yuan. 
He's a man of chivalrous mind and is capable of picking the right person for tasks. Notably, he believed that Yang Hu would serve as a good talent, which was proven in later years. 
He plays a rather prominent role in the Romance: Sima Yi elected Xiahou Wei and his brother as spearheads for his mastery of riding and shooting skills as well as the brothers' passion to avenge their father. Later, he participated in the expedition against Gongsun Yuan.

Xiahou En is most likely a fictitious character in the Romance as he is not seen any of official history record. 
He is portrayed as the general carrying Qinghong, one of the two swords owned by Cao Cao (the other being "Yitian" wielded by Cao Cao himself). In the Battle of Changban, he was slain by Zhao Yun with a thrust of spear, and Qinghong was taken as trophy.

Xiahou Dun, a native of Qiao County, Pei State, is a prominent general of Cao Wei, and a cousin of Cao Cao. 
He answered Cao Cao's call to arms, and lost his left eye from stray arrow. In the Romance, he is a ferocious warrior that "extracted the arrow and swallowed his destroyed eye". 
Later he was called the blinded Xiahou for the impairment, which he hates very much. 
He is the most trusted subordinate for Cao "used to take the same carriage with Dun, and granted free access of his bedroom like no other subordinate". 
Though portrayed as a ferocious commander and duelist, he's more of a diligent leader valuing discipline and leading a relatively humble life. His expertise in administration and logistics far exceeds his combat skills, and played the supportive role for years.

Xiahou Yuan is a prominent general under Cao Cao's command, and Xiahou Dun's younger kin of the same generation. 
With Xiahou Dun he answered Cao's call to arm, he is best known for assaults with a small force. After defeating Ma Chao, he volunteered to stand guard in Chang'an. He put an end to the unrest in Liang Province, discouraging the Western Qiang from invasion. 
He worked with Zhang He as the spearhead in the expedition against Zhang Lu. After Zhang's surrender, he stationed at Hanzhong. When engaging with Liu Bei's force at Mt. Dingjun, he didn't take the attack seriously and lost his life. 
Zhang Fei found Xiahou Yuan's niece and married her. 
Xiahou Yuan's ferocity is unparalleled at the time, but he's also called as the "champion of blind assault".

Xiahou Mao is a son of Xiahou Dun. 
When Cao Pi succeeded the throne, he assigned Xiahou to station in Chang'an, taking over Xiahou Yuan. 
In Shu's expedition, Wei Yan stated that Xiahou Mao is "a unwit craven" and suggested a direct assault on Zhiwu Valley to take Chang'an. Zhuge Liang did not accept the plan. 
In the Romance, he's portrayed as the son of Xiahou Yuan but trusted to Xiahou Dun. He was granted with authority to command but had never fought a battle. He volunteered to hold Zhuge Liang's northern expedition force, but his force was scattered in the battle against Zhao Yun on Mt. Fengming. This crushing defeat is followed by more losses. He then went to Qiangzhong and the pang of shame made him unwilling to return to Luoyang.

Xiahou De, a general of Wei, and the older brother of Xiahou Shang. He is most likely a fictitious character in the Romance as he is not seen in official history record. 
In the Battle of Hanzhong, he stationed at Mt. Tiandang, where the foodstuff of their force was kept. When Huang Zhong arrived with his men, he intended to hold the position with ease. Much to his surprise, Shu force was in high morale and launched a direct offensive, and with the stored foodstuff set on fire by Yan Yan, Wei force was in disarray. As Xiahou tried to extinguish the fire, Yan slew him.

Xiahou Ba, a prominent general of Cao Wei and late Shu Han, is the second son of Xiahou Yuan. 
After Xiahou Yuan's death, Cao Rei trusted Xiahou Ba to Cao Shuang and Sima Yi, and Cao Shuang offered Xiahou Ba many chances to prove his worth. 
When Sima Yi caused the Incident at the Gaoping Tombs and abdicated the throne of Cao Shuang, Xiahou Ba believed that the Simas will not spare him. 
As his cousin married Zhang Fei, and her daughter married Liu Shan, he was granted with a high position. 
After Xiahou surrendered to Shu, Jiang Wei asked him about the condition in Wei. Xiahou shared the key issues, and stated that Zhong Hui would become a huge problem.

Sun Shangxiang is the daughter of Sun Jian, the younger sister of Sun Ce and Sun Quan. 
Her true name is not seen in the official history record, the name "Shangxiang" was given by the people of a later time. 
She's said to be a sharp-minded, determined lady with maidens wielding blades. 
To secure the alliance with Liu Bei, Sun Quan offered his sister to marry Liu. As the sister of Sun Quan, she didn't respect rules or her spouse, and made Liu concerned about "problems right under his nose". 
In the Romance, she is portrayed to be relatively friendly to Liu Bei. She followed Liu back to Jing Province and the Wu force sent to capture Liu were fended off. 
It's said that after the Battle of Yiling, she drowned herself in the river when she heard that Liu Bei was killed in action.

Sun Xiu, the sixth son of Sun Quan, is the third ruler of Eastern Wu. 
Sun Chen had great influence at the time. Sun Xiu worked with Zhang Bu from one of the four major houses of Jiangdong as well as Ding Feng, one of the Twelve Tiger Ministers and successfully re-established his authority. 
Sun Xiu then aimed to restore the glory of Wu, and tried to grab the land of Shu when it was just conquered by Wei, only to be discouraged by Luo Xian, the last champion swearing fealty to Shu. 
Sun Xiu died of sudden illness, and trusted his heir to Puyang Xin and Zhang Bu. However, Puyang and Zhang elected Sun Hao, the son of Sun Xiu's deceased brother.

Sun He, the third son of Sun, was elected as the heir when the eldest son Sun Deng died of illness. 
Princess Quan repeatedly spoke ill of him, and worked with Sun Ba the King of Lu in starting the Conflict between Two Princes. As a result, Sun Quan revoked Sun He's title of the heir, sentenced Sun Ba to a suicide, and elected Sun Liang as the heir instead. 
Right before his death, Sun Quan sought to call Sun He back to made him the heir again, but gave up on the vigorous rejection of Princess Quan and Sun Jun. 
Soon after Sun Quan's death, Zhuge Ke was executed for seeking to support Sun He succeeding the throne, and Sun He was sentenced to a suicide which he had to oblige.

Sun Liang, the youngest son of Sun Quan, is the second ruler of Eastern Wu that succeeded the throne at the age of ten. The authority was held by the officials most influential, namely Zhuge Ke, Sun Jun and Sun Chen. 
After the death of the first two, Sun Chen took the power for his own. Sun Liang was not pleased of being a puppet. As he grew older, he trained his own force and launched new policies in hope of eliminating Sun Chen and reclaiming the authority entitled to him. With the plan revealed right before its fruition, Sun Chen took the initiative to launch a coup d'etat and abdicated Sun Liang's throne. 
Fearing that Sun Liang might seek reclaiming the throne, his successor Sun Xiu banished him to the south of Min. He died of illness before he could reach the destination.

Sun Huan, a native of Fuchun, Wu Commandery, is the third son of Sun He, a younger generation kin of Sun Jian. 
In the Battle of Yiling, he fought the invading Shu force with Lu Xun and was encircled by Liu Bei. The tide soon turned as Liu was caught in Lu Xun's plot. Sun Huan led his men to give chase and almost captured Liu alive.

Sun Qian, a native of Beihai, Qing Province, is a founding member of Shu Han. 
Recommended by the renowned scholar Zheng Xuan, Sun mostly contributed with his communication skills by persuading major powers such as Yuan Shao and Liu Biao for shelter. 
When Liu Bei entered Yi Province, Sun was honored as the General of Fidelity, and is considered as key founding members like Jian Yong and Mi Zhu.

Sun Jian is the father of Sun Ce and Sun Quan. 
He is known for the meit of fighting the Yellow Turbans. 
During the coalition against Dong, when the others hesitated due to the size of Dong's force, Sun Jian determined to push forward. He drove away Dong's force with a plot at Luyang, defeated Lu Bu twice, and even slew Hua Xiong. Sun rejected Dong's truce offer, and drove Dong from Luoyang. 
Sun found the imperial jade seal in Luoyang which Yuan Shu asked with the safety of Sun's consort. 
On Yuan Shu's order, Sun Jian fought Liu Biao, who sent Huang Zhu to defend. The first encounter ended in the decisive victory of Sun's force. Sun then laid siege and gave chase onto Mt. Xian, where he was shot dead. 
In the Romance, his merit was given to Guan Yu to show Guan's ferocity.

Sun Yi, a native of Fuchun, Wu Commandery, is the third son of Sun Jian. His method of coping is much alike Sun Ce, his eldest brother. 
After the assassination of Sun Ce, Zhang Zhao suggested to trust the authority of military command to Sun Yi, but Sun Ce insisted on choosing Sun Quan. 
He assumed the Magistrate of Danyang, the most crucial and dangerous region of Jiangdong at the time, and won the heart of populace. Unfortunately, he was murdered by Gui Lan, Dai Yuan and Bian Hong. 
His spouse Ms. Xu conducted the investigation on the murder, and even formulated a plan to put the rebellion to an end.

Sun Deng, a native of Fuchun, Wu Commandery, is the eldest son of Sun Quan. He was elected as the heir when Sun Quan gained the title of the King of Wu. 
Sun Deng is a man valuing filial piety, talent hunting, and the wellness of people. He maintained a good relationship with Lu Xun the Topmost General of Eastern Wu. Sun Quan would rather waging war against Cao Pi than making Sun Deng a hostage in Cao Wei. 
Right before he died of illness at the age of thirty three, he still wrote to Sun Quan to make suggestions about administration and talent candidates. 
After Sun Deng's death, Sun Quan elected Sun He as the heir but provided Sun Ba, the King of Lu, with much affection, leading to the Conflict between Two Princes.

Sun Ce is Sun Jian's eldest son and Sun Quan's brother. He married DaQiao. 
He went on expeditions with his father, and served Yuan Shu after his father's death. 
As suggested by Zhang Hong's "Jiangdu Plan", he recruited talents and took the whole Jiangdong. 
He left when Yuan Shu proclaimed the Emperor of Zhongjia. 
As a skillful leader, Sun Ce has the alias of the "Champion of Duelists". However, he took action without due deliberation. 
Guo Jia stated that "As a leader of the force in the number of a million, he is unaware of how important his own safety is. Any assassination from grudge puts him at great risk. I reckon that he'll die in the hand of an ordinary murderer." 
After Sun killed Xu Gong, a hanger assassinated him and gave Sun grave wounds, Sun died soon afterwards.

Sun Yu, the second son of Sun Jian's younger brother Sun Jing, is Sun Quan's cousin. 
After the major unrest of Jiangdong in the ninth year of Jian'an, he assumed the Magistrate of Danyang following Sun Yi, and won the heart of local people. 
Sun Yu is fond of literature, and he continued reading even during military maneuvers. 
Sun Yu fought Shanyue with Zhou Yu. Before death, Zhou suggested Sun to invade Shu. However, with Liu Bei being reluctant to yield the way, it was never put into motion.

Sun Li is a general of Wei. 
In the Battle of Shiting, he attacked with Cao Xiu. He advised Cao against going too deep. Cao insisted on pushing and the battle ended in a defeat. 
Cao Rui commenced a large number of construction programs while on the throne, which Sun advised against. Cao ignored and levied even more civilians for the construction effort, Sun adjusted the order to stop the program altogether. 
When Quan Cong, a general of Sun Wu, launched an offensive, Sun led his men to fight in person. 
During the conflict between Pingyuan and Qinghe Commanderies, he was demoted to a captain of gate guards for his straightforward remark upset Cao Shuang, and it was not until the Incident at the Gaoping Tombs was he granted with an important position again.

Sun Quan is the second son of Sun Ce. He proclaimed himself the Great Emperor of Wu. 
He carried on Sun Ce's will, formed an alliance with Liu in the Battle of Red Cliffs and defeated Cao. 
In later years, Sun Quan reclaimed Jing Province by sending Lu Meng to attack the castle when Guan was on an expedition, and sent Lu Xun to held off Shu force. 
After Liu's death, he sought to rebuild relationship with Shu to fight Wei. 
Sun Ce believed Sun Quan's skill as a ruler far exceeds his. Cao Cao also acknowledged Sun Quan's skills. 
In his early years, Sun was a considerate leader with a sense of humor. He sought to maintain good relationship with nearby states and become the example of discipline and justice. However, his choice of heir led to destabilization in the years to come.

Xu Huang is a prominent general of Wei. He is one of the Five Elite Generals. 
He joined Cao's faction after Cao escorted Emperor Xian. 
Xu played a role in Cao's conquest. In the Battle of Guandu, he defeated Yan Liang, took Baima, pushed to Yanjin, and slew Wen Chou. 
In the northern expedition against Wuhuan, Xu secured a major victory against Tadun. When Ma Chao started a rebellion, Xu managed to make space for Cao force. 
In the Battle of Fancheng, he feigned attack on Guan Yu for a decisive victory. 
In official history record, Xu and Guan were born in the same Commandery and became good friends. In the Battle of Fancheng, they did not duel, but kept a distance and had a chit-chat before returning to give orders. 
In the Romance, Xu was shot to dead by Meng in an expedition.

A chivalrous man at a young age, Xu Shu maintained a close relationship with Zhuge Liang and Pang Tong, and recommended Zhuge to Liu Bei. 
When Cao went on Jing Province expedition, Xu aimed to travel southward to Jiangxia with Liu. With Cao force taking his mother into custody, he had no choice but joined Cao. 
Though rarely seen in official history record, Xu was promoted to up to Right General of the Household and Deputy Minister of Control. 
In the Romance, Xu Shu's first battle under Liu's command was against Lus of Cao force and ended in victory. He solved Cao Ren's "Golden Lock of Eight Gates", and forced the retreat of Cao Ren and Li Dian. 
In order to invite Xu, Cao Cao took Xu's mother and sent a fake letter. Indignant, Xu Shu vowed not to offer strategies for Cao.

Xu Sheng, a native of Langya, Xu Commandery, is one of the Twelve Tiger Ministers of Jiangdong. 
He is best known for defeating the thousand-men unit under the command of Huang She, the son of Huang Zu, with just two hundred men.
