In the Battle of Ruxu, Xu Sheng's warships were blown towards the camps of Cao force. Xu led his men to charge at the enemies and won. 
In the Battle of Yiling, Lu Xun defeated Liu's force with fire, Xu also took supply depots in the process. 
When Sun Quan denied sending his son as captive, Cao Pi led an expedition against Wu. Xu fortified the vicinity of Jianye, erected fake defense towers, and deployed warships. When Cao saw such deployment, he was in the impression that the enemies are resolved to fight to the last man and decided to withdraw.

Xu Rong is best known for two major victories: His decisive victory in the battle against Cao Cao at Bian River cost Cao almost all of his force, and even his own life. 
The other is the battle against Sun Jian at Liangdong. It was not long after Sun slew Hua Xiong and defeated Lu Bu, and pushed towards Luoyang did he suffer a terrible defeat in the battle against Xu. 
After Dong's death, Xu sought to serve the imperial authority, then Li Jue, Guo Si and other Western Liang warlords that served Dong accepted Jia Xu's plan to lay siege on Chang'an. 
On the order of Wang Yun, Xu went to fight with Hu Zhen. However, with Hu already aligned to Li, Xu and his men alone could not hold the line, and only to find his demise in the Battle of Xinfeng.

Xun You was put into jail for planning to assassinate Dong, and was granted with Magistrate of Shu Commandery on request after being released. When he received an invitation from Cao, he accepted immediately. 
Xun You advised against Cao's plan to attack Zhang Xiu, Cao ignored and paid the price. 
When Lu Bu tried to hold Xiapi, Xun and Guo Jia suggested a swift offensive. With induced flooding, they captured Lu Bu alive. 
In the Battle of Guandu, Xun offered to distract Yuan's force, which relieved the stress on Baima. He offered to send feign attacks on Ye Commandery and Liyang to distract Yuan's attention, and launched the main offensive on Yuan's headquarters. Yuan fled in a panic. 
Xun You died on the way of expedition against Sun Quan.

Xun Yu is the top strategist under Cao Cao's command but swore fealty to Han instead of Wei. 
He first served Yuan Shao, then judged that Yuan not an ideal leader and joined Cao instead. Cao called Xun "the Zifang under his command". 
While on the expedition of Xu Province, a rebellion broke out and made way for Lu Bu to reach Yan Province. Xun was among the defense effort. 
He advised Cao to escort Emperor Xian to Xudu. 
In the Battle of Guandu, he urged Cao to be more aggressive. Cao did as suggested and won a decisive victory. 
Having sworn fealty to Han, Xun Yu advised Cao against naming himself the King of Wei. 
In the expedition against Sun Quan, he ordered Xun Yu to maintain the morale of his men. Distressed at the vacant meal box given, Xun Yu fell ill and died in Shouchun.

Yuan Shang is the third son of Yuan Shao, and the brother of Yuan Tan and Yuan Xi. 
Yuan Shao had an apparent liking of Yuan Shang but didn't nominate him as the heir. After Yuan's death, Pang Ji and his lot forged Yuan's will and named Yuan Shang the successor. 
This sparked the conflict over the title, with Yuan Shang getting the upper hand for a time. 
After the defeat, Yuan Tan sent Xin Pi to seek operation with Cao. However, Xin advised Cao to take Hebei for his own. 
Yuan Shang sought refuge in Yuan Xi's fief after the defeat, Cao continued his chase to Wu Huan. After taking another defeat on Mt. Bailang, they decided to visit Gongsun Kang of Liaodong. Fearing that Cao Cao might visit with a carnage, he executed Yuan Xi and Yuan Shang and sent their heads to Cao.

Yuan Yin, a native of Ruyang County, Runan Commandery, is one of Yuan Shu's cousins. 
After Yuan Shu's death, Yuan Yin brought along Yuan Shu's coffin, wife and loyal men and sought shelter in Wancheng, which was under the rule of Liu Xun, Magistrate of Lujiang of the time. Later, Wancheng was conquered by Sun Ce, then he was no longer seen in history record. 
In the Romance, Yuan Yin was caught and murdered by Xu Qiu, his jade seal was also taken and presented to Cao Cao.

Yuan Shao is Yuan Shu's commoner brother. He is an acquaintance of Cao. 
Yuan was later elected as the leader of the coalition against Dong Zhuo. After removing Dong from the stage, he defeated Han Fu, Gongsun Zan, Kong Rong and Zhang Yan, seizing the land north of the Yellow River. 
When Emperor Xian left the palace, he didn't feel like playing along. 
Tian advised Yuan to attack the rear of Cao when he's busy attacking Liu. Yuan rejected. 
An indecisive man reluctant to accept the advices from his strategists. Yuan's poor judgment cost him dearly at Guandu. After the defeat at Cangting, he died of illness in Ji Province. 
After his death, his three sons fought each other for domination.

Yuan Shu is Yuan Shao's brother. 
After He Jin's death, he sought to make himself the new emperor, and went hostile against Yuan Shao, who elected Liu Yu as the imperial heir. 
Believing in the role of element rotation in dynasty changes, he forced Sun Jian to hand over the jade seal, and proclaimed himself the founder of a new empire, with the alias of Zhongjia. 
He's proven a tyrant, however, and soon overwhelmed by other warlords. 
He intended to go north and seek shelter in Yuan Shao's circle of influence. Cao Cao sent Liu Bei and Zhu Ling for the chase. With famine ravaging the land, he could not find water and is said to spit blood before death.

Yuan Xi, a native of Ruyang County, Runan Commandery, is the second son of Yuan Shao. Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang are his brothers. He is the spouse of Miss Zhen. 
Yuan Shang visited Yuan Xi for shelter after being defeated by Cao Cao. They made it to Wuhuan and tried to give resistance, only to be owned by the Cao force at Mt. Bailang. They then visited Gongsun Kang, the Magistrate of Liaodong. Fearing that Cao Cao might visit with a carnage, and already considering to be Cao's vassal, he executed Yuan Xi and Yuan Shang and sent their heads to Cao.

Yuan Tan, a native of Ruyang County, Runan Commandery, is the eldest son of Yuan Shao. Yuan Xi and Yuan Shang are his brothers. 
After Yuan Shao's death, he stood together with Yuan Shang for a while to fight Cao Cao, before they turned against each other for dominance. 
Yuan Tan sent messenger to Cao Cao for surrender, and requested an attack on Yuan Shang as exchange. After Yuan Shang was defeated, he called his men to arms in hope of re-establishing the glory of House Yuan. Cao Cao then attacked and trapped him at Chenpi. 
With the assistance request sent to Liu Biao being ignored, and the attempt to re-surrender to Cao denied, Yuan Tan had no choice but fight, and was slain in the battle.

Hao Zhao is a general of Cao Wei. 
He started his military service at an early age, and was promoted to a general for his merits. He held the land west of the Yellow River for more than forty years, and his name alone could discourage any ambitious barbarian. 
After the Battle of Jieting, he believed that Zhuge would attack Chencang, and sent Hao and Wang for the defense, and a castle was built. 
Later, Zhuge's attack on Chencang came as expected. Hao Zhao put up a strong defense that successfully held the line even with all the possible means of siege used. More than twenty days later, the reinforcements of Wei to arrive. Zhuge then considered it impossible to take the castle and withdrew. 
Hao was granted with a title after this battle, though he passed away soon afterwards.

One of the important planners of the Yellow Turban Rebellion. Ma Yuanyi bribed the eunuchs Feng Xu and Xu Feng as their mole, to have gathered tens of thousands of followers in Jingzhou and Yangzhou, intending to stage an uprising in the following year. However, due to the whistleblowing from Tang Zhou (an follower of Zhang Jiao), Ma Yuanyi was arrested and executed in Luoyang. As Ma Yuanyi was killed, the information of the uprising leaked out, forcing Zhang Jiao to brought forward the uprising.

Ma Xiu, a native of Maoling, Fufeng, is Ma Teng's son and Ma Chao's younger brother. 
In the thirteenth year of Jian'an, Ma Teng accepted Cao Cao's invitation and assumed the guard captain. He then moved the family of Ma to Yecheng and swore fealty to Cao Cao, leaving his eldest son in Western Liang. 
Ma Xiu went with his father and was granted with the imperial carriage guard captain to maintain the security of the royal carriage, a position with a fief of two thousand bushels. 
With Ma Chao starting a rebellion, Ma Teng and Ma Xiu were executed by Cao Cao.

Ma Liang, a native of Yicheng, Xiangyang, is Ma Ji's older brother. 
He is said to have white eyebrows and is the most talented, and so there's a saying of the time, "Of the five talents of Ma family, The bearer of the white eyebrows is the most outstanding". 
Ma Liang joined Liu Bei on request when Liu secured control over Jing Province. He then defended Jing Province with Guan Yu as Liu Bei headed for Yi Province. 
To avenge Guan's death, Liu launched a full-scale offensive against Wu. As ordered, Ma Liang successfully convinced the Wuxi tribes in Wuling to join. The Battle of Yiling ended in the decisive defeat of Shu force, Ma Liang was killed in action.

Ma Dai, a native of You Fufeng, Sili Province, is a cousin of Ma Chao. 
Few historical record about him exists, the most notable is the execution of Wei Yan on Yang Yi's order. 
In the Romance, he and Ma Teng visited Xudu to assassinate Cao Cao but were attacked by Cao force. This ended in Ma Teng killed in action and Ma Dai fled in one piece. Later, Ma Chao sought revenge by attacking Cao Cao, and Ma Dai went into war with him. They fought together at Chang'an, Tong Gate and more. 
When Ma Chao joined Liu Bei, he followed. He went on Zhuge Liang's southern expedition against the southern barbarians and slew Mangya Chang. He took the will of Zhuge Liang to serve as the lieutenant of Wei Yan, and slew Wei when he started a rebellion.

Officer of Yuan Shang, and later under Cao Cao. In the succession struggle after Yuan Shao's death, Zhang Yi attacked Yuan Tan with Ma Yan. He later rode to aid Shen Pei's castle when it was attacked by Cao Cao, but was defeated and captured. He then surrendered and joined his captor. He later surrounded Zhao Yun alone in the battle of Changban, but lost to him. He reunited with a retreating Cao Cao during the Battle of Chibi, but was slain by Gan Ning.

Officer of Shu. Joined Zhuge Liang in his Southern campaign. Did well in a number of consecutive battles, but was captured along with Zhang Ni in the battle against Madam Zhurong, the wife Meng Huo. He rushed to help when Liu Bei was defeated by Lu Xun at the battle of Xiaoting and Liu Bei praised him saying that even though he had lost Huang Quan, he had gained Ma Zhon in his place.

Ma Wan is one of the Guanzhong generals in the ending years of Eastern Han, he sought to become one of the major warlords when Dong made a mess in the imperial palace. 
Cao Cao sent Zhong Yao to defend Guangzhong. Later, Ma Chao and Han Sui led a coalition of a hundred thousand men against Cao, but defeated by Cao in the Battle of Tong Gate. 
In the Romance, Ma Wan is portrayed as one of Ma Chao's eight lieutenants. Cao Cao cast a bone between Ma Chao and Han. When Han and Ma Wan were formulating a plot to capture Ma Chao, he broke in carrying a sword, taking five on his own and slew Ma Wan.

Ma Chao is the eldest son of Ma Teng, and one of the Five Tigers of Shu in the Romance. 
Ma Chao is well known by the Qiang tribes. 
In the official history record, Ma Chao started a rebellion with Han Sui without thinking about his own family. Their early victory was followed by losses, then they had to request a truce. Jia Xu alienated Ma and Han, creating a chance for Cao force to take a swift and decisive victory. 
After Cao returned, he held Ma Teng accountable and executed him. 
In his next attempt, he fell prey to a plan, and sought to join Zhang Lu after the loss. 
Zhang held Ma Chao with high respect and intended to marry his daughter to Ma but gave up. 
Ma later wrote to Liu Bei, offering to join him. After joining Liu, he was promoted to up to the General of Fast Cavalry.

Ma Su is Ma Liang's brother. 
As a talent interested in discussing strategies and operations, Ma Su won the trust of Zhuge Liang. Liu Bei, however, has gained more insight of Ma's nature, and told Zhuge, "Ma Su talks big but he's not as skilled as he appears, you must not trust him with crucial duty."
While in the southern expedition, Ma suggested "persuasion is favored over conquest". From Meng's surrender to the very end of Shu, there was no more large-scale conflicts with the southern barbarians. 
After Zhuge left Mt. Qi, he ordered him to hold the key strategic place Jieting. Ma Su gave up the water source and stationed on the heights as he believed it gave him advantage. Zhang He easily cut off his supply line. With Jieting lost, Zhuge had to retreat and executed Ma Su.

Ma Teng, a native of You Fufeng, is a warlord of Liang Province and Ma Chao's father. 
In the Romance, he answered Cao Cao's call to arms to fight Dong Zhuo, then fought Cao with Dong Chengyi. With the latter being unsuccessful, he returned to Western Liang. 
After the Battle of Red Cliffs, Cao Cao meant to get rid of the threats on the boundary of his territory, and Ma Teng is one of them. Ma Teng knew Cao Cao's plan but obeyed the order. He planned to put up resistance but failed, then being executed with Ma Xiu and Ma Tie that came along. To avenge their death, Ma Chao started a rebellion. 
In the history record, however, they've been independent warlords that went to Luoyang to assume the guard captain on imperial order.

Ma Tie, a native of You Fufeng, is Ma Teng's son and Ma Chao's younger brother. 
In the thirteenth year of Jian'an, Ma Teng accepted Cao Cao's invitation and assumed the guard captain. He then moved the family of Ma to Yecheng and swore fealty to Cao Cao, leaving his eldest son in Western Liang. 
Ma Tie went with his father, and was granted with the royal guard captain. 
With Ma Chao starting a rebellion, Ma Teng and Ma Tie were executed by Cao Cao.

Gao Pei is a prominent general under Liu Zhang, the Governer of Yi Privince. 
Gao advised Liu Zhang against inviting Liu Bei numerous times, but was ignored. 
When Liu Zhang sent Liu Bei to attack Zhang Lu, then garrison at Jiameng Pass, Yang Huai and Gao Pei were sent to hold Fusui Pass. When Liu Bei decided to head for Yi Province, he lied that he would return to Jing Province, luring them out and murdering them.

Gao Ding is the barbarian leader in Yuegui Commandery. 
Yong Kai started a rebellion in Nanzhong, joined by local nobles Gao Ding and and barbarian leaders like Meng Huo. Zhuge Liang responded an expedition, during which Yong was slain. 
In the Romance, Magistrates Yong Kai, Zhu Bao and Gao Ding joined barbarian leader Meng Huo's rebellion to attack Yongchang Commandery, Zhuge Liang led the troops to the defense. Zhuge Liang used plots to alienate Yong, Zhu and Gao. Gao eventually executed Yong and Zhu, and offered to surrender with their heads. Gao Ding was granted with the Magistrate of Yi Province, with three commanderies under his administration.

Gao Shun is a fierce general under Lu Bu's command. 
As a man of discipline, he excels in both leadership and combat. In the "Records of Heroes", Wang Can acknowledged that the men under Gao's command are the "assault company". 
Though being a man of fidelity, Gao also directly pointed out Lu's shortcomings, "the end of a nation is not caused by the lack of loyal, wise talents, but by the lack of attention paid to them. Your lack of deliberation and mood swings have led to consequences." Lu was not at all pleased. 
When Cao Cao conquered Lu Bu, Gao was also captured and executed. 
Gao Shun has ever been loyal to Lu Bu but was not trusted. By knowing his talents but didn't put them to use, and refusing to accept sincere advices, Lu Bu has sealed his own fate.

Gao Gan, a native of Yu County, is Yuan Shao's nephew. 
He governed the Province of Bing for seven years, and his administrative capacity was appreciated by local residents. 
After the death of Yuan Shao, he still tried to attack Cao force but to no avail. With Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang fighting each other, it became too difficult for him to carry on. He chose to surrender to Cao Cao, and was granted with the Governer of Bing Province. 
Later, Gao Gan started a rebellion when Cao went on an expedition against the Yuan brothers in Wuhuan, and held against Li Dian and Yue Jin. In the next year, Cao Cao returned from the expedition and attacked Gao. Defeated, he sought to join Liu Biao, only to be slain by Wang Yan.

Gao Lan, a general that served Yuan Shao first then Cao Cao. 
In the Battle of Guandu, he led an attack with Zhang He to attack Cao's headquarters on Guo Tu's order, but held off by Xiahou Dun. To avoid being held accountable, Guo accused Gao and Zhang for not putting up their full effort, giving them no choice but surrendering to Cao. Gao is no longer seen in official history record since then. 
In the Romance, Gao followed Cao Cao back to Xudu for defense against Liu Bei's force from Runan. The two forces engaged at Rangshan. In the battle, Gao Lan slew Liu Pi, then was slain by Zhao Yun.

Zhang Yun, Liu Biao's nephew, along with Cai Mao are supporters of Liu Cong being the successor. 
In the Romance, he and Cai repeatedly came up with plots against Liu Bei and Liu Qi. After the death of Liu Biao, he surrendered to Cao Cao. He assumed the Navy Commander with Cai Mao to lead the Jing Province navy against Eastern Wu. Zhou set up a plot to make Cao Cao believe that Cai and Zhang had been cooperating with their enemies, and executed them.

Zhang Xiu, a native of Pengcheng, Xu Province, is a son of Zhang Zhao. 
As one of the four friends of Sun Quan's heir Sun Deng, he taught Sun Deng the "Book of Han", and has won Sun Quan's trust. 
After Sun Deng's death, Sun Quan granted Zhang Xiu with the commander of royal guard, and later promoted to the General who Spreads Martial Might. Despite his merit in defense during the battle of Shaopi, he was banished to Jiao Province for Quan Cong and his father speaking ill of him. 
Sun Hong, the eunuch director that had a grudge with Zhang, also spoke ill of him and sentenced him to suicide.

Zhang Ren, a native of Shu Commandery, Yi Province, is a prominent general under Liu Zhang's command. He is known for his boldness and integrity. 
When Liu Bei attacked Shu, Liu Zhang sent Zhang Ren and Liu Gui to hold Fucheng, they were driven back to Luocheng. Liu then pushed to Luocheng, and took Zhang in the Batlte of Yanqiao. 
Knowing that Zhang is a gifted talent, Liu offered surrender in earnest numerous times. Zhang denied with the statement "I, as a man, shall not serve another lord." Having no other choice, Liu executed Zhang. 
In the Romance, he is portrayed as the general shot Pang Tong dead; and in the anecdotes, he sought the same mentor as Zhang Xiu, Zhang Ren and Zhao Yun.

Zhang Jue is a leader of the Way of Taiping. He called himself the "Great Mentor", "General of the Heaven". Zhang Bao and Zhang Liang are his brothers. 
It is said that he was trusted with the "Taiping Essentials" by Immortal Nanhua, and founded the Way of Taiping with a follower count of hundreds of thousand. 
He began a rebellion with the rallying cry of "with the Empire coming to its curtain call, the new order shall take its stage", which is the Yellow Turban Uprising we know. 
In the beginning, the rebels were joined by people from all over the imperial territories and overwhelmed some locations with sheer number. The lack of organization and training, however, took its toll: the Yellow Turbans soon lost its advantage and gradually eliminated by the imperial representatives.

Zhang Cheng, a native of Pengcheng, Xu Province, is a son of Zhang Zhao. 
He befriended Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, Yan Jun when young, and won Sun Quan's trust. 
After Sun Quan took Jing Province from Guan Yu, Zhang Cheng assumed the commander of Changsha. Later, Sun Quan proclaimed his title and became enemies with Cao Pi. He granted Zhang with the General of Vehement Might and the commander of Ruxu theater, and ordered him to be the chief commander of the first defensive line to hold the attacks from Wei at Hefei. 
Zhang Cheng is good at looking into the nature of people and make good judgment. He is also the father-in-law of Sun He, the second ruler of Eastern Wu.

Zhang Song served Liu Zhang the Governer of Yi Province. 
With Cao force deployed in a way to threaten Zhang Lu of Hanzhong, Liu Zhang worried that Chengdu would be easy target. Zhang suggested him to invite Liu Bei to Shu and take Hanzhong before Cao does. Liu Zhang agreed with the plan and sent Fa Zheng as the guide. 
Liu Bei tried to win Zhang Song and Fa Zheng over. Zhang believed that Liu Bei is a wise leader, and shared all details with him, and advised Liu Bei to take Liu Zhang's place. 
Noticing Zhang Song's intent, his brother Zhang Su informed Liu Zhang. Zhang was then sentenced to execution. 
In the Romance, Zhang Song is said to trick Cao Cao and Yang Xiu.

Zhang Hu, a native of Yanmen Commandery, Bing Province, is Zhang Liao's son. 
He assumed his father Zhang Liao's old title after his death. 
In the sixth year of Huangchu, Cao Pi the Emperor Wen of Wei sought to start another expedition against Eastern Wu. He was assigned as the assistant general and relocated to Guangling to prepare for the war. It was a harsh winter, the waterway leading to Guangling was fully frozen, preventing the large warships of Cao Wei from entering Yangtze River. Zhang Hu fell ill and passed away there.

Yuan Shao also had a person with the same name under his account, but he was a different person. 
He and Feng Xi entered Shu from Liu Bei and eventually participated in the Battle of Yiling, where they fought hard but were eventually killed by the Wu army.

Zhang Zhao is the leader of officials of Eastern Wu. 
He joined Sun Ce on Sun's personal request. Sun trusted literally all affairs to him. Before death, he trusted Sun Quan to Zhang and stated that "you shall claim the throne if Zhongmou doesn't fit". 
As a man of pride, Zhang is abrasive and usually directly point out the problems, which made him rather unwelcomed. 
When it comes to possible invaders, Zhang is the dove that seeks to avoid direct confrontations. 
Zhang is an abrasive man that raised the discontent of Sun Quan and other officers and officials. As he's of dove faction and lacks decisive contribution, he was not promoted to the position of prime minister for the rest of his live.

Zhang Ying, a prominent general under the command of Liu Yao, the Administrator of Yang Province. He excels at navy battle. He held Yuan Shu's attacks for years. It was not until Sun Ce was sent for the offensive was Zhang defeated. 
In the Romance, this part is largely the same, but it is said that Liu Yao held Zhang accountable for the loss and almost executed him. After Liu Yao joined Liu Biao, Zhang and others fought Sun Ce again and lost. Zhang was slain by Chen Wu, Sun Ce's lieutenant.

Zhang Bao is Zhang Fei's eldest son. He died at an early age and there is very few recording about him in the official history record. 
In the Romance, he's portrayed as a fierce general just like his father that became brothers in arms with Guan Yu's son, and served as one of the important generals in the middle to late years of Shu Han. He followed Zhuge Liang for expeditions, and fell off cliffs to death while giving chase to an enemy general.

When under Yuan Shao's command, Zhang He was accused for the loss at Guandu by Guo Tu. He then joined Cao. 
After joining Cao, he attended in defending Ma's rebellion and the expedition against Zhang Lu with merit. 
In Zhuge Liang's first expedition, Zhang won a decisive victory at Jieting, and forced a full retreat. In Zhuge's fourth expedition, Zhang took a stray arrow and died afterwards. 
Zhang is said to be "capable of taking all variables into consideration and adapting accordingly, even Zhuge had to respect his versatility". 
There are also records of Zhang He being capable of seeing through enemy strategies, performing advanced military maneuver, and even calculating the supply needs of Zhuge's force to presume that Zhuge will retreat for running out of foodstuff.

Zhang Fei is a marshal of Shu. 
Best known for his ferocity, he along with Guan Yu are believed to "hold the enemies trying to overwhelm with sheer number". The most notable events about him include halting the Cao force at Changban. 
Before the Battle of Yiling, he was assassinated by lieutenants Zhang Da and Fan Jiang for harsh punishment, his head was chopped down and sent to Eastern Wu. 
There is a rumor of Zhang Fei skilled at calligraphy and painting arts, and possess a strategic mind. These are, however, from the sources dated in the Ming dynasty. As the Ming dynasty is more than a millennium away from the era of the Three Kingdoms, and the people of that time fond of flavor texts that are anything but historical truth, making it lack of creditibility.

Zhang Hong is a literature artist and a prominent official of Wu. Even Chen Lin, one of the Seven Scholars of Jian'an, stated that Zhang's talent is better than his. 
In the Romance, Zhang Hong is mentioned in a few words, and made like a faction member of Zhang Zhao; however, in official history record, Zhang Hong played a major role in the policy making of Eastern Wu. 
Sun Ce asked strategies from Zhang Hong at Jiangdu, and Zhang's reply later bacame the Jiangdu Plan of Eastern Wu. 
Cao Cao intended to take Jiangdong when Sun Ce was murdered, Zhang Hong managed to convince Cao not to do so. Even after Sun Quan's inauguration, Sun still called Zhang in his title of East Commandant instead of his courtesy name. 
Zhang Hong has served Eastern Wu for the rest of his life.

Zhang Wen, a native of Wu Commandery, is the representative of House Zhang, one of the four most prominent houses of Jiangdong. 
On the recommendation of Gu Yong, he joined Sun Quan's cause. 
When Liu Shan succeeded the throne, Sun Quan sent Zhang Wen as the envoy to Shu Han to rebuild the prior alliance. 
During his time as the envoy, he held Shu Han with higher respect in the written and verbal messages used as a means to show their faith. This pleased the Shu representatives, and they gifted Shu textiles in return. 
His effort to persuade Shu Han authority, however, upset Sun Quan. As he involved in the Incident of Jiyan, Sun Quan was revoked of his title, sent back to his homeland and never be granted with a position again.

Officer of Shu. Zhang Fei's subordinate. After the death of Guan Yu, Zhang Fei plans a campaign against Wu. He orders this man to prepare funeral clothes within 3 days. The next day, he and Fan Qiang beg for more time. A furious Zhang Fei has him whipped and threatens him with execution if he is late. To protect himself he stabs a drunken Zhang Fei and takes his head as a gift to Wu. When Liu Bei invades Wu, he is given to Liu Bei, who has him executed.

Zhang Wei, a native of Feng County, Pei State, is Zhang Lu's younger brother. 
In the twentieth year of Jian'an, Cao Cao led the expedition against Zhang Lu. Zhang Lu intended to surrender, while Zhang Wei insisted on putting up the resistance. Zhang Wei and Yang Ang led the defense at Yangping Pass, and built defensive structures along the tens of miles of ridges. 
Being unable to break the defense, and running out of supplies, Cao Cao intended to retreat, but Liu Yie and Guo Shen advised him to continue the attack. It turned out that Zhang's force was at the brink of collapse and soon surrendered.

Zhang Lu is the leader of the Way of the Five Pecks of Rice. 
He once served as Liu Yan's lieutenant, and led the believers to attack the local authority of Hanzhong. He then murdered Zhang Xiu and took the trophy for his own. 
Liu Zhang succeeded Liu Yan's position after his death. Zhang Lu was not at all pleased. Liu Zhang executed his family, Zhang then started a rebellion. 
When Cao Cao started an expedition against him, Zhang Lu's closest officials suggested him to destroy everything in the treasury and leave Cao nothing. Zhang Lu refused and stated that "the treasures belong the empire". 
Impressed of his integrity, Cao Cao sent men to convince Zhang to surrender with the condition of granting titles and benefits that also apply to his children.

Officer of Yuan Shu. After Yu Shu calls himself Emperor, he is given command of an army of 200, 000 and attacks Lu Bu in Xu. However, due to a plot by Chen Gui, one of Lu Bu's strategists, two of his officers, Han Xian and Yang Feng, switch sides and he is soundly defeated. After the death of Yuan Shu, he moves to join Sun Ce, but is waylaid by Liu Xun. He escapes and joins Cao Cao.

Zhang Heng is one of the Guanzhong warlords. 
After Cao Cao escorted the Emperor to his cause, Zhang found credit in the expedition against Li Jue with Duan Wei and Liang Xing. He was under the command of Zhong Yao, and yet he remained as a formidable warlord. 
When Cao Cao started an expedition against Zhang Lu, the Guanzhong warlords believed that he would also wipe them out of the picture. They followed Ma Chao and Han Sui in standing up against Cao Cao. 
He is no longer seen after the defeat in the Battle of Tong Gate. 
In the Romance, Zhang Heng and Cheng Yin fell into pit and died in the Battle of Wei River.

Zhang Liao is a prominent general of Cao Wei. He's known as the top of the Five Elite Generals. 
He first served Lu Bu, and was taken into custody when Lu was defeated. He chose to join Cao but was not trusted with important tasks. He then fought numerous major battles, and won his position. 
Cao is impressed of his abilities and virtues, "Zhang is a man of martial prowess, strategic mind, and undeniable fidelity". 
Of the battles fought, the most notable is the Battle of Xiaoyao Ford, in which they took on tens of thousand with just hundreds, and nearly caught Sun Quan. 
Zhang Liao maintained good personal relationship with Guan Yu, and anecdotes about them lived on until this day.

Zhang Ji, a native of Wuwei, Liang Province, served Niu Fu, the son-in-law of Dong Zhuo. 
He went on the expedition against Zhu Jun with Li Jue and Guo Si, and yet he received the report of Dong Zhuo and Niu Fu already dead. 
They intended to disband at the spot, then as suggested by Jia Xu they drove Lu Bu out of Chang'an and took the control of the castle. Though granted with the General who Stabilizes the East, Zhang Ji feared of the conflicts between Li and Guo, and helped the high officials of Han for an eastward trip. 
When attacking Nanyang, Jing Province, Zhang Ji was shot dead by a stray arrow. His nephew Zhang Xiu took the lead of his men and stationed in Wancheng.

Zhang Yi, a native of Jianwei, Yi Province, first served as a local official, and later promoted to peace-making commander to stabilize the relationship with southern barbarians. 
In the later phase of northern expedition, Zhuge Liang promoted Zhang Yi so he could fight on the frontline. As Zhang led his men with discipline, he was soon promoted to a position equal to Jiang Wei. They then served to watch over each other. In the Battle of Conquest by Wei, he stood to fight at the side of Jiang Wei. He also participated in Jiang's plan of feigning surrender and restoring Han. He and Jiang found their demise in Chengdu by the hands of Wei force.

Zhang Yi, a native of Ba Commandery, Yi Province, is a general of Shu. 
While Zhuge Liang is leading the northern expedition, Zhang Mu, the leader of the bandits in Hanzhong, Guanghan and Mianzhu sowed discord. With a plan, Zhang Yi neutralized the threat within ten days. 
By eliminating southern barbarian rebellions numerous times, he was granted with the magistrate of Yuegui. With the carrots-and-sticks policies, he developed the region and built road that directly leads Chengdu. When Zhang left Nanzhong, the people wished he would stay. It is said that a hundred local residents followed him in the trip of tribute. 
Despite being ill when Jiang Wei started a northern expedition, Zhang requested to follow and fight. He died in the skirmish against Xu Zhi, a general of Wei.

Zhang Xiu is a nephew of Zhang Ji. He later served Cao Cao. 
With Zhang Ji killed in action, Zhang Xiu took his men and Wancheng for his own. When Cao attacked Wan, Zhang Xiu feigned surrender to Cao as suggested by Jia Xu. Cao's interest in Zhang Ji's surviving wife irritated Zhang Xiu, leading to his rebellion. Cao lost his eldest son Cao Ang and Dian Wei in this battle. 
After the rebellion, Zhang Xiu worked with Liu Biao in fighting Cao. 
Before the Battle of Guandu, he surrendered to Cao again as suggested by Jia Xu. 
After Cao's death, Cao Pi scolded Zhang for his brother's death. Distressed, Zhang eventually ended his own life. Later, Zhang's son was also punished for involving in Wei Feng's rebellion. 
In folklore, Zhang Xiu is called the "lance master of the north".

As a chivalrous man at younger age, Zhang Miao was known as one of the "Eight Charitable Men". He became friends with Cao Cao and Yuan Shao. 
When Dong came to power, Zhang was sent to Chenliu to assume the magistrate. He participated in the coalition against Dong, and joined Cao after the defeat at Bian River. 
As he had a grudge with Yuan Shao, and maintained relatively good relationship with Lu Bu, Yuan told Cao to execute Zhang. Cao didn't comply. 
Convinced by Chen Gong, Zhang led Lu Bu into Yan Province when Cao Cao led an expedition against Tao Qian. With Lu Bu defeated by Cao Cao, he followed Lu to seek shelter in Liu Bei's circle of influence. Later, Lu sent him to ask for men from Yuan Shu, and he was murdered by subordinates on the way.

Officer of Yuan Shang, and later under Cao Cao. In the succession struggle after Yuan Shao's death, Zhang Yi attacked Yuan Tan with Ma Yan. He later rode to aid Shen Pei's castle when it was attacked by Cao Cao, but was defeated and captured. He then surrendered and joined his captor. He later surrounded Zhao Yun alone in the battle of Changban, but lost to him. He reunited with a retreating Cao Cao during the Battle of Chibi, but was slain by Gan Ning.

Cao Ren, a native of Qiao, Pei State, is Cao Cao's cousin. 
He answered Cao Cao's call to arms, and participated in countless battles. 
Cao Ren is trusted with important tasks such as defending key strategic points, or holding the line until the reinforcement arrives. The most notable is his unshakeable defense at Fancheng that held Guan Yu's northern expedition force at bay until Xu Huang came with reinforcements. 
Cao Ren is considered as a skilled defender but lacks luster in the art of aggression, and so he's also known as the "General of Iron Wall". However, possessing the mental fortitude to hold the line against all odds is no easy feat.

Cao Pi, a native of Qiao County, Pei State, is the second son of Cao Cao. He abdicated the throne and became Wei Emperor of Wen. 
Cao Pi is a versatile leader excelling in all aspects, much like his father. However, Cao Pi is more of a calculative person without much empathy. 
In order to win Cao Cao's trust, he put up a great performance in accepting constructive suggestions. Believing that the state would be in good hands, Cao Cao elected him as the heir. 
It was not until Cao Cao passed away did Cao Pi show his true face. 
Also a gifted scholar of literature, Cao Pi is known as one of the "Three Scholars of Cao", the leader of Jian'an scholars.

Cao Xiu, a native of Qiao, Pei State, is Cao Cao's kin of the younger generation. 
He lived in Wu Commandery until answering Cao's call to arms. Believing that Cao Xiu is a man of potential, Cao Cao treated him like his own son, allowing him to study together with Cao Pi. Later, he even trusted the commander of Tiger Leopard Cavalry to him. 
When Cao Pi succeeded the throne, Cao Xiu assumed the crucial position of leading the renowned generals such as Zhang Liao, and made major contributions in the expeditions against Wu. 
When it came to the rulership of Wei Emperor Ming, Cao Xiu was caught in Sun Quan's plot, suffered a terrible defeat and was grievously wounded. He died soon afterwards.

Cao Ang, a native of Qiao County, is Cao Cao's eldest son. He joined Cao Cao's ranks when young. 
In the second year of Jian'an, Cao Cao started an expedition against Zhang Xiu. Zhang offered a feigned surrender then started a rebellion, trapping Cao Cao in Wancheng. He and his steed Jueying was shot. 
Cao Ang offered his steed for his father, and left behind with Dian Wei to buy time for escape. 
It was not until Cao Cao regrouped his men in Wuyin did he learn of the death of Dian Wei and Cao Ang.

Cao Fang is the third ruler of Cao Wei. 
Cao Fang is not the biological son of Wei Emperor Ming Cao Rui, and yet his true origin is not specified in any history record. According to the "Chronicles of the Clans of Wei", he is the son of Cao Kai the Rencheng King. 
He succeeded the throne at the age of eight, with Cao Shuang the Great General and Sima Yi the Imperial Mentor as regents. The Simas abdicated his throne when he was eighteen: After the death of Sima Yi, Sima Shi started a coup d'etat and forced Cao to become a puppet. 
When Cao Fang was twenty three, Sima Shi forced Empress Dowager to give the order of abdication, making Cao Fang the King of Qi. He was demoted to the Duke of Shaoling at the foundation of Jin dynasty, and died at the age of forty four.

Cao Hong is a prominent general of Cao Wei and one of Cao Cao's cousins. He joined Cao early. 
When Cao Cao lost his horse on the way in Xingyang, Cao Hong offered his steed and held the enemies so he could escape. 
Cao Hong went on expeditions with Cao Cao, and notably, he made Zhang He surrender, defeated Zhang Fei at Hanzhong. 
Though being a man of fidelity and merit, he's known to be greedy, stingy and arbitrary. After Cao Pi's inauguration, these disgraceful events were used the reason to punish him. 
By taking the state of affairs at that time, Cao Pi fell ill at the time, he might have taken such drastic measure to discourage anyone seeking to succeed the throne entitled to Cao Rui.

He was the son of Cao Cao and a famous general of Cao Wei. Attacked Nan with Xiahou Shang after Cao Pi's defeat of Wu. When Xiahou Mao was defeated by Zhuge Liang of Shu's northward campaign, he stepped up to fend off the attack. Unable to match Zhuge Liang's talents, a letter of provocation drove him to die of rage.

Cao Chun, a native of Qiao, Pei State, is Cao Ren's younger brother. 
He's a man with relentless passion for knowledge, showing a liking of scholars, and valuing both combat prowess and discipline. He assumed the commander of Tiger Leopard Cavalry when it was founded. 
Cao Chun made major contributions while leading this force: he slew Yuan Tan, Yuan Shao's eldest son, and captured tribe leader Tadun in the Battle of Mt. Bailang. 
In the southern expedition of Jing Province, he gave chase to Liu Bei and managed to take Liu Bei's daughter into custody. He died of illness soon after the Battle of Red Cliffs.

Cao Bao is a lieutenant under Tao Qian's command. 
When Cao Cao attacked Xu Province to avenge his father's death, he garrisoned at the east of Tancheng with Liu Bei. 
After Tao Qian's death, Liu Bei assumed the Governer of Xu Province and led the man to hold invading force of Yuan Shu, Zhang Fei garrisoned at Xiapi. 
Cao Bao had a grudge with Zhang Fei, and led Lu Bu the way to attack Xiapi. Enraged, Zhang executed Cao, but with the castle in chaos, Lu Bu successfully took Xiapi.

Cao Shuang, a native of Qiao, Pei State, is Cao Zhen's son. 
Before death, Wei Emperor Ming trusted the position of regent to Cao Shuang and Sima Yi. 
In the beginning, Cao Shuang didn't show his ambition and consulted Sima Yi for every important matter. However, he soon tried to grab power. Cao granted Sima Yi with the Imperial Mentor to reduce Sima's influence over the military force, then assigned his men to crucial positions. 
Sima Yi had no choice but put up the Incident at the Gaoping Tombs when Cao Fang and Cao Shuang visited the tombs to pay respect to Wei Emperor Ming. The authority of Cao Wei as a state then fell to House Sima.

Cao Zhi is Cao Cao's fourth son. 
Cao Zhi never assumed crucial positions for the rest of his life, as Cao Cao knew that the rivalry for the throne would be a threat for the longevity of the state. Cao Cao found an excuse to execute his close friend Yang Xiu. Stricken, Cao Zhi led a life of decadence and gave up the competition. 
After Cao Cao's death, Cao Pi made numerous attempts to kill Cao Zhi, but was told off. 
When succeeding the throne, Cao Rui intended to grant Cao Zhi a position. The officials believed that he would not be content, and therefore he was not trusted with any crucial task. He sunk into distress and eventually died at the age of forty one. 
He noticed that Sima Yi is of malicious intent and offered advices, but were ignored by the ruler.

Cao Zhang is Cao Cao's third son. 
He meant to become a military general since young, and joined numerous expeditions led by Cao Cao. When the Wuwan rebellion broke out, Cao Zhang went to eliminate them as the General of Valiant Cavalry, then conquered Xianbe led by Ke Bineng, such merit surprised Cao Cao. 
When Cao Pi succeeded the throne, Cao Zhang believed that he deserves an important position. Cao Pi, however, treated him as regular. Cao Zhang was not at all pleased. Out of discontent, he went demanding on his subordinates. 
He was granted with Rencheng King, and soon died of sudden illness. 
In "A New Account of the Tales of the World", Cao Zhang is said to be poisoned by Cao Pi, though the creditability of such material in novels is dubious at best.

Cao Cao is the founder of Wei State. 
Some sources portray this man of reputation and controversies as opportunistic. 
According to Xu Shao, Cao Cao is "a fine minister with all-round talents who sought to dominate when the empire is in disarray". 
He became well known for his contribution in eliminating the Yellow Turbans. Later he escorted Emperor Xian to Xuchang "to settle the affairs with those who are disobedient". He took Lu Bu, Yuan Shu and Yuan Shao off the map and made the northern lands his dominion. 
The bitter defeat in the Battle of Red Cliffs, however, cost him the chance for taking it all. 
In novels, he is portrayed as a betrayer of Han dynasty. 
Cao Cao also excels at military art. He dug into "the Art of War" and even made annotations.

Cao Rui is the second ruler of Cao Wei, also known as Emperor Ming. 
As Cao Pi's eldest son, he is known to master literature. His mother was sentenced to suicide, and Cao Rui was also blamed and demoted to Pingyuan Lord. As Cao Pi intended to elect Cao Li the Jingzhao King, the son of Lady Xu, as the heir. 
It was not until Cao Pi invited him to a hunt, where Cao Pi shot the mother deer and asked him to shoot the calf, but Cao Rui wept and refused, that Cao Rui was elected. 
After succeeding the throne, he sought to expand southward with the aid of talents. Later he led a lifestyle of decadence. 
Before his early death, Cao Rui trusted his heir to Cao Shuang and Sima Yi. Cao Shuang soon made the new ruler a puppet, Sima Yi answered with a coup, and House Sima rose to power.

Liang Xing, a Guangzhong warlord, is one of the Ten Generals of Guanzhong (the other nine are Ma Chao, Han Sui, Hou Xuan, Cheng Yin, Yang Qiu, Li Kan, Zhang Heng, Cheng Yi, Ma Wan). 
He executed Li Jue and presented Li's head to Cao Cao. 
He later joined the rebellion started by Ma Chao and Han Sui, and fought the Battle of Tong Gate. After the defeat of the Guanzhong generals, Xiahou Yuan slew Liang.

A fictional character in "Romance of the Three Kingdoms", he was a general of Cao Ren's men. 
He captured Mi Zhu at the battle of Chang Ban Po, but was killed by Zhao Yun immediately.

Chunyu Qiong is a native of Yingchuan. 
As one of the Eight Lieutenants of Xiyuan, he was a friend of Cao Cao and Yuan Shao. 
When the warlords came to the consensus of standing up against Dong Zhuo, he joined Yuan Shao and was trusted with important position. In the Battle of Guandu, he was given the task of defending Wuchao, where Yuan Shao kept his foodstuff. Cao Cao launched a raid and he was captured by Yue Jin. 
Cao Cao didn't mean to execute his old friend, but Xu You advised him to for "this prisoner of war may resent for losing his nose in the battle".

Ze Rong, a native of Danyang. 
As a leader of Buddists of his time, this man of deceit and cruelty tried to take advantage of religious belief to rise to power. 
He first served Tao Qian but used the wealth and supplies in the treasury to build temples. Ze fled as soon as Cao Cao attacked Tao Qian. 
He then sought to join Zhao Yu, Xue Li and Liu Yao, but soon turned his back on each of them, resulting in the death of Zhao Yu, Xue Li and Zhu Hao, a subordinate of Liu Yao. 
Liu Yao put an end to Ze's ambition, and left him at the mercy of civilians.

A native in Pingyu of Ru'nan County, a famous critic of the late Eastern Han Dynasty. When he was young, he held a "Monthly Calligraphy and Painting Selection" in Ru'nan with his cousin Xu Jing to review the artistic works from all over the world. Those who were commented by the two were all famous for a while. Recommended by Qiao Xuan for a visit, Cao Cao got the comments of "A talented courtier in the era of peace but a treacherous traitor in turbulent times". It is worth mentioning that Xu Shao "despised him" and was unwilling to give comments on him, but Cao Cao laughed and left. Later, Xu Shao ran away from calamity to the south region of the Yangtze River and died of illness in Yuzhang County due to the wars in the Central Plains for years.

Xu You first served as a strategist of Yuan, and later joined Cao Cao. 
Right before the Battle of Guandu, he was accused of receiving bribe by Shen Pei. Xu then decided to join Cao, and advised to scorch the foodstuff stored in Wuchao. This resulted in the decisive defeat of Yuan force. 
After Yuan Shao's defeat, Cao Cao attacked Ji Province but caught in a stalemate for the castle was well defended. Xu You advised to flood the castle with Zhang River, which worked out as intended. 
Believing that the success is his merit, he showed arrogance and even said "Cao Cao would not have made this far if it were not me" when they entered the gate of Yecheng. Cao's close guard told Cao of Xu's bad manners, giving Cao a proper reason to execute him.

A native in Pingyu of Ru'nan County, Xu Shao's cousin. When he was young, he and Xu Shao were both famous for the"Monthly Calligraphy and Painting Selection" in Ru'nan, but the two did not get along. Later, due to Dong Zhuo's rebellion, he went to multiple vassals and warlords for shelter, and was finally accepted by Liu Zhang. When Liu Bei attacked Yizhou, Xu Jing abandoned the city and fled, but was captured by Liu Bei. Liu Bei despises his unrighteous and timid, but Fazheng took Xu Jing's reputation as an excuse to persuade Liu Bei to appoint Xu Jing as a high-ranking official with no real power in order to buy popularity and recruit the talented people.

Xu Zhu is a fierce general under Cao Cao's command. He's known as the "Tiger Fool". 
When Xu joined, Cao stated that "Xu would be the Fan Kuai under my command!". 
After the death of Dian Wei, Xu took his position as Cao's personal guard. He successfully saved Cao from assassinations. 
In the second expedition against Zhang Xiu, Cao sent Xu as the spearhead. Xu won a decisive victory. 
In the Battle of Tong Gate, he managed to buy enough time for Cao to escape. In Cao's negotiation with Ma Chao and Han Sui, Xu's fierce stare convinced Ma Chao that the attempt to capture Cao is unwise. 
Xu Zhu remained loyal to and maintained a deep connection with Cao. 
Cao Pi also put his trust in Xu Zhu, and made him the commander of the central royal guard.

A native of Nanyang County, an adviser of Yuan Shao. Used to be the counselor of He Jin, and later served Yuan Shao. Once proposed to exploit Gongsun Zan to attack Han Fu and persuade Han Fu to relinquish Jizhou, which made Yuan Shao to have succeeded in occupying it. When Yuan Shao was defeated in the Battle of Guandu, he regretted not accepting Tian Feng's plan. Pang Ji was afraid of being blamed and lied that Tian Feng knew that Yuan Shao was defeated and mocked Yuan Shao, which led to Tian Feng's death. After Yuan Shao's death, Pang Ji and Yuan Tan feuded. Fearing that Yuan Tan would seek his life after taking the throne, he tampered with the posthumous edict of Yuan Shao into ordering Yuan Shang to take the throne. Afterwards, Yuan Tan asked Yuan Shang for reinforcements but was rejected, so he killed Pang Ji in a fit of anger.

Guo Si, a native of Zhangye, Liang Province, made a living as one of the riding bandits before serving as the lieutenant of Niu Fu, Dong Zhuo's son-in-law. 
After Dong Zhuo's death, he and Li Jue took Chang'an and forced Emperor Xian to grant a position to exercise his influence. Later, he and Li turned against each other. Li Jue took the Emperor and His consort, whereas Guo took the officers for their power play. This came to an end with a reconciliation facilitated by Zhang Ji. Emperor Xian took the chance to return to Luoyang, then escorted to Xudu by Cao Cao. 
Guo was eventually murdered by his lieutenant Wi Xi, and his men joined Li Jue.

Guo You Zhi, a native of Nanyang, is a Palace Attendant of Shu state. 
Rarely mentioned in the official history record, he is known for being mentioned in Zhuge Liang's "Chu Shi Biao" before his northern expedition. 
Zhuge also stated that Guo as well as Fei Yi and Dong Yun are said to be loyal talents trusted by Liu Bei, and advised Liu Shan to consult them for national affairs.

Guo Yi, a native of Yangdi, Yingchuan, is Guo Jia's son. 
After Guo Jia's death, he was brought to Cao Cao's manor in Xudu. Though being as resourceful as his father, he died at an early age. As a good friend of Guo Yi, Wang Chang stated that he's"a narrow-minded man that forms bond with those close to him, and looks down on anyone he deems unworth of his attention", and warned his son to avoid such way of life.

Guo Huai is a prominent general of Cao Wei. 
He participated in Hanzhong expedition, then garrisoned there as Xiahou Yuan's Marching Officer of War. Liu Bei later launched a counter-offensive to seize Hanzhong back, Xiahou Yuan was killed in action. Guo Huai regrouped the remnants, followed the lead of Zhang He in holding Han River. 
Since then, Guo garrisoned at western lands to keep watch of the border, and did this job well. In Zhuge Liang's first expedition, Guo Huai launched a feign attack to distract Shu force, which is also a factor of Zhang He's decisive victory in Jieting. In Zhuge's fourth expedition, he successfully convinced the Qiang people to halt their hostility. In Zhuge's fifth expedition, he successfully held the attack of Shu force.

Guo Jia is one of Cao Cao's strategists. 
He joined Cao on the recommendation of Xun Yu. 
As a far-sighted talent, Guo Jia is good at looking into the nature of people, and is highly adaptable to variables. 
For instance, he pointed out the essential factors of Cao's victory at Guandu, advised Cao to take action when Liu Bei just seized Xu Province, stated that Liu "is an empathic leade, and he's not going to be content with an official position", and Sun Ce "is unaware of how important his own safety is. I reckon that he'll die in the hand of an ordinary murderer." After the death of Yuan Shao, he is the only one advised against immediate action, and it was not long before the Yuan brothers fought each other for the heir. 
Guo Jia died of illness in Wuhuan expedition.

Guo Tu is a strategist of Yuan Shao. 
Guo first served Han Fu. By successfully persuading Han to grant the Governor of Ji Province to Yuan Shao, he was then invited by Yuan. 
After joining Yuan, he advised against offering shelter for Emperor Xian. 
In the battle of Guandu, Cao attacked Wuchao. Guo Tu suggested to launch a major attack on Cao headquarters, while Zhang He advised to save the foodstuff storage since a solid defense can be expected at enemy headquarters. It turned out that Zhang was correct. 
After Yuan Shao's death, Guo Tu and Xin Ping incited the conflict between Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang, and even sought Cao's assistance to attack the latter. Later, Cao attacked Nanpi, defeating Yuan Tan and executing Guo Tu.

Chen Shi, a general of Shu Han. 
He participated in the battle of Hanzhong, but was defeated by Xu Huang at Mamingge. 
In the Battle of Yiling, he and Wu Ban led the navy and garrisoned at Yiling. As they were on the river and pulled back in time, they took minimal damage. 
In Zhuge Liang's third northern expedition, he managed to take Wudu and Yinping Commanderies, then he's never seen in history record again. 
It is rumored that Chen Shi is the father of Chen Shou, the author of the Recordings of the Three Kingdoms, which is not true. As a subordinate of Ma Ji, Chen Shou's father was also blamed for the bitter loss and excluded from promotion. Chen Shi, however, was one of the commanders in three northern expeditions.

Chen Wu, a native of Lujiang, Yang Province, is a general of Sun Wu. As one of the Twelve Tiger Ministers of Jiangdong, he is skilled at troop training. 
He joined Sun Ce's ranks and went on Jiangdong expedition at a young age. After defeating Liu Xun and subjugating Lu Jiang, Sun picked the elites and trusted them to Chen. Chen did the job to perfection and provided Sun with the most skilled and fearless fighters. 
When succeeding the throne, Sun Quan trusted him with five battalions and military training. 
Chen was killed in action while Sun Quan attacked Hefei. It pained Sun much for this loss and he visited Chen's funeral in person.

Chen Gong is a native of Dong Commandery, Yan Province. 
Chen first served Cao Cao then joined Lu Bu. When Cao Cao went on the expedition against Tao Qian, he and Zhang Miao planned to lead Lu Bu to take the Governor of Yan Province. With the commanderies and counties answering the call, Cao Cao almost lost his ground. 
He then continued serving Lu Bu and offered plans until Lu was captured. 
Cao Cao intended to persuade Chen to surrender. Chen rejected stubbornly and went to the execution ground by himself. Cao Cao saw him off, and treated his family well as promised. 
In the Romance and the renowned drama "Catch and Release Cao", Chen Gong is portrayed as a county magistrate that captured Cao Cao, who was wanted for assassinating Dong Zhuo, and released him out of favor.

Son of Wei's Chen Qun. Defeated Xiahou Ba with Guo Huai and fought many battles against Jiang Wei's northward push. Praised Deng Ai for saving Wang Jing in the Battle of Didao. Was the only Wei official to refuse Sima Zhao's invitation after the assassination of Emperor Cao Mao. When Xun Yi came for him, he lamented that he had fallen lower than his uncle, and said he had to make an example of Jia Chong.

Chen Lin, a native of Sheyng, Guangling, is one of the Seven Scholars of Jian'an. 
He first served as one of Yuan Shao's staff. In virtue of his literature talents, he worked on Yuan Shao's official documents, with "A Declaration of War for Yuan Shao to Cao Cao" being the most notable. It states the crimes of Cao Cao and his paternal ancestors. 
After Yuan Shao's death, Cao Cao managed to capture Chen Lin, and offered Chen to join. 
Chen's writing is said to be good enough to distract Cao Cao from his serious chronic headache.

Chen Deng, a native of Xiapi Commandery, Xu Province, is one of the nobles in the ending years of Eastern Han. 
When Lu Bu seized Xu Province, Chen showed obedience despite his distaste. After winning Lu's trust, he intervened in the political marriage of Lu with Yuan Shu, and expressed his intent to cooperate with Cao Cao on the envoy trip to Xudu. 
When Cao Cao attacked Lu Bu, Chen Deng was the first to turn against Lu and served as the spearhead. 
After Lu's death, Chen Deng assumed the Magistrate of Guangling, and held off Sun Ce's invasion numerous times. 
He's a lover of raw fish, and died from the complications of parasite infestation.

Chen Qun is an official of Cao Wei. 
Chen Qun served as the aide of Liu Bei when Liu assumed the Administrator of Yu Province. After Tao Qian died of illness, Liu intended to succeed the Governer of Xu Province. Chen warned Liu that Yuan would certainly put up a fight over this piece of land, and it could be even worse if Lu Bu took the chance to strike. It turned out that Chen's concern was correct. 
After Cao took Lu Bu out of the picture, he joined to serve Cao. With his talent of looking into the nature of people, he recommended various talents. 
At the foundation of Wei State. Cao Pi granted him promotion several times. He established the "Nine-rank System" while assuming the Deputy Minister of Control.

Chen Zhen, a native of Nanyang, Jing Province. He joined when Liu Bei assumed the Governor of Jing Province. 
He first assumed the local official, then Chief Secretary, and Shu-Wu envoy. 
When Sun Quan's inauguration, he visited Eastern Wu on order, managed to come into the pact of Wu and Shu sharing the old imperial territory. 
Chen is also good at looking into the nature of people, and advised Zhuge Liang not to trust all of Li Yan's words.

Chen Jiao, a native of Dongyang County, Linhuai Commandery, is an official of Cao Wei. 
Before answering Chen Deng's invitation, he rejected the offers from Sun Ce and Yuan Shu. 
In the first year of Jian'an, Sun Quan attacked Guangling. Chen Deng sent Chen Jiao to request reinforcement from Cao Cao. Cao Cao did not intend to send force but want to keep Chen Jiao. Chen replied that it is indecent to betray the current lord, and offered a weighing of the sending reinforcement. Cao Cao agreed to help. 
Chen Jiao joined Cao Cao afterwards and served three rulers of Wei State at important position. According to the people of the time, he's a man of fairness, selflessness and justice.

Chen Lan is a general under Yuan Shu's command. 
When Yuan Shu was struggling, he tried to seek help from Chen Lan but was rejected and eventually ended up with no resource and died of illness. 
Chen Lan and other generals managed to recruit tens of thousand of men for their cause. With the use of guerrilla and an alliance with Sun Quan, they remained a hassle. In the fourteenth year of Jian'an, Cao Cao sent Zhang Liao to deal with Chen Lan. Chen was defeated and executed by Zhang.

Lu Xun is a prominent general of Sun Wu. He's one of the four commanders of the state. 
Served as Lu Meng's delegate, Lu Xun wrote to Guan Yu with humble words. Guan took them not a threat, allowng them to take Jing Province. 
In the Battle of Yiling, Lu Xun lured Liu Bei's force into the Three Gorges, and held the line until Shu force grew tired and moved into the woods. A fire attack was then commenced for a decisive victory. 
In the Battle of Shiting, Lu defeated Cao Xiu and wore down Cao Wei force. 
In the later years, he involved in the conflict over heir election. Sun Quan punished Lu Xun for this matter. Distressed and furious, Lu fell ill and died.

Lu Ji, a native of Wu County, Wu Commandery, is an official of Eastern Wu and shares the same ancestry with Lu Xun. 
He is the of main character portrayed in "Take Orange for Parents" of the "Twenty-four Filial Exemplars". Though assuming an official position, he paid little mind to his achievements in the career, he was more fond of the pursuit of knowledge. 
He made annotations for the Classic of Changes. He's a master in astronomy, calendar, mathematics and divination. Before death, he made a prophecy that the era of warlord will end within sixty years. Jin dynasty later put an end to the time of divisions.

A literary man from Wei and one of the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove. He married Cao Cao's great-granddaughter, revered nature, and, following the Qingtan movement, avoided common society. He was sentenced to death with his friend when he sided with him in a quarrel over refusing to back Shan Tao's appointment as minister. A master Qin player, people declared the melody he played before his execution would die along with him, since he had taught it to no one.

Fu Shi Ren, a native of Guangyang, You Province, is an official first served Shu then Wu. 
His name is Shi Ren, "Fu" is likely to be added by mistake in the copying of history records. 
He was in a poor relationship with Guan Yu, and surrendered to the attacking enemy with Mi Fang when Guan Yu went on Xiang-Fan expedition, leading to Guan's loss and demise at Maicheng. 
It is also said that he held the castle for a while, before Lu Meng sent Yu Fan to convince him. 
In the Romance, he and Mi Fang found the invading Shu Han force is in formidable number, and so they meant to rejoin Shu. Liu Bei, however, executed them.

Fu Rong, a native of Yiyang Commandery, is a general of Shu Han. 
He went on the expedition against Wu with Liu Bei. When Shu force was defeated at Xiaoting and had to retreat, Fu Rong served to hold the route of retreat. Wu force offered a surrender, and Fu stated that "there's no surrendering general of Han" and fought to his last breath. 
His son Fu Qian carried on his father's legacy, served as a general of Shu Han, and helped Jiang Wei in the northern expedition against Wei. 
In the Romance, his name is incorrectly presented as Fu Tong.

A native of Lingzhou, a general of Cao Wei, son of Fu Xie. 
Fu Gan had for Ma Tang to explain the advantages and disadvantages, prompted Ma Tang and Cao Cao to work together. 
After vesting in Cao Cao, Fu Gan and Chen Qun, Zhong Yao and other people are long in prison, in favor of severe punishment and restoration of meat punishment. 
In addition, in the military and political situation is also quite far-sighted, has on Liu Bei into Shu and Cao Cao's conquest of Sun Quan and other matters to express their views, all hit.

A native in Suiyang of Liang, whose surname was Qiao in the official history. Qiao Xuan was smart and righteous. When he was young, he served as a local examiner of the county, later was recommended Xiaolian, and served as the left lieutenant of Luoyang. When he was the Duliao General, he settled the border riots of Hulu and Bogu and was granted the highest title as San Kung when he was summoned back to the capital. Qiao Xuan can tell greatness from mediocrity. When he met Cao Cao before well-known, he asserted that "The world will be in turmoil. You can't save it without great talent. I'm afraid you're the one who can stabilize the world, right?" He then introduced Cao Cao to Xu Shao, thus making Cao Cao famous. Qiao Xuan and Cao Cao became good friends. After Qiao Xuan's death, each time passing by Qiao Xuan tomb, Cao Cao would pay homage to this old man and even write the funeral oration for him.

Qiao Mao, a native of Suiyang, Liang State, is a child of Qiao Xuan and the Magistrate of Dong Commandery in the ending years of Eastern Han. 
In the Romance, his surname is presented as the "bridge without the radical of wood" Qiao (喬). In the official history record, however, his surname is the "bridge" Qiao (橋). 
He joined the coalition against Dong, and was slain by Liu Dai. He's the author of the Declaration of War Against Dong in the official history record, the Romance gives the credit to Cao Cao.

He first served Yuan Shao. 
After Yuan Shao's death, he became interested in claiming a title for his own. He attacked Yuan Shang and Yuan Xi, forcing them to escape to Wuhuan, then assumed the Administrator of You Province and joined Cao Cao. 
In the Romance, he is said to be slain by Han Dang right before the Battle of Red Cliffs.

Cheng Wu, a native of Dong Commandery, Yan Province, is the eldest son of Cheng Yu. He succeeded the Lord of Homeland Safety after Cheng Yu's death. 
However, he is rarely seen in official history record. 
In the Romance, Cheng Wu served as Xiahou Mao's staff during Zhuge Liang's first northern expedition and engaged Zhao Yun's force on Mt. Fengming. 
As suggested by Cheng Wu, Wei force put up an ambush to encircle Zhao Yun. However, with the arrival of Zhang Bao and Guan Xin, Wei force was defeated.

Cheng Bing, a native of Nandun, Runan, is a famed scholar in his homeland. He is said to be the apprentice of Zheng Xuan, the master of classics. 
He fled to Jiao Province to stay away from the wars and destructions, and won the trust of Shi Xie, the magistrate of Jiao Province. 
When Shi Xie surrendered to Sun Quan, Sun offered Cheng Bing to be the mentor of his heir Sun Deng. 
After inauguration, Sun Quan requested Cheng Bing to hold Sun Deng's wedding ceremony with Zhou Yu's daughter. Cheng held a classic and elegant ceremony, which Sun Quan and his son were satisfied.

Cheng Yu is an prominent official of Cao Wei. 
Upon entering Yan Province, Cao Cao offered Cheng Yu to join, Cheng obliged. 
When Cao went on Xu Province expedition, Chen Gong and Zhang Miao turned against Cao and led Lu Bu into Yan Province. With the commanderies and counties answering the call, Cheng and others managed to hold Juancheng. Cheng then visited Fan and Dong E Counties to persuade the prople, and successfully prevented from losing these locations. 
As Cheng managed to procure foodstuff when there was a famine caused by locusts, he's a major contributor of reclaiming Yan Province. 
While not being the most notable strategists like Xun You or Guo Jia, he's also the backbone of Cao's staff.

Cheng Pu is the top of the Twelve Tiger Ministers of Jiangdong. 
He served three rulers, and went on the expedition against Yellow Turbans and Dong Zhuo with Sun Jian. 
Sun Ce once got encircled by the Shan Yue rebels incited by Yuan Shu, Cheng came to his rescue. 
When Sun Quan succeeded the throne that raised dissent in numerous commanderies and counties. Cheng Pu went on a cruise inspection and restored order. 
He was one of the hawks right before the Battle of Red Cliffs. At first, he looked down on Zhou Yu as Zhou was much younger. Soon he was impressed of Zhou's temperament and talents, and assumed the commanders together to get a decisive victory. He even pushed towards Nan Commandery and defeated Cao Ren as well. He died of plague soon after.

Cheng Yuan Zhi is a fictitious Yellow Turban general in the Romance. He is said to attack Zhuo Commandery, Liu Bei's homeland, with fifty thousand men. 
With five hundred men, Liu Bei, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei engaged them at the foothills of Mt. Daxing. Cheng Yuan Zhi sent his lieutenant Deng Mao for the first duel, only to be slain by Zhang Fei with a thrust of his spear. 
When Cheng Yuan Zhi noticed something is wrong and tried to run, Guan Yu gave chase and slew him with a swing of his weapon. 
With the general slain, the Yellow Turban army disbanded at once. Liu Bei's force gave chase, slew a few Yellow Turbans, and called it a victory.

Cheng Yin is one of the Guanzhong generals in the ending years of Eastern Han, he sought to become one of the major warlords when Dong made a mess in the imperial palace. 
Cao Cao sent Zhong Yao to defend Guangzhong. Later, Ma Chao and Han Sui started a rebellion with the eight generals of Guanzhong, including Cheng Yin. In the Romance, Cheng Yin is portrayed as one of Ma Chao's lieutenants. 
Cheng Yin is then no longer seen in official history record. In the Romance, it's said that Ma Chao didn't find Cheng Yin when regrouping and counting his men after the bitter defeat at Weinan.

He was a famous doctor during the Three Kingdoms period. Together with Bian Que, Zhang Zhongjing and Li Shizhen, Hua Tuo was one of the four famous doctors in ancient China, he also is the creator of anesthesia powder. Hua Tuo did not want to serve for Cao Cao, and was executed by Cao Cao later. In the play, Hua Tuo is entrusted to scrape Guan Yu's bones and heal his wounds, which shows Guan Yu's courage and Hua Tuo's excellent medical skills.

His life is not stated in official history record. He's a general under Dong Zhuo's command, slew and beheaded by Sun Jian. His surname is Yeh. The name Hua Xiong is likely a typo made popular with drama. 
In the Romance, he volunteered to hold the coalition at Sishui Pass. He managed to slay Bao Xin's brother Bao Zhong, Sun Jian's subordinate Zu Mao, Yuan Shu's lieutenant Yu She, and Han Fu's marshal Pan Feng before Guan Yu volunteered a duel. Cao Cao got a cup of warmed booze, Guan told Cao to hold until he's back, and returned when the booze is still lukewarm.

Hua Xin is a talent of reputation at a young age. 
With the ability of looking into the nature of people, he knew that Wang Fen was incapable of abdicate Emperor Ling, and his family would also get involved. 
Hua Xin suggested Yuan Shu to chase Dong but turned down, then he made his leave. 
He won popular favor when assuming the magistrate of Yuzhang, Sun Ce showed interest in him and treated him as a respected guest. When Cao Cao sought to invite Hua, Sun Quan didn't feel like to agree, Hua convinced Sun by telling him that this is a way to maintain good relationship with Cao. 
Hua Xin is known to be a scholar of decent personal virtue, yet according to official history record, he's also to involve in numerous incidents of dispute.

DiaoChan does not exist in official record, but there's a record of Lu Bu having relationship with Dong Zhuo's handsmaiden, from whom DiaoChan is most likely to borrow concept. The author of the Romance took ideas from drama, songs and anecdotes, and portrayed DiaoChan as one of the four finest ladies in Chinese history. 
First served as the singeress in Wang Yun's manor, Wang took her as foster daughter to help put an end to Dong Zhuo's tyranny. 
When Cao Cao attacked Lu, Chen Gong advised Lu Bu to garrison at the vicinity of Xiapi to put up a good fight. DiaoChan and Lu's wife Ms. Yan held Lu back for"anyone can take the chance if you head out". Lu was then trapped in Xiapi Castle. 
After Lu Bu's death, DiaoChan was taken to Xudu and never seen in the novel again.

Fei Shi, a native of Jianwei, Yi Province, first served Liu Zhang. 
When Liu Bei attacked Mianzhu, he surrendered with Li Yan, and was granted with important position. 
He convinced Guan Yu and Huang Zhong to accept the title of Four Direction Generals, but demoted for advising against Liu Bei's inauguration. He was promoted back again at Zhuge Liang's southern expedition against Meng Huo. 
Fei Shi makes fast and accurate judgment, and uses his eloquence in speaking the truth. After Zhuge Liang's death, Jiang Wan still assigned him to important position. His offspring also assumed official position in Western Jin.

Fei Yi is a prominent official, one of the four prime ministers of Shu Han. 
After Liu Bei entered Shu, he joined Liu and was trusted with important tasks by Zhuge. As the envoy to Eastern Wu, he managed to convince Sun Quan and his officials. 
He assumed the prime minister after the death of Zhuge Liang and Jiang Wan. His aim is to avoid unnecessary military operation to save resources, which contradicts with Jiang Wei's expeditions. Historians of later generations believed that this policy cost Shu Han the best chance of getting the most from expeditions. 
As a benevolent man, Fei Yi didn't keep distance from surrendered enemies. Zhang Yi once advised Fei to take precaution though was ignored. Later in a feast, he was assassinated by Guo Xiu, a surrendered Wei general.

E Huan, a fictitious character of the Romance, is a lieutenant of Gao Ding that wields a two-bladed halberd with ease. 
In Zhuge Liang's expedition against the rebellion led by Zhu Bao and Yong Kai, E Huan was able to hold Wei Yan's attacks until Wei catch him with a plan. Zhuge Liang treated him with respect, and used him to incite a conflict between Gao and the other two. Gao sent E Huan to slay Zhu Bao and joined Shu Han. E Huan was granted with the General of the Headquarters for this merit.

Huang Yue Ying, a native of Baisui, Miannan, is the daughter of Huang Cheng Yan, and the spouse of Zhuge Liang. 
Her name or life is not seen in the history. The name Huang Yue Ying, Huang Shou and Huang Shuo are taken reference from unofficial history record or folklore drama and legends. 
It is said that despite not the finest in terms of look, she's a talented lady mastered the classics. As suggested by Huang Cheng Yan, Zhuge married her and had children including Zhuge Zhan. 
Legend has it that the invention of"wooden ox and flowing horse" as well as noodles came from her wisdom.

Huang Zhong is portrayed as one of the Five Tiger Generals of Shu State in the Romance. 
He first served Liu Biao, then joined Han Xuan the magistrate of Changsha after Liu Biao got killed in action. 
He joined Liu Bei with Han Xuan. In the Battle of Hanzhong, he and Fa Zheng won a decisive victory at Mt. Dingjun, slaying Xiahou Yuan. In the same year, he was promoted to the General who Conquers the West, then promoted to the General of the Rear when Liu Bei proclaimed himself the King of Hanzhong. Huang died from illness in the next year. 
In the Recordings of the Three Kingdoms, Huang is given a paragraph of only three hundred words and lacks annotation. Huang Zhong is probably the magistrate of Changsha himself. 
In the Romance, he is said to put a good fight against Guan Yu.

Huang Zhu is a general under Liu Biao's command, and assumed the magistrate of Jiangxia. 
Lost in a battle against Sun Jian, he sought to held the line on a mountain. Sun Jian took a reckless assault and met his own demise, and it was also when he became a mortal enemy of House Sun. 
Sun Ce and Sun Quan engaged Huang's force numerous times, with various results. Gan Ning, who served Huang at the time, is said to drive away Sun force by shooting their prominent general Ling Cao dead. 
In the thirteenth year of Jian'an, Sun's expedition force broke Huang's last defense. He then went on the run but was slain by Wu soldiers. 
As an impatient, irritable man, Huang Zhu executed Mi Heng when provoked, raising the eyebrows of scholars of the time.

Huang Gai, a native of Lingling, Jing Province, is the second most prominent officer of the Twelve Tiger Ministers of Jiangdong that served Sun Jian, Sun Ce and Sun Quan. 
In the Battle of Red Cliffs, he noticed that Cao Cao's warships are deployed unusually close to each other, and suggested Zhou Yu to use a fire attack. To successfully launch the fire attack, he feigned a surrender and approached with tens of ships that were ignited and ran straight into Cao's fleet with the help of the wind. It led to the destruction of Cao's fleet. 
When giving chase, he took a stray arrow and fell into the water. Han Dang spotted and rescued him to safety. After the battle, he assumed the magistrate of Wuling.

Huang Quan is a general of Shu that surrendered to Wei later. 
He first served Liu Zhang, and was against Liu Zhang's plan to invite Liu Bei to Shu. When Liu Bei attacked Yi Province, Huang held the castle until Liu Zhang surrendered. 
Before the Battle of Yiling, he advised against this battle. Liu insisted on his own judgment and garrisoned Huang Quan at the north as a precaution against Wei force. With the Battle of Yiling resulted in a terrible defeat, and Huang's route of retreat cut off by Wu force, he had no choice but surrender to Wei. 
Learning that Huang surrendered, the officials suggested Liu Bei to execute Huang's family. Liu refused. Liu still treated Huang's family with respect. Huang is said to shed tears when learning that Liu Bei passed away.

Yang Ren, a subordinate of Zhang Lu. Other than being slain when Cao force attacked Yangping Pass, he is not seen in the official history record. 
In the Romance, he's said to put up a fair fight with Xiahou Yuan, who then feigned defeat and slew Yang with a surprise slash.

Yang Feng was the leader of Hedong Baibo bandits, later served as Li Jue's lieutenant. 
When Li Jue and Guo Si fought each other in Chang'an, Zhang Ji brokered a peace between them, and successfully persuaded them to escort Emperor Xian back to Luoyang. Then appointed as General Xing Yi by Emperor Xian, Yang Feng escorted the emperor back east with Dong Cheng and the others. 
Proud of the successful escort mission, Yang Feng became arrogant. When Cao Cao took Emperor Xian under his protection, Yang Feng tried to stop him but was defeated and forced to retreat. 
Yang Feng then followed Yuan Shu and Lu Bu respectively before being killed by Liu Bei in the end.

Originally serving under Li Jue, he then joined Zhang Lu's forces. 
While Li Jue's and Guo Si's forces fought in Chang'an, Yang Ang was convinced by Zhong Yao to betray Li Jue and thus Emperor Xian was able to return east to Luoyang. 
Afterwards, Ma Chao invaded Long Shang area and Mount Long. Zhang Lu then sent General Yang Ang to help Ma Chao siege Jicheng. 
When Cao Cao's forces attacked Zhang Lu, Yang Ang was tasked to guard Yangping Pass. After Zhang Lu surrendered, there's no further record of Yang Ang. 
In Romance of the Three Kingdoms, he was killed by Zhang He in the Battle of Yangping Pass.

Staff officer of Zhang Lu officer. He urged Zhang Lu to accept Liu Zhang's offer of land to fight Liu Bei. After Liu Bei's messenger Sun Qian greased his palm, however, he said that Ma Chao, marching to Liu Zhang's aid, had actually betrayed him. This made the two warriors hate each other. He was also bribed by Cao Cao into sabotaging the defense of Hanzhong. Lastly, he deceived and handed Zhang Lu over to Cao Cao, who then slew him for his selfishness.

Named Yang Bai in official records serving under Zhang Lu, his name was changed in Romance of the Three Kingdoms. 
No much about him was documented in official records. Yang Bai never liked Ma Chao and once questioned that he's overrated. When Zhang Lu was planning to marry his daughter to Ma Chao, one of his aides said, "If a person can't even love his family and relatives, can he still love others?" It was rumored that Yang Bai was the one who said that. Another theory is that Yang Bai and Yang Ang were the same person.

He was a local warlord in Guanzhong. 
After losing the battle of Tongguan to Cao's army, he joined Cao Wei. 
After the reign of Cao Pi, there is still a record of the rebellion.

He was the nephew of Yuan Shu and the son of Yang Biao, a contemporary scholar. 
He was so talented that Cao Cao sighed at himself. He was a good friend of Cao Pi and Cao Zhi, and was especially close to Cao Zhi. 
Cao Cao wanted to help Cao Zhi to become a great man, Yang Xiu helped him repeatedly; and the letters and poems between Cao Zhi and Yang Xiu showed that Cao Zhi might have great ambitions, so Cao Cao was angry and afraid that Cao Pi and Cao Zhi would compete for the first son. 
In the Battle of Hanzhong, Cao and Liu confronted each other for a long time, Cao Cao inadvertently said "chicken ribs", and before the military order was given, Yang Xiu broke the intention of retreating from the army, and packed his preparations in advance, so his intention to kill Yang Xiu became stronger. 
Later on, Cao Zhi and Yang Xiu were executed by Cao Cao for drunkenly trespassing on the gate of Sima and slandering Cao Chang. 
Cao Zhi is also killed by the death of his best friend, so he becomes more indulgent and indulges in drinking.

Yang Yi was a Shu official trusted by Zhuge Liang. 
He first worked in Wei before joining Guan Yu. Though appreciated by Liu Bei, he didn't get along with Liu Ba and was demoted Hongnong Administrator.
