Yang Yi was valued by Zhuge Liang on Northern Expeditions but he had disagreements with Wei Yan. 
When Zhuge Liang died, Yang and Wei accused each other of treason. In the name of Zhuge Liang, Wang Ping dissuaded Wei Yan's soldiers and they deserted. Yang Yi then ordered Ma Dai to chase and kill Wei Yan. 
Ostracized, Yang Yi made a remark of revolt, "I should have brought along my men and defected to Wei!" 
Considering his past achievements, Liu Shan only demoted him commoner. But Yang Yi continued to act with contempt. In the end, he was arrested and committed suicide in jail.

A general loyal to Liu Zhang, since Liu Bei's takeover of Shu, he'd been on guard against him. 
Pang Tong once said Yang Huai and Gao Pei were both Liu Zhang's great generals who controlled great military forces and crucial passes. 
As Cao Cao was attacking Sun Quan, Liu Bei followed Pang Tong's strategy, feigned their return to Jing Province, lured out the two generals, and swiftly killed them while they're off guard. 
After that, Yi Province became defenseless and Liu Bei's forces soon came to Chengdu and Liu Zhang surrendered.

From Zhijiang, Nan Commandery, he's an Shu Han official who, alongside Jiang Wan and Fei Yi, served as the head of Shu Han government after Zhuge Liang died. 
In Chu Shi Biao, Zhuge Liang recommended Dong Yun to Liu Shan, the successor, in the hopes that he would listen to their advice. Liu Shan then promoted Dong Yun Palace Attendant. 
Dong Yun was loyal, offering honest advice and suppressing potential threats. Liu Shan favored Eunuch Huang Hao but he was unable to gain greater power because of Dong Yun.

Dong Zhuo was the culprit of the warlord rivalry in Eastern Han. 
Deposed for failing to quell the Yellow Turban Uprising, he was reinstated because of the barbarians in Northwest. 
When He Jin tried to eliminate the eunuchs, he summoned Dong Zhuo but was killed. Yuan Shu took control of the capital so Dong Zhuo advanced quickly. He encountered Emperor Shao and the future emperor Xian. 
After the successful escorting, Dong Zhuo replaced Emperor Shao with Emperor Xian. Regional officials formed a coalition against him and though he was defeated, the coalition was dismissed from internal conflicts. 
After the dismissal of the coalition, Dong Zhuo became ruthless and tyrannical. In the end, Wang Yun turned Dong Zhuo and Lu Bu against each other and Lu Bu assassinated Dong Zhuo.

From Zhijiang, Nan Commandery, he's the father of Dong Yun. 
He used to serve under Liu Zhang as a official who's humble and admired by the locals, and even the Southern Barbarians. 
After Liu Bei's takeover of Shu, Dong He was summoned as an equal to Zhuge Liang, whom he became great friends with. 
As a general, Dong He was attentive and would check the same document dozen of times. When he initiated discussions with Zhuge Liang, he was also always honest.

From Hejian Commandery, he's an official of the late Eastern Han whose daughter was a concubine of Emperor Xian. 
As he escorted Emperor Xian's escape from Chang'an, he was valued and appointed General of Guard. 
In January of Jian'an Year 5, through a secret imperial edict, Dong Cheng plotted with Liu Bei and the others to assassinate Cao Cao but was caught. All of them and their families, including Dong Cheng's pregnant daughter Lady Dong, were executed except Liu Bei, who was away organizing the army. 
When Liu Bei became the emperor afterwards, he openly stated he was working with Dong Cheng to eliminate Cao Cao.

From Longxi, Liang Province, he was Dong Zhuo's younger brother. 
When Dong Zhuo came to the capital, Dong Min killed He Miao, General of Chariots and Cavalry then, then took over the army. 
After Luoyang was burnt down and they escaped to Chang'an, Dong Zhuo promoted Dong Min to Left General, who was in charge of guarding the treasure Dong Zhuo looted and the Dong family in Meiwu. 
When Wang Yun and Lu Bu worked together to kill Dong Zhuo, Dong Min was killed in Meiwu by Huangfu Song.

Pang De's subordinates. 
Guan Yu besieged Cao Ren at Fancheng, Cao Cao Yu and Pang De rescued Cao Ren, and Dong Heng also went with his army. 
Guan Yu floods the seven armies and Dong Heng's generals try to escape to the dike, but they are stopped by a rain of arrows. Dong Heng and Dong Chao intended to surrender to Guan Yu, but Pang De was informed and killed Dong Chao and Dong Heng.

From Kuaiji, Yang Province, he was a general of Sun Wu and one of the twelve tiger ministers of Jiangdong. 
Dong Xi was recruited by Sun Ce in Kuaiji and helped him suppress the bandits in Shanyin, making great achievements in his first battle. 
He then followed Sun Ce to fight in Lujiang and Wancheng. After Sun Ce died, he greatly supported Sun Quan to succeed the position. 
During the Battle of Jiangxia, he led suicide warriors with Ling Tong to breach the river defense line set up by Huang Zu and defeated his forces. 
During the Battle of Ruxu, a storm capsized the ship and Dong Xi drowned after refusing to abandon the ship.

Yu Fan was a politician of Wu, an expert on classics, medicine, and fortune telling. 
First under Wang Lang, whom was defeated by Sun Ce, Yu Fan helped him escape before submitting to Sun Ce. 
When Sun Ce was assassinated, the situation in Jiangdong was tense. Worried about the tribes, Yu Fan stayed in Shouchun instead of attending the funeral and kept the peace. 
Though talented, Yu Fan was ruthless, offending his superiors repeatedly or insulted other officials. He eventually enraged Sun Quan and got exiled to Jiao. 
Even in exile, Yu Fan was still concerned about Wu. When Sun Quan asked Gongsun Yuan for horses, Yu Fan wanted to oppose the plan but had no means. In the end, Sun Quan failed and regretted exiling Yu Fan. He wanted to get Yu Fan back but he already passed away.

Jia Chong was an official in Wei and a founding official of Jin. He was greatly trusted by Sima Zhao and Sima Yan. He was the father of Jia Nanfeng. 
He assisted Sima Zhao in many ways including warning him about Zhuge Dan's possible revolt, assassinating the Wei emperor Cao Mao, foreseeing Zhong Hui's rebellion in Chengdu, advising Sima Zhao on choosing the right successor, among others. 
When the Wu emperor Sun Hao surrendered to Jin and came to Luoyang to meet Sima Yan, Jia Chong sarcastically asked Sun Hao what torture methods he used as an emperor, to which Sun Hao replied, "If a subordinate planned to murder his emperor or was treacherous, I would use those punishments on him." The sarcastic remark about Jia Chong killing Cao Mao left him remorseful in silence.

Ping Yang County, Xiangling County, Jia Chong's father, Minister of Wei. 
After Cao Cao's death, Cao Chang led his troops into the capital. When Wu's Zhou wanted to surrender the county to Cao Hu, Jia Kui told him that there must be a fraud, but Cao Hu did not listen to him and led his troops to station outside Wancheng. Later, Jia Kui brought his troops to his rescue and spread his banners so that the Wu army was afraid to attack and Cao Xiu was able to escape.

A fictional character in Romance of the Three Kingdoms who was a general of Eastern Wu. 
During the Battle of Hefei, he served as Sun Quan's guard. When Sun Quan was ambushed by Yue Jin, Jia Hua and Song Qian worked together to repel Yue Jin. 
When Liu Bei was in Nanxu to marry Sun Shang Xiang, Jia Hua was ordered to ambush him in Ganlu Temple but was found by Lady Wu, who even wanted to have him executed. In the end, Liu Bei and Lord Qiao advised against it and he was spared.

Jia Xu served under Dong Zhuo, Li Jue, Guo Si, Zhang Xiu, before joining Cao Cao. 
After Dong Zhuo died, Li Jue was able to seize control of Chang'an in the dire situation because of his advice. 
When Li Guo attacked Chang'an, Jia Xu escorted Emperor Xian on his escape. He befriended Zhang Xiu, served under him. 
When Zhang Xiu turned against Cao, Jia Xu instructed him to first counter Cao's attacks then form an alliance with Liu Biao, leading Zhang Xiu to turn the situation. 
Before Battle of Guandu, he advised Zhang Xiu to turn down Yuan Shao and rejoin Cao and thus kept him safe. 
Other incidents like defeating Ma Chao by sowing discord and advising Cao Cao to be cautious of the power struggle between his sons all proved that he was one of the best strategists of his time.

A powerful tribal chief in Nanzhong, Yi Province. 
Soon after Liu Bei died, Yong Kai, Gao Ding, and Zhu Bao started a rebellion in Nanzhong, during which Li Yan tried to dissuade him 6 times but in vain. 
Then under urging from Shi Xie and Bu Zhi, Yong Kai pledged allegiance to Wu again and focused on attack Shu Han. But as Lu Kai and Wang Kang stand their ground and Yong Kai's army wasn't able to advance, he then sent Meng Huo to urge the Nanman tribes to rebel instead. 
In the end, Zhuge Liang sent the army southbound and Yong Kai was killed in Zhuge Liang's attacks. Another theory is that he was killed by Gao Ding's subordinate.

An underling of Liu Bei. Shortly after controlling the Shu area, Liu Bei launched the attack against Hanzhong, confronting Cao's army. Before the engagement, Zhou Qun and Zhang Yu both persuaded Liu Bei to suspend the military actions and settle down the newly joined people of Shu first. But Liu Bei turned a deaf ear to them, and ordered Wu Lan and Lei Tong to march into Wudu, causing the officers to die in battle.

A general under Yuan Shu. 
When Yuan Shu was struggling, he tried to seek help from Chen Lan and Lei Bo but was rejected and eventually ended up with no resource and died of illness. 
His name never appeared in the history records again.

From Xiangyang, Jing Province, Liao Hua was a Shu Han military general. 
He's originally a registrar under Guan Yu. After Guan Yu was defeated and killed, he was forced to surrender to Sun Wu before faking his death and returning to Shu. On the way, he encountered Liu Bei on his way to attack Sun Wu and was recruited again. 
As senior generals of Shu Han gradually waned, Liao Hua was greatly valued. He joined Zhuge Liang and Jiang Wei on their northern expeditions and both won and lost battles against Wei. During the Conquest of Shu by Wei, he guarded Jiange with Jiang Wei before getting the order from Liu Shan to surrender. They surrendered to Zhong Hui at Fu County before Liao Hua died of illness the next year while they were moving to Luoyang.

Man Chong was a Wei general. 
As Prefect of Xu, he had no fear of Cao Cao's power and executed Cao Hong's retainers who broke the law, which was praised by Cao Cao as it was similar to what he did in his early years. 
When Cao fought Yuan, Man Chong was Administrator of Runan and conquered over 20 strongholds. 
When Guan Yu attacked Fancheng, Cao Ren's generals advised him to escape but Man Chong asked Cao Ren to resist. Xu Huang soon came with reinforcements, forcing Guan Yu to retreat. 
Man Chong stationed in the southeast for years and knew the area well. He built a new city in Hefei to resist Wu's invasion. Sun Quan invaded personally many times but failed because of this. 
Royal, Man Chong served under four Cao leaders. Sadly, in his later years, he lost power to calumny.

Zhen Fu was Zhen Yi's daughter and Yuan Xi's wife. After Cao Cao killed Yuan Shao, she married Cao Pi and gave birth to Cao Rui and Princess Dongxiang. 
Beautiful and studious, she had a good reputation and was liked by Cao Pi and Lady Bian. 
As Zhen Fu got older and Cao Pi became the emperor, he married Concubine Guo, Noble Lady Li and Yin and Zhen Fu became less favored. Cao Pi believed the calumny that Lady Zhen was complaining in secret so ordered to execute her. He regretted it immediately but it was too late. 
In literary works, it was often mentioned that Cao Zhi was in love with Zhen Fu. The goddess descirbed in Luo Shen Fu was meant to be Ms. Zhen. Another theory was that judging by the time Cao Pi got Ms. Zhen, Emperor Ming Cao Rui was probably the son of Yuan Xi.

One of the Yellow Turban generals. 
He led tens of thousands of Yellow Turban rebels to attack Beihai. Kong Rong, who was Beihai Chancellor then, was trapped in the city and the situation was dire. Then, Taishi Ci, took a letter by Kong Rong to Liu Bei for help. Liu Bei, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei came to the rescue and Guan Hai retreated, knowing he was no match to them. 
In Romance of the Three Kingdoms, a part in which he was killed under a horse by Guan Yu was added and his remnants were defeated by Liu Bei and Kong Rong's troops.

A fictional Yellow Turban general in Romance of the Three Kingdoms. 
After the Yellow Turban rebels failed, he occupied Mount Woniu with Zhou Cang. He tried to rob Red Hare from Guan Yu but was defeated by him so he swore allegiance to Guan Yu with Zhou Cang. 
Then, Pei Yuan Shao and Zhou Cang were ordered to gather forces in Mount Woniu but Pei Yuan Shao tried to rob Zhao Yun's horse. As he rushed in, he was killed by Zhao Yun while Zhou Cang and the rest were defeated into fleeing.

From Zhending, Changshan, Zhao Tong was the eldest son of Zhao Yun. 
He was an officer in Huben Division, in charge of the imperial guards. Liu Shan trusted and valued him no less than Zhao Yun. During the Yanxi era, he became Xing General, a position only slightly lower than the then Wei General, Zhuge Zhan. And Zhuge Zhan used to be Yulin Household General. From this, it was obvious that to Liu Shan, Zhao Yun was no less than Zhuge Liang. 
After that, there was no documentation of Zhao Tong, who might have died during the Jingyao era.

A general of Shu Han of the three kingdoms, Zhao Lei was Controller of Guan Yu's guards. 
Loyal to Guan Yu, he refused to surrender even when Guan Yu was defeated in Maicheng. In the end, he was captured by Wu General Ma Zhong, along with Guan Yu and his son. Sun Quan ordered to have Guan Yu and Guan Ping executed but what happened to Zhao Lei wasn't mentioned. 
In Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Zhao Lei died in battle when trying to break out of the siege with Guan Yu.

A Shu general and one of the Five Tigers. 
Zhao Yun first served for Gongsun Zan and later went to Liu Bei, who treated him like a brother. In Battle of Changban, Liu Bei lost his wife in chaos and Zhao Yun risked his life to protect her and Liu Shan. 
When Liu Bei married Lady Sun, she became unbridled. Liu Bei had Zhao Yun oversee domestic affairs and while Liu Bei was away, Lady Sun tried taking Liu Shan back to Jiangdong but Zhao Yun and Zhang Fei stopped her. 
When Liu Bei founded Shu, Zhao Yun advised Liu Bei to not reward the officials and gave the farms back to his subjects instead, winning their loyalty. On Zhuge Liang's expedition, while the Shu army was retreating, Zhao Yun counterattacked to secure the army and supplies. 
He was dignified, wise, and a man of bravery.

From Zhending, Changshan, Zhao Guang was Zhao Yun's second son. 
When his father died, Zhao Guang was still young. Only when Zhao Guang became an adult was he appointed Standard Officer by Jiang Wei, who was in charge of the Shu army and restarting the northern expeditions. He then followed Jiang Wei on the northern expeditions and died in battled in Tazhong. 
Shu Han and Cao Wei fought in Tazhong several times. It was undetermined when Zhao Guang passed away. One theory was that he died in the fall of Shu.

Zhao Fan was the Administrator of Guiyang. After the Battle of Red Cliffs, Liu Bei led his forces to conquer the four commanderies in Jing Province and all four Administrators surrendered. 
Zhao Yun was ordered to take over the Administrator of Guiyang and Zhao Fan even suggested Zhao Yun to marry his widowed sister-in-law but was rejected. 
Afterwards, Zhao Fan held unkind intentions but was afraid Zhao Yun would see through. He lived in fear before choosing to go on a run and became missing.

From Nan Commandery, Jing Province, Kuai Liang was an adviser under Liu Biao. 
When Liu Biao first got to Jing Province, he struggled as the local clans refused to follow him. As he wanted to recruit soldiers to cease the uprisings, he turned to Kuai Liang and his brother, Kuai Yue, for advice. 
Kuai Liang suggested him to rule with kindness and the subjects would turn to him naturally. Then, he wouldn't need to worry about recruiting soldiers. 
Liu Biao was pleased to hear that and praised Kuai Liang for his "Strategy Good as Yongji." 
In the Romance, he proposed a scheme to Liu Biao in which Huang Zu faked his retreat while they set up ambush for Sun Jian. Sun Jian was therefore killed and Liu Biao's crisis was solved.

From Nan, Jing, Kuai Yue was Kuai Liang's brother. 
He's an important adviser for Liu Biao. After Liu Cong surrendered to Cao Cao, he served under him instead. 
He once advised He Jin to executed the eunuchs but He Jin hesitated and was killed by them. 
When Liu Biao first governed Jing Province, Kuai Yue advised Liu Biao to lure the bandit leader and killed all those who were cruel to win the public's trust. Liu Biao praised him for being as strategic as Jiu Fan. 
Kuai Yue predicted the rise of Cao Cao and convinced Liu Biao not to assist Yuan Shao before Battle of Guandu for Yuan Shao would certainly lose. After Liu Biao died, Kuai Yue pursuaded Liu Cong to surrender to Cao Cao, who was glad to have Kuai Yue, saying, "I am not glad for getting Jing but for getting Kuai Yue."

Liu Ba used to serve as Prefect of the Masters of Writing in Shu. 
An official in Jing known for his talent, he was praised by Zhuge Liang for his logistics planning and strategies. 
When serving for Liu Zhang, he advised him to be wary of Liu Bei. It was documented that Ba said, "Liu Bei is known as a hero. If you let him in, he will bring you misfortune." When he came, Ba again said, "If you send him against Zhang Lu, it would be like releasing a tiger into the mountains." 
All of his advice was proven right. 
When he served for Liu Bei, Yi's economy was suffering. Liu Bei turned to Liu Ba and they made a new currency, stabilized prices of goods, and set up government-owned businesses. The treasury of Yi was filled and the foundation of Shu's development was established.

From Muping County, Donglai Commandery, Liu Dai was Liu Yao's older brother and the Inspector of Yan Province. 
He was one of the warlords to oppose Dong Zhuo and had disagreements with Dong Commandery Administrator Qiao Mao, whom he led his army to steal military resources from and killed. That was one of the incidents that led to the split of the coalition against Dong. 
Then, Yellow Turban rebels invaded Yan Province and Liu Dai was defeated and killed.

Cao Cao's subordinate general was the governor of Dong County during the Battle of Guandu. 
On the eve of the Battle of Guandu, Yuan Shao's general Yan Liang attacked Liu Yan, the Shogun of Dongxian, at Baima, and Cao Cao sent Zhang Lia and Guan Yu to rescue him. When Guan Yu saw Yan Liang's command, he killed him with his horse and returned with his head cut off in the midst of thousands of people. 
In the "Romance of the Three Kingdoms", it is said that Liu Yan did not give Guan Yu a hard time when he was riding alone for a thousand miles in return for his kindness in relieving the siege.

Liu Biao was a general who occupied Jing in Eastern Han, who's one of the "8 famed officials" of the time. 
On his way to Jing, he was stopped by clan bandits and Yuan Shu so he left his entourages and went alone. With the help of Kuai Liang, Kuai Yue, and Cai Mao, he secured Jing. 
After the fall of the coalition against Dong, Yuan Shao tried to hold back Yuan Shu with Liu Biao. Yuan Shu was also planning to take over Jing so he fought Liu Biao along with Sun Jian. Sun Jian defeated Liu Biao and besieged him in Xiangyang. But he died from a stray arrow and Liu Biao turned the tide and won. 
When old, he lost his bravery and was also slow to appoint a successor, causing the two sons to fight. After he died, Liu Cong succeeded, followed the officers wish, and surrendered to Cao.

Liu Feng's bravery was documented in the Records, "He won every battle he was in." 
When Guan Yu attacked Wei, Liu Feng and Meng Da refused to send reinforcements as they had just occupied the commanderies in Shangyong and domination hadn't been established. Guan Yu was then defeated. 
Meng Da soon defected to Wei and attacked Shangyong, who also advised Liu Feng to surrender. He firmly rejected but their forces differed greatly in power. With Shen Yi and Shen Dan defecting, Liu Feng lost and returned to Chengdu. 
Liu Bei blamed Liu Feng and made him take his own life. Before Liu Feng died, he cried out, "If only I had listend to Meng Zidu!" The key reason Liu Feng had to die might have been what Zhuge Liang said, "Feng's prowess might become a threat if he joined our enemies."

Liu Du was the Administrator of Lingling Commandery, one of the four commanderies in Jing Province. 
Briefly mentioned in the official records, he originally served under Liu Biao and was one of the few Jing officials who favored Liu Qi. 
In Romance of the Three Kingdoms, he was a cowardly and indecisive man who let his son, Liu Xian, make all the decisions. On Liu Xian's advice, Lingling Commandery sent army to resist Liu Bei's invasion but General Xing Dao Rong and Liu Xian were captured by Zhao Yun. Liu Xian was then sent to his father, Liu Du, and convinced him to surrender.

Liu Yan was a warlord in Eastern Han and Liu Zhang's father. 
Liu Yan gave local clans and officials governorship and control over armies to maintain order, causing the rise of warlords in late Eastern Han. Dong Zhuo worsened the situation by promoting officials in the attempt to gain power by bribery. 
Liu Yan first wanted to be the governor of Jiaozhi but heard Yi might be auspicious so applied to be Governor of Yi instead. 
In the campaign against Dong Zhuo, Liu Yan stayed and guarded Yi. Guanzhong became chaotic from war and many refugees fled into Shu, indirectly making Yi stronger. 
Later, his sons Liu Fan and Liu Dan invaded Chang'an but failed and got killed. After losing his sons and the fire in Mianzhu, Liu Yan was forced to move to Chengdu before dying of illness.

Liu Bei was Emperor Zhaolie of Shu. 
He studied under Scholar Lu Zhi and was good with people like Emperor Gaozu. 
He befriended GuanYu and Zhang Fei and they were close like brothers. 
When entrusted with Xu, he lost it to Lu Bu and was forced to go to Cao Cao, who praised him, "You and I are the heroes of our time." 
Involved in Dong Cheng's rebellion and worried he would lose his place, Liu Bei revolted, failed, and escaped to Yuan Shao and Liu Biao. 
He recruited Zhuge Liang, formed alliance with Wu. After winning Battle at Red Cliffs, he secured Jing, Yi, and Hanzhong. He declared himself King of Hanzhong then established Shu. But Battle of Yiling to avenge Guan Yu resulted in defeat and he died with grief. 
Liu Bei established a kingdom from scratch and was a true hero.

From Jingling County, Jiangxia Commandery, Liu Xun was the son of Liu Zhang. 
When Liu Bei attacked Yi Province, Liu Zhang sent Liu Xun to guard Luocheng. Liu Xun and Liu Gui lasted a year before being defeated. Afterwards, Liu Xun surrendered to Liu Bei.

Liu Qi was Liu Biao's eldest son. 
The two looked similar and he was once favored. 
But Liu Biao's second wife, Lady Cai, wanted her son Liu Cong to hold power. She worked with Cai Mao and Zhang Yun against Liu Qi. 
Liu Biao believed the calumny and became distant to Liu Qi. 
Liu Qi turned to Zhuge Liang and the latter suggested him to leave Jiangxia. 
When Liu Biao was dying, with Cai and Zhang's interference, Liu Qi wasn't able to meet his father until he died. 
Cao Cao then invaded Jing and Liu Qi went to Liu Bei. 
After Battle of Red Cliffs, Liu Bei recommended Liu Qi to be Governor of Jing to gain trust of the commanderies in Jing. In the same year, Liu Qi died of illness and ended his mediocre life. No wonder Cao Cao sarcastically said, "Liu's sons are equivalent to dogs."

Liu Cong was Liu Biao's second son. 
The Romance stated Lady Cai helped Liu Cong as he's her son but most records didn't mention that. The Book of the Later Han wrote, "Cong married Biao's second wife Lady Cai's neice. That's why she favored Cong and criticized Qi." 
After Liu Biao passed, Liu Qi succeeded the position of an official. When Cao Cao came south with his army, with the advice from Kuai Yue, Han Song, and Fu Xun, Liu Cong surrendered to Cao. 
Securing Jing without no loss, Cao Cao gladly appointed Liu Cong Inspector of Qing and granted him Marquis. 
The part in the Romance about Liu Cong being killed on the way to Qing wasn't historically correct. In a note Pei Songzhi wrote for the Records, Cao Cao personally praised and promoted Liu Cong to Counsellor Remonstrant.

Liu Zhang was Liu Yan's son. 
After Liu Yan died, Liu Zhang succeeded as Inspector of Yi and was promoted Governor. 
Liu Zhang was born cowardly and Zhang Lu, who viewed him as his master, started to disobey him. Out of rage, Liu Zhang killed Zhang Lu's family and the two became enemies. When Cao Cao came to Jing, it was rumored he would attack Yi. 
Facing two enemies, Liu Zhang let Liu Bei into Shu but he soon rebelled with the excuse that Liu Zhang failed to send reinforcements. Liu Bei's army was once losing but Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, and Zhao Yun came to his rescue and besieged in Chengdu. Unwilling to see his people suffer, Liu Zhang surrendered. 
Kind yet unwise, Liu Zhang was holding the land desired by everyone. Having it taken might not have been a misfortune.

Liu Ye was a Wei scholar. 
He was praised by Xu Shaozeng for his talent to support world rulers. 
When Cao Cao invaded Hanzhong, the long standoff made him want to retreat. Seeing the enemies disorganized at night, Liu Ye suggested to attack and thus won. He also predicted when Liu Bei first secured Shu, his subjects wouldn't submit. He advised Cao Cao to attack but was rejected. Shu refugees later proved that right. 
As Cao Pi succeeded, he knew Liu Bei would invade Wu and Sun Quan didn't genuinely submit. He advised Cao Pi to attack but he refused. When Sun Quan defected, it was too late. 
In later days, Liu Ye was a counsellor who fawned. During Cao Rui's rule, he framed Chen Jiao and the emperor found him speculating his intentions. Liu Ye was distanced and driven mad.

Liu Shan was Liu Bei's son and the last emperor of Shu. 
The newly ascended Liu Shan had Zhuge Liang in charge and the ruling was strict. 
As Zhuge Liang passed, the succeeding chancellors Jiang Wan, Fei Yi, Dong Yun favored recuperation and Jiang Wei, who suggested to reinforce the army, was distanced. The kingdom was on the wane and they failed to be aware of Wei, leading to the fall of Shu. 
After the fall of Shu, Liu Shan was moved to Luoyang and appointed Duke of Anle. Sima Zhao held a banquet for him and asked the musicians to play Shu music. The old Shu officials were in tears but Liu Shan was unmoved. Sima Zhao asked and he said,"I'm happy here. I don't miss Shu." Sima Zhao laughed and knew he had no intention to defect. He then lived safely for the rest of his life.

From Muping, Donglai Commandery, Liu Yao became Inspector of Yang Province after Chen Wenren and was promoted to Governor later. He fought Sun Ce, who was under Yuan Shu, but failed to appreciate a great general under him, Taishi Ci, and was defeated by Sun Ce. 
Later, he assisted Zhu Hao in defeating Zhuge Xuan under Yuan Shu but Zhu Hao was lured and killed by Ze Rong. Liu Yao lost first but fought again and repelled Ze Rong. He then appointed Hua Xin as Administrator of Yuzhang. Then, Liu Yao died from a serious illness and Hua Xin surrendered to Sun Ce. In Chu Shi Biao, Zhuge Liang commented that he was upright but incompetent and a bad example for Liu Shan.

From Yinan, Wei Commandery, Shen Pei was first under Han Fu before he served under Yuan Shao and Yuan Shang. 
Loyal to Yuan Shao for life, he refused to surrender even when the Cao army took down Yecheng. However, he was the one who altered Yuan Shao's will with Feng Ji and made Yuan Shang the successor, leading to fraternal strife and the rapid fall of the Yuan family.

From Jincheng, Liangzhou, Fan Chou was a general under Dong Zhuo. 
After Dong Zhuo was killed by Lu Bu, Fan Chou sent his forces along with Li Jue and Guo Si to repel Lu Bu. Fan Chou was appointed General of the Right, the leader of officials, along with Li Jue and Guo Si. 
Soon afterwards, Ma Teng and Liu Yan attacked Chang'an together. Fan Chou's army repelled Ma Teng but Li Jue suspected that Fan Chou was working with Ma Teng. Fearing Fan Chou's growth in power, he set Fan Chou up and had him killed.

From Yangping, Yan, Yue Jin was one of the Five Elite Generals of Wei. 
When Cao Cao was raising troops, he was already following him and often served as a vanguard. He fought and defeated Zhang Xiu, Lu Bu, Liu Bei. In Battle of Guandu, as Cao Cao's vanguard, he fought hard and captured Yuan Shao's general Chunyu Qiong. 
After losing in Chibi, Cao Cao made Cao Ren and Yue Jin stay to guard Jing Province. When Guan Yu cut Xiangyang General Cao Ren's way of retreat, he was repelled by Yue Jin and Wen Pin. He then worked with Zhang Liao and Li Dian and greatly defeated Sun Quan in the Battle of Hefei. 
Yue Jin was famous for a great battle record but for some reason not much was documented in historical records. When Pei Songzhi wrote notes, there was barely any reference either.

A fictional character in the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Pan Feng was a general under Han Fu, Governor of Ji Province. 
He appeared when the Eastern coalition was attacking Dong Zhuo. Hua Xiong, Dong Zhuo's great general was guarding Sishui Pass then. He first defeated Sun Jian's forces then started provoking the Eastern coalition. 
Yuan Shu's underling, Yu She, went in battle first but was killed. Han Fu then recommended Pan Feng to go into battle but he was also quickly killed by Hua Xiong.

From Dong Commandery, Yan Province, Pan Zhang was one of the twelve tiger ministers. 
He was already following Sun Quan when he was Yangxian Chief. Pan Zhang not only settled the Shanyue tribes for Sun Quan but also guarded the border of Jing Province. His battle record was well decorated. In the Battle of Hefei, facing Zhang Liao's charging army, only Pan Zhang remained calm. 
He then captured and killed Guan Yu in the Battle of Xiangfan and killed Liu Bei's great general Feng Xi in the Battle Lingyi. He could be said to be the general with the best battle record in Eastern Wu.

A native in Hanshou of Wuling, a well-known great Confucianist in Jingzhou. Once worked as an official in Jiang Xia under Liu Biao and was quite famous. After Liu Biao died, he was recruited by Liu Bei, but he had an uneasy relationship with Guan Yu. After Sun Quan captured Jingzhou, he personally invited Pan Jun to work for him and handed over the military authority of Jingzhou to Pan Jun. After Sun Quan became emperor, Pan Jun was granted the official of the central administration. Not only did he quelled the foreigners' revolt in Wuling for Sun Quan, his upright personality also helped Sun Quan rein in his political affairs.

From Shouchun, Jiujiang, Jiang Qin was one of the twelve tiger ministers of Jiangdong. 
He first served under Sun Ce and helped him settle Jiangdong. After Sun Ce died, Jiang Qin continued to assist Sun Quan. 
When they were retreating in the Battle of Hefei, Zhang Liao attacked fiercely and Jiang Qin, along with other generals like Gan Ning, Ling Tong, Lu Meng, risked his life to fight so Sun Quan could escape to safety. 
Then he took over Jing Province from Lu Meng and was a honored general. 
In the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Jiang Qin excelled at shooting and was originally a bandit along with Zhou Tai.

From Lingling, Jing Province, Jiang Wan was one of the four famous officials of Shu Han. 
He once neglected his duties while drunk and was almost punished by Liu Bei. Zhuge Liang knew Jiang Wan's talent very well and dissuaded Liu Bei from it. 
Zhuge Liang saw Jiang Wan as his successor. After Zhuge Liang died, Jiang Wan assist Liu Shan and led the army to defend against Wei. Different from Zhuge Liang, who eagerly went on northern expeditions, Jiang Wan advocated recuperation but they therefore missed the chance to invade Wei while it was in chaos.

From Jiujiang, Jiang Gan was an official in Cao Wei. 
The official records had it that he was "good-looking and known as an excellent debater in Jiangnan and Huai River regions." 
Before the Battle of Red Cliffs, Cao Cao sent Jiang Gan to talk Zhou Yu into surrender. Zhou Yu treated him politely but firmly rejected to surrender. After Jiang Gan returned to Cao, he highly praised Zhou Yu for being generous and loyal. 
In the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, to show the dexterity of the Sun-Liu alliance, it was made up that Jiang Gan fell for their discord scheme and chain stratagems, leading to the defeat of Cao's forces.

Jiang Yiqu was a general under Yuan Shao. Some said Jiang Qi and him were the same person. 
After losing the Battle of Guandu, Yuan Shao, along with hundreds of his close followers, crossed the river hastily into Jiang Yiqu's camp. Jiang Yiqu then announced the order on Yuan Shao's behalf, gathered the remaining forces, and slightly calmed the Yuan army so they wouldn't all get eliminated by the Cao army. 
Afterwards, there's no document of him in the historical records.

A fictional character in the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Cai He was from the same family as Cai Mao. 
When Cao Cao came south to Jing Province, he surrendered to Cao along with Liu Cong, Cai Mao, and Zhang Yun. 
After Cao Cao fell for the discord scheme and killed Cai Mao wrongly, Cao Cao sent Cai He and his brother Cai Zhong to Eastern Wu as spies. But Cao Cao's scheme was seen through by Zhou Yu, who went along and took the two in. Zhou Yu then put on a false injury scheme with Huang Gai, making Cao Cao believe Huang Gai wanted to surrender. In the end, before the Battle of Red Cliffs, Cai He was executed.

A native inYu Chenliu, 
He was the father of Cai Wenji, a talented woman in the Eastern Han Dynasty. 
In addition, he was an expert in calligraphy, and he was also a master of music, and it was said that Cai Yong was the master of the Jiao Wei zither and the Ke Ting flute. 
In order to gain fame, Dong Zhuo threatened Cai Yong to force him to serve in the government because of his contemporary reputation. 
Later on, Dong Zhuo was killed and his body was exposed in the city, Cai Yong was saddened by his treatment and was imprisoned for this crime by Situ Wang Yun. 
After his death, his family's book collection was lost due to war, and if Cao Cao had not redeemed Cai Yan and allowed him to complete it, many of the classics would have been extinct.

From Yu, Chenliu, Cai Yan was Cai Yong's daughter. 
Her life was turbulent. She was married to Wei Zhongdao, who died early. During the Dong Zhuo chaos, she was captured by his general, taken to South Xiongnu, and married to the chieftain Zuo Xianwang. 
Cao Cao used to be close to Cai Yong. After hearing about Cai Yan, he paid a heavy ransom for her release and had her married to Dong Si. 
Later, Dong Si committed a capital crime and Cai pleaded for him. Cao Cao couldn't bear it and pardoned him. 
Cai Yong had more than 4000 books at home but all were lost at war. The knowledgeable Cai Yan rewrote 400 chapters and made a great contribution to the preservation of the Chinese culture. 
Cai Yan was also good at music. It was said that she composed Eighteen Songs of a Nomad Flute.

From Xiangyang, Nan Commandery, Cai Mao was the younger brother of Lady Cai, the second wife of Liu Biao. 
When Liu Biao went to Jing Province with little resource, he went to Cai Mao, Kuai Liang, and Kuai Yue for advice. With their assistance, he was able to settle Jing and Xiangyang. 
When Liu Biao was seriously ill, Cai Mao was worried Liu Biao would appoint Liu Qi as his successor so he forbade him from entering Xiangyang. After Liu Biao passed away, Cai Mao, Zhang Yun and the others inaugurated Liu Cong and convinced him to surrender to Cao Cao. 
In the Romance, he commanded the navy for Cao Cao. But before the Battle of Red Cliffs, Zhou Yu sowed discord between him and Cao Cao, leading to his execution.

Officer of Liu Biao and brother of Cai Mao. During the attempted murder of Liu Bei, his brother had him hold the northern gate of Xiangyang Castle. He later followed Cao Cao and fought in a skirmish leading up to the Battle of Chibi along with his brother. A member of the vanguard, he died when Gan Ning shot him with an arrow.

From Langya, Xu, Zhuge Liang was Chancellor of Shu. 
He met Sima Hui, Pang De Gong and other famous scholars in Jing, befriended Xu Shu, Pang Tong, and was given the nickname Crouching Dragon. 
After Liu Bei's three visits, Zhuge Liang was recruited. His Longzhong Plan helped Liu Bei become Emperor. 
Longzhong Plan, Jiangdu Plan, and Tashang Strategy were all similar, occupying Jing to build up momentum for an empire powerful enough to fight the central forces. 
Zhuge Liang excelled at political affairs and commanding military. After Liu Bei passed, he kept Shu running and handled all matters himself. In the end, he became ill from the burden and died. 
In the Romance, his parts were exaggerated, painting him as a deity-like figure which in the end overshadowed his true talent.

From Langya, Xu, Zhuge Ke was Zhuge Jin's son and an Eastern Wu official. 
Clever and famed as a debater when young, he was praised by Sun Quan to be a jade from Lantian. 
He quelled the Shanyue tribes by starving them and forcing them to surrender and became General-in-Chief after Lu Xun passed and took over the affairs in Jing. 
Before Sun Quan passed, he could tell Zhuge Ke's willfulness and didn't wish to favor him. But at the officials' insistence, he still entrusted Zhuge Ke with his son. 
At first, Zhuge Ke practiced kind laws and earned the subjects' respect. After winning Battle of Dongxing, his popularity made him arrogant. With both political and military powers, he waged a war against Wu but lost. He lost his people's trust and in the end was assassinated by Sun Jun.

From Langya, Xu Province, Zhuge Jin was an important Eastern Wu official. 
He was Zhuge Liang's elder brother and a military general of Eastern Wu. 
When Sun Quan sent him to Shu to see Liu Bei, he only met Zhuge Liang in the meeting and not in private. His separation of public and private affairs were praised. 
Before the Battle of Yiling, he wrote a letter to Liu Bei, advising him not to attack Wu just to avenge Guan Yu, though the content of the letter seemed to have another meaning. 
Though Zhuge Jin never accomplished any world-changing achievements, he was generous, kind, and great at evaluating situations. Always interacting with Sun Quan sauvely, he was deeply trusted by the officials and subjects of Eastern Wu and had a smooth career all the way to General-in-Chief.

From Langya, Xu Province, Zhuge Dan was a Cao Wei general and the cousin of Zhuge Liang and Zhuge Jin. Among the famous Qinglong scholars, he was one of the eight celebrities from "the 4 wise, 8 celebrities, 3 heirs." 
When the Sima family held power, Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin rebelled. Zhuge Dan helped settled the rebellion and became Senior General Who Attacks the East. 
However, as his friends Deng Yang and Xiahou Xuan were killed by Sima, fear grew in his heart so he secretly started bribery and recruited suicide warriors to protect himself. To test if Zhuge Dan had the intention to defect, Sima Zhao summoned him to the palace. Out of fear, Zhuge Dan rebelled and was defeated and killed in the end.

From Jiyang, Yiyang, Deng Ai was a Wei general. 
He was disregarded for stuttering until he was scouted by Sima Yi. 
When Jiang Wei contacted the Qiang tribes for northern expeditions, Deng Ai resisted with Guo Huai and Chen Tai. After the successful resistance and suppressing the rebelling Guanqiu Jian, he became valued and guarded the west of Wei against Shu Han. 
When Deng Ai and Zhong Hui attacked Shu, Zhong Hui was caught in a standoff against Jiang Wei, Deng Ai, in his seventies, led elites through the dangerous Yinping into Chengdu and killed Zhuge Zhan. Liu Shan therefore surrendered and Shu fell. However, Deng Ai grew arrogant and was enemies with Zhong Hui. When Jiang Wei was encouraging Zhong Hui to rebel, Zhong Hui accused Deng Ai of treason and he was killed.

From Xinye, Yiyang, Deng Zhi was a famous general of Shu Han. 
After Liu Bei passed away in Yongan, Deng Zhi went to Wu on Zhuge Liang's behalf to mend relations with them. 
Deng Zhi was honest about the pros and cons of the situation, which Sun Quan valued. Sun wrote a letter to Zhuge Liang, praising Deng Zhi and saying, "Only Deng Zhi could make the two kingdoms work together." 
Deng Zhi was dignified and reserved. He rarely built a bond with anyone but admired Jiang Wei greatly. He treated his subordinates fairly, never holding back rewards or punishments and was famous for it.

Deng Xian was originally Liu Zhang's subordinate and he was Meng Da's nephew. 
After Liu Bei and Liu Zhang became enemies, generals such as Deng Xian and Zhang Ren led the forces to face the enemies in Fucheng but was drawn back to Mianzhu by Liu Bei's army. As Liu Zhang surrendered, he became a follower of Liu Bei as well before betraying Shu along with Meng Da. 
When Meng Da planned to betray Wei and returned to Shu, Sima Yi worked with Deng Xian in secret and the latter opened the city gate for the Wei army, leading to Meng Da's arrest and death.

Gong Zhi wasn't mentioned in the official records and was a fictional character in the Romance of the Three Kingdoms. 
He was the subordinate of Jin Xuan, the Administrator of Wuling. When Zhang Fei attacked Wuling, Gong Zhi advised Jin Xuan to surrender. However, Jin Xuan refused and led the army himself to fight. To his surprise, Gong Zhi took over the city while he's away and even shot him to death and presented his head to Zhang Fei. 
When Wuling was settled, Gong Zhi was appointed the Administrator of Wuling by Liu Bei for his achievement.

One of the Yellow Turban leaders, Gong Du occupied Runan along with Liu Pi after the Yellow Turban Uprising. 
In the Battle of Guandu, Liu Pi and him supported Yuan Shao in Runan and fought Cao Cao's forces from behind. 
Yuan Shao sent Liu Bei with their army to Runan and met up with Gong Du and Liu Pi, he was then defeated by Cao Cao. Liu Bei abandoned Yuan Shao and went to serve under Liu Biao and Gong Du was then missing.

Lu Su was an Eastern Wu politician. 
His images in historical records and the Romance were different. In official records, he was ambitious and decisive. 
He met Zhou Yu when young, who recommended him to Sun Quan. 
Lu Su proposed the Tashang Strategy to Sun Quan. His insight of dividing and conquering was before Longzhong Plan was made! 
In Battle of Red Cliffs, Zhou Yu and him predicted the situation and allied with Liu Bei before Cao's army arrived. 
Before Zhou Yu died, he recommended Lu Su as his successor. As Liu Bei occupied Jing and Guan Yu drove the officials from Eastern Wu away, the situation became tense so Lu Su negotiated with Guan Yu. He was generous and reasonable and the two sides set Xiang River as the border with Lu retrieving Changsha, Guiyang, and Jiangxia.

From Zhuo, Lu Zhi was a scholar in Eastern Han. Gongsun Zan and Liu Bei were both his pupils. 
When the Yellow Turban Uprising broke out, Lu Zhi repeatedly defeated Zhang Jiao. But he refused to bribe Eunuch Zuo Feng, who framed him, had him arrested and almost killed. Lu Zhi was replaced by Dong Zhuo in battle but he was instantly defeated. 
When planning to eliminate the eunuchs, He Jin summoned Dong Zhuo to assist him. Knowing Dong Zhuo couldn't be trusted, Lu Zhi tried to dissuade him but failed. He was proven right. 
After Dong Zhuo rose to power, he wished to depose the emperor and only Lu Zhi stated his opposition, infuriating Dong Zhuo. Lu Zhi knew Dong Zhuo would never tolerate him so he resigned. 
Later, Yuan Shao appointed Lu Zhi military adviser but he died soon after.

A native in Baxi of Yizhou, originally Zhang Lu's aide, and later joined Cao Cao with Zhang Lu. Zhang Lu wanted to proclaim himself the king of Hanzhong, Yan Pu advised Zhang Lu that he should not overstep, but he should assist the emperor, and follow the example of Emperor Weng of Jin and Emperor Huan of Qi, and Zhang Lu followed the advice. Later, when Cao Cao attacked Zhang Lu, he analyzed the situation for Zhang Lu. Zhang Lu accepted his advice one by one. In the end, Zhang Lu surrendered to Cao Cao, and Cao Cao treated them generously because of the previous behaviors of the two.

From Zhijiang, Nan Commandery, Huo Jun was originally Liu Biao's military general before serving under Liu Bei. 
After Liu Bei entered Shu and became enemies with Liu Zhang, Huo Jun was ordered to guard Jiameng, during which Zhang Lu sent Yang Bo to advise Huo Jun to surrender. Jiameng was then besieged by Liu Zhang's army. Huo Jun had only a few hundred troops but managed to resist for a year before finding the enemies' weakness and defeating them.

Bao Xin was from Pingyang County, Taishan Commandery. 
He joined the coalition against Dong with his brother, Bao Tao. The insightful Bao Xin didn't side with Yuan Shao but chose Cao Cao, who had little power then, and advised him to settle in Yan Province so he could conquer the world. 
Then, the Yellow Turban forces of Qing Province invaded Yan Province and Liu Dai, the Yan Governor, died in battle. Bao Xin then recommended Cao Cao to be the Governor of Yan Province. 
But Cao Cao was attacked by the Yellow Turban forces before he could stabilize Yan Province. To help Cao Cao retreat, Bao Xin fought to his death on the battlefield with his body lost and couldn't be retreated, much to Cao Cao's dismay.

From Donghai Commandery, Xu Province, Mi Zhu was a politician in Shu Han. 
From a wealthy family in Xu Province, at Tao Qian's request, Mi Zhu welcomed Liu Bei to rule Xu Province. After Lu Bu took over Xu Province, he still followed Liu Bei, even gifting him their family possessions and marrying his younger sister to Liu Bei. 
Though Mi Zhu had no particular talent, he was generous and composed. As he still chose to follow Liu Bei in his worst times, when Liu Bei ruled Yi Province, Mi Zhu was promoted General Who Pacifies Han, position higher than that of Zhuge Liang. 
Later, his younger brother, Mi Fang, betrayed Shu for Wu which led to the death of Guan Yu. Though Liu Bei didn't hold him responsible, Mi Zhu still felt so ashamed that he fell sick and died.

From Donghai Commandery, Xu Province, Mi Fang was a politician in Shu Han and Mi Zhu's younger brother. 
Mi Fang served under Liu Bei along with his brother even through the most turbulent years. 
After Liu Bei's forces entered Shu, Guan Yu was appointed the Administrator of Xiangyang and Mi Fang the Administrator of Nan Commandery. The two guarded and ruled Jing Province together but didn't get along. 
In the Battle of Xiangfan, as Mi Fang and Shiren delayed the delivery of military supplies, Guan Yu claimed to wish to put the two to trial so they surrendered to Sun Wu, leading to Guan Yu losing parts of Jing Province and was in the end defeated in Maicheng.

From Zhuyi, Pei Commandery, Xue Zong was a politician in Eastern Wu. 
When young, he fled to Jiao Province with his family and studied under the famous scholar Liu Xi. 
After Shi Xie submitted to Eastern Wu, Xue Zong was summoned by Sun Quan and first served as a local official in Jiao Province to assist Lu Dai in settling the rebels. 
Later, recognized for his literary talent, he was summoned to the palace and promoted Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.

From Yingchuan, Zhong Hui was Zhong Yao's son and a general in the late Wei. 
He followed Sima Shi to settle the uprising of Guanqiu Jian. Sima Shi died on the way back and Zhong Hui was hired by Sima Zhao. 
As Zhuge Dan revolted in Shouchun, Zhong Hui tricked Quan Yi into surrendering. The remaining generals lost trust in each other and he was able to quell the rebellion. 
In Wei's conquest of Shu, Zhong Hui attacked Jiang Wei in Jiange so Deng Ai could ambush Chengdu. Liu Shan therefore surrendered. 
Zhong Hui then tried to rebel. He framed Deng Ai, had him arrested before trying to invade Chang'an but his generals were against him. He died in a riot. 
Zhong Hui also excelled at calligraphy and had great influence on metaphysics studies. But he was also described as petty.

From Yingchuan, Yu, Zhong Yao was an important Wei politician. 
After Dong Zhuo died, his generals Li Jue and Guo Si revolted. Zhong Yao persuaded Li Jue's subordinates to rebel so Emperor Xian could escape. 
As Emperor Xian re-established the capital in Xuchang, Ma Teng and Han Sui turned against each other. It was Zhong Yao who had them submit. 
Zhong Yao also uppressed the Xiongnu and Hedong rebels, helping Luoyang and Guanzhong regain former prosperity. He then followed Cao Cao to attack Zhang Lu and Xu Huang in Battle of Fancheng. 
After Cao Pi usurped, Zhong Yao, Hua Xin, and Wang Lang were appointed Three Ducal Ministers, whom Cao Pi called "The Greats of the Time." 
Zhong Yao excelled at politics and calligraphy, being called "Zhong and Wang" along with Wang Xizhi.

Han Xuan was the Administrator of Changsha. 
In the official records, little was documented and it was greatly different from that in the Romance, such as Han Xuan possibly being Huang Zhong's subordinate. Also, there was no document of him being brutal and violent. 
The Romance of Three Kingdoms depicted him as the brother of Han Hao, a Wei general. After the Battle of Red Cliffs, Guan Yu attacked Changsha and Han Xuan sent Huang Zhong in response. Huang Zhong and Guan Yu battled for 3 days. They both saw each other as a hero and admired each other. Han Xuan therefore suspected Huang Zhong of collaborating with the enemies and ordered to have Huang Zhong executed. At this time, accusing Han Xuan of being brutal and cruel, Wei Yan rebelled and killed him.

From Henei Commandery, Han Hao was a military general of Wei. 
When Dong Zhuo revolted, Han Hao led the army to fight Dong Zhuo and his forces in Mengjin and became famous. 
Later, Yuan Shu appointed him as Riding Duwei but didn't regarded him highly. He was then recommended to Cao Cao by Xiahou Dun. 
Han Hao initiated the military-agricultural colony policy, which was implemented in a massive scale by Cao Cao. After that, Cao Wei almost had no food production problems until the end. 
In the Romance of Three Kingdoms, it was stretched that he was the brother of Han Xuan while the two where not actually related.

From Yiyang, Jing, Han Song was Liu Biao's suordinate. 
First an underling of Liu Biao, he repeatedly advised him to adhere to his rule as a governor. 
Before Battle of Guandu, Liu Biao was hesitant between following Yuan Shao or Cao Cao. Han Song analyzed the situation and stated Cao Cao's advantages. Liu Biao therefore sent him as an envoy to the capital, Xuchang. 
Before Han Song left, he informed Liu Biao that if he was summoned by Emperor Xian, he would have to comply. 
In Xuchang, Han Song was indeed appointed Palace Attendant and Administrator. He returned to Liu Biao, praising the palace and advising Liu Biao to send his son there. Liu Biao was infuriated, doubted Han Song's loyalty and imprisoned him. Han Song wasn't released until Cao Cao acquired Jing Province.

From Liaoxi, You Province, Han Dang was a general of Eastern Wu and one of the twelve tiger ministers of Jiangdong. 
In his early years, he was first under Sun Jian. With his extraordinary arm strength and excellent archery skills, he served under three generations of the Sun family. Diligent and honored, he was greatly appreciated by Sun Quan. 
Han Dang could be seen in many major and minor battles of Eastern Wu. 
He followed Zhou Yu to defeat Cao Cao in the Battle of Red Cliffs, ambushed Nan Commandery with Lu Meng, won against Liu Bei in the Battle of Yiling with Lu Xun, and eliminated the bandits in Danyang. It was true that he spent his whole life on the battlefield.

From Jincheng, Liangzhou, Han Sui was one of the warlords in Liangzhou. 
Originally named Han Yue, Han Sui wreaked havoc in Liangzhou and the Guanzhong region miltiple times. 
After Cao Cao welcomed Emperor Xian to Xuchang, Han Sui submitted to the palace and was appointed General Who Attacks the West. But after a few years, he rebelled with Ma Chao and was defeated by Cao forces in the Battle of Tong Gate. Originally planning to escape to Liu Bei, but Han Sui was persuaded by his subordinate Chenggong Ying to submit to the Qiang tribe in Jincheng who assisted him in the past. One theory had it that he died of illness and one was that he was killed by Qu Yan, Jiang Shi, and the other generals in Jincheng.
Fictional character in Romance of The Three Kingdoms. Served Cao Cao and guarded Luoyang, later he was killed by Guan Yu during the Thousand League Journey.

Han Xian was a White Wave Bandit leader in the late Eatern Han. 
Originally a bandit, he was summoned by Yang Feng to escort Emperor Xian out of Chang'an and promoted Zhengdong General. 
When Cao Cao intended to welcome Emperor Xian to Xuchang, Han Xian and Yang Feng led their troops to stop it but they were greatly defeated by Cao Cao and had to escape and submit to Yuan Shu. 
He then defected to Lu Bu and wreaked havoc in Xu, Yang, and other provinces. Disliked by the people, he was then attacked by Liu Bei and killed by Zhang Xuan on his escape to Bing Province.

From Yingchuan Commandery, Han Fu was a warlord in the late Eastern Han. 
Originally an official under Yuan, he was promoted to Governor of Ji Province by Dong Zhuo and later joined the campaign against Dong. 
After the dismissal of the coalition against Dong, Han Fu and Yuan Shao became rivals. On Feng Ji's advice, Yuan Shao secretly marched south with Gongsun Zan. Caught off guard, Han Fu surrendered without a fight and gave up Ji Province. 
After surrendering to Yuan Shao, Han Fu was attacked by Zhu Han as the two had old grudges. In fear that Yuan Shao would set him up, Han Fu left to serve under Zhang Miao. Not long after, Yuan Shao sent an envoy for a secret meeting with Zhang Miao. Han Fu thought the envoy was here to kill him and thus committed suicide.

From Zuo Commandery, Hebei, Jian Yong was a politician of Shu Han in the Three Kingdoms period. Along with Sun Qian and Mi Zhu, he was one of the most senior official in Shu. 
He met Liu Bei when young and had been following him since the Yellow Turban Uprising. 
Jian Yong was candid, relaxed, humorous, and articulate. He often served as Liu Bei's envoy or persuader. When Liu Bei came to Yi Province, Liu Zhang admired Jian Yong greatly. 
Later, when Liu Bei and Liu Zhang turned against each other over Yi Province, it was Jian Yong who was sent by Liu Bei to convince Liu Zhang to surrender. 
There was also one occasion where Jian Yong advised Liu Bei in a casual way to abolish overly strict laws.

From Langya, Xu, Yan Liang was one of Yuan Shao's generals. 
In official records, he was said to be courageous. But there were also comments that he only had bravery and could be captured as the battled started or brave but couldn't be trusted with responsibility. 
In the Romance, Wen Chou, Gao Lan, Zhang He, and him were known as the"Four Generals of Hejian." 
In Battle of Sishui Pass, the advancement was stopped by Hua Xiong and Yuan sighed, "Hua Xiong would not be a threat if Yan Liang or Wen Chou were here." In Battle of Guandu, Cao and Yuan's forces fought in Baima. Yan Liang slayed Cao Cao's men Wei Xu and Song Xian and defeated the famous general Xu Huang. Cao Cao sent out Guan Yu, who moved swiftly on his Red Hare Horse and decapitated Yan Liang before he could react.

From Yiyang, Jing, Wei Yan was a Shu general. 
First a soldier, he scored many military exploits. When Liu Bei declared himself Emperor of Hanzhong, he promoted Wei Yan as Administrator of Hanzhong. 
Wei Yan grew his army and applied Double Gate Strategy to repel the Wei army many times. 
In the Romance, Zhuge Liang was suspicious of Wei Yan, to the contrary of offical records. 
Wu Hou and Wei Yan had different views but both were loyal to Shu. Wu Hou depended on Wei Yan especially, appointing him as General on many expeditions. When critically ill, he said, "Have Yan be the rearguard. If Yan refuses, then retreat without him." 
It was obvious he trusted Wei Yan to never betray Shu. 
However, Wei Yan never got along with Yang Yi, who accused him of treason and killed him.

Wei Xu was a military general under Lu Bu who often acted alongside Song Xian. 
When Lu Bu was surrounded in Xiapi, Wei Xu, Song Xian, and Hou Chen betrayed Lu Bu and arrested Chen Gong, Gao Shun and the others before opening the gates to surrender to Cao Cao. Lu Bu was caught off guard, arrested, and killed by Cao Cao. 
In the Romance of Three Kingdoms, it was changed to him capturing Lu Bu along with Song Xian before being killed by Yuan Shao's general, Yan Liang, in the Battle of Guandu in the end.

Pang Tong was Liu Bei's adviser. 
He had the nickname of Phoenix, equal to Dragon Zhuge Liang. Sima Hui praised him to be the best in Nan. 
First Officer of Merit, he was appointed Prefect of Leiyang by Liu Bei but was ousted for poor performance. Lu Su and Zhuge Liang advised Liu Bei to value Pang Tong so he was re-recruited. 
Pang Tong's position was only lower than Zhuge Liang, both Advisers of the Household. 
He outlined strategies to conquer Shu as well as making decisions in actual battles. 
Sadly, when they invaded Luocheng, Pang Tong was hit by a stray arrow and died young. 
In the Romance, he presented Cao Cao with Link Ship Strategy and made Zhou Yu's fire attack successful. 
Pang Tong was also described as ugly and arrogant but it was only the writer's description.

Pang Yi was from Yi, Henan. 
He followed Liu Yan into Shu. After Liu Yan's passing, he continued to serve under Liu Zhang. 
As he once saved Liu Zhang's son from Chang'an and became in-laws with Liu Zhang, he became arrogant and domineering. Other than resisting Zhang Lu, the reason Liu Zhang invited Liu Bei to Shu was to counter powerful officials like Pang Yi and Li Yi. 
After Liu Bei became the ruler of Yi Province, Pang Yi chose to serve under Liu Bei instead.

Pang De was from Nanan, Liangzhou. 
First under Ma Teng, Pang De scored many and was famous among the many great generals in the Ma Teng army. 
As Ma Teng assumed a position in the palace, Pang De followed Ma Chao and stayed in Xiliang before the two rebelled against Cao Cao. Upon defeat, they went to serve for Zhang Lu. Later, Ma Chao went to Shu while Pang De stayed under Zhang Lu and surrendered to Cao with him. 
In Battle of Fancheng, he tried to rescue Cao Ren with Yu Jin but was defeated and arrested. Guan Yu advised Pang De to surrender as his cousin, Pang Rou, who was an official in Shu. Enraged, Pang De refused and was decapitated. 
Cao Cao therefore lamented that despite his friendship of 30 years with Yu Jin, Yu Jin was less loyal than the newly recruited Pang De.

A fictional character In the Romance of Three Kingdoms, Tan Xiong was a general under Sun Huan of Eastern Wu. 
When Liu Bei attacked Wu to avenge Guan Yu, Tan Xiong faced them in Zigui along with Li Yi. When Li Yi was struggling to defeat Zhang Bao, Tan Xiong started shooting arrows at Zhang Bao from behind. Luckily, Guan Xing came to his rescue and even captured Tan Xiong and left him to Zhang Bao to kill.

From Xie, Hedong, Guan Ping was Guan Yu's son. 
Little was written in official records except he was captured along with his father and executed by Sun Quan. 
In the Romance, he was portrayed as Guan Yu's adopted son. In Battle of Xinye, he assisted Liu Feng and led to the success of Zhuge Liang's fire strategy. After Pang Tong died, he went to Jing for aid. After Zhuge Liang went to Yi Province, he stayed in Jing to support Guan Yu. 
When Guan Yu attacked Xiangyang, Guan Ping followed and scored exploits before marching to Fancheng with Guan Yu. With Cao Ren's resistance in Fancheng, Sun Quan took the chance to ambush Guan Yu while he was struggling. Surrounded by both Cao and Wu's armies, Guan Yu and Guan Ping escaped to Maicheng before both were captured and killed.

Guan Yu was Shu's leading general, who was a match for 10, 000 men and famed throughout China. 
When Liu Bei recruited for a volunteer army, he met Guan Yu and Zhang Fei and they were close like brothers. 
As Liu Bei betrayed Cao, Cao's army attacked and Guan Yu surrendered for Liu Bei's family's safety. 
Cao Cao knew he didn't submit willingly but he treated him well and said, "Not forgetting your roots means you're a great man." 
He killed Yan Liang and solved Baima Crisis to repay Cao for his hospitality before returning to Liu Bei. 
After Battle of Red Cliffs, Liu Bei entered Shu while Guan Yu guarded Jing. 
Later, Guan Yu went north surrounded Cao Ren in Fancheng but he was attacked from behind by Eastern Wu. He escaped to Maicheng and was killed as he refused to surrender.

Guan Suo was not mentioned in the official records but a fictional character in plays, stories, and folk tales. It was said that he was a good looking man. 
Called "Flower Guan Suo" in the Romance, he once guarded Jing Province with Guan Yu before going to Shu after Guan Yu died. In the southern expedition against Meng Huo, Zhuge Liang had Guan Suo as the vanguard. 
The opera Biography of Hua Guan Suo tells the story of Guan Suo and his wife, Bao San Niang, guarding Jiameng Pass.

The daughter of Guan Yu, whose real name is not known, is known as Miss Guan 3rd, also known as Feng or Yinping. 
The only record in the official history is that Sun Quan sent an envoy to propose marriage to Sun and Liu in order to consolidate the alliance and the issue of Jingzhou, but Guan Yu sternly refused, angrily scolding that the daughter of a tiger could not marry the son of a dog. This made Sun Quan more resentful of Guan Yu. 
According to legend, she was known for her beauty and intelligence, and Zhuge Liang played matchmaker to marry her to Li Cuo's son, Li Jue.

From Xie, Hedong, Guan Xing was Guan Yu's son. 
Famous when young as Attendant and Central Military Superviser, he was valued by Zhuge Liang, who wished to prepare him for great things. Sadly, Guan Xing died young. 
In the Romance, he first appeared in Battle of Fancheng. He was the messenger to report the victory when Guan Yu flooded 7 armies. Before he returned to Jing Province, Guan Yu already lost the battle. 
Before Battle of Yiling, he fought with the son of Zhang Fei, Zhang Bao, but with Liu Bei's mediation, the two became sworn brothers. He followed Liu Bei into the battle against Wu and was appointed Prancing Dragon General. 
Guan Xing was also one of the major generals for Zhuge Liang's northern expeditions against Cao Wei. But he died of illness before the 6th one.

Qu Yi was a general under Yuan Shao in the late Eastern Han. 
Originally Han Fu's subordinate, he then betrayed Han for Yuan Shao. 
In the Battle of Jieqiao, Gongsun Zan led the famous white horse army himself to battle Yuan Shao, who ordered Qu Yi to counter with archers and heavy infantry. 
Qu Yi arranged the archers and soldiers in a formation and had all the arrows launched at once when the cavalry were close. They greatly defeated the enemy and even slayed the great general, Yan Gang. 
Though Gongsun Zan was defeated, his stray soldiers accidentally encountered Yuan Shao, who only had dozens of personal guards with him. When Yuan Shao was in danger, Qu Yi came to his rescue and repelled the enemy. 
However, Qu Yi became arrogant for his merits and was killed by Yuan Shao.

A native of Ban in Pingyuan County, a litterateur in the late Eastern Han Dynasty. He was well known in the world for his talent, but arrogant and narrow-minded, and often humiliated others, and eventually perished as a result. Initially recommended by Kong Rong, he was appointed by Cao Cao. But because having repeatedly humiliated Cao Cao, Cao Cao was angry, but did not want to kill him due to his talent, so he was sent to Liu Biao. Liu Biao treated him with courtesy, but Mi Heng had some harsh words for Liu Biao, so Liu Biao deliberately recommended Mi Heng to Huang Zu, who was impatient and rude. Later, Mi Heng's harsh words caused Huang Zu to be angry as expected, and Huang Zu sent his man to strangle him.

From Wucheng, Wu Commandery, Yan Baihu was a mountain bandit in the Wu region in the late Eastern Han. 
When Sun Ce's forces were trying to conquer the local warlords in Jiangdong in the attempt to seize the region, Yan Baihu and Chen Yu, the self-appointed Administrator of Wu, fought against Sun Ce together. After he was defeated by Sun Ce, there was no more document of him in historical records. 
In the Romance, he sent his brother, Yan Yu, to battle Sun Ce but in vain. Retreating to the city of Wu, their plea for truce was rejected. He then allied with Wang Lang but still couldn't win against Sun Ce. In the end, he escaped to Yuhang and died in the hands of Dong Xi.

Yan Jun, a native of Pengcheng, Xu Province, was a politician of Wu. 
A famous and brilliant scholar of his time, he not only was an expert on classic books but had publications on tides and hydrology, which were sadly lost. 
After Lu Su died, Sun Quan originally wished that Yan Jun would replace him and take charge of the military of Sun Wu. However, Yan Jun knew that his talent wasn't enough for the great responsibility and rejected by saying, "I am only a simple scholar, unfamiliar with military affairs. If I take up this appointment I am not suited for, there will be regrets." 
After Sun Quan declared himself emperor and Yan Jun was sent to Shu Han as an envoy, he was deeply admired by Zhuge Liang as well.

Yan Yan, a native of Ba Commandery, was a general of Shu Han. He first served under Liu Zhang before submitting to Liu Bei. 
He predicted that Liu Zhang inviting Liu Bei into Shu was like nursing a viper in their bosom. 
When Liu Bei attacked Jiangzhou, they were defeated and captured by Zhang Fei. When asked by Zhang Fei why he wouldn't surrender, Yan Yan reprimanded him and said emotionally,"There are only dead generals but never surrendering generals!" 
Admiring him for his courage, Zhang Fei untied him personally and treated him lilke a guest. Deeply moved, Yan Yan therefore surrendered. The following was not documented in historical records.

From Shanyin, Kuaiji, Kan Ze was a politician of Eastern Wu. 
A great scholar of his time, Kan Ze specialized in calendar systems, promoting Qianxiang Calendar in Sun Wu, which was one of the most advanced calendars of that time. 
Many stories of him were added in the Romance of Three Kingdoms. In the Battle of Red Cliffs, he saw through Huang Gai's false injury scheme and presented a false surrender letter to Cao Cao for Huang Gai as well as acting with Gan Ning to trick Cai Zhong and Cai He, whom Cao Cao sent to investigate. 
When Liu Bei waged the Battle of Yiling to avenge Guan Yu, Kan Ze vouched for Lu Xun with the lives of his whole family that he would be the greatest choice to lead their army and Lu Xun in the end successfully defeated the Shu army.

From Wu County, Wu Commandery, Gu Yong was an official of Eastern Wu who was the Imperial Chancellor at one point. 
When young, he studied under Cai Yong. After he joined the civial service, he scored many merits, once governing Kuaiji on Sun Quan's behalf. He repelled bandits and kept the peace of Kuaiji Commandery. 
Gu Yong always acted composed and quiet. Sun Quan once praised him, "Whenever the quiet Gu speaks, he's always right."

Unmentioned in historical records, Wutugu was a fictional king of Wuge in the Romance. 
When Zhuge Liang waged expeditions against the southern tribe, the tribal leader Meng Huo souoght help from Wuge and Wutugu therefore sent reinforcements. With the army he took pride in that was equipped with rattan armor, which could resist blades and spears, Wutugu greatly defeated the Shu soldiers. But in the end, as he underestimated the enemy, he was trapped in Panshe Valley by the Shu army and was burnt to death along with his Wuge soldiers by Zhuge Liang.

Unmentioned in official records, Meng You was the brother of Meng Huo, the southern tribal leader, in the Romance. 
Meng Huo and him once made a false surrender together but their scheme were disclosed. He then recommended King Duosi to his brother. But they still failed and got captured. In the end, he surrendered to Shu Han along with Meng Huo.

From Jianning, Yi Province, Meng Huo was a local leader in Nanzhong. In the Romance, he was the southern tribal leader. 
After Liu Bei passed away, the situation in Shu Han became unstable. Yong Kai therefore gathered the local leaders for rebellion and Meng Huo was among them. 
Then, Yong Kai was killed by Gao Ding. Meng Huo organized the fleeing soldiers and continued to fight Zhuge Liang. To settle Nanzhong once and for all, Zhuge Liang captured Meng Huo and let him go 7 times until he submitted. He even had him rule Nanzhong, which indeed remained peaceful subsequently. 
In the Romance, he was described to be one of Sima Yi's five armies to attack Shu. When Zhuge Liang led his army to conquer the southern tribe, the mentioned underlings of Meng Huo were mainly fictional.

A fictional character in the Romance, Lady Zhurong was the wife of Meng Huo and Dailai Dongzhu's sister. It was said that she was the descendant of the southern fire deity, Zhurong. 
Famous for her knife throwing skills, she captured Zhang Yi and Ma Zhong respectively. She was then provoked to go deep into the enemy army by Wei Yan and Zhao Yun before being captured by Ma Dai. Meng Huo then redeemed Lady Zhurong with Zhang Yi and Ma Zhong. 
Later, she submitted to Shu Han along with Meng Huo.

A fictional character in the Romance of Three Kingdoms, King Duosi was the wisest man in the southern tribe and the lord of Tulong Cave. 
After Meng Huo was captured and released by Kongming for the 4th time, Meng You recommended King Duosi to Meng Huo. 
King Duosi suggested him to deter Shu's army with four poisonous springs. While Zhuge Liang was helpless, Meng Huo's brother, Meng Jie, came to his aid and solved the problem imposed by the springs. 
After, King Duosi was sent to guard Sanjiang City. He employed poisonous arrows but Kongming still went through his defense, leading to his death on the battlefield.

Shamoke was a tribal chieftain in the five valleys in Wuling Commandery. 
Before the Battle of Yiling, Liu Bei sent Ma Liangan to settle the valley tribes, who then joined the Shu Han army. The Battle of Yiling ended in the decisive defeat of Shu force and Shamoke was decapitated in action. 
In the Romance, he shot Gan Ning with an arrow. Later, when Shu was defeated, he encountered Zhou Tai on his escape and was killed by him.

Unmentioned in official records, Jinhuan Sanjie was a fictional character in the Romance of Three Kingdoms. He was the tribal leader Meng Huo's subordinate and the First Dong Marshal. 
When Meng Huo learned of Zhuge Liang invading with an army, he sent three forces in response and Jinhuan Sanjie was the Marshal of the middle force. However, before they faced the Shu army, their camp was ambushed at night by Zhao Yun and Wei Yan. Jinhuan Sanjie was slain by Zhao Yun, who then presented his head to Zhuge Liang.

Unmentioned in official records, Ahui Nan was a fictional character in the Romance of Three Kingdoms. He was a general under Meng Huo and the Third Dong Marshal. 
When Zhuge Liang attacked the southern tribe, he joined the battle but was captured by Zhang Yi. He was then released by Zhuge Liang. After Meng Huo's second release by Zhuge Liang, he borne grudges against the marshals, who tied him up and surrendered to Zhuge Liang. He then killed Ahui Nan and Dongan Na, whom he suspected was favoring to Shu Han.

Unmentioned in official records, Dongtu Na was a fictional character in the Romance of Three Kingdoms. He was the tribal leader Meng Huo's subordinate and the Second Dong Marshal. 
When Zhuge Liang attacked the southern tribe, he joined the battle but was captured by Zhang Yi. He was then released by Zhuge Liang. After Meng Huo's second release by Zhuge Liang, he borne grudges against the marshals, who tied him up and surrendered to Zhuge Liang. He then killed Ahui Nan and Dongtu Na, whom he suspected was favoring to Shu Han.

One of the chiefs of the Xianbei tribes. 
He was a brave man who was well respected by the Xianbei, and accepted the Han exiles to learn how to use their equipment and invoke the Han military law, making his tribe strong for a time. 
After Cao Cao's pacification of Youzhou, Kronk could submit to the court, but his attitude was erratic, if the Central Plains was strong, he would submit to the court; when the Central Plains was in turmoil, he would invade and violate the borders, and his relationship with Cao Wei changed from time to time. He was finally assassinated by Wang Xiong, the governor of Youzhou of Cao Wei. 
Contrary to the historical facts and the legend, not only did he not attack Shu, but also wanted to join hands with Shu and Han to attack Wei. 
In addition, it is said that the descendants were Khitan.

From Liaodong, You, Gongsun Du was a warlord in the late Eastern Han. 
With Xu Rong's recommendation to Dong Zhuo, he became Administrator of Liaodong. He soon killed Xiangping Magistrate Gongsun Zhao to assert dominance and ruled his territory with strict laws. 
Gongsun Du conquered Fuyu, Gaogouli, Wuwan, and the Fushan bandits, developing a power base in Liaodong. 
Seeing the chaos in the central region, he appointed himself Marquis of Liaodong and Governor of Ping Province and gave his father the courtesy name of Jianyi Marquis. The ceremonies and items he employed were the same as those of an emperor. 
Cao Cao once appointed him General of Military Might and Marquis of Yongning but Gongsun Du looked down on these titles as he already saw himself as the emperor of Liaodong.

From Liaodong, You Province, Gongsun Kang was a warlord in the late Eastern Han. 
He succeeded his father Gongsun Du's position as Marquis of Liaodong. 
When Yuan Xi and Yuan Shang escaped to Liaodong after their defeat, Gongsun Kang was suspicious of the two. Seeing that Cao Cao had no intention of sending his army to Liaodong, Gongsun Kang killed the two and deliver their heads to Cao Cao to show him affinity. 
A few years after, Gongsun Kang invaded Gaogouli and seized their captial.

From Liaodong, You Province, Gongsun Gong was the brother of Gongsun Kang and the uncle of Gongsun Yuan. 
When Yuan Shang and Yuan Xi brothers submitted to Gongsun Kang, Gongsun Gong suggested Gongsun Kang to executed the two for Cao Cao. After Gongsun Kang died, Gongsun Gong succeeded his position. Cao Rui appointed him as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Xiangping Marquis. 
Gongsun Kang's second son, Gongsun Yuan, had both academic and military talents and was born militant. He overthrew and even prisoned Gongsun Kang, who was only released after Sima Yi conquered Liaodong.

A native of the State of Pei, the father of Ding Yi, and a courtier of the Eastern Han Dynasty. Because of the same hometown, he had his acquaintance with Cao Cao when he was an courtier. When Emperor Xian went east and Cao Cao got Yanzhou, Ding Chong specially wrote to Cao Cao, persuading him to take the opportunity to assist Emperor Xian. But Ding Chong drank too much alcohol and eventually died as a result.

A native of Shanyin, Huiji, an important official of Sun Wu. 
He was on the staff of the prince Sun He during the dispute between the two palaces, but fortunately he was not framed as Lu Xun was and was blamed by Sun Quan for many things. 
Later, Sun Huo and Sun Hao both valued Ding Gu, and after Sun Hao moved the capital, he asked Ding Gu to guard the old capital Jianye.

From Anfeng, Lujiang, Ding Feng Jr. was a general of Eastern Wu and the younger brother of Ding Feng Sr. 
In the Battle of Wei's Conquest of Shu, Ding Feng Jr. was sent to aid Shu Han. However, according to Xiangyang Records, Ding Feng Jr. 's army actually went to ambush Yongan in the attampt to gain a new territory for Eastern Wu when Shu Han fell. 
Shu General Luo Xian put up great resistance. After a few months, Sun Xiu sent the son of Lu Xun, Lu Kang, with 30, 000 soldiers, leading Luo Xian to surrender to Wei and asking the Wei army to repel the Wu army.

A native of Pei Guo's Jimmy County, an official of Cao Wei. 
He is a very talented and resourceful person, and he is also a native of Jimmy County with Cao Cao, so he has always been liked by Cao Cao. 
When Cao Cao and Ma Chao were at war in Tongguan, Cao Cao crossed the river to set up his camp and was attacked by Ma Chao on the way. 
However, Ding Fei's greed and love of money were reported repeatedly, and he was once impeached and dismissed from his post, but eventually Cao Cao reinstated Ding Fei to his original post.
A fictional character, daughter of Ding Yuan.
Younger brother of Ding Yi. He and his elder brother Ding Yi were friends with Cao Zhi, which was harted by Cao Pi. Thus, House Ding was exterminated after Cao Pi ascended the throne.
A fictional character, daughter of Cao Cao and Mrs Ding. Prototype or taken from the Princess Qinghe.

From Pei State, Ding Yi was a famous official. He had an illness in one eye which made him physically unattractive. 
Cao Cao originally wished to recruit Ding Yi and married Princess Qinghe to him but Cao Pi looked down on Ding Yi's appearance and thought Princess Qinghe should have married the son of Xiahou Dun. 
Learning about this, Ding Yi loathed Cao Pi in secret and chose to help Cao Zhi in the strife between the princes. However, Cao Zhi was a heavy drinker and a reckless man. In the end, Cao Cao chose Cao Pi as his successor. 
After Cao Pi became the emperor, he had Ding Yi and his entire family executed.

A native of Qiao County in the State of Pei, son of Ding Fei, and a courtier of Wei. Had a good friendship with Cao Shuang, and being recommended by Cao Shuang, he started to serve Emperor Ming of Wei. When Emperor Ming died, Cao Shuang and Sima Yi became the assistant ministers. Ding Mi, one of the followers of Cao Shuang, offered a plan to deprive Sima Yi of his real power. After Sima Yi forbore and refused to go to the court by pretending to be ill, Cao Shuang and his followers became more domineering. The other courtiers all abused him as a dog, showing the abundance of his bad deeds. However, Sima Yi finally initiated the Rebellion of Gaoping Mausoleum and regained his power. Cao Shuang, Ding Mi and their followers were all punished for the crime of treason with the death penalty of their clans.

A native of Danyang, and an official of Wu. There was not much records of him in the official history, and only the name was mentioned. He used to be a follower of Sun Deng (Sun Quan's prince). Later, when he went to Shu, he brought back Sima Hui's works on the prophecy.

A taoist in the Eastern Han Dynasty, and a native in Langya County. According to the historical records, there should be two individuals. The Yuji in the times of Emperor Shun of the Han Dynasty was rewarded the Scripture of the Great Peace. His apprentice Gong Chong presented the Scripture to the emperor, but did not receive much attention before his disappearance.
