There was another person named Yu Ji in Wuyue area during the Three Kingdoms period, who criticized Sun Ce for "Enjoying Undeserved Fame", which made Sun Ce furious and ordered his execution.

Yu Quan was a general of Wu. 
When Zhuge Dan of Wei rebelled in Shouchun, Yu Quan was one of the Wu generals who went to Zhuge Dan's aid. When the Wei army successfully broke through the defense in Shouchun and killed Zhuge Dan, Yu Quan refused to surrender. He unequipped his armor and shouted, "When a man of dignity is order to rescue someone, if he can't win and is defeated, that is something I can't accept." He then charged into the battlefield and died.

A subordinate of Liu Yao. The official history only recorded that he was ordered to guard Hengjiang against Sun Ce under Yuan Shu's command. In the romance, he was captured by Sun Ce soon after the engagement and was crushed to death.

A native of Jiaozhou, Guangxin. Shi Xie's brother. In the official history, it is only recorded that he was the governor of Nanhai, and there is no mention of him in the Romance of the Three Kingdoms.

A native of Fufeng County, a loyal official of the Eastern Han Dynasty. 
He worked with Wang Yun to kill Dong Zhuo. 
However, after the death of Dong Zhuo, Wang Yun was autocratic, so Shi Sun Rui refused to receive the merit of the marquis. 
Later, when Emperor Xian ran east, Shi Sun Rui was killed in the chaotic while trying to protect the Emperor.

Wang Yi was Inspector of Yi, Zhao Ang's wife. 
When Zhao Ang was Prefect of Qiangdao, her and their children stayed in Xicheng, where Liang Shuang rebelled. Wang Yi rubbed dirt on her and fasted to keep her dignity. 
With the revolt quelled, they went to Jicheng as he was reassigned. Ma Chao started a revolt, sieged Jicheng, and kept their son Zhao Yue hostage. The two pretended to comply to gain his trust. With Yang Fu and Jiang Xu, they lured him out of the city then closed the gates, cutting off his resources and repelled him. 
They took back Jicheng but Zhao Yue was killed. 
Their stories were documented in Lienu Zhuan, "From the crisis of Jicheng to Mt. Qi, Ang came up with 9 creative strategies with Yi's help." 
Dignified and strategic, she was a true heroine.

A native of Jiaozhou, Guangxin. Shi Xie's brother. He was invited by Ding Gong to join the court as an official, and soon fled to his hometown because of the Dong Zhuo's rebellion. After Zhu Fu, the governor of Jiaozhou, was killed, Shi Xie appointed Shi Yi as the governor of Hepu.
A fictional character, daughter of Shi Xie.

A native of Huai County, Henei, one of the seven sages of the bamboo grove. The eldest of the seven sages, who became obsessed with official careers, Ji Kang once broke off friendship with him. Then Ji Kang was executed by Luo Zhi for offending Sima's family, Zhonghui and other dignitaries. He entrust his son to Shan Tao.

A native of Xincai County, Yuzhou, an official of the Eastern Jin Dynasty. He was ordered to write history and was good at Yixue. He is also the author of "Sou Shen Ji", the originator of mystery novels.
Sun Jian's subordinates, the relevant records are only figures. When crusading Dong, Sun Jian let him do it, and ordered him to return to the state to supervise the army provisions.

A native of Liaodong, Xianping, Gongsun Kang's eldest son and Gongsun Yuan's brother. After the death of Gongsun Kang, Gongsun Gong succeeded to the throne. He sent Gongsun Huang to the court as a hostage. After Gongsun Yuan seized power, Gongsun Huang had to stay in the court. Later, Gongsun Yuan rebelled and Gongsun Huang was sentenced to death by association.
A fictional character, daughter of Gongsun Zan.

Gongsun Fan, a native of Liaoxi, You Province, was one of Gongsun Zan's cousins. 
In response to Gongsun Zan hoarding army in Panhe, Yuan Shao offered the stamp of Administrator of Bohai to Gongsun Fan in an attempt to win him over. However, Gongsun Fan immediately allied with Gongsun Zan and set his Bohai army to aid Gongsun Zan in defeating Qing and Xu's Yellow Turban armies. In the Battle of Jieqiao, he was defeated with Gongsun Zan and gave up Jicheng.

He was a native of Liaoxi, Youzhou, and the son of Gongsun tzann. 
When he was besieged by Yuan Shao in Yijing, he asked Zhang Yan, a Black Mountain bandit, for help and agreed to hold a fire to attack Yuan Shao's army. However, the letter was intercepted by Yuan Shao, who lured Gongsun's army out of the city, and Gongsun's army was defeated by an ambush and trapped in Yijing. In the end, Gongsun Zhan set himself on fire and was killed by Tu Ge.

From Donglai, Qing Province, Taishi Xiang was the son of the famous Wu general, Taishi Ci. 
As Taishi Ci passed away young, Sun Quan cherished and took good care of Taishi Xiang. 
Though Taishi Xiang's talent in battle was inferior than his father, he excelled at political affairs. He once settled the mountain tribes in the territory and assumed important positions such as Imperial Secretary, Administrator of Wu Commandery, before in the end landing the position of Colonel of Yue Cavalry.
A fictional character, daughter of Tiashi Chi.
A fictional character, daughter of Kong Zhou.

There is no such person in the official history, which is a fiction in The Romance of the Three Kingdoms. As Cao Cao's subordinate, responsible for guarding Dongling Pass. When Guan Yu rode alone for thousands of miles, Kong Xiu blocked Guan Yu from passing through due to his duties, and was killed by Guan Yu. He was also the first commander to be beheaded.

A native of Qufu, Lu County, he is a grandson of the twenty-first generation of Confucius. Since he was a descendant of Confucius, Cao Pi appointed him to preside over the ceremony of commemorating Confucius.

A native of Hanyang County, and an official of Wei. Ma Chao attacked Cao Cao twice, and Longyou fell. Yang Fu, Zhao Ang and others conspired against Ma Chao, and Yin Feng was also involved. Since then, Yin Feng was promoted to the governor of Dunhuang due to his merits, but he did not make any significant achievements during his tenure.

Yin Da Mu was a family servant of Cao who often served by the emperor's side. 
In the Incident at the Gaoping Tombs, he falsely believed Sima Yi and convinced Cao Shuang to surrender but Cao Shuang was killed by Sima Yi instead. 
Yin Da Mu then pretended to serve Sima Shi to avenge in secret. When Wenqin and Guanqiu Jian wished to rebel against Sima Shi, Yin Da Mu, knowing of Sima Shi's serious eye illness and didn't have long to live, hinted that Wenqin should delay the rebellion. However, Wenqin didn't understand him and reprimand Yin Da Mu instead, even trying to shoot him with an arrow. Yin Da Mu then left howling.

From Tianshui, Liangzhou, Yin Shang first served in Wei then submitted to Shu. 
In the Battle of Tianshui, he surrendered to Shu along with Jiang Wei and was fairly valued. 
In the Romance, before Zhuge Liang invaded Tianshui, he sent Jiang Wei, who already submitted to Shu, to send a letter with an arrow into the city to disturb the morale. As Yin Shang and Liang Xu were long-time friends with Jiang Wei, they were suspected by Administrator Ma Zhun. Being doubted, the two went ahead and surrendered to Shu, opening the gates to let the Shu army into Tianshui.

In some official history, it may be written as "Yin Lu". 
He was subordinate to Zang Ba, a Taishan thief. 
After Lu Bu's defeat, he surrendered to Cao Cao with Zang Ba. When Sun Quan turned against Wei, Zang Ba was ordered by Cao Ren to go on an expedition, but was defeated by Sun Wu's Quan Zong and Xu Shan, and Yin Li was killed by Quan Zong in the battle.

A native of Linjiang, Ba County. Originally an official of Shu, and then used by Wei and the Western Jin Dynasty. When he was young, he studied under Qiao Zhou and was recruited by Fei Yi as an official. After the downfal of Shu, he followed Liu Chan to the court. After Sima Yan ascended to the throne, he admired Wen Li and repeatedly promoted. Wen Li wanted to return to his hometown, but he was retained by Sima Yan.

From Qiao Commandery, Yu Province, Wen Hu was the son of Wen Qin and the younger brother of Wen Yang. 
When Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin rebelled against Sima Shi, the two follow their father to war. Upon defeat, they sought refuge in Eastern Wu with their father. 
Later, Wen Qin was involved killed by Zhuge Dan for certain reasons. Wen Hu then went back to submit to Wei with his brother, Wen Yang. 
However, loathing Wen Yang for betrying Zhuge Dan, Sima Yao framed Wen Yang for rebelling, leading to Wen Yang and his family being executed and Wen Hu was therefore killed as well.
A fictional character, daughter of Wen Qin.
A fictional character, daughter of Wen Chou.

Wen Yang, from Qiao County, Pei State, was Wen Qin's second son. 
His father and him participated in Guanqiu Jian's rebellion and he raided bravely, leading to the aggravation of Sima Shi's eye illness. Wen Qin and his son were later repelled by Deng Ai and escaped to Wu but Sima Shi also died on the return of victory. 
Zhuge Dan then started a rebellion too. Wen Yang, his father and brother were ordered to lead the reinforcements. However, Zhuge Dan killed Wen Qin, whom he had issues with. Wen Yang and Wen Hu had to submit to Sima Zhao. 
In Jin, he was famed for a winning against Xianbei tribes. But he was ousted as Emperor Wu of Jin, Sima Yan, didn't favor him. Though appointed again, when Sima Yao, the Duke of Dong'an, falsely accused him of rebellion, Wen Yang was executed.

A fictional character in the Romance of Three Kingdoms, Fang Yue was a great general under Wang Kuang, Administrator of Henei. When the coalition against Dong was stopped by Lu Bu in HuLao Gate, Fang Yue stepped up to challenge Lu Bu. After a few rounds, he was killed by Lu Bu.

A native of Hedong, Wenxi, Wuqiu Dian's daughter, and her grandfather is Wuqiu Jian. After Wuqiu Jian was defeated, three generations of his family was killed, but because his mother's Xun family has the marriage relation with the Sima family, he escaped, which affected the modification of the implication penalty.

From Wenxi, Hedong, Guanqiu Dian was the eldest son of Guanqiu Jian. 
When Sima Shi monopolized state power and replaced Cao Fang with Cao Mao as the new Wei emperor, Guanqiu Dian advised his father that he should rebel against Sima Shi to practice justice for the kingdom. 
Before his father went to battle, Guanqiu Dian took the family to Mt. Ling in Xinan but they were captured and killed by Sima Shi's army.

A native of Nanzhong, Jianning, Shu Han and Western Jin official. During the Jiaozhi rebellion, he went out with the army, and later resisted the Wu army's invasion several times, had a couple of victories. In the end, they were defeated by the generals of Wu, Yu Si and Tao Huang. Because of Xiu Yun's persistence, they were cut belly and heart to death.
Local people of Henei County and official of Wei. Became highly respected due to his daughter as the empress of Cao Rui, who was the Emperor Ming of Wei.

Niu Fu was the son-in-law of Dong Zhuo and General of the Household. 
After Dong Zhuo was killed, he led the remaining forces to attack Chang'an in an attempt to avenge his father-in-law. Lu Bu sent Li Su in response and was greatly defeated as Niu Fu ambushed their camp at night. 
Later, chaos broke out in Niu Fu's camp. Falsely believing there had been a mutiny, he fled with all his valuables. However, Huchi'er, Niu Fu's close subordinate, coveted his valuables so he killed him and then sent his head to Chang'an.
A native of Qi, Guanghan, Shu Han Commander. When Zhuge Liang crusaded to south , he was transferred to the post of Yizhou Governor, but was killed by barbarians on his way to his post.

An official of the Eastern Han Dynasty, As Commandant and Assistant General of Yueqi. He and Dong Cheng and Wu Shuo were conspired to get rid of Cao Cao under the edict of Emperor Xian of the Han Dynasty. But the message leaked out, was noticed by Cao Cao, and was killed.

General under Dong Zhuo. The official history only mentions that he responded to Li Jue and Guo Si after Dong Zhuo's death and surrounded Chang'an. 
In "The Evolution", he opened the gates of Chang'an to allow Li Jue, Guo Si, Fan Chou and Zhang Ji to enter the city. In the end, Ma Tang rose to serve the king and was killed by Ma Chao.

From Linyi, Langya, Wang Rong was one of the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove. 
Wang Rong was one of the Seven Sages and preferred the Qingtan school. He was devoted to political affairs like another one of the Seven Sages, Shan Tao. Among the Seven Sages, he was seen as the one after fame the most as well as a stingy person. 
He participated in Jin's Conquest of Wu as General Who Establishes Might and invaded Wuchang.

A native of Langya, Linyi, an official of the Eastern Jin Dynasty, the elder brother of the power minister Wang Dun. Because Wang Han supported Wang Dun, he held a high position during the Wang Dun Rebellion. He was ignorant and violent, greedy, and was disreputable.

Liu Xun's wife. Because Wang Song had no children and there was the new love Sima, he planned to divorce his wife and marry with Sima. Wang Song left sadly and composed two poems on the road. Cao Pi also chanted poems on this matter.

From Guanghan, Yi Province, Wang Fu was originally Liu Zhang's subordinate before he served for Shu Han. 
In Battle of Yiling, he followed Liu Bei on a campaign against Wu and was killed in Zigui. 
In the Romance, he was a marshal under Guan Yu. Before Guan Yu attacked Fancheng, he was ordered to build beacon towers along Yangtze River. He suggested the governor-general of Jing Province to be replaced by the dignified Zhao Lei but Guan Yu rejected the idea. 
Later, Lu Meng stealthily crossed the river and occupied Jing Province, forcing Guan Yu to escape to Maicheng. Guan Yu and his son tried to escape while Wang Fu and Zhou Cang decided to guard Maicheng with their lives. Upon hearing about the death of Guan Yu and his son, he committed suicide by jumping off the city wall.

Was the Inspector of Jizhou of the Emperor Ling of the Eastern Han Dynasty , and he tried to abolish the Emperor Ling of the Han and set up Hefei Hou. However, because the Emperor Ling withdrew his military power, Wang Fen's actions were unsuccessful and committed suicide.

Claiming to be a god of Luoyang County in Linhai, he was named the King of Luoyang in the Eastern Wu Dynasty by Sun Quan, and he often predicted droughts and floods. Before Sun Quan passed away, he went missing.

A subordinate of Gongsun Yuan. Gongsun Yuan rebelled against Wei and set up as Yan Emperor himself , Sima Yi led troops to crusade and defeated Gongsun Yuan. Gongsun Yuan sent Wang Jian and Liu Fu to sue for peace, but both were beheaded by Sima Yi.

A native of Jiyin, and an official of Wei official. He was promoted by Cao Cao at the beginning, and he was quite famous for his practice of writing and respecting the worthy. But in his later years he was irritable and self-willed, which was disgusted by people of the time.

A native of Tan, Donghai County, the younger brother of Wang Yuanji. Knowing Confucian Classics, and established schools, promoted the Five Classics of Confucianism. Although he was a powerful relative of the Western Jin Dynasty, he was integrity and never went beyond the rules.

From Jinyang, Taiyuan, Wang Chang was a Wei general and Wang Hun's father. 
As the political turmoil in Eastern Wu ended, with Lu Xun dead and Zhu Ju exiled, Wang Chang suggested that they attacked Wu and achieved victory. 
After Sun Quan passed, Sima Shi waged a war against Eastern Wu again and ordered Wang Chang to lead the army. But Wu forces attacked first and the Wei vanguard in Dongxing was defeated, forcing Wang Chang to retrest. 
Wang Chang also assisted in settling the rebellion by Guanqiu Jian, Wen Qin, and Zhuge Dan in Shouchun. 
Other than his military performances, in his early days, he served as a tutor to Prince Cao Pi. He had also written Discussion on Governance and Military Book to the Wei imperial court in the hopes to change the overly strict laws in Cao Wei.
A fictional character, daughter of Wang Yun.

Nephew of the Later Han Dynasty's Senior Minister Wang Yun. He was close with Sima Lang and Jia Kui. When Wang Yun was killed by Li Jue, he escaped to his birth-place. Appointed prime minister by Cao Cao, he later became the inspector of Yan Province after Cao Pi's ascension. He contained Sun Quan with Zhang Liao and gained renown on the front lines against Wu. He plotted against Sima Yi, but the plan was discovered and he was forced to commit suicide.

Legend has it that she was nine years old, with supernatural powers. She was very beautiful and good at singing and dancing. Cao Pi once wanted to marry her, but the ending was unknown. In addition, Wangsun is compound surname.
The characters appearing in the book "Hua Guan Suo zhuan", both martial arts and beauty, after losing to Guan Suo, she and her sister married to Guan Suo together.

A native of Jiaxing, Wu County. When Sun Ce defeated Yan Baihu, Wang Sheng assisted Yan Baihu. After Wang Sheng was defeated and taken prisoner, he was saved from death because of his friendship with Sun Jian and his wife.
The characters appearing in the book "The Story of Hua Guan Suo", both martial arts and beauty, and her sister Wang Yue, after losing to Guan Suo, married Guan Suo together.

A native of Qingzhou Plain, one of the celebrities. He worshiped the great scholar Chen Shi as his teacher, and then returned to his hometown to establish school, which made the county determined to learn. During Dong Zhuo's rebellion, he avoided trouble in Liaodong and won the trust of Gongsun Du. Later, Cao Cao admired his talents and recruited Wang Lie into the court many times.

A native of Shangdang county, famous alchemist in the Eastern Han Dynasty. He created the method of fetal rest and health preservation, Cao Cao once called him and saw that his youthful appearance, showed that he was an extraordinary person, so ordered him to take charge of the alchemists.

A native of Guanghan, Liu Zhang subordinate. His talents and learning are well-known in the county, and even Jingxiang scholars knew him. Liu Zhang admired him and hired him to serve as an official. Routinely persuade Liu Zhang, once persuaded Liu Zhang to beware of Ma Chao's ambition and not to form an alliance with him.

A native of Yizhou, successively subordinated to Shu, Wei and Western Jin Dynasties. During the Jiaozhi rebellion , he was ordered to support Lu Xing, who rebelled against Wu, to appease the three counties of Jiaozhi. After that, he stayed there and fought with Eastern Wu several times, winning each other. In the end, Wu general Tao Huang took down Jiaozhi, and Wang Su was captured.

A native of Qucheng in Donglai, an Officer of State of Wei. When the Sima Shi conquered Wu Qiujian, he accompanied as Overseer. He recommended that the Nandun City should be obtained first, and then Wu Qiujian would be defeated smoothly. Recruited Sima Zhao as a general of Zhennan, participated in the suppression of Zhuge Dan, beheaded Zhu Yi and Tang Zi, and finally smashed into Shouchun City with Sima Zhao's army to pacify the rebellion.

A native of Qi, Guanghan. Successively subordinated to the Shu, Wei, and Western Jin Dynasty. There are often sharp criticisms of the monarchs and ministers of the Shu Han, and there is deep cherishment and regret for the Shu Han in the words.

From Linyi, Langya, Wang Xiang was an official of Wei and later served in West Jin. 
Famous for filial piety and dignity, he was the main character of He Lay on Ice in Search of Carp in the Twenty-four Filial Exemplars. Though he had no extraordinary military and political performances, he was still greatly admired by Sima Yan for his virtuous and noble personality until old age.

Official of Shu and negotiator. He repeatedly warned Zhuge Liang against leading an expedition south, but to no avail. He joined Shu during Liu Zhang's reign and became Zitong's minister. After the stabilization of Yi Province, he was entrusted the role of county magistrate and established an administration. He would later oversee the production and trade of salt and iron as the Colonel of Salt, greatly increasing the nation's revenue.

Because of his appearance resembling Zhuge Liang's son Zhuge Zhan, he counterfeited Zhuge Zhan's name and conspired in Jiangyuan and Linqiong, Shu County. But the rebels were defeated by Li Gao and Wang Fu was captured alive.

A native of Shanyang County. Was a famous Confucianist and Yi scholar of Wei, whose notes on the Book of Changes and Tao Te Ching had far-reaching influence. It is famous all over the world with his eloquence, and also knew the rhythm of music. But because he was arguable and often made fun of others with his superiors, he was disgusted by many scholar-officials.

There is no such person in official history, but a fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms". For Cao Cao's Xingyang Governor. Guan Yu rode solo for thousands of miles, Wang Zhi intended to murder Guan Yu, but was killed by Guan Yu.

From Jinyang, Taiyuan, Wang Hun served under Cao Wei and West Jin. 
He was in multiple battles against Eastern Wu and scored many military merits. In the Conquest of Wu, he led his army down from Heng River and sent his subordinates to kill Wu officials such as Zhang Ti and Sun Zhen, to the shock of the people of Wu. The Wu Lord Sun Hao sent an envoy to surrender soon after. 
However, he framed Wang Jun multiple times as the two fought over the merit of the conquest of Wu and was mocked for it. Wang Hun's reputation suffered as a result.

A native of Jinyang, Taiyuan, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. Taciturn, so most people in the world think he is foolish, but in fact, he was talented and restrained, and also had the skill of the horse. Later, the Emperor Wu of the Jin Dynasty learned of it and praised it as "below Shan Tao and above Wei Shu."

From Tan County, Donghai, Wang Su was the son of Wang Lang, the father of Wang Yuan Ji, and a great official of Cao Wei. 
He repeatedly appealed to the palace to prioritize settling the subjects and lifting severe punishments. He also advocated austerity and discouraged the large-scale construction of the palace. 
When Guanqiu Jian rebelled, Wang Su advised Sima Shi to lead the army himself soon before the rebel army infiltrated their forces and that the rebels' morale would be low since they still had families within the territory. 
Wang Su was also a great Confucian scholar of his time and his annotations on the 6 classics greatly influenced future scholars.

A native of Henei County, and an official of Wei. When he was lonely and poor, he became a slave, but he was tireless in learning. Yang Jun repeatedly supported him because of his love for talents, and bought a house for him to marry his wife. Wang Xiang was highly appreciated by Cao Pi because of his talents in the new generation of Wei. Wang Xiang has a handsome literary style, a gentle and generous personality, and a great deal of kindness. He had recommended benefactor Yang Jun to Cao Pi several times, but because Yang Jun recommended Cao Zhi to Cao Cao in the past years, Cao Pi had a long-term hatred. Later, when Yang Jun was implicated in prison for some reason, Wang Xiang pleaded with Cao Pi, splattered blood on his head, and Cao Pi refused. After Yang Jun died, Wang Xiang died of depression.

Officer of Shu. His treatment of the Qiang convinced them to submit to Shu, bringing peace to Shu's northern boundary. Because of this, when Jiang Wei campaigned to the north, the Qiang supplied the army with woolen goods and grains. When Wang Si is killed from a stray arrow during the campaign, thousands of Qiang attended his burial.

Staff officer of Lu Bu. When Cao Cao sieged Xiapi, marriage talks between Lu Bu's daughter and Yuan Shu's son were revisited, and Wang advised Lu Bu to ask Yuan Shu for reinforcements. He went to visit Yuan Shu with Xu Si and they managed to strike a deal that reinforcements would be provided after Lu Bu sent his daughter; however, they could not send her and they did not get their reinforcements.
A fictional character. There is no such person in history and romance.

From Qinghe Commandery, Ji Province, Wang Jing was a great official of Cao Wei. 
As Inspector of Yong Province, he resisted Jiang Wei's invasion to the Hanzhong region. Wang Jing was defeated and retreated to guard Didao. The crisis was averted when Deng Ai came to his aid. 
When Wang Jing served as Master of Writing, Emperor Shao of Wei, Cao Mao, secretly planned to banish Sima Zhao. Wang Jing tried to stop him but Cao Mao refused. Later, Sima Zhao executed Wang Jing and his mother for he didn't inform him of the secret attack.

From Donglai Commandery, Wang Qi was a general of Wei. 
When guarding the Northeastern border, he followed Guanqiu Jian on the conquest against Gaogouli and was requested to seek food supplies from Buyeo. He later served as the Administrator of Fang Commandery, during which he mediated the conflicts between Wakoku Queen Himiko and Kuna-koku King Himikoko. 
In Wei's Conquest of Shu, as the Administrator of Tianshui Commandery, Wang Qi was dispatched by Deng Ai. Though he wasn't one of the main forces, he still scored some military merits. He served as the Administrator of Runan in the end.

A native of Yingling County, Beihai. An official of Wei, and the son of Wang Xiu. Upright, Sima Shi and Sima Zhao were defeated in the battle of Dongguan. Wang Yi angered Sima Zhao and was killed because he claimed that the defeat was in Sima Zhao.

A native of Qixian County, Taiyuan. An official of Wei, and the son of Wang Ling, he is known for his knowledge. After Gao Pingling's rebellion, Wang Ling and his nephew Linghu Yu conspired to overturned the Sima family and set up the King of Chu, Cao Biao. However, at the beginning, Wang Guang was accused by others, and Wang Guang was implicated and killed.

The legendary female immortal. During Emperor Ming Dynasty, the daughter of Wang Gang, the gate Commandant. Wang Lulian saw his father gain the Dao, and since then aspired to cultivating the Dao. In Lu Shenshan, the immortal taught her the method of ascension, and she ascended in the day after he completed her practice.

Born in Linyi, Langya County, he was the Inspector of Jingzhou in the late Eastern Han Dynasty. During the period of crusading Dong, because of Cao Yin's fake official call, or Sun Jian deliberately did it, he died unjustly at the hands of Sun Jian. Later the Eastern Han Dynasty court appointed Liu Biao as Jingzhou herd.

A native of Lujiang, Eastern Wu officials. He is good at astronomical calendar calculation, once made the armillary sphere, and wrote "Qianxiang Calendar". In political affairs, he served as an envoy to the Shu Han and Western Jin Dynasty several times. However, Sun Hao was killed by Sun Hao because of his uprightness and treacherous remarks.

A native of Han Jia, served for Liu Yan, Liu Zhang, Liu Bei. Although there are few records in official history, both Liu Zhang and Liu Bei were think highly of him. When Jiang Wan asked Zhang Xiu to recommend talents in the later period of the Shu Han Dynasty, he still enjoyed a high reputation.

A native of Hu, Hongnong County, a general of the Jin Dynasty. Wang Jun was knowledgeable, open-minded and ambitious, but he was also criticized for his extravagance and indiscretion. He was valued by Yanghu, saying: "Jun has great talents, and he will do what he wants, and he can be used." After Wang Jun was ordered to build a ship, the Jin dynasty navy army was prosperous. In the fifth year of Xianning, he wrote a letter to the Eastern Wu and went down to Xiling, Xiakou, and Wuchang, and went straight to Nanjing, defeated Sun Hao.

A native of Linyi, Langxie, is the half-brother of famous Wang Xiang in "Twenty-Four Filial Piety". He has a deep love with his elder brother. He has served in Wei and Western Jin Dynasty, and is famous for his high moral character. Later generations Wang Dao and Wang Dun were the important ministers of the Eastern Jin Dynasty.

Retainer of Wei. Summoned by Cao Cao, he served as county magistrate for various regions, and formed an administration. Served as an official for both Cao Pi and Cao Rui, bolstering the defenses against the Xianbei and setting a good example of fairness to others. Later on, he would hold several high-ranking positions.

Staff officer of Wei. After vexing Cao Pi and imprisoned for being a fool, he changed his name to Linghu Yu. After prison, he rose steadily through the ranks, and Cao Shuang assigned him Yan Province Inspector. When Cao Shuang fell from grace and Sima Yi took over, Linghu Yu plotted with his uncle Wang Ling to oust Cao Fang and put Cao Biao on the throne. He died of illness before acting, and this revealed the plan. Wang Ling and the Linghu family were killed.

It was originally Shu general. When Jiang Wei expedition Wei, he was ordered to build a city and stick to it. But Chen Tai, a Wei general, used a scheme to cut off the food route and make him surrendered. When Zhong Hui crusaded Shu, he joined the war as Wei general.

A native of Hanchang, Brazil, he was a great general in the late middle period of the Shu Han Dynasty. Little is recorded in history, only mentioning that Jiu Fu was ranked alongside Wang Ping, Zhang Yi and Liao Hua, and his achievements were only slightly inferior to Wang Ping.

A native of Yuzhou, Pei state. A commander of Wei. His deeds can only be seen in "Wei Lue". When he was young, he followed Cao Cao and had the chivalrous style, but he was cautious and famous for his loyalty and bravery. Cao Cao let him to take charge of the guards or serve as the Overseer, which shows that he trusts him very much. He once crusaded Sui Gu followed the generals of Cao Cao, and he also had military exploits in the battle of Guandu, but there were few records.

The son of Emperor Wu of Jin and the younger brother of Emperor Hui of Jin. One of the princes and kings in the Eight Kings Rebellion, Sima Yi tended to be loyal to the court compared with the other careerists, resisting Sima Yan, Sima Yong, and Sima Ying successively. Although Sima Yi is in power, he is not arbitrary, accepting the courtier's proposal, and tries to reconcile with Sima Ying on his own initiative in order to settle the world. But Sima Ying asked to kill several ministers, Sima Yi refused, and fought. Sima Yi insisted on defending the capital. Although there was a famine in the city, the soldiers were united and morale remained high. However, Sima Yue misjudged the situation and asked Emperor Hui to issue an edict to seize Sima Yi's military power, imprisoned in Jinyong City, and died by fire a few days later.

The tenth son of Sima Yan. He is known for his loyalty and courage. After King of Zhao Sima Lun abolished Jia Nanfeng, he allowed his confidant Sun Xiu to dominate. Sima Yun knew that Sima Lun intended to usurp, saying that he was not in the wrong direction. Sima Lun was afraid of Sima Yun, who held the military power of the Forbidden Army, and changed him to the title of Taiwei, hoping to seize military power. Sima Yun was furious and led his troops to surround Zhao Palace. Emperor Hui of Jin sent Fu Yin to fight, but Fu Yin and Sima Qian, Sima Lun's son were better off, deceived Sima Yun with a false edict, and assassinated him when he was not prepared.

From Wen County, Henei Commandery, Sima Fu was the third younger brother of Sima Yi and a great official of Cao Wei. 
When young, he was studious and well read. For his literary knowledge, he was summoned by Cao Zhi. 
Sima Fu was loyal to Cao Wei his whole life. When Wei Emperor Shao Cao Mao was assassinated, no official dared to come close except for Sima Fu, who guarded his body, wept, and requested the murder to be investigated multiple times. 
When Sima Yan replaced Wei with Jin Dynasty, though Sima Yan was in a high position, he still claimed to be a subject of Wei and demanded to be buried as one when he passed.

A native of Wen County, Henei. An official of Wei. Sima Zhi's son, quite like a father, is just and good at governing prisons. However, because he accused the power minister Cao Shuang's partisan Deng Shao of unfair law enforcement, he worried that Deng Shao would retaliate in the future, saying that he was sick and resigned. He died of illness shortly afterwards, at the age of only thirty-five.

Mild-mannered and talented, Sima You was Emperor Wu of Jin, Sima Yan's brother and adopted by Sima Shi, Emperor Jing. 
As Sima Yan became Emperor, Sima You was appointed Prince of Qi. He assisted with political and military affairs and treated his subjects kindly. 
When Sima Yan empowered his imperial clan, Sima You opposed it, worried the princes would be overpowered but he was ignored. This led to the War of the Eight Princes. 
After eliminating Wu, Emperor Wu's got ill. The officials hoped to make Sima You the heir but Xun Xu, Feng Dan, and other close officials of Sima Yan advised Emperor Wu to send Sima You back to the vassal state. Sima You fell ill from worry. 
The emperor doctor, conjecturing Sima Yan's will, claimed that he had no illness, leading to Sima You's death.

A native of Wen County, Henei, a civil official of the Eastern Han Dynasty, he has eight sons, Sima Lang and Sima Yi, who are called "Sima Bada". One said it was named Fang. As Jingzhaoyin once recommended the fledgling Cao Cao as the northern lieutenant of Luoyang. Cao Cao promote to Queen of Wei in his later years and invited Sima Fang to drink. He also mentioned it as a pleasure.

Official of Wei. He was promoted when Cao Cao conquered Jingzhou, performing many a great work and climbing to the post of Henan magistrate. His rule was just and fair, especially to the weak, and his fame reached far. He became the Grand Minister of Agriculture during Cao Rui's age, where his declarations on the importance of agriculture won him trust.

The son of Sima Yi, one of the princes of the Eight Kings Rebellion. Before Emperor Wu of Jin died, relative Yang Jun and Sima Liang were appointed as auxiliary ministers, but Yang Jun wanted to take over the power and eradicate Sima Liang, but he was first eliminated by Jananfeng and Sima Wei , king of Chu. After that, Ja Nanfeng used Sima Liang as Regent. Because Sima Liang was fear of Sima Wei holding a heavy soldier in his hand and wanted to seize his military power, Jian Nanfeng saw it through and made the preemptive strike, let Emperor Hui issued an edict against Sima Liang and ordered Sima Wei to send soldiers to arrest him. Sima Liang consciously had a clear conscience, and he was captured, but Sima Wei used a heavy profit to make the soldiers kill Sima Liang.

The third son of Emperor Wu of Jin, Sima Yan. Benevolent and reticent, but gifted with an extraordinary retentive memory, he is quite fond of Sima Yan. After Emperor Hui came to the throne, Ja Nanfeng ruled, Sima Jian Mingzhe kept his nose clean, away from power struggles and was spared.

The nine son of Sima Yi, usurped the throne as the third emperor of the Western Jin Dynasty. Unbearable, terrible ambition. After overthrowing Ja Nanfeng, he tried to emulate the actions of his father and brother on behalf of Wei. Soon after forged Emperor Hui of Jin abdicated, which was despised by people at that time. The irony said: "The mink is insufficient, the dog's tail continues." After Sima Lun usurped the throne, Sima Jiong of Qi, Sima Ying of Chengdu, Sima Yong of Hejian, Sima Yi of Changshan rose up against Sima Lun, and Sima Lun was finally defeated and killed. The Eight Kings Rebellion also officially kicked off, and the power of the Western Jin Dynasty declined rapidly. The Eight Kings Rebellion, and even the next five barbarian tribes chaos, all broke out because of his usurpation of the throne.

The clan of the Western Jin Dynasty. Modest and thrifty, he has a reputation. Although he holds the military power and is in a high position, he did not intervene in the Eight Kings Rebellion, and at the same time, did not act to stabilize the chaos.

From Wen, Henei, Sima Lang was Sima Fang's eldest son and Sima Yi's elder brother. 
He was courteous, insightful, and valued simplicity. 
As Dong Zhuo came to the capital, Sima Lang foresaw the upcoming chaos so he returned to his hometown and advised his family to leave Henei to avoid the disaster. And the situation developed as Sima Lang predicted. 
During Jian'an years, grateful for Sima Fang's past recommendation, Cao Cao recruited Sima Lang as an official. As an official, Sima Lang was famous for being kind to his subjects and adopted beneficial policies. 
Later, in Jian'an Year 22, on a conquest against Sun Wu with Xiahou Dun, a disease broke out in the army and Sima Lang visited the camp and treated the sick himself. But he therefore contracted the disease and passed.
A native of Wen County, Henei, the clan of the Western Jin Dynasty. Known for his simplicity and lack of desire, he did not participate in the Eight Kings Rebellion.

Emperor Hui of Jin, son of Emperor Wu of Jin. It is generally believed that his aptitude is poor, and even ignorant. Later Wang Fuzhi even commented on him as a "Tu Mu Ou Ren." Emperor Wu was worried that Emperor Hui of Jin would be unbearable, and he was tested many times, but under the advice of his advisers, such as Crown Princess Jia Nanfeng and counselor Zhang Hong, he was successfully deceived Emperor Wu. However, the disadvantages became obvious after he came to the throne, unable to deal with politicians, Jia Nanfeng took power, and when Emperor Wu let the princes expand their influence, the Eight Kings Rebellion occurred, and the Western Jin Dynasty also quickly declined. Suspected of being poisoned by Sima Yue, king of the East Sea. Someone once reported to him that the people had no grain to eat because of the famine. Emperor Hui of Jin asked, "Why not eat meat?" He became a model of the faint emperor, and even his posthumous name "Hui" was later regarded as a genus of the faint emperor. Most emperors in the past avoid using it.

An imperial prince of West Jin, Sima Wang was originally the second son of Sima Fu and was adopted by Sima Lang. 
He was talented and favored by Cao Mao. Cao Mao then appointed him as General Who Attacks the West, who guarded the Guanzhong region and resisted Shu General Jiang Wei's invasion multiple times. 
After the fall of Shu and Jin replaced Wei, he was ordered to guard the Jiangxia region against Eastern Wu. 
Sima Wang was lenient and excelled at leading armies but he had been criticized for being a miser.

The son of Emperor Wu of Jin and the younger brother of Emperor Hui of Jin. One of the princes in the Eight Kings Rebellion, is brothers with Changsha King Sima Yi. First conspired with Jian Nanfeng to take down Yang Jun, the relative and power minister, and then killed Sima Liang. However, because he held great power, for establishing prestigeand, he killed Sima Liang and other ministers and princes, which caused Ja Nanfeng's fear. So he captured and killed Sima Wei for forging Sima Liang's handwritting and killed Sima Liang and Wei Guan, and the crime of hatch a sinister plot.
A fictional character, daughter of Sima Yi.

The son of Emepror Hui of Jin, Sima Zhong. After Emperor Hui of Jin ascended the throne, he was enrolled as the crown prince. He was extremely intelligent when he was a child, and he was even favored by Emperor Wu of Jin, Sima Yan. Somebody said that the reason why Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne is Emperor Wu placed great hopes on Sima Ju. However, as Sima Hu grew older and abandoned his studies, Sima Yu's deeds became more and more out of order due to the deliberate promotion of Jian Nanfeng. After Jiananfeng saw that the time was right, Emperor Hui issued an edict to abolish Sima Yu as a common man. In the end, Sima Lun, the king of Zhao, was fighting for power with Jiananfeng, made Jiananfeng to kill Sima Yu, and then under the name of avengeing the Crown Prince to suppress Jia Nanfeng.

The clan of the Western Jin Dynasty, the son of Sima Yi. Clever, filial piety, and have both ability and political integrity. Governing all places will let the rulers prosper and the people will return to their hearts. After the establishment of the country in the Western Jin Dynasty, he was appointed as the general of Zhenxi, the military governors of Yong and Liang Zhuzhou. During this period, the leader of the Xianbei tribe's leader Tufa Shujineng rebelled several times, and was defeated by Sima Jun. Tufa Jishuneng knew that he could not resist, and surrendered together with the heads of the tribes, and sent his son to the court. Sima Jun not only surrendered Xianbei, but also surrendered more than two hundred thousand Qianghu.

The clan of the Jin Dynasty, the father of Sima Rui, the founding monarch of the Eastern Jin Dynasty, Emperor Yuan. There is not much about his life in the history books. He married Xiahou Guangji as his wife and gave birth to Sima Rui. In order to discredit the legitimacy of the Eastern Jin court, the Northern Dynasties adopted the saying that "Niu Ji Ma Hou" in the current prophecy "Xuan Shi Tu", claiming that Sima Rui was born of Xiahou Guangji and Niu Jin's adultery.

A native of Linzi, the sister of Zuo Si, was named a concubine by Emperor Wu of Jin, Sima Yan, to Guiren. Only outstanding scholarship, but not good looking. Although Emperor Wu did not favor Zuo Fen, but he respected her very much and often talked about literature with her. Zuo Fen was good at writing fu, people thought that her literary talent was comparable to Fusheng Sima Xiangru.
A native of Linzi, he was the official of Wei and Western Jin Dynasty, the father of Zuo Si and Zuo Fen.

She was the wife of Liu Bei and the birth mother of Liu Zen. 
Her name was Mei in the local chronicles compiled in later times. When Liu Bei was in Xiaopei, he took Gan as his concubine. As Liu Bei's previous wives died or were separated, he was honored as his wife.
A fictional character, daughter of Tian Feng.

Served in Wei, Western Jin Dynasty. There are not many records, most of them went on the expedition as partial generals, and participated in the battle of Wei destroyed Shu, and the battle of fighting for Tufa Shujineng in the Western Jin Dynasty.

Officer of Wei. Originally served Liu Bei, but had to return home to support his aged mother. He later served Gongsun Zan. After Gongsun is killed, he goes on to serve Cao Cao and Wei. He proved himself a capable officer and advanced quickly, earning much fame. He was especially well-known for his defeat of the Wuhuan King, Gu Jin. During Zhuge Liang's 5th Northern Campaign, he aided in the defense of Xiangyang.

Tian Chou was from Wuzhong, Youbeiping. 
He first served under Liu Yu, Governor of You, and was later called to the palace. When he returned, Liu Yu had been killed by Gongsun Zan. 
Unwilling to work for the latter, he took his family to Mt. Xuwu to live in seclusion. He started a school, which attracted both the commoners and tribal people from Wuwan and Xianbei. 
As Yuan Shao rose to power, he tried to recruit Tian Chou but in vain. Only in Cao Cao's conquest of Wuwan did he serve as the guide for the army and helped them win the Battle of Mt. White Wolf. 
For his contribution, Cao Cao tried to recruit him, even sending Xiahou Dun, Tian Chou's friend, to persuade him but all offers were turned down. In the end, Tian Chou only accepted the counsellor title of no authority.

From Wuzhong, Youbeiping, Tian Xu was the grand-nephew of Tian Chou, an official of Eastern Han. 
After Cao Pi became Emperor, he wished to honor Tian Chou for his noble character but he had no offspirng. So he awarded Tian Xu, Tian Chou's grand-nephew, the title of a Secondary Marquis. 
Tian Xu participated in Wei's Conquest against Shu. 
The Book of Jin documented Tian Xu as Deng Ai's subordinate and was a part of the ambush in Yinping Path, where he disobeyed Deng Ai by refusing to advance and was therefore insulted by Deng Ai. However, in the Records of the Three Kingdoms about Zhong Kuai, Tian Xu was portrayed as Zhong Kuai's subordinate and part of Wei's army against Jiang Wei in Peicheng, who pursued Jiang Wei after they invaded the city.

From Shangyong, Yi Province, Shen Dan was the elder brother of Shen Yi. Originally a Wei Cao general, he submitted to Shu at one point before returning to Cao Wei once more. 
Originally a local leader in the Shangyong region who submitted to Cao Cao, he was defeated by Meng Da and Liu Feng and surrendered to Liu Bei, who appointed him General Who Attacks the North of the 4 attack generals. 
After the defeat and death of Guan Yu, as Meng Da and his brother, Shen Yi, both defected from Shu, after evaluation, Shen Dan chose to submit to Wei Cao. However, Cao Pi deemed him untrustworthy for his unpredictability and didn't favor him.

From Shangyong, Yi Province, Shen Yi was Shen Dan's brother. Originally a Wei general, he submitted to Shu once before returning to Wei again. 
Originally a local leader in the Shangyong region who submitted to Cao Cao, he was defeated by Meng Da and Liu Feng and surrendered to Liu Bei. 
After the defeat and death of Guan Yu, he defected from Shu to Wei with Meng Da, defeating Liu Feng before his defection and therefore appointed a marquis. However, Meng Da and him turned against each other over the position of the Administrator of Eastern Commanderies. Later, when Meng Da tried to rebel, Shen Yi immediately reported him to Sima Yi. 
After Meng Da was killed, Sima Yi condemned Shen Yi for forging a seal and the latter was arrested. No document of him was found later.

From Nanpi, Bohai, Shi Bao served under Cao Wei and West Jin. He was a metal vendor in the early years before being scouted by Sima Yi. He never held back his advice, correcting powerful officials such as Cao Shuang and his underlings. 
In the Battle of Dongxing, Wei suffered a great defeat. Many retreating soldiers died as no one was in command but only Shi Bao's army retreated safely. Shi Bao therefore earned Sima Zhao's trust. He was sent into multiple battles against Eastern Wu and won every one of them. 
Shi Bao also participated in Sima Yan's replacement of Wei but was subjected to calumny and doubted by Sima Yan at one point. Only after Shi Bao asked for forgiveness in person did he regain Sima Yan's trust. In the end, he was promoted Minister of the Masses.

A native of Jingzhou Nanjun, loyal minister of Kingdom of Wu. Good and able men promoted by selection and rufuse to be an official. He did not agree to Sun Xiu's recruitment until his later years. After the Jin defeated Wu, Emperor Wu of Jin heard of his name and ordered Shi Wei to be an official, but Shi Wei pretended to be crazy and stupid, and pretended to be blind, used every means to refuse to be an official in the Jin Dynasty.

The Nanpi people of Bohai, the son of Shi Bao, are famous for his extravagance. According to historical records, during his tenure as the Inspector of Jingzhou, Shi Chong robbed the rich of business travelers and became the richest in the world. Wang Kai and Shi Chong fought for wealth many times, and lost to Shi Chong over and over again. However, Shi Chong gained power because of his wealth and admiration for Jia Nanfeng. In addition, he was hated by Sima Lun's minion Sun Xiu for the famous prostitute Lvzhu, and was eventually killed by Simalun.

A native of Yingchuan. Official of Cao Wei. He took refuge in Jingzhou with Xu Shu and became friends with Zhuge Liang and Pang Tong. Afterwards they went their separate ways, and Shito worked for Cao Wei, but never held a prominent position in his life.

He was a native of Gaoping County, Shanyang, an official of the Eastern Han Dynasty and Cao Wei. 
He was known as one of the three sages of the Later Han Dynasty, together with Wang Chong and Wang Fu. He was good at writing and rhetoric, frank and outspoken, and had unrestrained behavior. 
He was recommended by Xun Yu to serve in the government. Zhong Changtong advocated "people-oriented", not to leave the fate of heaven, and opposed foolish loyalty and filial piety, which was in line with many of Cao Cao's ideas, but was not reappointed.

A native of Zhongmou, Henan, he served Cao Cao. 
During the rebellion of Dong Zhuo, he first persuaded Yang Yuan to defend himself, but after the alliance against Dong started, he persuaded Yang Yuan to join Cao Cao. Cao Cao was so pleased with Ren Jun that he not only promised his sister to him, but also often entrusted Ren Jun with the important task of supplying. 
However, Ren Jun's greatest achievement was to promote the cantonment of the fields, which was called in history: "The land was cultivated and the grain overflowed, and the mediocrity was achieved.

A native of Bochang, Le'an county, he served for Wei and Western Jin Dynasty. Sima Yan believes in his diligence, prudence, loyalty and integrity. However, because he was dissatisfied with the power minister Jia Chong and restrained Jia Chong many times, he was resented by Jia Chong and ordered the party members to slander Ren Kai. Ren Kai was dismissed from office. And even when he was recalled, he was never put in important position.

Subordinate to Liu Bei. When Cao Liu scrambled Hanzhong, he fought against Cao Hong with Wu Lan. Wu Lan saw that Cao's army was strong, wanted to retreat temporarily, but Ren Kui refused to follow him and went out battle by himself and was killed by Cao Hong's army.

A native of Langxie DongWu, an official of the Eastern Han Dynasty, father of Empress Xian Empress Fu. After Dong Cheng and others failed in their plot to kill Cao Cao, Empress Fu wrote to his father Fu Wan, asking Fu Wan to kill Cao Cao, but Fu Wan did not dare to agree. After the incident was revealed, Empress Fu was abolished and killed, more than a hundred people in his clan was killed too.

A native of Langxie DongWu, Emperor Xian of Han Empress. Go east with Emperor Xian andthrough thick and thin. After Dong Cheng and others failed in their plot to kill Cao Cao, Empress Fu wrote to his father Fu Wan, asking Fu Wan to kill Cao Cao, but Fu Wan did not dare to agree. After the incident was revealed, Empress Fu was abolished and killed, more than a hundred people in his clan was killed too.

From Wu Commandery, Yang Province, Quan Shang was a royal relative whose daughter was the queen to Sun Liang. 
When Sun Chen was acting authoritative and arrogant, Sun Liang and Sun Lu Ban secretly planned to assassinate Sun Chen and involved Quan Shang. 
However, Quan Shang informed his wife of this matter, who was Sun Chen's cousin, and the secret got out. One theory was that it was Queen Quan who informed Sun Chen. 
Sun Chen acted first. He captured Quan Shang, surrounded the palace with his army, demoted Sun Liang to Prince of Kuaiji, and crowned Prince of Langya, Sun Xiu, instead. Then, Quan Shang was exiled and killed by Sun Chen's assassinator on his way.

A native of Wu County, Yangzhou, son of Quan Shang, a relative of Eastern Wu. 
He helped his father, Quan Shang, in his war against the ruler Sun Qiun, but his mother, a cousin of Sun Qiun, told Sun Qiun about the incident, which led to the failure of the war. Another theory is that Empress Quan informed Sun Qiun. 
After Sun Liang was deposed and Quan Shang was killed in exile, and Quan Ji also committed suicide.

A native of Wu county, Yangzhou, the second son of Quan Cong. Quan Ji is a partisan of Emperor Lu Sun Ba, who participated in the succession battle and slandered the prince party. In the end, the crown prince Sun He were abolished, and Emperor Lu and his partisan were forced suicide, including Quan Ji.

The daughter of Quan Shang, Emperor Wu Fei, Empress Sun Liang. Sun Liang conspired to kill the power minister Sun Wei, and the Empress Quan contacted her father to participate in the plan, but because the biological mother was the cousin of Sun Wei, she informed Sun Wei of this matter, which led to the failure of the army. But there is a totally different one, referring to the Empress Quan's report to Sun Wei. Eventually she was abolished with Sun Liang.

From Wu Commandery, Yang Province, Quan Duan was the nephew of Quan Cong. He was ordered to guard the city west of Chao Lake. When Zhuge Dan rebelled against Wei in Shouchun, Eastern Wu sent Quan Duan, Quan Yi, Wen Qin, and Tang Zi as rescuers. However, the son of Quan Yi's brother submitted to Wei with Quan Yi's mother. In the fear of being convicted, Quan Yi and Quan Duan surrendered to Sima Zhao in Shouchun.

A native of Wu county, Yangzhou, the eldest son of Quan Cong. There is a great reputation whenhe was young. In the battle of Shaobei, Quanxu, Quanduan, Zhang Xiu, Gu Cheng successfully defeated Wei, and each had their own rewards. However, Quan Duan and Quan Xu believed that they deserved the first place. In order to fight for credit, and in the succession battle they belonged to different factions, they framed and slandered Gu Cheng and Zhang Xiu against Sun Quan, resulting in Gu Cheng being demoted and Zhang Xiu being forced suicide. In the battle of Dongxing, Quan Xu and Ding Feng jointly wrote a letter, suggesting that the troops should be led out first and occupy the important position. Wu army won a great victory in this campaign, and Quan Xu was named Ting Marquis for his merits.

From Wu Commandery, Yang Province, Quan Yi was the son of Quan Cong. 
When Zhuge Dan rebelled against Wei in Shouchun, Eastern Wu sent Quan Duan, Quan Yi, Wen Qin, and Tang Zi as rescuers. However, the son of Quan Yi's brother submitted to Wei with Quan Yi's mother. In the fear of being convicted, Quan Yi and Quan Duan surrendered to Sima Zhao in Shouchun.
Or as Ji Ben. In the late Eastern Han Dynasty, the Director of the Imperial Medical Bureau tried to rebel against Cao Cao in Xudu with Geng Ji and Wei Huang, but was defeated and killed immediately.

A native of Fengyi Chiyang, an officer of Wei and the present age scholar. Implicated by Ji Pi's rebellion, he was imprisoned and nearly executed. Fortunately, Zhong Yao found out the truth and he dodged a bullet.
Ji Pi's son, father and brother tried to rebel against Cao Cao in Xudu with Geng Ji and Wei Huang, but they were defeated and killed.
Ji Pi's son, father and brother tried to rebel against Cao Cao in Xudu with Geng Ji and Wei Huang, but they were defeated and killed.

A native of Huai County, Henei, one of the "Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove". Interacted with Ji Kang, Lu An, liked to talk about Lao-Zhuang, and once made a note on "Zhuangzi", but passed away before completion. His exposition influenced metaphysicians such as Guo Xiang of later generations.

Xiang Lang, a native of Xiangyang, Yicheng, was an official of Shu Han and the uncle of Xiang Chong. 
When young, he studied under Sima Hui, along with Xu Shu and Pang Tong. Originally Liu Biao's subordinate, he submitted to Liu Bei after Liu Biao's passing and excelled at domestic politics. 
In his senior years, he resigned from political and world affairs and devoted himself to research and education.

A native of Shanyang, Henei, he served in Wei and the Western Jin Dynasty. Upright and gracious. Once in prison, he was saved by Zhong Hui. Later, Zhong Hui die due to the rebellion, and Xiang Xiong lay his body in a coffin in return for his past grace.
A marquis of Shu Han. After Cao Pi usurped Han, Xiang Ju and others pushed Liu Bei to proclaim emperor. The history records are only here.

A native of Nanyang, Jingzhou, a Commander of Cao Wei. Appreciated by Sima Yi, he was promoted to Governor. When Zhuge Dan rebelled, he led his army to resist Kingdom of Wu and defeated Zhu Yi. There are not many records of him in the official history, but his evaluation is very high, called him "good at military", counted with Deng Ai.
That is Cheng Gong Zhi Qiong, from "Taiping Guang Ji", "Sou Shen Ji" and other books. According to legend, she was an Apsara, married to Xian Chao of State of Wei as his wife.

From Jincheng, Chenggong Ying was a close general of Han Sui. 
After a serious defeat in the Battle of Tong Gate, Han Sui intended to submit to Liu Bei. But Chenggong Ying advised him to turn to the Qiang tribes instead, believing that he would rise up again as the Qiang tribes owed him favors. 
As expected, Han Sui gained the support of tens of thousands of Qiang people but he soon passed away. Chenggong Ying had no choice but to submit to Cao Cao but he never forgot his former leader.
A native of Baima in the East County, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty, a well-known contemporary writer, he was good at Fu. He also revised the law with Jia Chong and others.

Pang De ministry. Guan Yu defeating strong enemies with flood, and the troops led by Yu Jin and Pang De were defeated. After Pang De made a generous statement to Cheng He, who was still close by his side, he made clear his will and did not surrender.

Brother of Cheng Ji. When Cao Mao who was emperor of Cao Wei led his guards to attack Sima Zhao, Cheng Ji was ordered to kill Cao Mao. Later, Cheng Ji was punished by Sima Zhao for the crime of killing the king, even implicated three generation, Cheng Cui died, too .

Sima Zhao's tribe. Cao Mao led his guards to attack the power official Sima Zhao. Cheng Ji was ordered by Sima Zhao and Jia Chong to kill Cao Mao. Later, he was punished by Sima Zhao for the crime of slaying the king, implicated three generation.

A native of Danyang, son of Zhu Zhi. He was a commander of Kingdom of Wu, who was very talented, tolerant of criticism, and made progress continuously. Sun Quan also liked Zhu Cai very much, and often ordered Zhu Cai to stay with him.

A native of Wu Commandery, Wu County, Emperor Wu Jing, Empress Sun Xiu, daughter of Zhu Ju. Pei Lan's name comes from the wild history. After Sun Xiu's death, he originally intended to let the prince accede, but the power ministers Puyang Xing, Zhang Bu, Wan Yu persuaded the Queen Mother Zhu to change to set up Sun Hao, and the Queen Mother Zhu allowed, but Sun Hao forced the Queen Mother to die soon after he took the throne.

A native of Pei State , Cao Wei official, was famous for anthroposcopy, and was equally famous with Guan Lu. Once helped Cao Pi, Xun You, Zhong Yao and others divine, all came true. Zhu Jian Ping can not only divine peole , but also horses, was amazing.
A fictional character. There is no such person in history and romance.

A native of Shangyu, Kuaiiji County, the son of Zhu Jun. Zhu Fu was killed by local barbarians during the tenure of the Inspector of Jiaozhi. Or say the rebellion of barbarians, is because of Zhu Fu's tyranny.

A native of Danyang, Guzhang, the son of Zhu Cai, a general in the late Kingdom of Wu. The Xiling governor of the Kingdom of Wu Bu Chan arrive to the Western Jin and the battle of Xiling broke out. Zhu Wan followed Lu Kang to fight against the rebel generals, and assisted in the defense of the Western Jin army from Bashu, helping the Wu army to win the battle of Xiling.

A native of Shangyu, Huiji County, the son of Zhu Jun, an official in the late Eastern Han Dynasty. Zhu Hao and Liu Yao jointly attacked Zhuge Xuan, the Governor of Yuzhang, who was appointed by Yuan Shu. Liu Yao sent Ze Rong to assist Zhu Hao, but after Ze Rong arrived, he immediately killed Zhu Hao by trick.

A native of Wu county, Wu County, an official of Kingdom of Wu, and the son of Zhu Ju. After Sun Liang succeeded to the throne, he investigated the murder of Sun Luyu, The princess Sun Luban was afraid of being investigated by Sun Liang for his past actions, framed Zhu Xiong and Zhun Sun up, got two people killed for it.

Yuan Shao's subordinates, held the grudge with Han Fu. After Han Fu surrendered to Yuan Shao, Zhu Han wanted to cater to Yuan Shao and use his position for private revenge. He arbitrarily led his troops into Han Fu's residence and broke the legs of Han Fu's son. After Yuan Shao knew about it, he killed Zhu Han to console Han Fu.

A native of Wu county, Wu County, an official of Kingdom of Wu, and the son of Zhu Ju. After Sun Liang succeeded to the throne, he investigated the murder of Sun Luyu, The princess Sun Luban was afraid of being investigated by Sun Liang for his past actions, framed Zhu Xiong and Zhun Sun up, got two people killed for it.

Zhu Ju, a native of Wu County, Wu Commander, was a prominent official of Eastern Wu. 
Proficient in handling both civil and military affairs, he was deemed by Sun Quan the successor of Lu Meng. Sun Quan heavily valued him, even marrying his daughter, Sun Lu Yu, to Zhu Ju. 
However, Zhu Ju got involved in the discord of Yin Fan and the rivalry between two princes and was gradually distanced by Sun Quan and demoted to an assistant official in Xindu Commandery. Later, while Sun Quan was sick, Sun Hong forged an imperial decree ordering Zhu Ju to commit suicide.

After the reign of Cao Wei, Western Jin Dynasty, and Sima Yan ascended to the throne, Zhu Zheng participated in the formulation of new court rituals, and eventually became Book of Documents, confer on Guang Xinghou.

Officer of Wei. One of the Four Friends of Cao Pi. He was close to Cao Pi, the prince of Wei, and along with Sima Yi, Chen Qun, and Wu Zhi were called the Four Friends. When Wu Zhi made fun of Cao Zhen's obesity and his own gauntness, he showed his anger by cutting the ground.

Commander of Wei. He was second-in-command of the vanguard sent by Grand General Cao Zhen to intercept Zhuge Liang during his first campaign north. Zhuge Liang outmaneuvered him twice before he was eventually killed by Zhao Yun.
A native of Mount Tai Nancheng, a Commander of the Western Jin Dynasty. During the Zhangchang Rebellion, Yang Yi was ordered to guard Wan City, and was killed when Zhang Chang invaded Wan City.
A native of Mount Tai Nancheng, a Cao Wei official, and the son of Yang Xu, there is little record of his life story in historical materials.
A native of Mount Tai Nancheng, a Cao Wei official, the son of Yang Xu, and the husband of Xin Bi's daughter Xin Xianying, there is little record of the relevant life story in historical materials.

A native of Mount Tai Nancheng, a minister of the Western Jin Dynasty, the son of Yang Dan and Xin Xianying. In the early years, he conquered Shu-Han with Zhong Hui, and when Zhong Hui betrayed, he admonish strenuously, but Zhong Hui not to be swayed. Yang Xiu and Sima Yan had been in friendship since they were young, and they had made suggestions for Sima Yan and helped him win the crown prince. However, he was extravagant and often violated the law and prohibitions. He was repeatedly impeached and dismissed for crimes, but he reinstated official soon afterwards. Finally, due to strong advice that Simayou, the king of Qi, could not be allowed to leave the town, he angered Emperor Wu, and was demoted, frustrated and died of illness. Although Yang Xiu lacks of moral character, he is good at recruiting talents and giving preferential treatment to his subordinates. He is well-respected among officers and soldiers.
A native of Mount Tai Nancheng, an official of the West Jin Dynasty, the son of Yang Dan, and the brother of Yang Xiu, there is little record of the relevant life story in historical materials.
A native of Mount Tai Nancheng, third Wife of Sima Shi, sister of Yang Hu. She was wise and generous, she used to ask for title for Xiahou Hui.

A native of Mount Tai Nancheng, an official of the Eastern Han Dynasty, the grandfather of Yanghu. As an upright official of the end of Han dynasty , the anecdote of the "hanging fish in the vestibule" spread through the ages. Serving as a local official has quite a record of governance, and has repeatedly flattened the Yellow Turban Army and the riots.
A native of Shu, Pixian County, an official of Shu-Han. First work for Liu Zhang, and next for Liu Bei. He is good at the art of divination and once elected Liu Bei as emperor.

A native of Ru'nan county, an official of Kingdom of Wu. Claims to be Sun Quan's old ministry, begging for official position to Sun Hao. During his tenure , he was domineering and falsely accused his colleagues because of private resentment. After the misdeeds were revealed, Sun Hao ordered to be killed.

A native of Danyang Jurong, wife of former prince Sunhe, mother of Sun Hao. After the succession battle, Sun He was abolished. When the powerful minister Sun Jun manipulate power for personal ends, Sun He was forced suicide, and He Ji raised Sun He's sons alone.

From Yuan, Nanyang, He Yan was an official of Cao Wei, Cao Cao's adopted son, and Cao Shuang's close associate. 
His mother Yin first married into the Eastern Han royal family He. After the He family was eliminated by Dong Zhuo, Yin became a concubine of Cao Cao with He Yan adopted by him. 
He was a handsome man who loved Daoism, Confucian classics, Wei Jin metaphysics, and the mainstream Confucianism. 
When Cao Shuang and Sima Yi co-controlled Wei's political affairs, the former had a 5-member faction, He Yan included. The faction planned the dispossession of Sima Yi's military power together. Guan Luzeng once said He Yan "looked like a withered tree" and a disaster was meant to come. In Incident at the Gaoping Tombs, Sima Yi killed Cao Shuang all five members of the faction.

Official of Shu. Indulgent, but also has talent, so got Zhuge Liang's appreciation and promotion. As the Governor, Inspector has outstanding achievements in governance, regardless of the Han and Yi are sincerely convinced.

A native of Yangxia in Chen County, he served in both the Wei and Jin dynasties. 
He was known for his wealth, and was known for his "He spend ten-thousand-dollar for meals a day, but he still said there is nothing worth of eating". Despite this, he didn't indulge in sex, and he had no faults or high achievements as an official. He was also involved in the cronyism of Jia Chong, which was much criticised by the people at that time.

A native of Lujiang County, he served in Cao Wei and Western Jin. 
When he completed his work, Cao Rui who is emperor of Wei asked Ho Zhen to write the "Poetry of XuDu", after he done, Cao Rui was so impressed by his talent and he was promoted to the post of right minister. During the rebellion of the Xiongnu king Liu Meng, Ho Zhen was ordered to invade Liu Meng and defeated him, even lured Li Ke slayd Liu Meng, surrendered to Dynasty Jin.

A native of Nanyang Wan, the second Empress of Emperor Han Ling, He Jin's halfsister, real names are unknown, He Mi is recorded in the unofficial history novels of later generations. doughty and jealous, Emperor Xian's mother was poisoned by her; together with her brother He Jin forced the palace, the Queen Mother Dong was confined to death. After Dong Zhuo took power, she was given poisoned wine and killed herself.

A native of Yangxia, Chen county, son of He Zeng, official of the Western Jin Dynasty. It is said that he was talented when he was young, but because of his extravagant, and also acted arrogantly and was later impeached and dismissed.

A native of Pixian, Shu county, he has been an official in Shu and Western Jin Dynasty. In the battle between Jin and Wu, there were many suggestions to help Jin smoothly dominate the world. He is a loyal and resolute man, and he has repeatedly admonished Emperor Hui in an attempt to revive the court. In addition, he is also integrity and cherishing the talents. Chen Shou, the author of "Records of the Three Kingdoms", has been helped by him.

A native of Yangxia, Chen county, official of Cao Wei. A distant relative of Yuan Shu, Yuan Shu recruited He Kui, He Kui refused, and even fled to hide. After agreeing to Cao Cao's request, he was appointed. He is good at quelling chaos, serving as Governor of many places, and has records of Suppressed the Yellow Turban Rebellion, civil disturbances, and pirates. Later, due to his achievements, he was transferred back to the court by Cao Cao and served as the Royal Preceptor of prince, assisting Cao Pi.

Participated in the secret imperial edict hidden in the clothing pocket, and conspired to punish Cao Cao with Dong Cheng, Wang Zifu, Liu Bei. But the deeds were revealed, except for Liu Bei, who was outside leading the army, all those involved were killed by Cao Cao.

From Changsha, Jing Province, Wu Ju was Liu Biao's military general and an old associate of Liu Bei. 
After Liu Biao died, Liu Bei originally planned to take shelter under Wu Ju. But Lu Su dissuaded him by saying, "Ju was an ordinary man in a remote commandery. His territory will soon be occupied by someone else." Liu Bei complied and allied with Sun Quan in Fankou, Exian. 
Later, when Sun Quan appointed Bu Zhi as Inspector of Jiao Province, Wu Ju became disobedient in secret, leading to Bu Zhi luring him into a death trap.

Wu Gang was a official of Cao Wei and a subordinate of Zhuge Dan. 
When Zhuge Dan led his army to conquer Sima Zhao, he sent Wu Gang to escort his son, Zhuge Jing, to Wu as a hostage in exchange for reinforcements. After the Wu lord agreed to an alliance, Wu Gang returned to Shouchun to inform Zhuge Dan.

Official of Wu. He was talented in fortune-telling and calendar-making. He worked under Sun Quan and predicted fortunes and disasters, gaining fame for his accuracy. He predicted the defeat of the Huang Zu, Liu Bei's Shu invasion, Guan Yu's capture, the alliance between Wu and Shu, Sun Quan's ascension, and more. Sun Quan is said to have resented Wu Fan for not telling him the secret to his fortune-telling.

From Jiyin, Wu Zhi was an official in Cao Wei. 
As an expert on literature, he was friendly with the sons of Cao Cao, especially Cao Pi. When Cao Pi was fighting for the position of the heir, Wu Zhi once served as his adviser. Cao Pi's famous work, Letter to Wu Zhi, was a prose elegant in style and rich in sentiment, same as Wu Zhi's letter in reply. 
Though Wu Zhi was valued by Cao Pi, he was arrogant, rude, and disliked by people of his time. In the historical records, it was documented that he enjoyed mocking Cao Zhen and Zhu Shuo.

A native of Wu County, he was a official of State of Wu and the Western Jin Dynasty. When the Western Jin Dynasty sent troops to destroy Wu, he fought until the last moment and surrendered after knowing that the Kingdom of Wu was destroyed. Although he had a poor background, he was promoted by Great Mounts Supervisor Lu Kang and participated in the Battle of Xiling. Seeing the sawdust flowing down the Yangtze River, he realized that the Western Jin Dynasty was building ships to conquer Eastern Wu, so he informed Sun Hao and asked for more troops to Jianping to resist the Jin army, but Sun Hao refused his request. He surrenderedd to the Western Jin Dynasty, but was still concerned about the old country, but he did not neglect his duty and have two ambitions. Served as governor of Jincheng, Nanzhong and Jiaozhou, with outstanding political achievements.

From Wucheng, Wu Commandery, Wu Can was an official of Wu. 
Wu Can was honest and considerate of his subordinates. First scouted by Sun Heshang, he was then valued by Sun Quan, gaining a reputation equal to that of Lu Xun and Bo Jing. 
He first guarded against the advancement of Cao Xiu's army by a cave along with Lu Fan and He Qi, then settled the mountain tribes with Lu Dai. For his merits, he was brought back to serve in the palace. 
During the conflict of the two princes of Wu, he was framed by Lu Lord Sun Ba and Yang Zhu and got executed.

Officer of Liu Biao. When Liu Biao was attacked by Sun Ce, Lu Gong used a ploy of Kuai Liang's. He had troops hide in the mountains, then trigger a rockslide and hail of arrows on Sun Jiang when he came by. This slew Sun Jiang, and though Lu Gong gave chase after the retreating army, he ran into Cheng Pu and was slain.

A native of Dongping County, Yanzhou, an official of Cao Wei. He and his elder brother Lu Xun are both friends of Ji Kang. Lu Xun raped sister-in-law, Lu An wanted to sue his elder brother. Lu Xun asked Ji Kang to comfort Lu An, and finally made Lu An abandon the complaint. However, Lu Xun framed Lu An up and imprisoned Lu An. Ji Kang came forward to defend his friend. Zhong Hui was dissatisfied with Ji Kang and seized the opportunity to persuade Sima Zhao to execute these two together. Lu An and Ji Kang were therefore punished.

Cao Cao's old friend. In order to avoid Dong Zhuo, Cao Cao passed Lu Boshe's house on his way back to his hometown. The Lu family treated Cao Cao graciously, but Cao Cao was suspected that the Lu family had other aims. He escaped after killing the Lu family at night, and even sighed, "I would rather betray the world than let the world betray me!" Many versions of this story have been spread to the world, but most of them all derived from Cao Cao's suspicion. Although the records in"Wei Lue" are completely different, they are afraid of making up for the sake of avoiding fiction.

From Guangling Commandery, Xu Province, Lu Dai was a prominent official of Eastern Wu and one of the officials Sun Quan entrusted his son with. 
Lu Dai went to Jiangdong to be away from the chaos in the central region and was scouted and recruited by Sun Quan. Lu Dai was the reason Eastern Wu was able to include Jiao Province as its territory. Lu Dai also sent his envoys further down south and had kingdoms like Funan and Linyi offer tributes. 
Yet, though Lu Dai scored merits for settling Jiao Province, his cruel and devious methods were hugely contraversial.
Yuan Shao's subordinate. During the battle of Guandu, he and Chunyuqiong was responsible for escorting grain, and was beheaded when Cao Cao burned the Wuchao granary.

A native of Bowang, Nanyang County, a Commander of Cao Wei. For many years, he served as the Governor of Xiangyang, Guan Yu sent troops to the northern expedition, surrounded Lu Chang in Xiangyang, and Lu Chang stick until Guan Yu retreated.
A fictional character, daughter of Lu Meng.

From Wuyuan Commandery, Lu Wen was the daughter of Lu Bu. In historical texts, there was no mention of her name and little about her life. It was only known that she was originally married to the son of Yuan Shu. More about her could be found in unofficial records and literary works.

A native of Wujun in the Eastern Han Dynasty, Xu Sheng's wife, whose deeds can be found in "The Book of the Later Han Biography of Women". Virtuous and ladylike , she often persuades her gambling husband Xu Sheng to study. Xu Sheng is grateful for his wife's never leave and diligently study. Xu Sheng was killed, and she killed the foes. Later, the county where she was located was rioted by thieves. The thieves wanted to rape Lu Rong, and Lu Rong died because of refusing. There is a saying that Lu Rong died under the Yellow Turban army.

From Xiyang, Runan, Lu Ju was the son of Lu Fan, an official of Sun Wu, and the offspirng of a famed general. He succeeded in multiple conquests against mountain and valley tribes. He was appointed a crucial position of defending Sun Wu against the invasion of Cao Wei. 
In Taiping Year 1, Lu Ju intended to overthrow the powerful official, Sun Chen, but failed. Unwilling to submit to Cao Wei either, he committed suicide in lament.

Formerly Sun Wu official. Because of the greed and tyranny of the Jiaozhi Governor Sun Di. the lord of Wu, Sun Xiu sent Deng Xun to forcefully conquer rare animals, which caused public grievances. Lu Xing led the rebellion, occupied Jiaozhi, and took refuge with Cao Wei, known as the "Jiaozhi Rebellion".

A native of Fuhan, Longxi County. At the end of the Han dynasty, Song Jian seized the opportunity to occupy Fuhan. He named himself "He Shou Ping Han Wang," changed his reign, and appointed a hundred officials. He became a emperor for more than 30 years before he was conquered by Cao Cao.
The concubines of Emperor Xian of the Han Dynasty were named Gui Ren and fled east with Emperor Xian.

Song Qian was a general of Eastern Wu. He participated in the Battle of Yiling along with Lu Xun. After Liu Bei was defeated and retreated to guard Baidi, Song Qian once advised to chase Liu Bei. However, Lu Xun and the others were concerned Cao Wei would take the chance to invade Wu and rejected Song Qian's suggestion. There was no other mention of him in historical records afterwards.

Eunuch of Wu. Cen Hun was beloved by Sun Hao, and when Puyang Xing and Zhang Bu admonished him, Sun Hao grew enraged and killed their families. When the Jin Army threatened to invade, he suggested blockading the Yangtze with chains. Wang Jun broke through, however, and the Jin army invaded. Then, after many surrenders blamed on Cen Hun weakened the Wu army, he was killed by other retainers.

A native of Qi County, the daughter of Li Yi, a female Commander of the Western Jin Dynasty. Li Yi supervised Ningzhou, and Ningzhou was besieged by the Southwest Yi rebels. Li Yi died before crushing the rebellion. Li Xiu was ordered to take command of the military and politics, and eventually defeated the barbarians. After that, Li Xiu took charge of the Ningzhou area for more than 30 years. Died in the state post.

Staff officer of Shu. Brother of Li Chao. Highly evaluated, he was known as one of the Three Dragons of the Li family. When Zhuge Liang marches on is campaign against the Nanman, he is left in charge, but he dies that year. In later years, when Zhuge Liang praises Jiang Wei, Ma Liang and Li Shao were brought up in comparison.

Officer of Lu Bu. When Cao Cao attacked Lu Bu, Li Feng and Xue Lan was order to defend Juye, they tried to let Li Qian surrender. , then Li Qian was killed bcause he refused. After Li Zheng, son of Li Qian reorganize the army to beat force of Lu Bu, he kill Li Feng and Xue Lan. Or Lu Bu kill them because of their defeat.

The fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms", is the concubine of Huang Kui, the assistant minister, but she has an affair with Huang Kui's wife's brother Miao Ze. After Li Chunxiang detected Huang Kui, Ma Teng conspired to kill Cao Cao, he informed Miao Ze, and Miao Ze immediately reported to Cao Cao. Huang Kui and Ma Teng's plan was revealed and killed. Cao Cao despised Li Chunxiang and Miao Ze for their immoral, and then executed them both in the marketplace.

A native of Xiangping County, Liaodong, and he has served in the Cao Wei Dynasty and the Western Jin Dynasty. He was recruited as an Aide by Sima Zhao and won the trust of Sima Yan, Emperor Wu of Jin. Li Yin was a clean official throughout his life, and his family was poor. Even his son had no money to buy medicine. His family had no spare money, which was completely different from the atmosphere of the ministers in the court pursuing luxury.

A native of Jiangxia, Zhongwu, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. Both talents and virtues have always been highly regarded. During the Rebellion of the Eight Kings, Sima Lun was in charge of the political affairs and forced Li Chong to be an official. Li Chong, under threats, became anxious and died of illness.

From "Taiping Yulan". According to legend, his father was the iron officer in charge of smelting weapons in the Eastern Wu, but he failed and consumed a lot of materials, so he was accused. Li'e threw himself into the furnace, so the gold liquid boiled and overflowed at the mouth of the furnace. After that, Li'e was worshipped as a furnace god by the blacksmiths of Wu.

The leader of Shanyue in the Luling area of the Eastern Wu, or called Li Heng. Li Huan and Luo Li rebelled in Luling, Sun Quan ordered Lu Dai to lead an army to conquer. Li Huan and Luo Li were captured by Wu Can and Tang Zi respectively, and were immediately beheaded.
