The fictitious character in The Romance of the Three Kingdoms is an official Liu Biao. After Liu Biao's death, Cai Mao and others falsely claimed his last life, and set up second son, Liu Cong. Li Gui bluntly said that his eldest son Liu Qi should be the lord of Jingzhou, and he even bluntly accused Cai Mao and others of forging Liu Biao's last words, so was executed by Cai Mao.

A native of Baxi, official of the Western Jin Dynasty. Once captured Wang Fu who rebelled under the name of Zhuge Zhan. During the Battle of Pacify Wu, he went with Wang Jun and He Pan to capture Sun Hao. But when Wang Hun and Zhou Jun competed with Wang Jun and He Pan, he claimed that Li Gao burned Sun Hao's palace down.

Kingdom of Wu officials. In the first year of Jianheng, Sun Hao sent Li Xu and others to lead the army due to the Jiaozhi rebellion, but Jian'an seaway is impassable, so turn back. Sun Hao's minion He Ding was rejected because he had proposed marriage to Li Xu, and he took the opportunity to make a calumny, causing Li Xu to be executed by Sun Hao.

A native of Fengyi, Dong County, daughter of Li Feng, wife of Jia Chong. Quite a talented woman. Because his father Li Feng conspired to kill Sima Shi and failed, she was implicated and sentenced to exile. Although she was pardoned by Emperor Wu, Sima Yan of Jin Dynasty, she was not accepted by Jia Chong.

A native of Qianwei, he was originally an official of the Shu Han Dynasty, but later served in the Western Jin Dynasty. He served his grandmother with filial piety and was known for his essay "The Table of Emotions". 
He studied under the tutelage of Qiao Zhou and became famous for his intelligence and wit when he was young. After serving in Jin, he was a stern and upright official with a good reputation, but was never reappointed to the imperial court. He was dismissed from his post by Emperor Wu of Jin because of a complaint in a poem he wrote before he left for the post of governor of Hanzhong.

A native of Yizhou Jianning, the nephew of Li Hui, a famous official of the Shu Han Dynasty. When Cao Wei defeated Shu, he followed Zhuge Zhan and others to defend Mianzhu against Deng Ai, and eventually all died in Mianzhu.

From Pingchun, Jiangxia, Li Tong was a general of Cao Wei. When young, he was a warrior of righteousness and once quelled the Yellow Turban Army. In Jian'an Year 1, he submitted to Cao Cao. 
After he joined Cao Cao's forces, he soon served as a vanguard in the conquest against Zhang Xiu and defeated the latter's army. When the Battle of Guandu came to a stalemate, most officials in Cao Cao's army began having doubts. Only Li Tong demonstrated his loyalty by killing the enemy envoy. After the Battle of Red Cliffs, Zhou Yu surrounded Cao Ren in Jiangling, Li Tong led his army through the sieging enemies but he soon fell ill and passed away.

From Nanyang, Jing Province, Li Sheng was an official in Cao Wei. He's a member of Cao Shuang's faction who once suggested Cao Shuang to attack Shu but the latter suffered a serious defeat. He then visited Sima Yi with the excuse of assuming Inspector of Jing Province. He was tricked by Sima Yi, who pretended to be ill, and Cao Shuang therefore let down his guard. In the end, Sima started the Incident at the Gaoping Tombs. Li Sheng, Cao Shuang and the others and their families were all killed.
From Hedong Commandery, Sili, Li Kan joined Ma Chao with his army when the latter betrayed Cao. He was defeated by Cao's army in the Battle of Tong Gate and killed.
Xiahou Xuan's wife. She's said to be a Taoist immortal. Other records are unknown.

Official of Shu. When Jiang Wei used Xiahou Ba's surrender to Shu to invade northward, Li Xin built a castle on Mt. Qu with Gou An as a forward base. Guo Huai and Chen Tai of Wei saw this and quickly surrounded it, cutting off supply lines. Li Xin desperately escaped a blockade to warn Jiang Wei, then was sent to Xichuan to recover.

Born in Dongxian, Fengyi, he's a subordinate of Cao Cao. Also known as Li Hui in history books. He's born in the same county as Yan Gan, and both are from a poor family. Later, Li Yi was enlisted as an aide by Cao Cao. After Cao Pi ascended the throne, he was also highly valued and ranked among the Nine Chamberlains.

A native of Fuxian, Zitong, he's an official of the Shu Han. In addition to the Confucian classics, he likes all kinds of miscellaneous studies and arts, but because of his frivolous behavior, he is despised by people of the time.

Born in Dongxian, Fengyi, he's a Cao Wei official, and son of Li Feng. Because Xiahou Xuan and Li Feng conspired to overthrow Sima Shi, Li Tao also participated in it and helped Li Feng contact his followers many times. After the deeds were revealed, Li's entire family was terminated.

The fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms", he is a Commander of Wei. During the Northern Expedition of the Shu Han, Sima Wang led Li Peng and Wang Zhen to resist the Shu army, and Li Peng was killed by the Shu general Fu Jin.

Born in Duling, Jingzhao, he's a Cao Wei official, and son of Du Ji. Being upright, concentrating on official duties, and not forming parties for personal gains, he was highly regarded by Xin Pi, and later served as the Inspector of Youzhou. Yuan Kan once advised Du Shu to beware of Cheng Xi, but Du Shu didn't take it seriously. He was framed by Cheng Xi and was nearly executed.

A native of Chengdu in Shu County, he's the younger brother of Du Zhen. Together with Du Zhen, he was appreciated by Sima Yan, the Emperor Wu of Jin, and praised by history for being honest, sensitive, flat and pure.

Born in Jingzhao, Sili, he's Du Yu's elder cousin. He's quite talented. During the Rebellion of the Eight Kings, he served as the Huangmen Servant. Sima Lun killed Jia Nanfeng, and Du Bin was implicated for no reason and was killed by mistake.

A native of Chengdu in Shu County, the brother of Du Lie. When he was young, he studied under Qiao Zhou, a great Confucian scholar in Shu Han. When he became a local official, he made outstanding achievements in governance, and the local people were all satisfied. Later, he was appreciated by Sima Yan, Emperor Wu of Jin Dynasty, and wanted to be called into the court, but Du Zhen died of illness.

A native of Fucheng, Zitong, he's originally a subordinate of Liu Zhang, and later an official of the Shu Han Dynasty. Both Liu Zhang and Liu Bei wanted to appoint Du Wei, but Du Wei pleaded that he's ill and left office, or simply stayed close in door. After Liu Bei's death, Zhuge Liang also wanted to entrust Du Wei as an aide, but Du Wei was only willing to serve as an imperial advisor.

A Commander of Shu Han. There are few relevant records in history excepts that he assumed office in several counties. When Li Yan neglected his duty and falsely reported the situation of the war, he wrote a joint letter with Zhuge Liang to impeach Li Yan. Later, he also resisted Cao Shuang's invasion of Shu.

From Jingzhao, Sili, Du Yu was a politician, military strategist, and a scholar in Cao Wei and West Jin. 
He once followed Zhong Hui on the conquest of Shu. After Zhong Hui defected, most of the officials who followed him died but Du Yu survived with his wit. 
After returning to the palace, he was recommended by the famous general Yang Hu as the latter's successor. He then terminated Eastern Wu, which helped with the unification of West Jin. 
In addition, idioms "like splitting bamboo" and "split as it meets the knife" both came from Du Yu on his conquest of Wu,"The morale is high and the conquest will be like splitting bamboo. It will soon split as it meets the knife and there's no way to turn it around."

The fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms" , he was originally a commander of the Yellow Turban Army. After the defeat of Yellow Turban, he went rogue with Liao Hua. Later, Liao Hua wanted to surrender to Guan Yu. Du yuan refused to accept and was killed.

From Duling, Jingzhao, Du Ji was a minister of Eastern Han and Cao Wei. 
When Cao Cao conquered Hebei and Wuhuan, Gao Gan, already surrendered, rebelled in Bing Province. The Hedong region fell into chaos and Xun Yu recommended Du Ji to be Administrator. 
Du Ji subdued the counties, structured defenses, and hid all the supplies. The rebels failed to have any gain. Cao's forces later quelled the rebellion thanks to him. 
Du Ji governed by rewarded farming and promoted education. Hedong prospered and provided abundant supplies for the army. 
As Cao Cao became Duke of Wei, he summoned Du Ji to the palace. After Cao Pi succeeded the throne, he too valued Du Ji, having him in charge of the imperial tower ship. But while testing the ship, it sank from heavy winds and Du Ji drowned.

Native of Chengdu in Shu County, he first served Liu Zhang and later became a Shu Han official. He and famous scholar, Qiao Zhou both studied with Du Qiong at Shu Han once. Du Qiong was good at astrology, but seldom expressed his opinions. He was highly valued by Jiang Wan and Fei Yi.

A native of Henan, Sili, he's a famous musician in the Three Kingdoms era, and made outstanding contributions to the preservation and inheritance of ancient music. He was dismissed for offending Cao Pi. 
Du Kui is also good at Fuqin, and is best at playing "Guangling San". Later, Du Kui's son Du Meng passed this song to Ji Kang.
Yan Xian's daughter, Fu Xuan's second wife. There is only one sentence in the Book of Jin, saying that Du Wei had virtue.

A native of Yuancheng, Yangping, a scholar in the Western Jin Dynasty. There are several volumes of tadpole writings in bamboo calligraphy and lacquer characters in the tomb of King Li stolen from Jijun. Shu Xi, Xun Xu and Wei Heng sorted out these ancient books and wrote 75 pieces of the book of Jizhong. 
During the Rebellion of the Eight Kings, Sima Lun asked Shu Xi to assume office, but Shu Xi resigned and went home to teach her disciples.

From Huaiyin, Linhuai, Bu Xie was a general of Eastern Wu and the eldest son of Bu Zhi. When Liu Shan first surrendered to Cao Wei, generals like Lu Kang and Bu Xie took the chance to invade Shu lands. But the former Shu general, Luo Xian, put up a resistance and the Wu army returned with no success.

From Huaiyin, Linhuai, Bu Lianshi was the wife of Sun Quan and the mother of Sun Lu Ban and Sun Lu Yu. 
She was married to Sun Quan as a concubine for her beauty. For her non-jealous, and accepting character made her the most popular among the concubines. 
After Sun Quan became Emperor of Wu, he repeatedly wished to make Bu Lianshi the empress but his son, Sun Deng, and most ministers insisted Lady Xu, the prince's adopted mother, should be the empress. In the end, Sun Quan didn't appoint any empress as a emperor for more than a decade. However, when Bu Lianshi was mentioned, most would refer to her as the empress. 
After Bu Lianshi died, Sun Quan missed her greatly and wrote the decree to honor her as the queen himself, in which much sentiment was shown.

Born in Huaiyin, Linhuai, he's a Wu commander, son of Bu Xie. He guarded Xiling with his uncle and brother. 
Because Sun Hao suddenly summoned Bu Chan, Bu Chan was worried about being questioned by Sun Hao. He took refuge in the Western Jin Dynasty and sent Bu Xuan into the Western Jin as the quality. 
Later, SunHao sent Lu Kang to attack Xiling. After capturing the city, Sun killed the whole Bu family.

Born in Huaiyin, Linhuai, he's a Wu commander, son of Bu Xie. He guarded Xiling with his uncle Bu Zhan and brother Bu Ji all the year round. 
Because Sun Hao suddenly summoned Bu Chan, Bu Chan was worried about being questioned by Sun Hao. He took refuge in the Western Jin Dynasty and sent Bu Xuan into the Western Jin as the quality. 
Later, SunHao sent Lu Kang to attack Xiling. After capturing the city, Sun killed the whole Bu family. 
Bu Jing escaped a catastrophe because he was in Luoyang.

From Huaiyin, Linhuai, Bu Chan was a general of Eastern Wu and the second son of Bu Zhi. 
After Bu Zhi passed away, Bu Chan succeeded as Area Commander of Xiling and stationed in Xiling for years. As Sun Hao transferred Bu Chan all of a sudden, Bu Chan was worried he would be prosecuted so he submitted to West Jin, even sending Bu Xuan there as a hostage. 
Later, Sun Hao sent Lu Kang to invade Xiling. After they broke through the city's defense, the entire Bu family was killed.

Shen Ying was a general of Sun Wu. 
When West Jin attacked Wu through Bashu, Sun Hao ordered Zhang Ti to lead the resistance forces. Predicting that Jing Province would be lost, Shen Ying advised Zhang Ti to stayed and guarded Niuzhu but was ignored. Later, the Wu army lost the battle with Zhang Ti and Shen Ying both killed. 
Shen Ying was an expert on hydrology, who wrote Linhai Soil and Water Body. Some modern scholars think the Yizhou mentioned in the book is the modern day Taiwan.

Sun Quan's personal general, his origins are not known. According to the "Jiang Biao Zhuan", a slave of Sun Quan he was originally . 
He got appreciated and became Sun Quan's bodyguard because of his loyalty and integrity. 
At the Battle of Xiaoyaojin, Sun Quan retreated to the Xiaoshi Bridge, which was broken and could not be crossed. He was followed by Gu Li, who helped Sun Quan to leap over the broken bridge with his horse.

From Yangdi, Yingchuan, Xin Chang was an official of Cao Wei and the son of Xin Pi whose sister was Xin Xian Ying. 
In the Incident at Gao Ping Tombs, Xin Chang was in Cao Shuang's army. In the fear of getting involved, he delayed action and sought advice from Xin Xian Ying. Xin Xian Ying deemed Sima Yi's coup mainly a way to eliminate the powerful official Cao Shuang and advised Xin Chang to fulfill his duties. Later, Sima Yi indeed only killed Cao Shuang and his close associates without getting the rest involved.

From Yangdi, Yingchuan, Xin Xian Ying was Xin Pi's daughter and the famed Jin general Yang Hu's aunt. 
Clever and wise, she excelled at interpreting situations. 
In the Incident at Gao Ping Tombs, her brother, Xin Chang, was serving under Cao Shuang and caught in the conflict. He asked Xin Xian Ying for a way to secure his safety. 
She asked him to return to Cao Shuang to show his loyalty. To her, Sima Yi's action was to eliminate Cao Shuang and his associates. As a subordinate, Xin Chang was unlikely to be involved. Later, Xin Xian Ying was proven right. 
Besides, she also saw that Zhong Hui was planning a rebellion. When Zhong Hui recruited her son, Yang Xiu, as a soldier, she repeatedly warned him and thus kept Yang Xiu safe when Zhong Hui did rebel.

A native of Maoxian, Hejian, he's a Cao Wei official. 
He persuaded Tian Chou to serve Cao Cao. Although Tian Chou did not serve Cao Cao, he still offered his plan when Cao Cao conquered Wuwan to help Cao Cao successfully defeat Wuwan. 
Later, Cao Cao hesitated because of the establishment of a heir, Xing Yong persuaded Cao Cao not to abandon the elder. After Cao Cao established Cao Pi as the prince, he hired Xing Yong as the tutor of the prince. 
After Cao Pi became emperor, Xing Y often held a high position.

A native of Weishi, Chenliu, he's the nephew of Ruan Ji, is also one of the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove. 
Shan Tao praised: "Pure and true, he has few desires, nothing can change him." He was recommended to serve Emperor Wu of the Jin Dynasty, but he was not entrusted due to alcohol addiction and excessive violation of ethics. 
Ruan Xian was also good at rhythm and created a stringed instrument similar to the pipa. Later generations referred to this qin as "Ruan Xian", and it was also the predecessor of Yueqin and Qinqin.

Native of Xinye, Yiyang, an official of the Shu Han Dynasty. 
He was a guest of Liu Zhang when his brother-in-law, Huang Wan, who was a distant relative of Liu Zhang, was sent by Liu Zhang to welcome him to Shu. 
After Liu Bei gained access to Shu, he served Liu Bei. He was a member of a prestigious family in the state of Jinchu, and was known as a senior scholar. However, he was often dismissed from his post because he did not know how to control his words and was careless in his actions.

The protagonist in Qinqiang's "The Singing Girl in Quetai". She was originally a famous lorette in Luoyang. He was appreciated by Cao Cao and took refuge in Cao Cao in the rebellion of Dong Zhuo. 
Later, Lai Ying'er fell in love with Wang Tu, the guard in Cao Cao's mansion, but Wang Tu was sent to jail for delaying the military operation. Lai Ying'er pleaded with Cao Cao, willing to die for Wang Tu. Cao Cao was moved by her true feelings and promised to release Wang Tu. However, Wang Tu said that he was just playing tricks. Cao Cao was very angry and wanted to kill Wang Tu, but he thought about Lai Ying'er and finally expelled Wang Tu without telling Lai Ying'er the truth.

From Jiwu, Chenliu, Dian Man was the son of Dian Wei and an official of Cao Wei. 
Regretful of Dian Wei's death, Cao Cao cared for Dian Man greatly, first promoting him to the palace as a langzhong and soon promoted Dian Man to Major in Cao's army as he missed Dian Wei, almost treating him like an adopted son. After Cao Cao passed away, Cao Pi treated Dian Man in the same way, appointing him as a Commandant and granting him the title of a Secondary Marquis. 
Secondary Marquis was the second highest among the 20 rankings in Han. Dian Man acquiring this title meant that the Cao father and son's appreciation of Dian Wei lasted long without waning.

Bei Yan was a major general under Gongsun Yuan. 
When Cao Rui, Emperor Ming of Wei, passed, Gongsun Yuan declared himself an emperor as well as negotiating with Eastern Wu in a plan to defect from Wei. 
Later, Sima Yi was ordered to conquer Liaodong. Gongsun Yuan sent Bei Yan to multiple battles agaisnt Sima Yi but in vain. He eventually surrendered in Xiangping. 
In the Romance, Bei Yan was killed by Xiahou Ba.

Officer of Shu. When Chengdu came under attack from Liu Bei, Zhuo Ying, serving under Liu Zhang, showed up with Zhang Yi to help Zhang Ren. However, he surrendered to Zhao Yun when Zhang Ren was trapped and captured by the enemy and Liu Zhang's army was routed. He then joined Liu Bei's ranks and gained acclaim under Huang Zhong in the attack on Chengdu.

A native of Huiji. He studied under Chen Fan and was a master of divination and was known for his virtue. 
He was the governor of Danyang during the time of Anti-Dong War, he helped Cao Cao to raise 10, 000 soldiers. 
Although Zhou Xin was a neighbour of Yuan Shu, he despised him for his lack of virtue and was always at odds with him. Yuan Shu sent Wu Jing to attack Zhou Xin, but Wu Jing was unable to overcome him and took the people as hostages. Zhou Xin could not bear to see the people suffer, so he dispersed his troops and returned to his hometown. 
When Sun Ce came to Jiangdong, Wang Lang sent Zhou Xin to fight against Sun Ce, but Zhou Xin was defeated by Sun Ce and was killed.

He was the son of Zhou Tai, a great general of the Eastern Wu Dynasty. 
He served as a cavalry captain and was in charge of the forbidden army. He defeated Cao Ren at the Battle of Moosu and defeated Cao Xiu at the Battle of Shiting with Lu Xun. He died the year after the Battle of Shiting.

A native of Le'an County, an official of Cao Wei Dynasty, he is also a famous contemporary alchemist, especially good at interpreting dreams. He tried to stop Cao Pi from killing Zhen Mi with the theory of interpreting dreams, but it was too late in the end.

A native of Hanyang. After Dong Zhuo entered the Capital, Zhou Bi and Wu Qiong were entrusted. They also recommended several celebrities to Dong Zhuo, but later, the celebrities such as Zhang Miao, Han Fu and Liu Dai responded to the Anti-Dong alliance. 
Anti-Dong alliance is strong, and Dong Zhuo fought unfavorably for several times. When he planned to relocate the capital to Chang'an, they gave advice, which angered Dong Zhuo and were killed by him.

A native of Shu County, Lujiang, a general of the Eastern Wu Dynasty, second son of Zhou Yu. Sun Quan originally wanted to reuse Zhou Yin, not only allowing him to lead the army stationed in Jingxia, the land and waterway hub of public security, but also promised a daughter of his clan. 
When Zhou Yin was later exiled for his crimes, the important ministers of the imperial court submitted a joint petition to Sun Quan to forgive him, but Zhou Yin had already died of illness.

A native of Ancheng, Ru'nan, he's a commander of the Western Jin Dynasty. 
He was an official in Wei, and he gradually become important in Jin. During the Jin-Wu war, he went to battle with Wang Hun, and defeated the elite troops led by Zhang Ti, the Chancellor of Wu. After this war, Eastern Wu had no resistance anymore.

The native of Yangxian, Wu County, he's the son of Zhou Pi , the Governor of Poyang. 
When he was young, he was a disaster to his neighborhood. Later, he mended his ways and left a legend of "eliminating three evils". 
After the subjugation of Wu, Zhou Chu became an official of Jin. He was hated for reporting the lawlessness of Sima Rong. After the Northwestern Diqiang rebellion, Sima Rong recommended Zhou Chu to accompany the army to counter the rebellion. Although Zhou knew that he would die, he still followed it. Sima Rong and Xiahou Jun forced Zhou Chu to be the vanguard, only gave 5, 000 troops and ordered him to attack, causing Zhou Chu killed in the battle.

A Yuan Shao officer and brother of Zhou Xin and Zhou Ang. He started out working with Cao Cao, immediately gathering him 2, 000 troops after a crushing defeat. After the coalition against Dong Zhao disbanded, he joined Yuan Shao and fought Sun Jian in Yu. Later, he went to aid his brother, Zhou Ang, against Yuan Shu, but was defeated and killed by Xu Gong when he returned home to Huiji.
A native of Zhong, Baxi, he served Liu Zhang and later became a Shu Han official. He was a famous astrologer who predicted the death of Liu Biao and the outcome of the Battle of Hanzhong.
Born in Shuxian, Lujiang, she's the daughter of Zhou Yu, concubine of the prince Sun Deng.
The wife of Liu Bao, the Zuo Xianwang of the Southern Xiongnu, and the mother of Liu Yuan, the founding monarch of Former Zhao.

A native of Xiping, Ru'nan, he's a Cao Wei official. Because of the war in the Zhongyuan, he and his family took refuge in Jingzhou. Liu Biao treated him favorably. But He Qia saw through Liu Biao's old age and went south to Wuling again. It was not until Liu Cong surrendered to Cao that He Qia accepted Cao Cao's assignment. 
After Cao Cao's conquer of Hanzhong, He Qia first proposed to move the people of Hanzhong to Guanlong and other places. Cao Cao did not accept his words at first, but due to the stalemate with Liu Bei, he finally acted according to his plan. Although Liu Bei won Hanzhong, he had no real population income, which also affected the development of the national strength of Shu Han.

From Meng County, Jiangxia, Meng Zong was a general of Eastern Wu. 
Though talented, famed, and a high-ranking official, Meng Zong was most famous for his filial piety. He Cried and the Bamboo Sprouted in Twenty-four Filial Exemplars was his story and the bamboo from the story was therefore named Meng Zong Bamboo.

A native of Danyang. Her birth and death years are unknown. She should be a poetess from the Three Kingdoms to the Northern and Southern Dynasties. Poems such as "Mengzhu" and "Yangchun Song" are famous in history.

A native of Anping, he's a Cao Wei official. He was appointed because he had a relationship with Queen Mother Guo. At first, he was despised by others, he gradually gained a good reputation for his dedication to public service. He has made outstanding contributions in phonology, exegesis, textual research and other knowledge. Unfortunately, his works have been lost.

A native of Zhuti County, Yizhou, he's an official of Shu Han. When Zhuge Liang conquered Nanzhong, he surrendered with Meng Huo and others. Until Zhuge Liang's fifth Northern Expedition, Meng Yan was ordered to lead the army, occupied the east bank of Wugong and fought Sima Yi. There is no relevant record in history books since then.

An official in Shu Han and Western Jin Dynasty. During the rebellion of Jiaozhi, they sent reinforcements with Yang Ji, Cuan Neng, Li Song, Mao Jiong and others, and succeeded in occupying Jiaozhi, but they were immediately defeated by Wu. 
Meng Gan, Li Song, Kuan Neng and others made a false surrender and fled, but only Meng Gan succeeded in escaping back to Luoyang.

A native of Anzhong, Nanyang, a minister of Shu Han. 
When Liu Bei attacked Yizhou, he accompanied Zhang Fei to Shu and stayed in Shu afterwards. 
After the death of Zhuge Liang and the turmoil between Wu and Shu, Zong Yu was appointed to go to Eastern Wu. Zong Yu's straightforward and tactful answers endeared him to Sun Quan, and the situation between the two countries was restored to a stable state. Later, Zong Yu made several more trips to the Eastern Wu and was treated with great respect by Sun Quan.

The alchemist of the Eastern Wu. When Sun Hao, the monarch of Wu, summoned Shang Guang to ask about conquering the world, Shang Guang replied: "I'm divining for your majesty. Good omen. In the year of Gengzi, your Majesty's army should capture Luoyang."
After Wu subjugated in the year of Gengzi, Sun Hao entered Luoyang as a captive.

A native from Ru'nan County. Because of the chaos in Zhongyuan, he took refuge in Jiangdong. 
After being an official, he was known for his integrity and loyalty, and he wrote to Sun Quan many times, asking Sun Quan to aid the people. 
During the Dispute of Two Princes, he, Lu Xun and others persuaded Sun Quan not to arbitrarily abolish the prince to avoid turmoil in the country. However, they angered Sun Quan. After being court-beated, they gave up and dismissed to the countryside.
A native of Cao Wei. Originated from "Taiping Guangji", "Sou Shen Ji" and other books. According to legend, his wife Chenggong Zhiqiong is a goddess in the sky.

Yu Quan was a general of Wu. When Zhuge Dan from Cao Wei rebelled in Shouchun, he requested reinforcements from Sun Wu and Yu Quan was part of the reinforcement army. Later, Cao Wei broke through the defense of Shouchun city. Unwilling to surrender, Yu Quan unequipped his armor before charing in and dying on the battlefield.

A native of Taishan County. He and Zang Ba were the same bandit of Taishanand and surrendered to Cao Cao together. 
However, Chang Xi rebelled against Cao Cao several times afterwards, but all of them were put down. The last time he surrendered to his old friend Yu Jin, but he died by Yu Jin's hand. 
Later, when Pei Songzhi wrote a commentary on the Three Kingdoms, he used the surrender of Yu Jin as a comparison and criticized Yu Jin, saying that Yu Jin was blamed for his death and received a bad reputation.

A native of Zhuyi, Peiguo, he's a Cao Wei official. There are few history records on him, only that he is an fair-minded official, and known as an elegant scholar. He's respected by Zhang Liao, Zang Ba, Hu Zhi and others.

A native of Zhuyi, Peiguo, he's an official in Cao Wei and Western Jin Dynasty. He's the son of Wu Zhou. 
Wu Mao is fair-minded, and was famous for his virtue. Jia Nanfeng killed the powerful Minister Yang Jun. because Xun Kai wanted to make friends with Wu Mao in the past, he was rejected, and had a long resentment. He took the opportunity to slander and frame up, resulting in Wu Mao being killed.

A native of Zhuyi, Peiguo, he's the eldest son of Wu Zhou, has served as an official of Cao Wei and Western Jin Dynasty. When he was young, he was good at judging people and was kind to Sima Zhao, which was highly valued.

Staff officer under Yuan Shao and son of Ju Shou. He served Yuan Shang following Yuan Shao's death. When Cao Cao and his army invaded Ji Province immediately following Yan Tan's surrender to him, Ju Hu fought back at Handan. He barely exchanged blows with Zhang Liao before being driven back and was shot and killed while fleeing.

A native of Danyang County, Yangzhou. His brother Rui Liang had followed Sun Ce to pacify Jiangdong. After Rui Liang's death, Rui Xuan succeeded him. In addition, Rui Xuan's daughter is the prince Sun Deng's concubine.

Unmentioned in official records and the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Hua Man was first seen in the Qing Opera Long Fong Jin as the daughter of Meng Huo, the southern tribal leader, and Lady Zhurong as well as the wife of Guan Suo. 
She was defeated by Guan Suo and the two gradually fell in love. After Meng Huo surrendered, Zhuge Liang held a wedding for the two.

Born in Chenliu, Yanzhou. Li Jue appointed Handan Shang as the Inspector of Yongzhou and managed the four counties of Hexi. Handan Shang and Zhang Meng, the Governor of Wuwei, were at odds. He plotted to attack Zhang Meng, but Zhang Meng attacked him first, so he's defeated and imprisoned. But the Handan Shang took advantage of the gap and fled, and was eventually killed by Zhang Meng.

Born in Zhuxu, Beihai. Together with Hua Xin and Guan Ning, he was called "Yilong". They're the celebrities at that time. Studious and virtuous, Kong Rong once recommended him to be an official, but because of the chaotic situation in the Zhongyuan, Bingyuan went to Liaodong to take refuge. 
Then he served under Cao Cao. Cao Cao respected Bing Yuan and even ordered Cao Pi to learn from him.

A native of Yangping County, he's a Cao Wei official. He warned Sima Zhao that if Zhong Hui was appointed to attack Shu, Zhong will rebel after Shu subjugated. However, Sima Zhao analyzed the situation and believed that even if Zhong would rebel, he'd not be a cause for concern, and the consequences were just as Sima Zhao expected.

A native of Kuaiji County, Yangzhou, he's an official of Wu. Guo Dan, the Governor of Kuaiji County, was questioned and imprisoned for failing to report the rumors. Shao Chou, the Examiner of Guo Dan, turned himself in and committed suicide to prove Guo Dan's innocence in order to save him.
A fictional character, she's daughter of Jin Xuan.

From Jingzhao Commandery, Jin Yi was the son of Jin Xuan, the Wuling Administrator. 
Wei Huang, Geng Ji, Ji Ping, and him planned a rebellion against Cao in Xuchang. Though they successfully burned down the gate and shot Wang Bi, they were immediately captured by Wang Bi and Yan Kuang. Jin Yi, Ji Ben, and the other accomplices were all killed.

Officer of Wei. As a vassal of Cao Cao, he was given the task of defending Wan Castle against an attack by Guan Yu. However, seeing the suffering of the people of Nanyang district, he and Wei Kai allied with Guan Yu to cause an uprising against Wei. They captured the Governor of Nanyang, Dongli Gun, but were convinced to allow him to go free. Dongli then went on to gather troops and surround the city. Hou Yin petitioned help from Guan Yu, but Cao Ren arrived first with the Wei army and he is defeated and killed.

Hou Xuan was from Hedong. 
When sent Sili Lieutenant Zhong Yao to conquer Zhang Lu, the generals in the Guanzhong region were disturbed. Hou Xuan, Ma Chao, and Han Sui rebelled against Cao and the Battle of Tong Gate broke out. Upon defeat, Hou Xuan sought refuge from Zhang Lu. Later, he surrendered to Cao under Zhang Lu and resumed his original position.

Yu She was a fictional character in Romance of the Three Kingdoms who was a general under Yuan Shu. When the coalition against Dong battled Dong Zhuo's great general, Hua Xiong, in Sishui Pass, Yu She requested to join the fight but was slain by Hua Xiong after 3 rounds.

A native of Ba County, Yizhou, he's an official of Shuhan. Known in the country, he was friendly to Zhang Yi and Gong Lu. He was recruited as an official when Liu Bei entered Shu. Later, because of the combination of hardness and softness, he was praised by Zhuge Liang for his talent selection.

General under Liang Province Inspector Wei Kang and cousin of Yang Fu. In 213, when Wei Kang was killed by Ma Chao, he was visited by Yang Fu in Licheng where they discussed avenging Wei Kang. Encouraged by his mother, he decided to raise an army, and staged a revolt against Ma Chao, with Zhao Ang and Yin Feng. He was defeated by an enraged Ma Chao in battle, but they managed to drive Ma Chao away when reinforcements from Xiahou Yuan arrived.

The Shanmin in Yongan, Wu, he gathered people to revolt because they were dissatisfied with Sun Hao's forced labor and led to a harsh life. After Shi Dan hijacked Sun Hao's younger brother Sun Qian, he attacked Jianye, with an army potential of more than 10, 000 people, but was finally defeated by Wu generals Ding Gu and Zhuge Liang.
In the Zhen Gao, she was believed to born in Shanyang, and she was the daughter of Shi Ji, a famous general of Wu. In addition, there is no relevant record.

Wu officer. After winning renown defeating foreigners, he became a Wu general like his father before him, battling many a time with Wang Chang and others from Wei. After Zhuge Ke was murdered, he worked with his enemies to drive Zhuge Rong to suicide, purging both. He devoted himself to Wu's survival, even working with Shu. Later in life he took back his birth name and became grand minister. Even in Wei they proclaimed him "grand minister of the bandit kingdom."

A Wu bureaucrat. He was recruited by Sun Quan to handle the kingdom's secrets. He fully supported Lu Meng after Guan Yu's defeat, rising up the ranks through exploits such as plotting to lure out Cao Xiu during the Battle of Shiting. He was greatly respected by Sun Deng as his aide. He later did his utmost for the kingdom, working without fear of Lu Yi and fighting to prevent internal conflict.
Sima Yi's concubine. She's the biological mother of Sima Lun, King of Zhao, of the Rebellion of the Eight Kings. She was loved by Sima Yi, and the rest of her life was not recorded in history books.

Subordinate of Gongsun Yuan. Gongsun Yuan rebelled against Wei and established himself as king, and he had secret communication with the eastern Wu. Sima Yi led his army to attack Gongsun Yuan. After Gongsun Yuan's defeat, he sent Chancellor Wang Jian, and Imperial Secretary Grandee Liu Fu as envoys, to ask Sima Yi to surrender. But Sima Yi refused, and the two were also beheaded.

A native of Chengdu in Shu County, he was a general of the Shu Han Dynasty. He is not recorded in the "Three Kingdoms", but only in the "Huayang Guo Zhi". 
When he was young, he was famous together with his fellow countrymen Du Zhen and Liu Shen. He followed Jiang Wei in his many northern expeditions. He was a man of great wisdom and he was the brave leader of three armies. 
In the battle of Wei's destruction of Shu, Zhong Hui led his army to conquer Hanzhong, but he was helpless against Liu Yin and his army could not advance an inch. Finally, he relied on Deng Ai to sneak through the Yinping trail and reach Chengdu. It was only after the surrender of Liu Shan that Liu Yan surrendered to the Wei army.
It is recorded in the "Chinese Ancient and Modern Notes" that she was a palace lady in the court of Cao Pi. She invented the ancient cosmetic purple powder.
There are few relevant records in the official history. Its name can be found in "Nvhong Yu Zhi" and "Shi Yi Ji". It is one of the four beauties of Sun Liang's imperial harem.

A native of Chaona, Anding, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. It was appreciated by Engineering Supervisor Zhang Hua and was entrusted. 
During the Rebellion of the Eight Kings, Sima Yong's influence was getting bigger and bigger. His subordinate Li Han had a rift with Huangfu Shang and Huangfu Zhong, and he persuaded Sima Yong to get rid of the two. After that, Sima Yong dispatched Han Zhi, the Governor of Longxi County, and You Kai, the Governor of Jincheng County, to lead the four counties' troops to besiege Huangfu Zhong for many years. When there was no way to ask for help, there were no ammunition and food, a mutiny happened and Huangfu Zhong was killed.

An official in Cao Wei and Western Jin Dynasty. Former subordinate of Wang Jing. After the execution of Wang Jing, he managed the funeral for Wang. When Baimahu of Houwen Mountain invaded the tribes, Huangfu Yan did not listen to the advice of many subordinates and forcibly sent troops. Zhang Hong, the Yamen General, was afraid of northern barbarians and danger of Wenshan mountain road. They rioted at night and killed Huangfu Yan.

A native of Chaona, Anding, his great-grandfather was Huangfu Song, a famous general in the Eastern Han Dynasty. He's a grand secretary in the Western Jin Dynasty, and a famous doctor. Indifferent to fame and wealth, he was recruited by Emperor Wu of Jin for many times but refused to be an official in his life. He has edited books such as "The Biography of Women", "Diwang Shiji", "Gaoshizhuan", "Xuanyan Chunqiu", "Almanac", "A-B Classic of Acupuncture and Moxibustion".

The favorite concubine of Cao Fang, the third emperor of Wei. Cao Fang's discord with Queen Mother Guo intensified because of the funeral of empress Li and Guo's mother. In a rage, Guo killed Cao's concubine Yu Wan and Zhang Meiren.

A native of Luoyang, Henan. He Jin plotted to kill the eunuch and summoned Dong Zhuo to the Capital, but He Jin was suspicious and sent Chong Shao to announce an edict to stop Dong Zhuo. Dong Zhuo refused. Zhong Shao angrily scolded Dong Zhuo and ordered Dong Zhuo to return to Xiyangting. 
After Dong Zhuo's dictatorship, whether demoted or transferred far away or show kindness with high officials and high salaries, Zhong Shao didn't obey the orders. 
After Dong Zhuo's defeat, Li Jue and Guo Si took power, Zhong contacted Ma Teng and Han Sui with Ma Yu and Liu Fan as internal contacts. They attacked Li Jue and Guo Si, but they were defeated and killed.

Born in Luoyang, Henan, the father of Zhong Shao. After Dong Zhuo's death, Li Jue, Guo Si and others led their troops to break through Chang'an, killed Wang Yun the Education Supervisor, and rushed into the palace. Zhong Fu resisted the insurgents from entering the palace and was killed by Li Jue.

Due to the dictatorship of Cao Cao, Emperor Xian of the Han Dynasty ordered Dong Cheng to eradicate Cao Cao by secretly issuing an edict. Zhong Ji, Wang Zifu, Wu Shuo, Liu Bei and others also participated. After the news leaked out, all the conspirators were killed, but Liu Bei was spared because he was away.

A native to Moling, Danyang, he's an important official in Wu. After Sun Jun took power, he sent Ji Zhi to accuse Sun He, the crown prince, and made Sun He commit suicide. However, Ji Zhi privately advised Sun He to defend himself, which angered Sun Jun. 
After Sun Hao ascended the throne, Ji was ordered to send an envoy to Cao Wei. His responses were orderly, which safeguarded Sun Wu's dignity and attracted Sima Zhao's special respect.

Huche'er was a general under Zhang Xiu. 
After Zhang Xiu surrendered to Cao, Huche'er was gifted gold and silver by Cao Cao for his exceptional courage. Zhang Xiu thought Cao Cao was bribing his aides so as to assassinate him, which was one of the reasons Zhang Xiu betrayed Cao Cao. 
In the Romance, it was said that he "could hold 500 jin and walk 700 li." Before Zhang Xiu ambushed Cao's camp at night, Huche'er made Dian Wei drunk and took his dual polearms. Dian Wei was forced to fight unarmed until he died.
A native of Linjing, Anding, she's the favorite concubine of Emperor Wu of Jin. Because of his charming appearance, no words, and frankness, she was favored by Emperor Wu of Jin.
There is no such woman in official history. She originated from "Hua Guan Suo Biography" and "Three Kingdoms Ping Hua", as Guan Yu's wife and Guan Suo's mother.

A native of Shouchun, Huainan, he's the son of Hu Zhi. He served in Cao Wei and the Western Jin Dynasty. 
He accompanied the army to put down the rebellion of Zhuge Dan. He and his father are known for being clean and honest. During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Jin Dynasty, Hu Wei wrote a letter stating that the current policies were too lenient and should be strictly enforced. The book of Jin attributed it to the Biography of Good Officials, which shows one or two of his character and style.

A native of Yingchuan, he's a celebrity, and Sima Yi was once his student; he is also a calligrapher, and his calligraphy skills are equal to that of Zhong Yao. Yuan Shao and Cao Cao had called Hu Zhao in several times, but Hu was unwilling to assume office. He lived in seclusion in Luhun mountain, closed his door and kept quiet.

From Linjing, Anding, Hu Lie served under Cao Wei and West Jin. He was a courageous general of his time. 
When Zhuge Dan rebelled in Shouchun, Hu Lie repelled the great general of Eastern Wu, Zhu Yi, with an ambush. He later participated in the Conquest of Shu, the settling of Zhong Hui's rebellion, before leading his army to aid Yongan, which was surrounded by Wu's army. 
Later, as the Xianbei tribes in Yong and Liang became restless, Hu Lie was appointed as the Governor of Qin Province. In the next year, a drought broke out in Liangzhou, the Xianbei tribes revolted, and Hu Lie was killed by Tufa Shujineng.

A Wu bureaucrat. He served under Sun Ce at the age of 14 and studied with Sun Quan. He was assigned secretary by Sun Quan after Sun Ce's death and kept kingdom secrets with Shi Yi and Xu Xiang. He also showed talent in battle and defeated the traitorous Jin Zong in the Battle of Xiaoting. He advanced his position as Sun Quan ascended the throne, writing most of his letters and edicts.

From Shouchun, Huainan, Hu Zhi was an official in Cao Wei. 
Equally famed as Jiang Ji and Zhu Ji, Hu Zhi was recommended by Jiang Ji to serve under Cao Cao. 
As Governor of Jing Province, Hu Zhi sent reinforcements to Fancheng, which was besieged by the Wu general, Zhu Ran. His act settled the subjects in the city and they were able to guard Fancheng until Sima Yi's army arrived. 
He later served as General Who Attacks the East and scored merits in terms of farming, military, and canal development.

From Linjing, Anding, Hu Fen was the son of Hu Zhun who served under Cao Wei and West Jin. 
When young, his father and him followed Sima Yi on a conquest against Gongsun Yuan. He later served in many battles: resisting against Jiang Wei's northern expeditions, settling Zhuge Dan's rebellion, attacking Xiongnu Liu Meng in the north, and guarding the border. 
In addition, Emperor Wu of Jin's concubine, Hu Fang, was the daughter of Hu Fen.

Hao Zun, a native of Linjing, Anding, was a general of Cao Wei. 
Proficient in handling both civil and military affairs, he was recommended by Zhang Ji as a civil servant before being scouted and valued by Sima Yi. 
He once resisted Zhuge Liang's northern expeditions before following Sima Yi on the conquest against Gongsun Yuan. He later served as General Who Attacks the East. After Sun Quan died, he invaded Wu along with Wang Chang and Guanqiu Jian but was defeated by Zhuge Ke. Later, when Guanqiu Jian and Wen Qin revolted, he followed Sima Shi to the suppression.

From Yiyang, Hu Ji was a military general of Shu Han. 
He once participated in Zhuge Liang's northern expeditions. Later, Hu Ji agreed to meet Jiang Wei's army in Shanggui but failed to arrive. Jiang Wei's army fought on its own and suffered a massive defeat by Deng Ai.

A native of Guangling, the wife of Sun Qi from the imperial clan of Wu, and the daughter of Fan Shen. In the conflict between the two parties, she was killed by Sun Quan for being a follower of Sun Ba, the King of Lu. Fan Shen intended to remarry her daughter, but Lady Fan refused and disfigured her face by cutting off her ears and nose.

A native of Guangling, and a high-ranking courtier of Wu. Although there was no separate biography for him, he served the four emperors of Sun Quan, Sun Liang, Sun Xiu, and Sun Hao successively, so he deserved the reputation of the most trustworthy minister.

A native of Waihuang in Chengliu, and a loyal courtier of Wei. In his early years, he used to refuse the recruitment. After he became an official, he had a reputation and performance in all his posts. When he was appointed the Governor of Wuwei, he recruited talents to promote learning and promoted farming, so that the foreigners did not dare to invade. Until Sima Shi seized the power, Fan Can was loyal to Wei and refused to serve. He kept silent for thirty-six years. He lived alone in his cart, where he finally died.
A native of Waihuang in Chengliu, and the father of Fan Can. He was written into the historical records because his son Fan Can was loyal to Wei. The rest of his life and deeds are hardly recorded.

From Yunyang, Wu Commandery, Wei Zhao was a historian of Wu. 
When Chen Shou was writing the Records of the Three Kingdoms, to avoid the naming taboo of Sima Zhao, he changed Wei Zhao's name to Wei Yao. 
He wrote On Gambling to admonish the world not to be addicted to games such as gambling or Go. 
He was one of the editors of the Book of Wu. After the coronation of Sun Hao, the two had conflicted ideas about whether Sun Hao's father, the deposed prince Sun He, should be among the emperor biographies. Wei Zhao was later executed by Sun Hao for a fabricated crime.

A native of Duling, Jingzhao, and an official of Cao Wei. He was recommended by Xun Yu when Cao Cao was seeking for talents. 
After the death of his father Wei Duan, he took over his father's post of Liang's Prefecture. 
Later, Ma Chao twice stirred up trouble in Xiliang and besieged Wei Kang in Ji City for several months, but help did not arrive, Wei Kan could not bear people suffering, so he surrendered and be killed by Ma Chao.

A native in Duling of Jingzhao, an official of Wei, and father of Wei Kang and Wei Dan. At the end of the Eastern Han Dynasty, Ma Teng and Han Sui fought against each other for many years. Cao Cao sent Zhong Yao and Wei Duan to mediate and reconcile the two.

A native in Duling of Jingzhao, and an official of Wei. He was a well-known calligrapher, especially good at cursive script and inscribed plaques. In addition, he was also proficient in ink making, and was known as the Three Masters with Brush Pen Master Zhang Zhi and Paper Master Zuo Bo.

A general of the Eastern Wu. His father Xiu Ze was killed by Mao Gui, a Jin general. Afterwards, Xiu Yun accompanied Tao Huang to fight in the battle of Jiaozhi, but Mao Gui and his men were defeated and surrendered to the Wu army. Xiu Yun asked to kill his father's enemy, Mao Gui, but was stopped by Tao Huang. Mao Gui, fearing for his life, conspires to attack the Wu army, but is discovered by Tao Huang, so Xiu Yun killed Mao.

A general of the Eastern Wu. He was defeated by Jin's army in several attacks on Jiaozhi. Later, Yang Ji sent Mao Gui and Dong Yuan to counter-attack the Wu army at Hepu, and the Wu army was defeated, Xiu Ze killed by Mao Gui.

Wei bureaucrat. When Cao Cao stationed troops in Huainan, Cang Di was assigned commandant of Sui Ji. He came to be magistrate of Chang'an in Cao Pi's age and was loved for his fair rule. He rose to Dunhuang Governor in Cao Rui's age. Dunhuang was a lawless land led by powerful locals at the time, but he suppressed them, redistributed land, made trials fair, and encouraged trade with foreign groups, winning him esteem.
When Gongsun Yuan rebelled against Cao Wei, Lun Zhi and Jia Fan opposed so that they were both killed by Gongsun Yuan.

From Licheng, Xu Province, Tang Zi was originally a military general of Cao Wei who later fled to Sun Wu. 
During the rule of Cao Pi, Emperor Wen of Wei, there was a revolt in Licheng and Tang Zi was chosen to be the leader. They were soon defeated by the Wei army and Tang Zi escaped to Eastern Wu. 
After fleeing to Eastern Wu, he was recruited and valued by Sun Quan, promoted to General of the Left. 
Later, when Zhuge Dan of Cao Wei rebelled in Shouchun, Tang Zi and Wen Qin, who also defected from Cao Wei, led the Wu forces as reinforcements. In the end, he was defeated, captured, but not prosecuted and still recruited by Sima Zhao as a general.

A native of Zou County, Lu, he was an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. He was known for his bravery when he was young, and later studied history and scripture. Although he was greedy for money, he did not seem to have many bad traits and was appointed by Emperor Wu of Jin as a supervisor of the military affairs in Badong.

Xiahou Lingnu was from Qiao Commandery, Pei State. A famous woman of loyalty in Biographies of Exemplary Women. Unwilling to be remarried, she cut her hair, ears and nose respectively to show her will.

From Qiao Commandery, Pei State, Xiahou Xuan was an official of Wei Cao and the son of Xiahou Shang. 
Friendly with Cao Shuang, in his early years, Xiahou Xuan was deposed at one point by Emperor Ming of Wei in the Fuhua Incident. When Cao Shuang became Emperor, Xiahou Xuan was promoted to a high position. 
After Cao Shuang was killed after the Incident at Gao Ping Tombs, Xiahou Xuan was demoted multiple times so he planned to kill and replace Sima Shi. However, his plan got out and Sima Shi took action first, arresting Xiahou Xuan and the others and killing their families. 
In addition, Xiahou Xuan was a pioneer in Wei Jin metaphysics studies and started the common practice of taking powdered medicine.

Xiahou Yuan's niece and Zhang Fei's wife. Was captured by Zhang Fei when looking for firewood at the age of 14 and was made his wife. Buried Xiahou Yuan's body after he fell in battle. 
There is another saying, in early years of the Central Plains famine, Xiahou Yuan gave up his own son to save his late brother's daughter, this daughter may be Xiauou Juan.

From Qiao Commandery, Pei State, Xiahou Hui was an official of Wei Cao, the son of Xiahou Yuan, and the younger brother of Xiahou Ba. 
A man talented in writing and debating, Xiahou Hui debated with Zhong Yuchang often, with Xiahou Hui winning most of the time. 
In the Romance, when Zhuge Liang launched a conquest on Wuzhang Plains, Sima Yi praised Hui for his insight and recruited him for his army. Xiahou He and him seized the Shu supplies multiple times, leading Sima Yi to believe they were winning while it was in fact a scheme planned by Zhuge Liang. After Sima Yi fell for Zhuge Liang's trick of his false death, Xiahou Ba and him placated him.

A native of Qiao County in the State of Pei, and an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. Wealthy in knowledge and beautiful in appearance, he was called "Lian Bi" together with Pan An, a well-known handsome man in China. He also drafted and compiled the History of Wei Dynasty, but after reading "The History of the Three Kingdoms" of Chen Shou, he believed that his was inferior and destroyed it.

He was the son of Xiahou Yuan, when he was young, he was very clever and intelligent, and could be called a prodigy. Accompanied by his father Xiahou Yuan in Dingjun Mountain to meet the Shu army, Xiahou Yuan was killed in battle, Xiahou Rong did not want to live alone, rushed to the battlefield and died at the age of 13.
A fictional character, daughter of Xiahou Dun.

A general of Cao Wei and the younger brother of Xiahou Shang. He once accompanied Zhang Ji to defeat the Qiang Hu. When Wu General Zhu Ran besieged Fancheng, Xiahou Ru was ordered to rescue, but he did not dare to attack because of the small number of troops, and only disturbed the enemy with drums and blowing. Only when Sima Yi led his army to reinforce him, he dared to follow him into the army.
A native of Qiao County in the State of Pei, wife of Sima Shi. She was poisoned because she often assisted Sima Shi in planning strategies and found out that her husband was intent on rebellion.

A native of Qiao County in the State of Pei, and an official of Wei. He was originally one of the assisting ministers appointed in the testamentary edict of Cao Rui, the Emperor Ming, but was replaced by Cao Shuang and Sima Yi at the suggestion of Liu Fang and Sun Zi.

A native of Zhending in Changshan. He was originally a subordinate of Cao Cao but was captured by Zhao Yun during the Battle of Bowang. Because of his friendship with Zhao Yun, he accepted the persuasion to surrender and pledged allegiance to Liu Bei.

A native of Fuchun in Wujun, a member of the imperial clan of Wu, and the younger brother of the powerful minister Sun Chen. In order to seize the power, Sun Chen ordered his siblings to control the imperial army. After that, he dethroned Emperor Sun Liang and replaced him with Sun Xiu. Later, Sun Xiu first conferred great titles on Sun Chen and his siblings to paralyze Sun Chen, and conspired with the elder courtier Ding Feng, and finally succeeded in overthrowing Sun Chen and executed his clan.

A Wu bureaucrat. Treacherous and cunning, Sun Hong brown-nosed his way to the top. When the Wu court split, he favored Sun Ha. When slander sent Zhang Xiu, someone he never liked, off to Jiaozhou, he slandered him more to get Sun Ba to kill him. When Zhu Ju of Sun He's side opposed Sun Liang's princedom and was demoted, he forged documents to make him kill himself. He attempted to kill his co-heir, Zhuge Ke, after the death of Sun Quan, but was killed by him instead.

He was the fourth son of Sun Jian and the younger brother of Sun Ce and Sun Quan. He was the grandfather of Sun Xiu. After Sun Jian's death, he inherited the title of Marquis of Wucheng. 
When Cao Cao and Yuan Shao were fighting for hegemony in the north, he married his brother's daughter to Sun Kuang to pacify Sun Ce's army in Jiangdong and ordered the governor of Yangzhou to appoint Sun Kuang as a filial candidate and mao cai. However, he died at the age of 20 before he could take up his post.

From Fuchun, Wu Commandery, Sun Xiu was a royal of Eastern Wu. 
After a large-scaled coup in Wu, the last emperor, Sun Hao, regained the throne. He first promoted the royals but felt uncertain about Sun Xiu controlling the army on the front line. In the name of hunting, he sent soldiers to Xiakou to arrest Sun Xiu. 
Sun Xiu already heard about other royals being executed by Sun Hao so he took shelter under West Jin. Emperor Wu of Jin, Sima Yan, was very pleased and exceptionally granted him a high position and a title of a duke.

A native of Fuchun in Wu Country, and a member of the imperial clan of Wu. Handsome and talented. In the conflict between the two parties, he was one of the followers of Sun Ba, the King of Lu. After the King of Lu was executed by Sun Quan, Sun Qi was also killed.

A native of Fuchun in Wujun, he was a member of the clan of Wu. Sun Hao was saddened by the death of his wife Wang and did not attend court for a long time. It was rumored that Sun Hao had died and that Sun Feng or Sun Fan would inherit the throne of Eastern Wu. Hearing the rumors, Sun Hao ordered the execution of both of them.

A native of Fuchun, wujun, he was a member of the clan of the Eastern Wu Dynasty and was good at making friends with people. He was friendly with Lu Xun, who often corrected Sun Song's misbehavior. He may have had dealings with Zhuge Liang, who mentioned Sun Song in his family letter with Zhuge Jiang and lamented his death.

A native of Fuchun, Wujun, the son of Sun Jian's clan, or "Yu" is his real last name. 
He was a member of Sun Jian's inner circle and was responsible for leading his own troops. After Sun Jian's death, he continued to assist Sun Ce and Sun Quan. 
Later, Sun Yi, the third son of Sun Jian, was killed by Gui Lan, Dai Yuan and Bian Hong, and Sun He rushed to the accountability. Gui Lan and Dai Yuan afraid of be kill, so they rebelled and killed Sun He, then greeted Liu Fu to Danyang.

A native of Beihai, he was the first Chancellor of Eastern Wu. Still Somehow, there is no mention of him in the history books nearly, except that he was a officer of Kung Rong in his early years, followed Liu Yao to Jiangdong, and finally served the Sun family. The reason for Sun Shao's appointment as the first Chancellor of Eastern Wu is a matter of debate, and there is still no definitive answer.

A native of Fuchun in Wu Jun, an officer of Wu, son of Sun He, and younger brother of Sun Huan. "The History of the Three Kingdoms" stated that: he was magnanimous and versed in both literature and military affairs.

A native of Fuchun in Wujun, he was a member of the clan of the Eastern Wu Dynasty. He was a quiet man, but he was good at ruling the army. After the death of his elder brother Sun Jiao, Sun Huan inherited his troops and duties and became the governor of Jiangxia and supervisor of Xia Kou, where he confronted the famous Cao Wei general Wen Pin for many years.

A native of Fuchun in Wujun, and a member of the imperial clan of Wu. As the son of the late prince Sun Deng, he tried to overthrow Sun Jun, but the information was leaked. Investigated by Sun Jun, he was forced to commit suicide. There was another saying that he was inadvertently involved in a power struggle and committed suicide as a last resort.
Cousin of Sun Ce. Fought with Sun Jian everywhere. After Sun Jian died, he followed Sun Ce to join Yuan Shu. He finally died of illness in Shouchun and failed to assist Sun Ce for the independence.
A fictional character, daughter of Sun Jian.

From Fuchun, Wu Commandery, Sun Jun was a royal of Eastern Wu. 
One of the regents Sun Quan appointed in his will, Sun Jun killed and replaced the powerful official Zhuge Ke after setting him up, which led to the peak of the chaos caused by the royals in Wu. 
Sun Jun had an affair with his aunt, Sun Lu Ban, and killed royals and officials such as the deposed prince Sun He and Sun Lu Yu. Suddenly, it's every man for himself in Eastern Wu. 
Later, when Sun Jun wished to invade Wei, before departure, he dreamed of Zhuge Ke coming to take his life. He fell ill and died after passing his position to his cousin, Sun Chen.

A native of Fuchun in Wujun, the son of Sun Jian, youngest brother of Sun Quan, alias Sun Ren. 
After Cao Pi became emperor, he sent Cao Xiu to invade Wu. Lu Fan led an army to meet the enemy, and Sun Lang was the military general accompanying him. When Sun Lang ordered a fire to be set, he accidentally destroyed his own supplies and was unable to defend against the enemy. When Sun Quan learnt of this, he was enraged and had his family expelled from the Sun family, changing their surname to Ding, and sentencing Sun Lang to life imprisonment.

A native of Fuchun in Wujun, a member of the imperial clan of Wu, and the nephew of Sun Quan. In the 2nd year of Qinglong, Zhuge Liang launched the 5th northern expedition, and Sun Wu also sent troops to the New City of Hefei in response. Sun Tai was shot and killed by Commander Man Chong of Wei in battle.

The leader of the civil upheaval in the territory of Wei. Because Zhang Gu, the governor of Lu Hun, forcefully recruited men to enrich the strength of Hanzhong, the people uprose because of the overburdened military service, and the number of the responders were growing. Later Sun Lang contacted Guan Yu, who granted him the military seal and ordered him to continue the chaos in order to contain Wei. At the same time, Guan Yu also launched the battle of Xiangfan.

From Fuchun, Wu Commandery, Sun Ru was the younger sister of Sun Jian who later married Xu Zhen. Unmentioned in official records, the name Sun Ru was fabricated by future generations. Some said she was the wife of Lu Xun, a famed general of Eastern Wu, while some said Sun Ru was the daughter of Sun Ce.

A native of Fuchun in Wujun, and a member of the imperial clan of Wu. In the battle that Wei defeated Shu, Sun Xiu, the Emperor of Wu, ordered Ding Feng and Sun Yi to sail upstream along the Han River with the army. But before the engagement, the Shu had already surrendered to the Wei. The record was unknown afterwards.

From Fuchun, Wu Commandery, Sun Jiao was an Eastern Wu royal. 
The cousin of Sun Ce and Sun Quan, he was trusted by Sun Quan to lead the elite soldiers and resisted the Cao army in Hefei and Ruxu. He later succeeded Cheng Pu's position and supervised the hub Xiakou. 
Sun Jiao was merciful, and respected. A conflict with Ganning once broke out but with the advice from Sun Quan, Sun Jiao admitted his mistakes and rebuilt their relations. He also ordered soldiers not to harrass the subject of Cao Wei, which earned him trust in the Jiang, Huai regions and many submitted to Wu. 
When Sun Quan attempted to seize Jing Province while Guan Yu's away, he wished to make Lu Meng and Sun Jiao the Left and Right Commanders. From this, it was clear he was the best among the royals.

A native of Fuchun in Wujun, he was a member of the clan of the Eastern Wu Dynasty. He succeeded his elder brother Sun Cheng in overseeing Xia Kou. 
After Zhuge Ke was killed, Sun Jun ordered Sun Yi to attack Zhuge Rong, Zhuge Ke's brother. 
After Sun Jun's death, Sun Chen had a good run of power, but because of Sun Yi's growing power, Sun had a good run of suspicion and intended to take advantage of the opportunity when he went to rescue Zhuge Dan by sending troops to Shouchun to take Sun Yi, however, then Sun Yi defected to Cao Wei.

It is recorded in the "Orally Taught Proverbs from Immortals" that she was born in the imperial clan of Wu and was a Taoist nun. After eloped with Du Qi, she learned Taoism from him, and then she was enlightened and became immortal in the Hualao Mountain.

A native of Fuchun, Wujun, he was the last ruler of Eastern Wu. 
When he first ascended to the throne, he was a wise ruler, but he soon revealed his arrogant, tyrannical and superstitious nature, killing his ministers and causing political turmoil and unrest in Eastern Wu. 
Sun Hao's ego was so inflated that he broke off diplomatic relations with the Western Jin, and when Sun Wu had a slight advantage in the initial confrontation, Sun Hao became even more aggressive. 
General and people went to West Jin one after another, finally Easterm Wu can't resist the attack of West Jin, so Wu destory.

Officer of Sun Jian, and his nephew. He served as an official during the Later Han and joined Sun Jian when he formed his army in Changsha. After his leader's death, he continued to fight under Yuan Shu, Yuan Shao, and others. He is said to have helped Sun Ce defeat and expel Liu Yao, and when Yuan Shu became emperor, he remained at Sun Ce's side to stand against Huang Zu. He spent his later years in charge of prisoners.

A native of Zhongdu in Taiyuan, an official and literati of the Western Jin Dynasty. It was once said: "The reason why I pillow my head on water was to clean my ears, the reason why I gargle with pebbles was to sharpen my teeth." This is the origin of the Chinese idiom Zhen Liu Shu Shi.

A native of Fuchun in Wujun, a member of the imperial clan of Wu, and son of Sun Shao. Inheriting his father, he guarded the important northern territory of Wu. However, when Sun Qian, brother of Sun Hao was abducted by Shanyue insurgents, Sun Kai was accused by Sun Hao that he didn't send reinforcements to rescue Sun Qian in time. Later, Sun Hao summoned Sun Kai to return to the court. Sun Kai was worried about being killed by Sun Hao so he went to the Kingdom of Jin.

From Fuchun, Wu Commandery, Sun Xin was a royal of Eastern Wu and Sun Hao's cousin. 
He was General of Agile Cavalry and the commander of Yue County. When West Jin sent Du Yu, a great general, to invade Wu, Sun Xin, seeing there were only 800 enemy vanguards, sent out his troops boldly. The enemies were soon defeated. Sun Xin saw it as a great chance and chased them. 
To his surprise, the Jin army already set up an ambush. Sun Xin broke through the enemy forces and retreated with the remaining soldiers. As he felt relieved, he didn't realize there were Jin spies in the army who, upon seeing the city gates were opened, slain Sun Xin on the spot.

A native of Rencheng in Dongping, and an official of Wei. He served Cao Rui and the three young emperors successively, and was one of the famous literati at the time. He also participated in the compilation of the historical records, but most of which were not handed down to the future generations.

A native of Zhongdu in Taiyuan, he was an important official of Cao Wei. 
He was highly regarded by Cao Pi and Cao Rui, and was one of the most important officials of the court during the reign of Emperor Ming, he often made plans to Cao Rui and usually repeated achievements. 
However, his choice of Sima Yi as a minister to assist him was considered by later historians such as Pei Songzhi to be selfish, and was the cause of the rapid decline of the imperial family in Wei.

A native of Fuchun in Wujun, a member of Wu clan, and cousin of Sun Ce. After Sun Ce's death, Sun Hao intended to stand on his own feet, but Yu Fan warned and dissuaded him. In addition, Sun Jun and Sun Chen, the powerful ministers in the later period of Wu, are both grandsons of Sun Hao.

From Fuchun, Wu Commandery, Sun Chen was a royal of Eastern Wu and the cousin of the powerful official, Sun Jun. 
After Sun Jun, he too became a dictatorial regent, killing generals and ministers unfairly to secure his own power. 
As the young emperor, Sun Liang, grew up, Sun Chen became fearful of losing his power. He gathered the royal army and worked with his aunt, Sun Lu Ban, to depose Sun Liang and made Sun Xiu the new emperor. 
Any official who opposed was killed. 
After the coronation of Sun Xiu, he set up a trap banquet with Zhang Bu and Ding Feng to have Sun Chen arrested and executed.

A native of Fuchun in Wujun, and cousin of Sun Ce and Sun Quan. Following Sun Ce, he pacified Jiangdong and achieved multiple merits. But because he believed that Sun Quan was unable to keep Jiangdong, he secretly interacted with Cao Cao. Being reported by others, he was put into confinement in exile. Or, as Chen Lin said, he was executed by Sun Quan.

From Fuchun, Wu Commandery, Sun Shao was born Yu Shao. He was in-laws with Sun Jian and a foster son of Sun Ce, therefore the changed family name Sun. 
When he was 17, a revolt broke out in Jiangdong with Sun Quan's younger brother Sun Yi and cousin Sun He assassinated. Sun Quan ordered Sun Shao to take over Sun He's troops and guard Wu Commandery. 
After Sun Quan quelled the revolt, he conducted a trial night ambush on Sun Shao but the defense army was well-organized. Sun Quan then promoted Sun Shao to the main general of the Xu Province defense line. After Sun Quan became the emepror, Sun Shao was promoted to General Who Guards the North. 
He guarded the northern border of Sun Wu for years. As he valued intelligence when organizing the army, he scored hundreds of victories.
A native of Fuchun in Wujun, son of Sun Quan. He was a talented and intelligent man who had a great deal of respect for his talent, both civil and military.

Born in Fuchun, Wujun, a member of Wu clan, and the son of Sun Ben. He was famous when he was young. He inherited his father's office and governed Yuzhang. He made great achievements in governance during this period, so he was recruited into the court.
Born in Fuchun, Wujun, a member of Wu clan, and the son of Sun Lin. He had been great general. During the Jin-Wu war, he fought with the Chancellor of Wu against the Jin army and died.

Born in Fuchun, Wujun, she's the eldest daughter of Sun Quan, and sister of King of Wu. She was originally married to Zhou Xun, the son of Zhou Yu. Zhou Xun died early and later remarried Quan Cong. Therefore, Sun Luban is also known as Princess Quan. Sun Luban was favored by Sun Quan, which affected the prince's inheritance and led to the dispute between the prince and Sun Ba, King of Lu. Finally, Sun Quan abolished Sun He and made Sun Liang, the seventh son, the crown prince, and gave death to Sun Ba. It can be said that Sun Luban was responsible for the instability of the regime in Wu after Sun Quan. Sun Luban also had an affair with his nephew Sun Jun and framed his sister Sun Luyu, so that Sun Luyu was killed by Sun Jun. After Sun Jun's death, Sun Chen succeeded to the throne. Sun Chen was autocratic and overbearing. Sun Liang and Sun Luban conspired to kill Sun Chen. However, his deeds were exposed. Sun Chen dismissed Sun Liang as the King of Kuaiji, and Sun Luban was exiled to Yuzhang.

Born in Fuchun, Wu County, the third daughter of Sun Quan. She and Sun Luban were daughers of Bu Lianshi. Married to Zhu Ju, she is also called Princess Zhu. When Sun He was the crown prince, sun Luban wanted to join Sun Luyu to abolish Sun He, the crown prince, and establish Sun Ba, the king of Lu as the crown prince. Sun Luyu refused, and there was a feud between the sisters. In the second year of Wufeng, Sun Yi and others conspired to kill the powerful Minister Sun Jun. Sun Luban falsely accused Sun Luyu of conspiring with Sun Yi, so Sun Luyu died. It was not until Sun Xiu ascended the throne that he proved his sister Sun Luyu's innocence. He hated and dug Sun Jun's grave.

Born in Fuchun, Wu County, he's the fifth son of Sun Quan. He violated laws and regulations, killed officials indiscriminately, and was abolished as a common man. It was only during Sun Liang's reign that he was re-granted marquis. Later, Sun Hao ignored politics for a long time because he was sad about the death of his second wife Wang. It was rumored that Sun Hao was dead and the throne of Wu would be inherited by Sun Feng or Sun Fen. After hearing the rumors, Sun Hao ordered them to be executed.

A native of Fuchun in Wujun, a member of the imperial clan of Wu, and the younger brother of the powerful minister Sun Chen. In order to seize the power, Sun Chen ordered his siblings to control the imperial army. After that, he dethroned Emperor Sun Liang and replaced him with Sun Xiu. Later, Sun Xiu first conferred great titles on Sun Chen and his siblings to paralyze Sun Chen, and conspired with the elder courtier Ding Feng, and finally succeeded in overthrowing Sun Chen and executed his clan.

An official of Wu. During his tenure as the Governor of Jiaozhi, he forced local labor and ordered to capture peacocks, wild boars and other things to pay tribute, which aroused public discontent. The people elected Lu Xing, a county official, to take the lead of rebellion and kill Sun Chen and other officials. It is called "Unrest of Jiaozhi" in history.
A fictional character, daughter of Sun Ce.

Born in Fuchun, Wu County, he's the younger brother of Sun Jian. When Sun Jian recruited troops to fight against Dong Zhuo, Sun Jing recruited volunteers from his hometown to defend his homeland. When Sun Ce went to Jiangdong, Sun Jing led his troops to join him, and offered his own advice as the vanguard, breaking Wang Lang and Zhou Xin's coalition forces. After the war, Sun Ce wanted to ask Sun Jing to dominate the country together, but Sun Jing only wanted to protect his hometown. Since then, although he led Wu army's official post, he did not participate in any foreign war all his life.

Born in Fuchun, Wu County, a member of Wu clan, and the younger brother of Sun Hao. During Sun Hao's reign, Shi Dan, a native of Wuxing, launched a rebellion, kidnapped Sun Qian, Marquis of Yongan, and made him emperor. After that, Sun Qian was rescued by Ding Gu and Zhuge Liang, Sun Hao still poisoned sun Qian.

A native of Fuchun in Wujun, a member of the imperial clan of Wu, and the younger brother of the powerful minister Sun Chen. In order to seize the power, Sun Chen ordered his siblings to control the imperial army. After that, he dethroned Emperor Sun Liang and replaced him with Sun Xiu. Later, Sun Xiu first conferred great titles on Sun Chen and his siblings to paralyze Sun Chen, and conspired with the elder courtier Ding Feng, and finally succeeded in overthrowing Sun Chen and executed his clan.

Born in Fuchun, Wu County, the fourth son of Sun Quan. After the death of crown prince Sun Deng, Sun Quan changed Sun He to the crown prince and enfeoffed Sun Ba as King of Lu. However, Sun Ba and his followers still covet the position of Prince, and a conflict with Sun He started. After years of struggle between the two sides, Sun Quan finally abolished Sun He, changed his seventh son Sun Liang to crown prince, and killed Sun Ba, Quan Ji and other party members.

Born in Taishan, he was a Mount Tai bandit just like Zang Ba. They all surrendered to Cao Cao. After they surrendered, they suppressed the bandits in Qingzhou and Xuzhou, took the lead bravely, and closed the Marquis and made the general for his achievements. Later, when fighting with Sun Quan's army in Ruxukou, Sun Guan fought with an arrow in his left foot. Cao Cao heard about this and personally comforted Sun Guan. Soon after, he died due to the deterioration of arrow wound infection.

He was born in Langxie during Emperor Shun of the Eastern Han Dynasty era, After learning from Yu Ji, he was awarded the Scripture of the Great Peace. In Emperor Shun era, he presented the book, but it was not included in the Treasury. After that he came to Zhuyu and ascended.

The fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms", he's Cao Hong's subordinate, who is good at wielding Three-tipped Blade. He appeared in the battle of Changban and confronted with Zhao Yun. At that time, Mrs. Mi committed suicide. Zhao Yun tied up the Liu a-Dou with Breast Protector and was about to break out of the siege. Yan Ming led the troops to stop him, and Zhao Yun killed Yan Ming in three rounds.

General of Cao Wei. When attacking Shu, Deng AI sent his son Deng Zhong and Shi Zuan to attack, but they were all defeated by the Shu army led by Zhuge Zhan. Deng Ai was so angry that he threatened to kill the generals and ordered them to fight again. After the fall of Shu, Zhong Hui rebelled. Shi Zuan hated Deng Ai and joined with Zhong Hui and others to falsely accuse Deng Ai of rebellion. Finally, Shi Zuan, Deng Ai and Deng Zhong died in the rebellion.

During the Battle of Guandu, Xu Ta and others attempted to rebel. They planned to assassinate Cao Cao while Xu Chu was not beside Cao Cao, but unexpectedly Xu Chu returned, and Xu Ta and others were all killed by Xu Chu.

A native of Dongguan County, a subordinate of Cao Cao. He is loyal and upright. In his early years, Sun Ce wanted to recruit Xu Yi as an official, but he refused to obey Sun's orders and returned to Zhongyuan. Later, he became an official of Cao Cao, which was highly valued by Cao Cao. He was one of Cao Cao's aides, and he also fought against Ma Chao with Cao Cao. After the defeat of Ma Chao, Cao Cao left him in Chang'an to suppress the unrest in Guanzhong area. After Guanzhong was stabilized, he was recruited to the court again.

A native of Haixi, Guangling, a Cao Wei official. In his early years, he took refuge in Jiangdong. Sun Ce recruited him, but he refused to be appointed and returned to his hometown, Guangling. He has served for Cao Cao, Cao Pi and Cao Rui. There is not much ink in the history books, but Cao Pi called him "an important minister of the country." Cao Rui praised him and said"youccan repose on the destiny of the country on him, he's an important minister like a cornerstone." It shows that he has both virtue and ability.

A general of Wei. During the Battle of Xiangfan, Cao Cao sent Xu Shang and Lu Jian to Xu Huang's army to issue orders, and ordered Xu Huang and other troops to assemble before fighting Guan Yu. "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms" contains a lot of ink of him as Xu Huang's subordinate. Xu Huang ordered Xu Shang and Lu Jian under his own banner to attract Guan Ping, and Xu Huang led elite soldiers to attack Yancheng.

A native of Fuchun, Wu County, he had a marriage relation with the Sun family, and he's the cousin of Sun Ce and Sun Quan. He fought against Dong Zhuo with Sun Jian. After Sun Jian died, he assisted Sun Ce. Sun Ce was able to pacify Jiangdong, and Xu Kun contributed greatly. When he followed Sun Quan to fight against Huang Zu, he was killed by an stray arrow.

A native of Dongwu, Chengyang, Jia Nanfeng's wet-nurse. There are few ink in the official history. At present, she's deeds are known from the epitaph "the inscription of Xu, Queen Jia Nanfeng's wet-nurse". The article says that when Yang Jun was in power, Empress Dowager Yang Zhi recruited empress Jia Nanfeng into the palace to kill Jia Nanfeng. Xu Yi asked Jia Nanfeng to leave, so Jia Nanfeng escaped. However, many of the these records differ greatly from official history, especially empress dowager Yang's plot to kill Jia Nanfeng. When Jia Nanfeng was the princess, Yang advised Jia Nanfeng many times and saved her in front of Emperor Wu.

A native of Wucheng in Wu County, Wu was an official of the Eastern Wu Dynasty. He was a trusted advisor of Sun Quan and served under Sun Quan's authority for a long time. During the Battle of Yiling, he was ordered to recruit soldiers; later, he became an official in charge of Wu's army.

A fierce commander in the late Wei period. During the fourth north expedition led by Jiang Wei, he followed Chen Tai to confront the Shu army. During the seventh north expedition, he killed Zhang Yi, a Shu general. But Li Jian, a comrade in arms who guarded Didao, surrendered, there was no way out and he was defeated and died.

Born in Ji, the State of Yan, he's a Cao Wei official and served Cao Cao, Cao Pi, Cao Rui and Cao Fang. In his official career, Cao Rui often served as a local governor and made many achievements in governance. Therefore, Cao Rui appointed Xu Miao as the Inspector of Liangzhou. After Xu took office, he promoted agriculture, built salt ponds, connected the western regions, and promoted education, which stabilized the situation in Liangzhou, which was originally poor and turbulent.

A native of Julu County, Hebei, an official of Cao Wei. Known for his integrity and integrity, Shi Miao came in an ox cart when he took office in Shouchun. One year later, the cow gave birth to a calf. Soon after he resigned, Shi Miao left with the excuse: "There was no such calf at the time, and the calf was born in Huainan."
He was a member of Yuan Shao's men and served as the governor of Wei County, but was later attacked and killed by Yu Poison, one of the leaders of the Black Mountain Bandits.

Born in Longkang, State of Pei. Known for being pure and upright, he has no fear of eunuchs, and once put down the Yellow Turban unrest in Xingyang. Later, he conspired with He Jin to eliminate the eunuch, but failed because the plan was first noticed by the eunuch.
Born in Xiapi, a Cao Wei official. He's quite a literary talent, and he wrote "Hunyu Jing" when he was eighteen years old. This book has now been lost.

A native of Linxiang, Changsha, he was originally a subordinate of Sun Jian and later served in Cao Wei. When Sun Jian attacked Liu Biao and died in battle, Huan Jie went to Liu Biao's camp and asked for Sun Jian's body regardless of safety. After serving Cao Cao, he was upright and defended the officials who were framed and persecuted many times. He once persuaded Cao Cao to establish Cao Pi's position as Crown Prince, so as not to cause disputes and regrets. After Guan Yu sieged Xiangfan, the ministers were frightened and even persuaded the capital to be moved, and asked Cao Cao to personally lead the army. Huan Jie overcame all opinions, and the situation was as predicted.
A native of Linxiang, Changsha, son of Huan Ji, an official of Cao Wei. He died in the Battle of Dongxing when he accompanied Zhuge Christmas and other generals to attack the Eastern Wu.

Born in Longkang, Pei State. Cao Wei official. He was resourceful and was even referred to as "a bag of wisdom". 
Cao Shuang and his brothers often went out on excursions, Huan Fan tried to advise them to be more mindful but they ignored him.
