During the Incident of Gaoping Tombs, Huan Fan was ordered to take command of the troops under Cao Xi, but his son urged him to side with Cao Shuang. So he took the advice and fled to seek out Cao Shuang. 
Huan Fan urged to bring Cao Fang to Xucang and send troops to attack Sima Yi. But Cao Shuang eventually chose to surrender to Sima Yi. Later Huan Fan, Cao Shuang and the the rest of their families were executed.

Born in Jingzhou. When Liu Bei was Shepherd of Jingzhou, Sun Quan sent an envoy to discuss with him about the joint attack on Shu. So Yin Guan advised to agree on Sun Quan, but held the forces for the moment. In this way, Sun Quan wouldn't cross Jingzhou and attack Shu alone.

Born in Shangdang. Cao Wei general. He and Yu Jin came to rescue Xiangfan, but Hao Zhou was captured by Guan Yu after defeat. Later when Guan Yu died, he was captured by Sun Quan troops and was sent back to Wei. 
Because Sun Quan treated Hao Zhou well, he put in a good word for Sun Quan before Cao Pi several times. But Sun Quan was capricious about sending his son to Wei as hostage, so Cao Pi was angery about it. Hao Zhou was therefore distanced and had never been put on any important post ever since.

Born in Changshan, Kuaiji. Wu official. During the conquest of Shu by Wei, he and Ding Feng was ordered to attack Shouchun in hopes of save Shu, but they had to withdrawal because Shu surrendered early. 
Later Sun Hao held grudge against him for minor mistakes and gave him poisonous wine. Luckily, he got antidote in advance and survived. Months later, he still died in anger and depression.

He was a native of Changshan, Huiji, and an official of the Eastern Wu Dynasty. During the Battle of Dongxing, Liuliu was ordered by Zhuge Ke to guard the eastern city. Later, he became the governor of Nanhai and died in the Guo Ma Rebellion.

Born in Changshan, Kuaiji. Wu official. 
He was injured when supressing the Yellow Turban remnants in Kuaiji areas. 
Recommended by Ling Tong, he joined the army again. Later he was promoted to General of the Left for his contributions in the Battle of Dongxing. 
During the Rebellion of Guanqiu Jian, Liu Zan still led troops in spite of his age. On the journey, he fell seriously ill, but he never quited. Eventually, he was killed by Jiang Ban.

Subordinate of Sun Jian. During the campaign against Dong Zhuo, the troops of Sun Jian were defeated by Xu Rong, so Zu Mao took Sun Jian's red turban and wore it to distract the enemies. 
In the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Zu Mao planned to ambush Hua Xiong, but was killed instead.

The leader of Danyang bandits. He rivaled against Sun Ce many times. Later, incited by Yuan Shu, he joined forces with Shanyue to attack Sun Ce, but Cheng Pu repulsed Zu Lang. After regrouping, Sun Ce captured Zu Lang. And Zu Lang surrendered afterwards.

Yuan Shang ordered Guo Yuan, Huchuquan and Gao Gan to attack Hedong. The counties along the way all surrendered, except Jia Kui, who refused and was therefore imprisoned. 
After knowing Jia Kui was righteous and upright, Zhu Gongdao saved Jia Kui from the prison and left without taking credit for it. 
In Records of Wei, there is a counsellor under Guo Yuan named Zhu Ao, who is probably is Zhu Gongdao.

When Gongsun Yuan surrendered, Sun Quan sent Zhang Mi and Xu Yan as envoy to Liaodong, Qin Dan was also among the delegation. 
But when they arrived in Liaodong, Gongsun Yuan yielded to Wei and covetted the property brought by the delegation. But the delegation came with a large army, so Gongsun Yuan put Qin Dan and Huang Jiang in Xuantu. 
After the plot to rebel came to light, Qin Dan fled and through hardships he returned to Wu eventually.

Born in Mianzhu, Guanghan. Shu Han official. Well known for his wisdom and eloquence since young, but he was never appointed on important post. When he advised Liu Bei against attacking Wu, Liu Bei intended to execute him. 
After Liu Bei died, he was favored by Zhuge Liang. And he won the debate against Zhang Wen, the envoy of Wu.

A fictional character in "Romance of the Three Kingdoms", he was a general of Xiahou Dun and the nephew of Cai Yang, the sixth general to be killed during Guan Yu's "Thousand Miles to Ride Alone" and "Guan Wu Guan".

He was a native of Nanxian County, Jingzhou, and the governor of Nanyang in the Eastern Han Dynasty. After the Yellow Turban Rebellion, he defeated the Yellow Turban Army several times. Later, he was killed due to the rebellion of Zhao Ci, a soldier of Jiangxia.
She is a self-proclaimed immortal, the handmaiden of Wang Biao, the king of Luoyang in Eastern Wu, and is said to be able to communicate with the immortals.

Subordinate of Han Fu. When Han Fu intended to gave up Yizhou to Yuan Shao, Geng Wu, Min Chun and others strongly advised against it, but Han Fu didn't adopt it. So after Yuan Shao owned Yi Zhou, Geng Wu and these people were executed.
Born in Maoling, Fufeng. Together with Ji Ben, Wei Huang and Jin Yi, they rebelled against Cao Cao and attacked Xu City under the cover of night. But they were soon defeated by Wang Bi and Yan Kuang.

Native in Yingyin, Yingchuan. Jin Official. The records about him can be learned from the Epitaph of Xun Yue in Yanshi of Henan Province. According to the historians, he and Xun You are of the same clan.

Native in Yingyin, Yingchuan. Cao Wei official. The elder brother of Xun Yu. When Cao Cao was away on a campaign against Yuan Shang, Gao Gan seized the chance to start a rebellion and even plotted to make moves on Ye City. But Xun Yan found out and was conferred the title of nobility.

Native in Yingyin, Yingchuan, a Western Jin official, descendant of Xun Yu, grandson of Sima Yi. With his elder brother Xun Kai, he was valued by Sima Yi since childhood, who called Xun Kai the son of a tiger and Xun Yu the son of a dragon.

Native in Yingyin, Yingchuan. Served under Cao Wei and Western Jin successively. He was a talented musician and painter. 
But he was also controversial, for example, he was attached to the powerful minister Jia Chong, falsely claiming the merits of Jia Nanfeng and Sima Ji to Emperor Wu of Jin; he deliberately moved away from Ruan Xian because he was jealous of him, etc.

Native in Yingyin, Yingchuan. High rank official and great scholar of late period of Eastern Han Dynasty. 
Xun Shuang was the uncle of Xun Yu and together with his seven brothers was called "Xun's Eight Dragons", while Xun Shuang himself was known as "Wu Shuang" and was also known for his legendary deeds of "being the third male in white clothes". 
When Dong Zhuo was in chaos, Xun Shuang and Situ Wang Yun worked together to overthrow Dong Zhuo, but they passed away before they could implement it.

Native in Yingyin, Yingchuan. Son of Xun Yu. Though being fond of women's good looking, he was fully devoted to his wife Cao. After she died of illness, Cao Can was so deeply upset over it and died a few years later.

Native in Yingyin, Yingchuan, Cao Wei and Western Jin. He was the son of Xun Yu's concubine. Although he was known as a genius since his childhood, his character and morals were very different from his father's, and he was notable for his enthusiasm for power and influence and his desire to please those in power.
A fictional character, daughter of Yuan Tan.
A fictional character, daughter of Yuan Shao.

Native in Fule, Chen County, he served Yuan Shu, Lu Bu and Cao Wei in succession. He is from the Yuan family of Chen County, not the Yuan family of Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu. 
When he was serving Lu Bu, he refused to write a letter for him to insult Liu Bei because"only virtue can insult people, but not by insults. 
It is suggested that Cao Cao should rule the country with benevolence and righteousness, and that the implementation of the cantonment should not be forced on the people, but on their own will, so that the people would be happy to join.
He was a native of Fule in Chen County and the father of Yuan He. He fought with Zhang Wen and others against the rebellion of the Qiang, Bei Gong Bo Yu, Bian Zhang and Han Sui.
Born in Ruyang, Ru'nan. Uncle of Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu. He was the Royal Preceptor at that time. After Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu rebelled against Dong Zhuo, he was implicated and executed by Dong Zhuo.

Born in Deyang, Guanghan. Wang Shang'e wife. After Wang Shang died, her parents forced her to remarry Zhang Feng, but she was unwilling to accept it and even plotted to murder Zhang Feng. Eventually, she committed suicide because she was concerned that her parents would be implicated.
Bron in Yingchuan, Yuzhou. Shu Han general. Except he and Zhuge Liang reported Li Yan's mistakes, there are few accounts about him. He was Vanguard General and General of West Conquest.

Born in Ruyang, Ru'nan. Cousin of Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu. 
Cao Cao highly appreciated his being studious. 
Participant of Anti-Dong Zhuo Alliance. During his service as the Inspector of Yangzhou, he was defeated by Yuan Shu and killed by his subordinate afterwards.

Born in Yiyang. He switched allegiance between Liu Bei and Sun Quan repeatedly. Sun Quan blamed Hao Pu after Yin Fan rebelled because they were close friends, Hao Pu was afraid and committed suicide. Together with Shi Ren and Mi Fang, they are known as the Three Traitors of Shu Han.

Born in Yanshi, Henan. He served under Shu Han and Western Jin successively. 
After the fall of Shu, he followed Liu Shan and moved to Luo Yang. 
On the banquet hosted by Sima Zhao, Liu Shan said he enjoyed the life here and did not think of Shu at all. So Xi Zheng sought out Liu Shan and told him the appropriate response was to lament how far he had been removed from his family tombs. 
He asked for permit to return to Chengdu, but Sima Zhao saw through his true intentions.

Born in Yanshi, Henan. He was the Inspector of Yizhou, but his greed and cruelty caused discontent among the people. When Liu Yan was appointed as the Inspector, he arrested Xi Jian. Later, he died in the rebellion of Ma Xiang and Zhao Zhi.

Born in Maoling, Fufeng. Descendant of Ma Rong, the great scholar of Confucian Classics. Together with Lu Zhi, Cai Yong and Yang Biao, they proofread the Five Classics. 
When Wang Yun wanted to kill Cai Yong, Ma Midi advised against it. He was also tasked with conferring the appointment General of the Left and the noble title "Marquis of Yangzhai" on the warlord Yuan Shu. But Yuan Shu treated him rudely and even seized fu from him. Feeling frustrated and humiliated, Ma Midi vomited blood and died.
Ma Teng joined forces with Du Bing, Ma Yu, Liu Dan and Chong Shao to fight against Li Jue. But they were defeated, Ma Yu were captured and executed by Fan Chou.

Native in Fufeng. Cao Wei official. He was a contemporary craftsman and was known as "the most famous craftsman in the world". He improved the loom, tilting cart, Zhuge crossbow and so on, and recreated the guide car.
Native in Maoling, Fufeng, son of Ma Chao. The Three Kingdoms Magazine only records that Ma Cheng inherited the title of Ma Chao after his death.

Native in Maoling, Fufeng. Her father was the great scholar of Confucian Classics in Eastern Han Dynasty and she was the sister of Ma Lun. 
The "Biographies of Exemplary Women" records that she was talented and righteous. She lost her parents when she was young and felt sorry for them, so she composed the "Shen Eros".

Born in Nanyang, Jingzhou. He claimed himself Yellow Turban. After killing Yu Ji, the governor of Yizhou, he marched to Baxian and Gandan and claimed to be the emperor, but he was soon defeated by Jia Long, a Yizhou official.

Born in Maoling, Fufeng. Son of Ma Chao. When Ma Chao defected to Liu Bei, he left his wife Lady Dong and his son Ma Qiu in Hanzhong. After Zhang Lu surrendered to Cao Cao, Ma Qiu was killed by Zhang Lu.

Cao Wei official who defected to Wu, someone said he was espionage. Sun Quan trusted him and conferred him nobility. When Sun Quan was out on a safari, Ma Mao, Zhu Zhen, Yu Qin and Zhu Zhi conspired to assassinate Sun Quan. But their plot was exposed and were executed along with the rest of their families.

Native in Maoling, Fufeng. Her father was the great scholar of Confucian Classics in Eastern Han Dynasty and she was the wife of Yuan Wei. The anecdote about the debate between she and her husband can be learned from Biographies of Exemplary Women.
A fictional character, daughter of Ma Chao.

Character from Anti-Romance of the Three Kingdoms. 
In the novel, she was the daughter of Ma Teng and sister of Ma Chao. 
She and Ma Chao went on the expedition against Cao to get revenge for their fater. Later Ma Chao, Ma Dai and she paid allegiance to Liu Bei. During the Battle of Yizhou, she met Zhao Yun and fell in love at first sight. So she asked Zhuge Liang and Fa Zheng to be her matchmaker, Liu Bei to preside over their marriage. 
After the wedding, she and Zhao Yun were active in many battles in Jinzhou areas.
A fictional character, daughter of Ma Su.

Cao Wei Tianshui Governor. During Zhuge Liang's first Northern Expedition, Ma Zunzheng followed Yongzhou Governor Guo Huai and led his officials Jiang Wei and others on a patrol. On the way, he heard that Zhuge Liang came to attack, and many Cao Wei officials had secretly communicated with Zhuge Liang. Guo Huai thought that he should immediately switch to Shanggui, but Jiang Wei thought it was impossible. Ma Zun determined that Jiang Wei had colluded with enemy, and after returning to Shanggui, he closed the city gate and prevented Jiang Wei from entering the city. Jiang Wei had no way to advance and retreat, and finally surrendered to Shu Han.

The Officer in the last years of the Shu Han Dynasty, was responsible for guarding the Jiangyou. In the battle between Wei and Shu, the army of the State of Wei stalemate with Jiang Wei in Jiange, Wei generals Deng Ai and Tian Zhang used elite soldiers to take the Yinping Ancient Road and bypass the Jiange to attack Chengdu. After leaving the mountain road, first went to Jiangyou. Although Ma Miao sent ambush troops to fight, but was broken by Tian Zhang and had to surrender. Deng Ai and others immediately fought Zhuge Liang's son Zhuge Zhan, and went all the way to Chengdu to destroy the Shu Han.

A fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms", Lieut. General of the Yellow Turban Army Zhang Bao. When Zhang Bao was attacked by Zhu Jun and Liu Bei, Gao Sheng invited him to fight, and Liu Bei sent Zhang Fei to fight. Within a few times, Gao Sheng was stabbed by Zhang Fei.

A native of Chen Liu, Yu County, Cao Wei official, brother of Gaogan clan; or cousin. An official of Cao Cao to Cao Huan. With knowledge, he predicted that Zhang Miao would rebel against Cao; when Cao Cao wanted to kill Zhang Lu, he also advised that this move might cause turmoil in Guanzhong, and then Ma Chao and others rebelled. Cao Cao once wanted to get rid of Gao Rou due to the rebellion of Gao Gan, but Gao Rou as Ci Jian Ling Shi do his duty, and Cao Cao appreciated him. Gao Rou is upright and he also values reason. Even at the emperor's instructions, he does not favor favoritism. He has disagreed with Cao Pi and Cao Rui on several occasions. During Gao Pingling's rebellion, Gao Rou supported Sima Yi and occupied Cao Shuang's barracks as Jiajie did general affairs.

A native of Taishan Pingyang, Cao Wei official. The descendants of Gao Tangsheng, a scholar of Western Han Dynasty. He dared to speak out, offended his colleagues in his early years and fled to Jinan. Then offered his service to Cao Cao, an official of Cao Cao, Cao Pi, and Cao Rui. During the tenure, he didn't change his true character, and repeatedly advised. Even when he was old and sick, he still wrote: "We should guard against eagles within Xiaoqiang," reminding Cao Rui to beware of Sima Yi.

A native of Jingzhou Nanjun, a Commander of Shuhan. Although from official to general, there are very few records about it in history books. When Liu Bei attacked Hanzhong, he was already under his command. Later, he participated in Zhuge Liang's first and fourth Northern Expeditions. During the four Northern Expeditions, he defeated Sima Yi with Wei Yan and Wu Ban, and took many equipments. In the novel, Zhao Yun joined forces with Zhang Yi to rescue Zhao Yun when Zhao Yun attacked Tianshui County and was besieged. In the battle of Jieting, stationed in Liucheng in the northeast to support the main general Ma Su. During the Fourth Northern Expedition, he was responsible for the use of wooden cows and horses to transport grain, and under Zhuge Liang's instructions, Wei Jun deliberately let Wei Jun take away the equipment several times. The complacent Wei Jun was defeated.

When Han Ling Emperor, the leader of the rebellion in Changsha, professing to be a general, gathered more than tens of thousands of people with Zhou Chao, Guo Shi, but was quickly pacified by Sun Jian, the Governor of Changsha at the time.

A native of Yi, Le'an County, Cao Wei official. A student of Zheng Xuan, a master of Confucian classics at the end of the Han Dynasty, was devoted to studying ancient times, and Zheng Xuan praised him as a national pillar. After served Cao Cao, he was responsible for the farming matters, and within five years, the treasury was rich and the people lived in peace. When Cao Cao conquered Guanzhong, he served as logistics and suppressed the rebellion of Tian Yin and Subo. In the end, the official to the Taipu, ranked Jiuqing. Even as a minister, he is still frugal and self-sufficient, and he is quite benevolent.

A native of Nanyang County, served Cao Cao as a minister. When he was young, he met with Cao Cao, and later wanted to defect to Liu Biao, but finally chose to rely on Cao Cao. During the Battle of Pass Tong, Cao Cao was trapped on the Weihe River bank and was unable to make progress. Lou Gui offered advice that took advantage of the cold weather to build a fortress with water and sand. This allowed Cao army to quickly build a barrier and successfully cross the river. Lou Gui has repeatedly made merit, but because of his carelessness, was killed by Cao Cao on the grounds of being ungodly.

A native of Qinghe Dongwu City County, celebrity Cui Yan's younger brother. Cui Yan once commented: "The so-called late bloomers will eventually arrive far away." As he expected, Cui Lin eventually became Engineering Supervisor.

The fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms", Guo Si's general. When Emperor Xian was escaping east, Guo Si ordered Cui Yong to chase him eagerly, and was slashed by Xu Huang, who was then under Yang Feng's command.

People from Anping, Zhuojun. The Emperor of Han Ling sold the official post, and Cui Lie paid for Education Supervisor, the court and the commonalty discussed and laughed. But Cui Lie didn't give up, so he asked his son Cui Jun again, and Cui Jun answered honestly: "The critics think it smells like copper." This is where the term copper smell comes from.

A native of Qinghe County, originally belonged to Yuan Shao and later belonged to Cao Cao. Once Yuan Shao condoned his subordinates to dig graves and robbers to replenish his military resources, Cui Yan once admonished that he should not do it, and it was a benevolent act to collect the corpses for those who exposed the corpse; he also discouraged Yuan Shao from launching the battle of Guandu. After Yuan Shao's death, Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang quarreled, and both recruited Cui Yan, but Cui Yan turned down because of his illness. When Cui Yan first served Cao Cao, he straightened out that Cao Cao should not be pleased by winning soldiers, but should pay attention to the people's livelihood and save the people. Cui Yan was respected by Cao Cao for this. Cui Yan was upright and elegant, and was a celebrity at the time. Chen Shou said in "Three Kingdoms": "Cui Yan's morality is the best." In the end, he offended Cao Cao because of his unintentional word, and was framed by a traitor and was given death.

A native of Wen County, Henei, Cao Wei official. He is respected by people with noble morals. Served as local officials, all had governance achievements, but was transferred to the court by Cao Cao and ordered him to assist Cao Pi. When Cao Cao conquered Ma Chao, Tian Yin and Su Bo rebelled in the Hejian area, and You and Ji also responded. Cao Pi originally wanted to go on an expedition himself, but Chang Lin analyzed the pros and cons and made Cao Pi dismissed the idea. After that, the chaos was quickly settled down.

A native of Jiangyuan, Shu County, the daughter of Chang Qia, and the wife of Zhao Qian, no more record. There are several lines of "Huayang Guozhi" in which she cried bitterly after her father was killed.

A native of Jiangyuan, Shu County, he has served in Shu Han and Western Jin Dynasty. He was clean and honest as the official. When the Shuhan fell, the counties were in turmoil, and there were countless people who abandoned their official posts and left their posts. Chang Xu still held on to the city until Liu Chan surrendered.

In the third year of Huangchu, due to Sun Quan repeated, Cao Pi sent Cao Ren to the Dong Wu, fighted with Wu army at Ruxu. Zhu Huan died down, showing weakness to lure the enemy. Cao Ren was trapped, ordered Chang Diao, Zhuge Qian, Wang Shuang and others to attack Zhu Huan's army. As a result, Zhu Huan beheaded Chang Diao and captured Wang Shuang alive.

A native of Jizhou, he was originally a subordinate of Yuan Shao and later surrendered to Cao Cao. Because of a gap with the Shen Pei, he sneered when Shen Pei was captured and was scolded by Shen Pei.

Minister of Dong Wu. Emperor Wu Jing, Sun Xiu, used Zhang Bu and Ding Feng to kill the powerful minister Sun Chen. After success, he became left general, but he also colluded with the prime minister Puyang Xing to control the government. After Sun Xiu passed away, he and Wan Yu make Sun Hao the emperor. But after Sun Hao succeeded to the throne, Wan Yu, in order to seize power, sued Puyang Xing and Zhang Bu that were regret making Sun Hao emperor. Sun Hao was furious and exiled the two. On the way to exile, he sent people to kill Zhang Bu and Puyang Xing and implicate three generations. In addition, Zhang Bu had two daughters, both were beautiful. After Zhang Bu died, they were forcibly taken into the harem by Sun Hao.

Formerly a general in the Western Jin Dynasty, Huangfu Yan's subordinate. When the Baima Hu in Wenshan County invaded and plundered all the Hu, Huangfu Yan forced himself to go on an expedition regardless of dissuasion. Zhang Hong took advantage of Wenshan Road to be dangerous and feared the Hu crowds, killed Huangfu Yan at night. Later, he was attacked by Wang Jun, Li Yi, Mantai and others.

A native of Peiguo, Feng County, the daughter of Zhang Heng and sister of Zhang Lu; another one is said to be the daughter of Zhang Lu. At the age of seventeen, dreamed light into her mouth and became pregnant. After being blamed for this, Zhang Yulan did not want to be humiliated, saying she was going to die, and ordered her maid to have a laparotomy after her death to prove her innocence. When the night Zhang Yulan died without disease, something like a lotus suddenly appeared from her belly. This is the "Benji Sutra".

The real name is suspected to be Zhang Sheng, but there is no corroboration in official history. It should be a black Bandit or a Yellow Turban Commander. Because he often rides a white horse, Zhang Baiqi is said to ride a white horse. Zhang Baiqi rebelled in Hongnong, and Ma Teng sent Pang De to crusade, breaking Zhang Baiqi.

A native of Nieyang, Nanyang County, Zhang Zhongjing. At the end of the Eastern Han Dynasty, many people in Zhang Zhongjing's family died as a result of the epidemic. So he decided to study medicine and became an famous doctor, and wrote a work "Treatise on Cold Diseases". This book is the first classic collection of principles, methods, prescriptions, and medicines in the history of Chinese medicine. It has a great influence on later generations, such as Sun Simiao in the Tang Dynasty, Ye Tianshi in the Qing Dynasty, and even Korea and Japan have many famous doctors studying. Because of his superb medical skills, Zhang Zhongjing was called the "Three Magic Doctors of Jian'an" together with Dong Feng and Hua Tuo; he was also listed as the four famous doctors in China along with Bian Que, Hua Tuo and Li Shizhen. The Yuan and Ming dynasties were regarded hime as the "holy of medicine".

A native of Nanyang. They were at odds with Pang Tong, and both followed Liu Bei to attack Shu. Later, Pang Tong died. Zhang Cun spoke disrespectfully and angered Liu Bei and was dismissed from office. The historian also did not write a biography for him because of his improper words and deeds.
A fictional character, daughter of Zhang Xiu.

A native of Shujun, Wang Zun's wife, Zhang Ba's granddaughter. The three generations of Yang Jin and Wenji's mother-in-law and daughter-in-law were all well-known for being virtuous, and they were called the "Three mothers" at the time.

A native of Taiyuan, Zishi, the concubine of the famous Cao Wei minister Zhong Yao and the mother of Zhong Hui. Vigorous and talented, cautious in words and deeds, a well-known good wife and mother in the Three Kingdoms period. Zhong Yao and others asked Zhang Changpu about the dictatorship of Cao Shuang, and Zhang Changpu also foresaw the Gao Pingling's rebellion. When Gao Pingling' rebellion, Zhang Changpu once again analyzed the situation for everyone, all as she said.

In order to gain support, Dong Zhuo appointed many officials, and Zhang Zi was named the Governor of Nanyang. When discussing with Dong, Zhang Zi did not make a clear statement. Sun Jian once again had a gap with him, so he took the opportunity to design a banquet for Zhang Zi, and ordered the Changsha First Secretary to hold him accountable, and then headed him.

It seems that there is no record in the official history. It was first seen in "Zhen Gao" by Tao Hongjing, a famous physician and alchemist in the Southern Dynasties, and it is rumored that she was Zhang Ji's sister.

A general of the end of the Eastern Wu Dynasty, supervised Xiling after succeeding Lu Kang. Jin general Du Yu raided Zhang Zheng. Zhang Zheng was defeated because of his negligence and unpreparedness. Zhang Zheng was ashamed, so he did not report to the Emperor Wu Sun Hao. Du Yu took the opportunity to make a dilemma and returned the prisoners to Sun Hao, ordered Sun Hao to revoke Zhang Zheng's Xiling governor position and be appointed Liu Xian instead.

A native of Fengyi, Gao Ling, Cao Wei official. He became an official when he was young, and was later expropriated by Cao Cao. When Cao Cao fought Yuan Shang and Gao Gan, Yuan Shang tried to contact Guanzhong princes for aid. Zhong Yao sent Zhang Ji to lobby the generals, and finally Ma Teng turned to support Cao Cao. Later, he followed Cao Cao to put down Ma Chao's rebellion and conquered Zhang Lu in Hanzhong, and appointed as Yongzhou Inspector. During Zhang Ji's tenure, he made outstanding contributions to stabilizing the situation in Yongliang, and Cao Pi praised him: "Only Zhang Ji that can settle Liangzhou."

A native of Pinggao, Henei. Sima Yi's legal wife. The historical records record that she has been virtuous since she was a child. When Sima Yi pretended to be sick and refused to be recruited by Cao Cao, was accidentally discovered by the maidservant that he was in good health. Zhang Chunhua killed the maid, and Sima Yi respected it. After that, Sima Yi lay sick in bed. Although Zhang Chunhua was out of favor due to her old age and decay, she still went to visit, and after being stabbed by her husband, she went on a hunger strike. The sons also followed their mother. Sima Yi was shocked and apologized.
When Emperor Xian of Han Dynasty abdicate to Cao Pi, Zhang Yin was ordered to submit Xishou to Cao Pi by Emperor.

A native of Xiangyang, Jingzhou, the last prime minister of Dong Wu. He was promoted by Zhuge Ke when he was young. After Zhuge Ke's death, he devoted himself to working hard for the country's revitalization. In the battle between Jin and Wu, he was ordered to lead the troops against the Jin army. The first battle was won. The Lieut. General Zhuge Liang once suggested Zhang Ti kill the soldiers, but Zhang Ti refused, and failed to strictly supervise the soldiers. After the battle at the front was defeated, the soldiers from the rear took the opportunity to rebel, Sun Wu's army was defeated, Zhang Ti was captured by the Jin army, and he calmly resigned.

A native of Yuyang, Zhongshan Governor in the late Eastern Han Dynasty. When Han Sui rebelled in Xiliang, he persuaded Mount Tai Governor Zhang Ju and Wuhuan to rise, claiming to be General Mitian and King Anding, with more than 100, 000 people, and looting the Youji. Later, Youzhou Shepherd Liu Yu used a plan to alienation Wuhuan, and even offered a high bonus to Zhang Chun. Zhang Chun was eventually assassinated by the doorman.

A native of Julu, the younger brother of the yellow turban leader Zhang Jiao, are regarded as "general of all" by the cultists of the yellow turban. After Zhang Jiao died of illness, the Yellow Turban Army was actually headed by Zhang Liang. Huangfusong and Zhang Liang fought at Guangzong and broke the Yellow Turban Army. Zhang Liang died on the spot. Since then, the Yellow Turban army has no leader, fighting the enemy separately, and failed.
A fictional character, daughter of Zhang Lu.

A native of Dunhuang, Liangzhou. Once served as the Governor of Wuwei, he was at odds with the Handan merchants of Yongzhou Governor. The Handan merchant wanted to attack Zhang Meng , was perceive by Zhang Meng , advanced troops to defeat the Handan merchant. The Handan merchant failed to escape and was killed by Zhang Meng. Zhang Meng led the Yongzhou Governor. After that, Cao Cao sent Han Sui to attack Zhang Meng. Zhang Meng was failed, and the government and the people rebelled. He set himself on fire and died.

The fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms", Commander of Cao Wei. Comparing with Man Chong who was a General of the Van at that time, he fought against the Wu army who attacked Hefei City under the command of Emperor Wei Ming Cao Rui. Zhang Qiu and Manchong each led five thousand soldiers, and separately attacked Zhuge Jin who was stationed in Hukou at night. Wu Jun went into chaos unpreparedly, and Zhang Qiu's army had already prepared fire equipment and set fires all around. Zhuge Jin fled, and Wei army returned in a big victory.

A native of Zhuo County in Youzhou, Zhang Fei's second son, Zhang Shao inherited the title after Zhang Fei's death because his eldest brother Zhang Bao died prematurely. Zhang Shao was not only the son of the founding hero of the Shu Han, but also the wife's brother of Liu Chan. After Zhuge Liang and Jiang Wan passed away, Liu Chan trusted him to serve as the bridge between the emperor and the minister: the Privy Counselor. In the battle between Wei and Shu, Wei general Deng Ai attacked arrived in Chengdu. Zhang Shao was ordered to take Yin Shou to surrender. Later, with Liu Chan in Wei under the title of marquis, enjoy the rest life.

A figure of Five-dou-grain Taoism in the Bajun area, he was once a general of Liu Yan. "The Book of the Later Han" regards him as the Bajun witch in the period of the Emperor Ling. Liu Yan sent him and Zhang Lu to attack Sugu, the Governor of Hanzhong, after which Zhang Lu killed Zhang Xiu, separated from Liu Yan and occupied Hanzhong. There is another saying that Pei Songzhi believes that Zhang Xiu is Zhang Heng, the father of Zhang Lu.

A native of Peiguo, Feng County, it is said that he was a descendant of Zhang Liang and the founder of Zhengyi Tao and Five-dou-grain Taoism. Known by Taoists as Taoist master, Zhengyi Zhenren, and together with Ge Xuan, Xu Xun, and Sa Shoujian are the four Taoist master. During Emperor Shun of the Han Dynasty, he founded the Five-dou-grain Taoism in Mount Heming. During Emperor Huan of the Han Dynasty, he ascend to heaven at Mount Qingcheng and his life is said to be 123 years old. When Zhang Daoling died, he passed the sword seal to his son Zhang Heng, who then passed his son Zhang Lu.
It is only mentioned in "Huayang Guozhi" that she is the daughter of Zhang Ze and married to Yang Ligui's eldest son as his wife.

According to legend, she was Zhang Lu's daughter, and in Shi Ce was unnamed, but later unearthed tombstones called her Qiying. After Zhang Lu surrendered to Cao, Cao Cao asked his son Cao Yu to marry Zhang Qiying.

A native of Fanyang, Fangcheng, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. Has promoted Chen Shou. When he was a teenager, he wrote "Jiao Liao Fu", commenting on the political gains and losses of Cao Wei, so he became famous and used by Cao Pi. Later, he served the Sima family, and Yang Hu, Du Yu offered the strategy of exterminating Wu, and the power was given to Engineering Supervisor. But it also became the first victim of the Upheaval of the Eight Princes in the Western Jin Dynasty. The bizarre book of ancient Chinese natural history, "Bo Wu Zhi", was also compiled by Zhang Hua.

General Liu Bei, who had participated in the battle of Hanzhong where Cao and Liu fought, was wounded during the war, and Zhao Yun helped him to get out of the siege. In "The Romance", he is Lieut. General of Huang Zhong, whose general experience is similar to that of official history.

A general of the end of the Eastern Wu Dynasty, when Jin destroyed Wu was a General of the Van. He was ordered to guard the Stone City, which was mutually dependent on Jianye. However, due to the low morale of Wu's army, they were unwilling to die for Sun Hao and surrendered.

A native of Bingzhou, Yunzhong. Originally a subordinate of Ding Yuan, the governor of Bingzhou, once belonged to the Xiyuan Army. Later, He Jin ordered to return to Bingzhou to recruit troops. At the time of Dong Zhuo's rebellion, Zhang Yang stood on his own and made an alliance with Yuan Shao, but he pleased Dong Zhuo to obtain the post of Henei Governor. After Emperor Xian of the Han Dynasty escaped from Chang'an, he was hungry and poor. Zhang Yang brought food to meet him, and he was given the title of Great Mounts Supervisor. But after seeing that Luoyang was broken and the Han Dynasty was weak, he went back to Yewang. Cao Cao took the opportunity to welcome the Emperor Xian to Xudu, Zhang Yang regretted it. When Cao Cao fought with Lu Bu, Zhang Yang wanted to help Lu Bu but was assassinated by his subordinate Yang Chou.

Cao Wei's eunuch, had a close relationship with the power minister Cao Shuang, and even smuggled Ming Emperor's harem concubine out of the palace to Cao Shuang. After Gao Pingling's rebellion, he and Cao Shuang were beheaded, implicated three generations.
A fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms". Zhang Jie was killed because he railed against the usurpation when Sima Yan forced Cao Huan, Emperor Yuan of Weim, to make a concession.

A native of Chengdu in Shu County who served Liu Zhang first and returned to Liu Bei later. When Liu Bei attacked Yizhou, he was ordered by Liu Zhang to hold off Zhang Fei. After the defeat, Liu Zhang ordered him to be the envoy to surrender to Liu Bei. After Liu Bei's death, Yong Kai surrendered to Wu with Gao Ding and Zhu Bao in the Nanzhong Rebellion, with Zhang Yi captured and handed over. Afterwards, Wu and Shu rebuilt the friendship, and Zhuge Liang sent Deng Zhi as an envoy to redeem Zhang Yi. Until then did Sun Quan know Zhang Yi's name. After a talk with Zhang Yi, he admired him greatly. After Zhang Yi returned to his hometown, Sun Quan was even more regretful.
A native of Shu County in Yizhou. He served Liu Zhang and Liu Bei in succession. He was good at divination, especially physiognomy. Later, he offended Liu Bei for some reason and was executed.
There was no such person in the official history. He was made up to be Zhang Jiao's daughter in the works of future generations.

A native of Xi'e in Nanyang, and an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. It is known in history that Zhang Fu was loyal to the state, aspiring to contribute to the prosperity. Being an official with honesty and integrity, he was even respected by Sun Xiu, a crafty sycophant among the courtiers. Later, he became the Inspector of Qinzhou. After taking office, he first killed Feng Shang, the Governor of Tianshui to gain prestige, and then mistakenly killed the eminent monk Boyuan, with the result that his colleagues, subordinates, and the tribes in the north and west were dissatisfied and rebelled. In the end, Zhang Fu was killed by Fu Zheng, a former subordinate of Feng Shang.

A native of Xiuwu in Henei, and an official of Wei. He enjoyed a good reputation for his hands-on performances and doing things in a measured way. He refused Yuan Shu's recruitment and eventually became an official under Cao Cao's command. Cao Cao respected him and ordered Cao Pi to consult Zhang Fan from time to time.

A native of Gaoling in Fengyi, an official of Wei, and son of Zhang Ji. When he was young, he served as the magistrate of Wen County under his father's rule. Because he offered effective strategies during the Northern Expedition led by Zhuge Liang, he changed to work in the imperial court. He successively worked in the Department of State Affairs, and the Central Secretariat, which was the most important military department. After The Rebellion of Gaoping Mausoleum, Zhang Ji's daughter became the Queen, and Zhang Ji became hostile to the increasingly powerful Sima Shi. In the end, he failed to attempt a coup to overthrow Sima Shi and was arrested. Being imprisoned, he was soon put to death.

A native of Pengcheng in Xuzhou, and an official of Wu. The grandson of Zhang Zhao, a high-ranking official of Wu. His mother was the daughter of Zhuge Jin, and his younger sister was married to the deposed prince Sun He, so that he was a member of the core group of Wu regime. Zhang Zhen was also involved when Sun Jun killed Zhuge Ke, a powerful official.

A native of Zhending in Changshan, the leader of the Black Mountain Bandits, nicknamed Feiyan. In its heyday, the Black Mountain Bandits had more than 100, 000 soldiers and spread over the counties in Hebei. Zhang Yan once helped Gongsun Zan fight against Yuan Shao, but mostly lost. After Gongsun Zan and Yuan Shao were defeated one after another, Zhang Yan led the Black Mountain Bandits to yield surrender to Cao Cao.
The daughter of Zhang Fei, the second queen of Liu Shan, and her sister was the Queen Jing'ai. Her name was not recorded in the official history, and Yanyan was a fictitious name in this game.

A native of Zhuo County in Youzhou, an official of Shu, grandson of Zhang Fei, and son of Zhang Bao. As the Assistant Master of Writing, he assisted Zhuge Zhan, who was Zhuge Liang's son and titled Guard General, to resist the army of Jin. In the battle that Wei defeated Shu, Zhang Zun and Zhuge Zhan were forced to retreat to Mianzhu, due to Deng Ai, an officer of Wei, risked his life to smuggle to Jiangyou from the Ancient Yinping Path and seizing Fu City. At the beginning, the Shu army had a strength of defense and won the first battle. However, Deng Ai's army conduct a desperate fight and Mianzhu was eventually breached. Zhugezhan and his son, and Zhang Zun were all killed in this battle.

A native of Yuyang and the former Governor of Taishan. He was persuaded by Zhang Chun to rebel with Wuhuan and proclaim himself the emperor, and conferred Zhang Chun the Senior General. Being ordered to attack Zhang Chun and achieved partial victory, Gongsun Zan, the Commandant of Cavalry, was yet defeated by the Wuhuan Cavalry. Later, Liu Yu, the Shepherd of Youzhou, persuaded Wuhuan. Zhang Ju saw that there was no chance to win, so he fled outside the Great Wall, and his whereabouts had been unknown.

A native of Nanzheng in Hanzhong, and the wife of Zhao Song. When Zhang Lu entered Hanzhong and killed Su Gu, the former Governor of Hanzhong, Su Gu, who was the First Secretary of Zhao Song, also fought and died. Intending to protect her chastity, Zhang Lixiu fled with her face painted and her hair messed, by pretending to be ill and with a knife in hand. After escaping from trouble, she raised her daughter until she grow up an adult.

A native of Pingyuan of Jizhou. A subordinate of Tao Qian, who was the former Shepherd of Xuzhou. He was ordered by Tao Qian to escort Cao Song, who was Cao Cao's father, however, he murdered him and looted all his belongings on the way, leading to the massacre of Xuzhou by Cao Cao. After Zhang Kai killed Cao Song, he fled to Huainan to pledge allegiance to Yuan Shu. Later, being entrusted by Yuan Shu, he deceived and killed Luo Jun, the Prime Minister of the Vassal State of Chen, and even usurped the throne and yielded surrender to Yuan Shu.

A native of Fang City of Fanyang, the son of Zhang Hua (Engineering Supervisor), and an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. When Zhang Hua was the Engineering Supervisor, there was an abnormal scene in the sky and the stars fell. People thought it was a sign of the death of the Three Counsellors of State. Zhang Wei then persuaded his father to resign his job, but Zhang Hua didn't care. Later Zhang Hua and his sons Zhang Wei and Zhang Yi were all killed by Sima Lun, the King of Zhao.

A native of Julu, the younger brother of the Yellow Turban leader Zhang Jiao. He was regarded as "The General of Earth" by the Yellow Turban cultists. When the Yellow Turban revolted in Julu, burning down the government and looting the surrounding area, Zhang Bao led hundreds of thousands of congregations and stationed in Xiaquyang County, which was the largest base of the Yellow Turban Army. The imperial court recruited Huangfu Song, the Governor of the North, and appointed him as the General of the Palace Gentlemen of the Left to fight against the rebels. After several twists and turns, he finally breached Qu Yang and killed Zhang Bao.
A fictional character, daughter of Zhang Liao.
The daughter of Zhang Fei, and the first queen of Liu Shan, the Queen Jing'ai. Her name was not recorded in the official history, and Yingying was a fictitious name in this game.

A native of Wu County, and an official of Wu. Famous and learned at his young age. When Sima Zhao passed away, he was sent to Jin as a envoy by the order of Sun Hao, the Emperor of Wu, to express condolences to Sima Zhao. During that period, a group of Jin officials tried to make things difficult for him, but they were all convinced by the talents of Zhang Yan. In addition, because the "Post Northern Expedition Memorial" was first written by Zhang Yan in his "Memorization", it is controversial whether the true author of this article was Zhuge Liang or Zhang Yan.

A native of Jingzhao County, a hermit in the late Eastern Han Dynasty and the Three Kingdoms period under the tutelage of the alchemist Mr. Qing Niu. After Mr. Qing Niu entered Shu, the two lost contact for some reason. After that, he moved to Ye and Luoyang, living beside the road and not interacting with people.

A native of Qiao County in Pei, cousin of Cao Shuang, and husband of Xiahou Lingnu. There are no other records besides these, and most of the historical records were about his wife Xiahou Linglu keeping her virginity.

Original from the Huai opera "Guan Yu Bade Farewell to Cao Cao", she was the adopted daughter of Cao Cao and was betrothed to Guan Yu as his wife by Cao Cao. When Guan Yu was riding alone for thousands of miles to meet Liu Bei, Cao Yue'e chased after and begged to go with him, but she was refused, so she drew her sword and killed herself.

A native of Qiao County in Pei, son of Cao Cao, father of Cao Huan, who was Emperor Yuan and the last emperor of Wei. A close friend of Cao Rui, the Emperor Ming of Wei. After Emperor Ming took the throne, Cao Yu was conferred the king and then recruited as an courtier. At the end of Emperor Ming's life, cao Yu was supposed to be an assist minister for the young emperor, but Cao Yu firmly refused. After that, the power of Wei was successively controlled by the powerful ministers of Cao Shuang and the Sima Clan, and it can not be denied that it had nothing to do with Cao Yu.

A native of Qiao County in Pei, and nephew of Cao Cao. During the Battle of Wancheng, Zhang Xiu yielded surrender before he rebelled again and attacked Cao's army at night, with the result that Cao Anmin, Cao Ang (Son of Cao Cao), and Officer DianWei all died in this battle.

A native of Qiao County in Pei, son of Cao Zhi. Quite talented at his young age, good at riding and shooting, and versed in both literature and military affairs. Cao Zhi valued this son very much. Though born from a concubine, he was still made the heir to the throne. After the Wei Dynasty being replaced by the Jin Dynasty, because of his pity for Sima You and his father Cao Zhi, he asked Emperor Wu of Jin for intercession for Sima You. As a result, he angered Emperor Wu and was deposed for a time. Later, he was hit hard and became moody because of the death of his mother. After Cao Zhi died, he was vilified by The Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

Originally served Hao Meng, who was Lu Bu's subordinate. When Hao Meng betrayed Lu Bu, he chased Hao Meng with Gao Shun and cut off Hao Meng's arm. Hao Meng eventually died at the hands of Gao Shun. After the rebellion was put down, he reported that Hao Meng and Chen Gong secretly contacted with Yuan Shu, both of which showed signs of betrayal. In "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms", Cao Xing was one the "Eight Powerful Officers" of Lu Bu. When Lu Bu was fighting with Cao Cao, he shot Xiahou Dun blind. Xiahou Dun was wounded and killed Cao Xing.

A native of Qiao County in Pei, the Emperor Yuan, who was the last emperor of the Wei Dynasty. After Cao Mao was killed, Cao Huan was enthroned by Sima Zhao. He reigned for five years before Sima Yan usurped the throne to end Wei and established the Jin Dynasty.

A native of Qiao County in Pei, son of Cao Zhen and younger brother of Cao Shuang. There were not many records in the official history. After the Rebellion of Gaoping Mausoleum, he and his brother Cao Shuang were killed by Sima Yi.

A native of Qiao County in Pei, son of Cao Cao. After the Rebellion of Gaoping Mausoleum, the power of the Cao Clan was usurped, and the Sima Clan grew their disobedience. Cao Biao and Wang Ling conspired to rise up against the Sima Clan in Shouchun, but their deeds were revealed and were all executed by Sima Yi.

A native of Qiao County in Pei, daughter of Cao Rui, Princess Qichang. Her name was not recorded in the official history, and Cao Qing was a fictitious name in this game. It was only recorded that she first married Li Tao, the son of Li Feng. Li Feng set himself against Sima Shi and led the death of the family, but Cao Qing were spared because she was the princess. Later she remarried Ren Kai.
Born in Qiaoxian, Peiguo, daughter of Cao Cao. Together with her sisters Cao Xian and Cao Jie, she was sent to the seraglio of Emperor Xian of the Han Dynasty.

Born in Qiaoxian, Peiguo, son of Cao Cao. At a young age, his mother Chen and Cao Cao died. He brought up by Cao Pi, so he often called Cao Pi "a Weng" when he was young. In ancient Chinese, "a Weng" is a honorific name for grandfather, father, husband's father or older man.

Born in Qiaoxian, Peiguo, daughter of Cao Cao. Together with her sisters Cao Xian and Cao Hua, she was sent to the seraglio of Emperor Xian of the Han Dynasty. The official history records are quite different from those in Luo Guanzhong's Romance of the Three Kingdoms. When Cao Pi usurped the Han Dynasty, she angrily denounced the envoy who asked for the jade seal and cursed: "The heaven will not let you last long!"
A fictional character, daughter of Cao Cao.

Born in Qiaoxian, Peiguo, son of Cao Cao. He died prematurely due to frailty. In "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms" and many unconventional histories, most of them made up that Cao Pi hold Cao Xiong accountable because he did not come to worship Cao Cao, causing Cao Xiong to hang himself in fear of crime.

He was the son of Cao Huo, a native of Jimmy County, Pei Guo. He was said to be a man of great talent. Before Emperor Ming's death, he ordered Cao Zhao to return to his position as a marquis, and ordered him to leave his post.

The fourth emperor of Cao Wei, who had no posthumous title of emperor because of Sima Zhao's false accusation, and was only called Noble Township Duke. After Sima Shi abolished Cao Fang, he wanted to establish Cao Ju, King of Pengcheng, the son of Cao Cao, as the emperor. In order to protect her status, Empress Dowager Guo opposed Sima Shi's establishment of Cao Ju, and finally changed the young Cao Mao into a puppet emperor. Zhong Hui once appreciated Cao Mao that he can shoulder the great responsibility of the country. As Cao Mao grew older, he was dissatisfied with Sima Zhao's dictatorship and power. He led 300 people to fight against Sima Zhao. Sima Zhao sent troops to suppress him and sent Cheng Ji to kill Cao Mao.
Born in Qiaoxian, Peiguo, daughter of Cao Cao. Together with her sisters Cao Hua and Cao Jie, she was sent to the seraglio of Emperor Xian.
Born in Qiaoxian, Peiguo, the son of Cao Cao. After Sima Shi abolished Cao Fang, the young emperor, he wanted to make Cao Ju emperor, but he gave up at the request of Empress Dowager Guo.

Born in Qiaoxian, Peiguo, son of Cao Zhen, younger brother of Cao Shuang. When Cao Shuang controlled the court, Cao Xi repeatedly advised Cao Shuang to pay attention to his actions; on the eve of Gaoping Tombs Incident, he also advised Cao Shuang to be cautious and not to ignore Sima Yi. But Cao Shuang didn't care, and eventually died.

Born in Qiaoxian, Peiguo. He is from the same family as Cao Zhen. Cao Zhen's surname is Qin. If so, Cao Zun's real name was Qin Zun. In his early years, he served Cao Cao with Cao Zhen, but died early. 
In the romance of the Three Kingdoms, Cao Zun died under Wei Yan during the first northern expedition.

A fictional character for the movie "Three Kingdoms: Resurrection of the Dragon". In the play, she was the granddaughter of Cao Cao, who was both literate and martial. She inherited Cao Cao's way of using troops and philosophy of life, and defeated the Shu army.

Born in Zhexian, Chen County, an official of Cao Wei. As local official, he had achievements in governance, so he was appreciated by Cao Cao and promoted to be the Inspector of Bingzhou. During his tenure, he made outstanding political achievements, selected talents and subdued barbarians, and no one can compare with him.

Yuan Shu's subordinate. When Cao Cao personally led an army to attack Yuan Shu, Yuan Shu fled in a hurry, leaving Qiao Rui, Li Feng, Liang Gang and Le Jiu behind. All four generals were executed after their defeat.

Born in Lujiang, Yangzhou. He rebelled with several Di tribes of Chen Lan when Cao Cao came to Jingzhou. Cao Cao sent Yu Jian and Zang Ba to fight against him. Mei Cheng was defeated. After pretending to surrender, he fled to the Mount Qian and occupied the critical Mount Tianzhu. He dealt with Cao Jun, communicated with Sun Quan, and received Han Dang's assistance. Finally, Zhang Liao led the army to attack the and wiped out the Tianzhu Mountain bandits in one fell swoop.

Born in Changyi, Shanyang, Cao Cao's subordinate. He eagered to learn and became a talent. Cao Cao heard it and recruited him to become an official. Later, he was appointed the Governor of Lelang and was forcibly detained by Gongsun Du on the way, hoping to let him tu serve under him, but Liang Mao resolutely refused. Gongsun Du took advantage of Cao Cao's expedition to Wuwan to discuss with his subordinates the opportunity to subjugate Ye, which was severely condemned by Liang Mao.

The fictitious character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms". A general served under Lu Xun of Wu. During the Battle of Yiling, Lu Xun ordered him to lead his troops to attack Fu Tong in order to explore Shu army. As a result, he was defeated and narrowly escaped back to Wu camp. However, Lu Xun also learned how the Shu army was deployed and decided to burn the camp of Shu army.

A native of Jinan County. After Emperor Shao was replaced by Emperor Xian by Dong Zhuo, he was appointed as Engineering Supervisor. When Li Fu became a power holder, he was appointed Education Supervisor. He was later dismissed for some reason.

Born in Guanjin, Anping. He was the son of Qian Zhao. He was an official of Wei and the Western Jin Dynasty. At that time, he was the Governor of Longxi. He fought against Shu with Deng Ai. After Shu's subjugation, Lan Hong was appointed the Governor of Shu. After Jin replaced Wei, he was appointed Inspector of Yangzhou. He once defeated Ding Feng, a famous general of Wu. He was also criticized for being "bold and resourceless, headstrong and can't calm the border", and finally died in the Tufa Shujineng rebellion.

Born in Guanjin, Anping, he was very friendly with Liu Bei in his teenage time. He first served under Yuan Shao and Yuan Shang, and later served under Cao Cao. When Ye was surrounded by Cao Cao, he was recruited to supervise the transportation of military rations. Yuan Shang had lost, Qian Zhao had to demote to Cao. Although he was a subordinate of Cao Cao, he also offered sacrifices to the dead yuan Shang, with a heroic personality. Later, he served as the Governor of Yanmen and made a lot of contributions to fighting against foreign nationalities at the border and digging channels. He rescued Tian Yu surronded by Kebuneng and warned the court of the possibility of the joint attack of Shu and Kebineng on Wei. He's a general in northern border as famous as Tian Yu.

A native of Dongping, Yanzhou, a Cao Wei official. When Cao Pi was reigning, he was confiscated as Prince Literary, so he was friendly with Cao Rui. After Cao Rui came to the throne, his son married Cao Rui's daughter. Bi Gui was arrogant because of the emperor's grace. Later, he became a confidant of Cao Shuang. In Gaoping Tombs Incident, he and Cao Shuang were both killed.

Born in Kuaiji, Yangzhou, he was friendly with Kong Rong. He was the Governor of Wu County and resigned due to illness. When Sun Ce pacified Jiangdong, he was afraid of Sheng Xian because of his reputation. Kong Rong worried that his friends would encounter accidents, and asked Cao Cao to recruit Sheng Xian to enter the court. However, Sheng Xian was already killed by Sun Quan.
Subordinate of Yuan Shao. During the Battle of Guandu, he escorted the grain with Chunyu Qiong and others. Cao Jun was killed when Cao force attacked Wuchao granary at night.

Originally the Heishan Bandit, he together with Yu Du and Bai Rao raided Dong County, but was defeated by Cao Cao. Later Zhang Yang's subordinate Yang Chou killed Zhang Yang and led the troops to Cao Cao, but Yang Chou was immediately killed by Sui Gu. Sui Gu collected all of them, stationed the army in Shequan, and wanted to join Yuan Shao in the north. Cao Cao sent troops to attack Sui Gu, and Sui was beheaded by Shi Huan, a general of Cao's army.

Born in Xiangyang, Jingzhou, he followed Liu Bei in his early years. After Guan Yu was defeated and killed, Wu attacked Jingzhou and all counties fell. Xi Zhen fought alone in Lingling. The Wu general Pan Jun tried to recruit Xi Zhen, but Xi Zhen angrily rebuked: "I'd rather be a ghost of the Han than a subordinate of Wu, and you can't force me." In the end, due to the lack of food and reinforcements, he drew his sword and committed suicide.
A native of Xiangyang, Jingzhou, daughter of Xi Zhu and wife of Li Heng. She has virtuous insight and has given her husband several suggestions, which has benefited Li Heng a lot.

A native of Xiangyang, Jingzhou, subordinate to Liu Bei. He is quite famous in the Jingxiang area, slightly inferior to Pangtong, and as famous as Ma Liang. But for some reason he seems to have not been entrusted, and there are not many records in history books.
One of Emperor Wen of Wei's most beloved concubines, Mo Qiongshu combed his hair into "cicada temples" style. Look's like ethereal wings of a cicada, so call it "cicada temples".

A native of Gaoyang , Jizhou, a Cao Wei official. His wife Ruan is ugly but talented. At the time of Gaoping Tombs Incident, Xu Yun, who was Shizhong the time, and Chen Tai, the Chief Imperial Secretariat, went to persuade Cao Shuang to surrender. After Cao Shuang surrendered, he was promoted to Chief Imperial Secretariat and the Imperial Guards Commander due to his merits. After failing to conspire with Xiahou Xuan and Li Feng to kill Sima Shi, he was exiled to Lelang and died on the way.

Born in Xiangyang, Jingzhou, first served under Cao Cao, and later defected with Chen Gong and others to Lu Bu. After Lu Bu's defeat, he took refuge in Liu Biao. He has a false name and no real talent. He was despised by Chen Deng and deeply hated. He even mentioned it when Liu Biao was entertaining guests, and was denounced by Liu Bei.

Served as Governor of Wu Jun. Sun Ce dominated Jiangdong, Xu Gong also lost to him, and Wu Jun was taken by Sun Ce. Xu Gong secretly appeared to the court, saying, "Sun Ce is similar to Xiang Ji, should be favored and summoned back to the capital. He has to be returned by the imperial edict, if he is released, it will be a disaster to the country." He persuaded Cao Cao to summon Sun Ce to Xudu. But the letter was intercepted by Sun Ce, and Xu Gong was killed and his family scattered. But Xu Gong's sects vowed revenge. Later, Sun Ce was assassinated by the Xu Gong sects when he's out hunting, and was wounded to death.
A native of Nanyang, Jingzhou, an official of Shu Han. He entered Shu with Xu Jing and was appointed as a Boshi, in charge of classics.

Born in Qiaoxian, Peiguo, a general of Wei, son of Xu Chu. During the war of Wei exterminating Shu, Zhong Hui ordered Xu Yi to open the way for the pioneer. He led the army to follow him. He passed a bridge. The hoof of Zhong Hui's horse stuck in the crack of the bridge. Later, Zhong Hui executed Xu Yi by military law because he failed to fulfill the responsibility of the pioneer in regulating the road. The fault was minor and Xu Yi should not be beheaded. The whole state of Wei was shocked. Historians of later generations believed that Xu's father and son were loyal to Cao's family. At that time, the people in power were Sima family. Zhong Hui was keen to cling to dignitaries, so he killed Xu Yi to make approaches to Sima's family.

The leader of the civil uprising in the late Eastern Han Dynasty. When Qu Xing led more than 10000 people to attack the besieged city of Changsha, Guo Shi and the Zhou Chao also set up troops in Lingling and Guiyang. However, they were all suppressed by Sun Jian, the Governor of Changsha. Sun Jian was awarded the Duke of Wucheng for his meritorious service.
The daughter of Guo Qian, the Du Liao General. She studied "Ling Fei Jing" and enlightened.
Born in Guangzong, Anping, the elder sister of Emperor Cao Pi. She married to the descendants of Mencius.

A native of Xiping, Liangzhou, an official from Cao Wei. After defeated by Jiang Wei, he was forced to surrender to Shu Han. He tried to assassinate Liu Chan, but failed because the guards prevented him from approaching. Later, when Fei Yi hosted a banquet, he assassinated Fei Yi.

A native of Peiguo, Yuzhou, he's Yuan Shang's subordinate, Zhong You's nephew. Yuan Shang orcered Huchuquan, Gao Gan, and Guo Yuan to attack Cao Cao. Zhong You sent Zhang Ji to lobby Ma Teng, and Ma Teng sent Ma Chao and Pang De to help Zhong Yao and Cao's army. They defeated Guo Yuan, who was killed by Pang De. Seeing Guo Yuan's head, Zhong Yu teared and said, "Although Guo Yuan is a nephew, he's a traitor of the country."

Born in Guangzong, Anping, the empress of Cao Pi, Emperor Wen of Wei. The official history does not record her name, and the name of Guo Zhao is fabricated by later generations. He lost his parents early and was exiled in distress. Later, he was recruited into the Palace and became a member of the prince's seraglio. Cao Rui, Emperor Ming of Wei was born to Zhen. After Zhen died, Cao Pi ordered her to raise Cao Rui.

Born in Yangqu, Taiyuan, she is the stepwife of Jia Chong, a powerful minister in the Western Jin Dynasty, and the mother of Jia Nanfeng, Queen of Emperor Hui of Jin. She is jealous and lacks virtue, but she has repeatedly warned Jia Nanfeng to be kind to crown prince Sima Yu and stay away from Zhao Can and Jia Wu. But Jia Nanfeng remained the same and hurt Sima Yu even more. Therefore, Sima Lun, King of Zhao, launched an attack and killed Jia Nanfeng.

A native of Jinyang, Taiyuan, or named Guo Huan. Rendu is known for his high kindheartedness and righteousness. After Han Sui was defeated, he returned from Qianghu and was attached to Guo Xian. Many people persuaded Guo Xian to kill Han Sui to show favor to Cao Cao, but he all refused. After Cao Cao heard about Guo Xian's actions, he was amazed and named him Guan Neihou.

A native of Henei, Shuhan official. There are only two records in the history books. One is that Zhuge Liang opened the mansion and named Jiang Wan as Maocai. Jiang Wan declined, hoping to replace it with Yinhua and others. The second is Sun Quan wrote a letter to Zhuge Liang, saying: "Only Deng Zhi is the only country in the two countries." There is a slight dissatisfaction with the Yinhua.
A native of Lujiang, Songzi, was a Commander of Dong Wu, and his grandfather Chen Wu was among the twelve tiger ministers. However, there is no detailed life record of Chen Yong in the historical.

A native of Runan, Yuzhou, a general of Shuhan. Following Liu Bei for a long time, his loyalty and courage are not inferior to Zhao Yun. The same generals of the four Armies, but most of the relevant historical materials lost. When Liu Bei was in Yuzhou, Chen Daoying had already taken refuge under his command. The troops under his jurisdiction were Liu Bei's elite guards "Bai Mao". Zhuge Liang once called the Bai Mao soldiers "Western soldiers." In the Battle of Changban, Liu Bei was able to retreat smoothly by relying on Baimao soldiers; when Yiling was defeated, the troops after the break might also be Baimao soldiers. Another said that the Baimao soldiers were elite soldiers from the "Five Tribes of Qing Qiang" ethnic minorities in the southwest, and they should have been established after Liu Bei entered Shu. After Liu Bei's death, Chen Dao and Li Yan guarded the Baidi Fortress and led Yongan Governor. Both places were critically important in the Shu Han, which shows that he is worthy of an important task. Although the name is not mentioned in "The Romance", historians of later generations believe that many of the achievements of Zhao Yun in "The Romance" and many unofficial histories may actually be Chen Dao's.
A native of Lujiang, Songzi, was a Commander of Dong Wu, and his grandfather Chen Wu was among the twelve tiger ministers. However, there is no detailed life record of Chen Yan in the historical.

A native of Lujiang, Songzi, the son of the Dong Wu general Chen Wu, had a reputation when he was young, and was elected to serve the then prince Sun Deng in the Eastern Palace. He was upright and filial. After his father died in the war, Chen Biao joined the army. He was very popular because of his kind treatment to the soldiers. Later, a rebellion broke out in Dong Wu, and Chen Biao said that his military situation was urgent, and he sent troops across the border to quell the rebellion without waiting for orders. Due to the special political environment of the Dong Wu, neither Sun Quan nor the Prime General Lu Xun blamed Chen Biao, but put him in an important position. But he passed away at the age of thirty-four.

A native of Yingchuan, Xuchang. An official of the Western Jin Dynasty. From a young age, he was known for his reputation, loyal and straightforward, without fear of officials, princes and kings. When the Upheaval of the Eight Princes occurred, Sima Lun, the king of Zhao, intended to usurp the throne. Chen Zhun tried to support the Huainan King Sima Yun to kill Sima Lun and deceived Emperor Jin Hui's White Tiger Banner. However, Fu Yin, who carried the flag to announcement, was given a heavy profit by the king of Zhao, who deceived Sima Yun to get down from the horse and assassinated Sima Yun.

A native of Sheyang , Guangling County. Serve the East County Governor Zang Hong. When Yuan Shao attacked Zang Hong, Zang Hong sent Chen Rong out of the city to avoid the disaster, and then Zang Hong was defeated and captured. Yuan Shao persuaded Zang Hong to surrender bu failed, so killed Zang Hong, but Chen Rong spoke out from a sense of justice and died together with Zang Hong.

A native of Xiapi, Xuzhou, the father of Chen Deng, Hua Tuo was elected filial piety during the tenure of Prime Minister Pei Guo. After Liu Bei took over as Xuzhou Mu, Chen Gui was noncommittal. However, after Lu Bu became the master, Chen Gui was very opposed to it. Various designs prevented Lu Bu from allying with Yuan Shu. However, when Yuan Shu's army attacked, Chen Gui tried to protect Xuzhou, just for Lu Bu out of the enemy. In the end, he sent his son Chen Deng to contact Cao Cao, as the inner ought to eliminate Lu Bu.

A native of Runan County, an official of the Han Dynasty, the grand-nephew of the celebrity Xu Jing, another version is nephew. When he was young, he was very talented, which was appreciated by Fei Yi, the Book of Documents of Shu Han at that time. After Fei Yi became Prime General, Chen Zhi was promoted as a servant, as a crony of Liu Chan. After Book of Documents was vacant, Fei Yi appointed Chen Zhi as an agent. Generally speaking, Chen Zhi colluded with the eunuch and was the sinner who caused the defeat of the Shu Han. However, due to the long-term love of Fei Yi, Chen Zhi was also a staunch supporter of the Northern Expedition. He even tried his best to protect Jiang Wei. In addition, Chen Zhi is good at arts such as divination.
A native of Lujiang, Songzi, son of Chen Biao, official of Soochow. The history books only record that Chen Aobai was the Mounts Supervisor of the other ministry, and he was given 400 soldiers.
A native of Yanzhou, Dongjun, daughter of Chen Gong. Chen Xue's name is a fictitious fiction.

A native of Hanzhong, Chenggu, was the wife of Zhang Ze. When Zhang Ze was an official in Fufeng, his subordinates suggested that the people should be governed by severe punishment and law. Chen Huiqian suggested to his husband: "Extend moral education, foster integrity and avoid shame." Education should be promoted and the people should be governed by morality. People at the time praised him as "the talent of the female Book of Documents."

A native of Runan, Yangzhou Inspector in the late Eastern Han Dynasty. Befriend with Cao Hong. At the beginning of Cao Cao's army, he went to Yangzhou to recruit soldiers. Chen Wen and Danyang Governor Zhou Xinyi helped Cao Cao more than 4, 000 people; he also sponsored Cao Hong two thousand Lujiang elite soldiers. Later, Yuan Shu was defeated by Cao Cao, and when he fled to Jiujiang, he killed Chen Wen.

A native of Huaipu, Xiapi. Was originally a member of Yuan Shu. After losing to Cao Cao, Yuan Shu defected to Chen Yu, but Chen Yu was unwilling to accept Yuan Shu, Yuan Shu turned to attack Chen Yu, and Chen Yu fled. Later he became the Governor of Wu county, and he clashed with Sun Ce, was defeated by Sun Ce, and defected to Yuan Shao.

A native of Hanan, Baxi, the author of "Three Kingdoms", an official in the last years of the Shu Han Dynasty, he served as the First Secretary of Gaurd General Wei Jiang, who was later dismissed by the eunuch Huang Hao. After the fall of the Shu Han, he was promoted by Zhang Hua, a great official of the Western Jin Dynasty, and served as a historian in the Jin Dynasty. He collected many historical materials from the Shu area and wrote excellent historical books of the Shu Han. He also regained the words of many families, and cited Wang Shen's "History of Wei Dynasty" and Yu Zong. His "Wei Lue", Wei Zhao's "History of Wu Dynasty" and other books eventually became the "Three Kingdoms".

A fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms", a subordinate of Liu Yao, the Inspector of Yangzhou. Liu Yao sent Xue Li, Zhang Ying, and Chen Heng to defend Moling. When Sun Ce attacked the city, Xue Li shot him down. Xue Li thought that Sun Ce was dead, so he sent Chen Heng and Zhang Ying out of the city to pursue them. Sun Ce led an ambush army to fight out suddenly, and his subordinate Jiang Qin shot Chen Heng to death with an arrow.

The fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms", is a subordinate of Zhao Fan, the Governor of Guiyang . When Liu Bei dispatched Zhao Yun to attack Guiyang, Chen Ying led three thousand soldiers to fight, and Zhao Yun singled out, but he knew that he was invincible when he failed the four or five rounds, and was captured by Zhao Yun. Later, he designed a surrender with Zhao Fan, but Zhao Yun saw it through and headed them.

A native of Linhuai Dongyang, an officer of Wei and the son of Chen Jiao. Founding father of the Jin Dynasty. When he was a teenager, he saw things wisely, did not be surprised at changes, possessed both civil and military skills, and was knowledgeable. After adulthood, the official movement prospered all the way, returned to the court during the reign of Sima Shi, loyal to Sima's family, participated in many conquests of the Shu Han and put down the Huainan mutiny, due to the wisdom of others, and good at supervising and commanding, all have military exploits. After Sima Yan usurped the Wei Dynasty, Chen Qian was promoted to Cheqi general and Great general, and he was the most important military attache hero in the creation of the Jin Dynasty.
A fictional character, daughter of Tao Qian.
"Liu's Genealogy Han Dynasty Genealogy Preface Ninth" records it as Liu Chan's harem concubine.

A native of Danyang, Moling was born in Sun Wu and the Western Jin Dynasty. When Sun Hao rebelled in Jiaozhou, officials killed Jiaozhi Governor and surrendered to the Western Jin Dynasty. Tao Huang volunteered for the thief and was defeated for the first time, but Tao Huang launched a night attack that night to regain a city, and then took a surprise attack Jiaozhi by sea. Not only did he see through the ambush, he also cleverly diplomatic alienation the enemy and gained an advantage. Sun Hao then ordered Tao Huang to take over as Jiaozhou Mu and started a long-term confrontation with the Western Jin Dynasty there. After the Eastern Wu descended to the Jin Dynasty, Emperor Wu of Jin once wanted to take the opportunity to take back the heavy soldiers. But Linyi's border incursions, the number of soldiers of Jiaozhou was not cut.

Born in Moling, Danyang, he served in Wu and Western Jin Dynasty. In the later period of the eastern Wu Dynasty, he was a military general, governor of Xuling and concurrently a shepherd of Jingzhou. In the third year of Tianji, there was a rebellion in Jiaozhou. Tao Jun led 7000 soldiers to detour from the west to cooperate with his brother Tao Huang, who was the shepherd of Jiaozhou at that time. When returning to Jingzhou, Tao Jun heard that the Jin army was going south, so he transferred to Wuchang. When he returned to Jianye the next year to report the military situation, Tao Jun said that it only needed 20000 troops to repel the enemy. However, when the soldiers arrived at the front line, they broke up. Since then, Tao Jun's whereabouts were unknown.

A native of Wuxian, Wu County, the second son of Lu Xun, a famous general in the later period of Wu. After Lu Xun was framed and depressed and died, Lu Kang defended his father, and cleared his late father, which made Sun Quan regret. Lu Kang had written to Sun Hao to put an end to eunuchs' power, as well as many suggestions on governing the country and appointing people. Unfortunately, they were not adopted. Lu Kang was the main force to resist Jin in the later period of Wu, and obstructed the south expeditions of Jin army for many times. His most famous battle was to suppress the Bu Zhan rebellion. The anecdotes he shared with Yang Hu, a general of the Jin Dynasty, were also a good story in the history.

A native of Wuxian, Wu County, an official of Wu. During the dispute of two princes, he was tortured because he kept secrets for Sun He, but he did not reveal a single word. Later, due to the rebellion of Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen, he was ordered to put down the rebellion. Lu Yin showed kindness to the people and quelled the civil unrest with gentle means, and as a result, more than 8, 000 soldiers were recruited in the rebel army.
A fictional character, daughter of Lu Xun.

A native of Wuxian, Wu County, an official of Wu, the son of Lu Kang. After the death of Lu Kang, his sons led his army and continued to fight against the Jin Dynasty. When Jin defeated Wu, Lu Yan and Lu Jing both died in battle.

A native of Wuxian, Wu County, and Governor fof Lujiang at the end of the Eastern Han Dynasty. He and Lu Xun belonged to the same family. His loyalty, righteousness, benevolence, governance of the locality, all convinced the people. Moreover, he was loyal to the Han Dynasty and still took the initiative to pay tribute when the political situation was chaotic. Later, Yuan Shu sent Sun Ce to attack Lu Kang because he refused to lend Yuan Shu grains. Troops and people of Lujiang rushed back to defend the city. Sun Ce and Yuan Shu army besieged the city for two years before breaching the city. Lu Kang died of illness soon after the city was breached.

Born in Wuxian, Wu County, an important minister in Wu. He was still eager to learn in the army. Later, he became more and more important and became an important minister. After Sun Hao ascended the throne, Lu Kai made several blunders. Although Sun Hao was dissatisfied, because the Lu family was powerful and famous, and there was Lu Kang besides Lu Kai, Sun Hao dared not harm him. After Lu Kai and Lu Kang died, he sentenced Lu Kai's family to exile.

A native of Wuxian, Wu County, he's Lu Xun's nephew, and he served in Wu and the Western Jin Dynasty. He was famous when he was young, and he's studious and talented. He claimed to have written many books, but most of them have been lost.

A native of Wuxian, Wu County, an official of Wu, the son of Lu Kang. After the death of Lu Kang, his sons led his army and continued to fight against the Jin Dynasty. When Jin defeated Wu, Lu Yan and Lu Jing both died in battle.

A native of Wuxian, Wu County, an official of the eastern Wu Dynasty, and Lu Xun's younger brother, both of whom are ministers of the central court. Sun Quan wanted to send troops to Liaodong for an expedition because of repeated rebellion by Gongsun Yuan, the governor of Liaodong, to kill the envoys of Wu. Lu Mao wrote successively, analyzed the current situation, stated his interests, obtained Sun Quan's approval and gave up sending troops.

A native of Wuxian, Wu County, an official of Wu, and the son of Lu Kai. Once served as the Imperial Assistant, and later served as an Assistant General. After Lu Kai died, he was transferred back to the central court. Hua He, the imperial historian, once praised Lu Yi, saying that his commander is better than Lu Su.

Born in Wuxian, Wu County, the daughter of Lu Ji. At the age of thirteen, she married Zhang Bai from the same county. But only three months after the marriage, Zhang Bai was implicated in the case of his brother Zhang Wen, and was sent into exile and died of illness. Lu Yusheng kept the chastity for him and refused to remarry.

Jing Zhaoren, Cao Wei official and historian. After Jin replaced Wei, he was not an official for life. The privately written "Wei Lue" has now been lost, and it is generally believed that "Dian Lue" is also part of this book. When Pei Songzhi and other later historians made annotations for "Three Kingdoms", they quoted a lot of "Wei Lue".

Born in Niyang, Beidi, he served in Wei and Western Jin Dynasty, and is a famous literati. He once participated in the compilation of the History of Wei Dynasty. After Wei replaced by Jin Dynasty, he was highly valued by Sima Yan, Emperor Wu of Jin.

A native of Niyang, Beidi, an official of Wei. He once persuaded Liu Cong to surrender Cao Cao. He is well versed in the way of being an official, whether it is to write a joint letter with the officials to persuade Cao Pi to take the throne; or to imply that Su Ze, so that Su will not be implicated. He is also known for his knowledge of people, judging Pang Tong, Pei Qian and others, all as he said.

A native of Yiyang County, the son of Shu Han general Fu Rong. Fu Rong followed Liu Bei to crusade against Wu and died in the battle of Yiling. Fu Qian was appointed as Palace Gentleman of the Left because of his father's merit. In the battle to destroy Shu, Fu Qian was ordered to resist Cao Wei. Jiang Shu betrayed Shu, and he led Wei to attack Yang'an Pass. Fu Qian died in battle.

A native of Niyang, Beidi, and an official from Cao Wei. At the age of 18, he became famous and was recruited by Engineering Supervisor Chen Qun as a subordinate. When Cao Shuang was in power, Fu Peng was dismissed for commenting that He Yan's "indulgence in personal interests and neglect of his own work". He once proposed a strategy for Cao Wei's attack on Wu, but it was not adopted. Although he was a official of Wei, he did his best to assist Sima Shi and Sima Zhao brothers.
A Yamen General of Wu, and a confidant of Sun Yi, Sun Quan's younger brother. After Sun Yi was assassinated, Sun Gao and Fu Ying helped Sun Yi's wife Xu kill Gui Lan and Dai Yuan.

A native of Shanyang County, and a Cao Wei official. Participated in Linggu Yu and Wang Ling's plan to overthrow Sima Yi. After their deeds were revealed, he was executed by Sima Yi for not reporting.

A native of Zhi, Qiao County, he was an official of Cao Wei and one of the seven sages of the bamboo grove. He opened the beginning of Wei-Jin metaphysics, and indulged in recklessness. Because of his talent and reputation, he offended Zhong Hui and was hated by Zhong Hui. Later, he was involved in the family affairs of the Lu Xun and Lu An brothers, defending Lu An, and was implicated in jail. At that time, the country's celebrities and three thousand students of Taixue were all begging for Ji Kang, but Zhong Hui took the opportunity to slander, and Sima Zhao finally decided to execute Ji Kang. Before his execution, Ji Kang asked for the Yaoqin from his elder brother Ji Xi, and calmly played a piece of "Guangling San". After the song, he sighed: "The"Guangling San" is severed today!"

A native of Zhi, Qiao County, he was the elder brother of Ji Kang and had been served in Wei and the Western Jin Dynasty. He was quite capable of commanding troops. He had resisted the invasion of the Wu and pacified the rebellion of generals of Wu. In the Book of Jin, he was called "a talent in the world."

A native of Gunghan, Yizhou. He was once punished by Liu Zhang, and he defected to Liu Bei. He was recommended by Pang Tong and Fa Zheng, but his "great ambitions are hard to be safe." After being entrusted, he became more arrogant and domineering. As a result, he was demoted. He tried to instigate Ma Chao to rebel. Ma Chao informed, and eventually he was convicted and killed.
The names are found in "Record of Gleanings". Chao Shu, Li Ju, Luo Zhen, and Jie Hua are the four concubines favored by Sun Liang, monarch of Wu.

Born in Changshe, Yingchuan, a subordinate of Cao Cao. He had followed Cao Cao in the Anti-Dong coalition.
