When Chen Gong rebelled against Cao and welcomed Lu Bu into Yanzhou, Zao Zhi stood firm in Dong E. In the first year of Jian'an, Cao Cao defeated the Ru'nan Yellow Turban Army and acquired a large number of cattle and farm tools. So Zao Zhi wrote a letter to recommend the implementation of the farming system. According to the historical records, after a year of trial in Xudu, they "produced millions of grains," and has filled the treasury. After the success of the farming method, Zao Zhi suggested that the military farming should be implemented again, and Cao Cao should follow it. But soon after, Zao Zhi died of illness. Many years later, Cao Cao still felt nostalgic for Zao Zhi because of his work in farming system and the friendship he followed in his early years.

Born in Rencheng County, he was a Cao Wei official. There are not many records in the history books, and all that are mentioned are his outspoken and daring remonstrance, and he has repeatedly admonished Cao Pi and Cao Rui.

Born in Niupi, Qianwei County, she was Zhang Wei's wife. Her deeds can be seen in "Chronicles of Huayang". After Zhang Wei's death, she was unwilling to remarry Wang Chong and committed suicide by drowning herself but survived.

Born in Langzhong, Ba County, he was first served under Liu Zhang, and later defected to Shu Han. When Pang Xi wanted to oppose Liu Zhang, Cheng Ji persuaded Pang Xi to stop, and he was entrusted by Liu Zhang. Later, Liu Bei attacked Wu for revenge of Guan Yu's death, and Cheng Ji set out with him. When the Shu army was defeated in the battle of Yiling, he refused to abandon the boat and fled. His troops were outnumbered, and he died on the battlefield.
Born in Dong E, Dongjun, a Cao Wei official, and the grandson of Cheng Yu. He is knowledgeable and once served as the Imperial Assistant and the Governor of Ru'nan.
The name of the dancing girl comes from Cao Pi's "Answers to Po Qin", in which he said that "the most wonderful dance of today comes from Jiang Shu."

Born at the end of Wei and the beginning of the Jin Dynasty, she's the wife of the Xu Jun, General of the Household. Her epitaph is included in "Compilation of Epitaphs of Han, Wei, Southern and Northern Dynasties".

A native of Gaotang, Pinyuan, he had served in the Wei Dynasty and the Western Jin Dynasty. He's the son of Hua Xin. He became an official at the age of 20. Sima Shi abolished Cao Fang and made Cao Mao emperor. Hua Biao and others welcomed Cao Mao to the throne. However, Hua Biao worried that when Cao Mao was old, he would not be willing to be suppressed by Sima, so he asked for leave under the pretext of illness, so he escaped a disaster when Sima Zhao killed Cao Mao.
Born in Gaotang, Pingyuan, he was the son of Hua Biao. He served under Cao Wei and Western Jin Dynasty. He is a historian and has compiled the Book of the Later Han Dynasty, but it has been lost.

A native of Guangling, Jiangdu, an official of Wu. Appreciated by Zhang Wen, he was promoted to Taizi Shuzi. Later, Teng Yin conspired to overthrow the power Minister Sun Chen, forcing Hua Rong and others to write a Book criticizing Teng Yin. Hua and others were killed by Teng because they refused.

A native of Wu Jun, Wu Jin, once served as the official historian of Wu. He has the talent of literature. After Sun Liang ascended the throne, he ordered Hua He, Wei Zhao, Xue Ying and others to compile the book of Wu. After learning of the demise of Shu, he wrote to Sun Xiu, King of Wu, and suggested strengthening armaments to prevent Wei from attacking Wu. In the later period of Sun Hao's reign, he was moody and punished all his officials at will. Hua He repeatedly defended his colleagues.

General Cao Wei, whose name may be Fei Yao. When Cao Zhen was in charge of Yongliang's military affairs, he was ordered to calm Zhang Jin's rebellion in Jiuquan with Zhang Ji and Xiahou Ru. After Cao Pi became emperor, there were many rebellions in Xiliang, and Fei Yao followed the Inspector to suppress the rebellion. He was appointed General of the Rear. Later, Zhuge Liang launched the northern expedition, and Fei Yao participated in blocking the Shu army many times, but he was often defeated by Zhuge Liang and Wei Yan. After Zhuge Liang died in Wuzhang Plains, there was no record of Fei Yao in history books.
Born in Jiangxia, Jingzhou, he was originally a subordinate of Liu Zhang, and later submitted to Shu Han. When Liu Bei attacked Yizhou, he defended Mianzhu Pass with Li Yan. Li Yan's close friend.

A native of Shanyin, Kuaiji, an official of Wu. Sun Hao angered Sun Hao for his fearlessness and straightforward advice, and was slandered by Sun Hao. Later, he had a stroke and couldn't speak, but Sun Hao suspected that he pretended to be ill, so he sent him to prison and tortured him to death. After He Shao died, his family was exiled to Linhai County.

A native of Shanyin, Kuaiji, an official of Wu. Gongsun yuan courted Sun Quan, who sent Zhang Mi, Xu Yan, He Da and others to Liaodong. However, Gongsun Yuan worried that Wu was far away and could not provide immediate assistance. He also wanted to make up with Wei, so he killed He Da and others, cut their head and sent them to Wei.

A native of Shanyin, Kuaiji, a general of Wu. When he was a young county official, he attacked Si Cong, who was in collusion with Shanyue, and successfully suppressed the rebels and frightened Shanyue by leading the local officials and civilians. After that, he made the main contribution of conquering local unrest and bandits, and created many new counties. When the Wei army attacked Ruxukou, He Qi and Lu Xun worked together to suppress the rebellion in Poyang County, and then became Andong General. He Qi is luxurious, but Sun Quan believes that he is not too polite. He still values his talent and trusts him.

Han Fu's Lieutenant. Han Fu wants to give Jizhou to Yuan Shao. Min Chun and Geng Wu advise Han Fu together, but Han Fu refuses. After Yuan Shao took over Jizhou, Min Chun was killed by Tian Feng under Yuan's command.

A fictional character in The Romance of the Three Kingdoms. She's Dong Cheng's concubine, and she had an affair with Qin Qingtong, a family slave, that led to the leakage of the Secret Imperial Edict.

A native of Anping County, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. He's a sycophant and was favored because he flattered Emperor Sima Yan of the Jin Dynasty. He was friendly with Jia Chong and Xun Kai and persuaded Sima Yan to let Prince Sima Zhong marry Jia Nanfeng, Jia Chong's daughter. He repeatedly slandered good generals and the backbone of the imperial clan. Zhang Hua and Sima You were alienated, and Sima You died of worry and anger.

Born in Nanjun, Jingzhou, a general of Shu Han. He followed Liu Bei when he entered Shu. Later, Liu Bei avenged Guan Yu and marched eastward against Wu. With Feng Xi as the commander, he breached two cities and defeated Li Yi. The army stationed in Yiling and joined Liu Bei's army. Unexpectedly, Lu Xun found out the camp of the Shu army and attacked the Shu army with fire. Feng Xi was killed by the subordinates of Pan Zhang, a Wu general in the chaotic situation.

Originally the Governor of Hanjia County of Shu Han. After the defeat of Yiling, Liu Bei fell ill in Baidi Fortress, Zhuge Liang rushed to the Fortress from Chengdu. Taking advantage of the emptiness of Chengdu, Huang Yuan started a rebellion, but was immediately denounced by Zheng Chuo and Chen Hu.

A native of Langzhong, Baxi, an official of the Han Dynasty, and the son of Huang Quan. When Wei invaded Shu, he and Zhuge Zhan fought against the Wei army together, persuaded Zhuge Zhan to seize the critical position and stifle Wei army, but Zhuge Zhan hesitated and missed the opportunity. Shu army retreated to Mianzhu, and Zhuge Zhan, Huang Chong, etc. were all sacrificed.

Wu official. He went to Liaodong with Zhang Mi, Xu Yan and he Da, but Gongsun Yuan defected to Cao Wei and killed Zhang Mi, Xu Yan and others, while Qin Dan, Zhang Qun, Du de and Huang Qiang were detained in Xuantu. The latter four fled to Koguryo. They skillfully persuaded the king of Koguryo, got the help of the king of Koguryo and returned to Wu.

Born in Anlu, Jiangxia. He involved in Party Forbiddance incident and imprisoned for more than 20 years. In the Dong Zhuo insurrection, he conspired with Wang Yun, the Education Supervisor, to kill Dong Zhuo. After Li Jue and Guo Si breached Chang'an, Huang Wan was imprisoned and died in prison.

An eunuch of Shu, favored by Liu Chan. When Dong Yun was alive, he often controlled Huang Hao. After Dong Yun died, Huang Hao was arbitrary and persecuted ministers. When Zhong Hui and Deng Ai attacked Shu, Huang Hao used divination to predict the national situation. Liu Chan was convinced and refused to send reinforcements. After that, he often hid the military information and reported good news without bad news, which finally led to Deng Ai's capture of Chengdu. After the subjugation of Shu, Deng Ai wanted to kill Huang Hao. His subordinates was bribed by Huang Hao and let him escaped.

A native of Jiuquan, Liangzhou, he's an official from Cao Wei. He rebelled with Qu Yan and Zhang Jin, and was defeated by Su Ze and Zhang Ji, and then he pledged allegiance to Cao Wei. Later, Wang Ling plotted to overthrow Sima and sent Yang Hong to contact Huang Hua, but Yang Hong and Huang Hua informed Sima Yi of the matter. Wang Ling committed suicide.
A fictional character, daughter of Huang Zhong.
The fictitious characters in the Henan opera "Catch the Gold" and "Receiving Ma Dai". Originally a femail bandit and later married Ma Dai as his wife.
Yuan Shu's subordinate. Yang Hong and Zhang Xun planned to defect to Sun Ce, but they were ambushed by Liu Xun, the Governor of Lujiang on the way, and there was no record thereafter.

Born in Wannian, Fengyi. He had the demeanor of Cao Cao when he was a district captain of Luoyang in the past. He was not afraid of dignitaries and killed Cao Hong's illegal disciples. Therefore, Cao Cao appreciated him and ordered him to be the county magistrate of Yexian. Later, he was promoted to Capital Mayor.

A native of Ba County, Yizhou, he served as an official in Shu Han and the Western Jin Dynasty. When Shu Han subjugated, Yang Zong joined the army of Luo Xian, the Governor of Badong. Wu took the opportunity to invade and besiege Yong'an. Luo Xian sent Yang Zong to break through and ask the Wei army for help. After that, Yang Zong repelled the invasion of Wu army several times. During his tenure as the Governor of Wuling, he comforted the Wuxi barbarians and made the barbarians submit.

A native of Tianshui County, he served in Cao Wei and the Western Jin Dynasty. He once followed Deng Ai to subjgate Shu, made meritorious service. After Qian Hong, he became the Inspector of Liangzhou and put down Linghu Hong's rebellion. When Xianbei's Tufa Shujineng rebeled, Yang Xin fought Ruoluobaneng, and he's defeated and killed.

Born in Guangling, a Wu official. As a follower of Sun Ba, King of Lu, he was imprisoned by Sun Quan for leaking secrets. He could not bear the punishment and pleaded guilty. Before his death, he falsely accused Lu Xun and listed 20 crimes. Sun Quan repeatedly blamed Lu Xun for this, which led to Lu Xun's death in sorrow and anger.

A native of Huayin, Hongnong, descendant of Sima Yan, Emperor Wu of Jin, and daughter of Yang Jun. She once prevented Emperor Wu of Jin from abolishing Jia Nanfeng and advised him to restrain several times, but Jia Nanfeng held a grudge against her. After the death of Emperor Wu, Jia Nanfeng killed Yang Jun, and pointed out that empress dowager Yang was an accomplice, imprisoned her, didn't give food, and starved her to death.

A native of Tianshui, he's a Cao Wei official. He has knowledge and insight, When Cao and Yuan fought, he's sure that Cao Cao would win. Su Bo's rebellion broke out again. Yang Fu predicted that Ma Chao would make a comeback, but Cao Cao was eager to withdraw and attack Su Bo, leaving no enough troops for defense. Soon after, Ma Chao broke the border again, several counties were lost. Fortunately, Yang Fu together with Jiang Xu and Zhao Ang expelled Ma Chao.

Born in Huojia, Henei, he's a Cao Wei official. Knowledgeable and insightful, he's good at distinguishing people, and good at recommending talents. He was friendly with Cao Zhi and was hated by Cao Pi for praising Cao Zhi. After Cao Pi ascended the throne, he pleaded guilty on the grounds that the market was not prosperous enough, and finally forced Yang Jun to commit suicide.

Born in Qianwei, Yizhou, first served under Liu Zhang, and later under Liu Bei. After Yiling's defeat, Liu Bei fell ill in Baidi Fortress, Zhuge Liang rushed to the Fortress from Chengdu. Taking advantage of the emptiness of Chengdu, Huang Yuan set up a rebellion, and Yang Hong sent Chen Zhen and Zheng Chuo to attack Huang Yuan.

A native of Huayin, Hongnong, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty, and the younger brother of Yang Jun. He was the favorite Minister of Emperor Wu of Jin Dynasty, but Yang Yao knew herself and repeatedly asked for dismissal. But then he began to form parties for personal gain and framed Sima You, King of Qi. When Yang Jun was killed, his whole family was also exterminated and Yang Yao were also killed.

The subordinate of Gongsun Yuan, Governor of Liaodong. When Gongsun Yuan rebelled against Wei, Sima Yi led the army to fight. Yang Zuo was ordered to lead the army to fight against Sima Yi. He fought and lost repeatedly, and finally surrendered in Xiangping.
A subordinate of Guo Si, Yang Mi was mentioned in only one sentence in the history books. When Guo Si wanted to kill Yang Biao, Yang Mi persuaded Guo Si and Yang Biao was able to survive.

A native of Huayin, Hongnong, and the father of Yang Xiu. He came from an aristocratic family in the late Eastern Han Dynasty. After Yang Xiu was executed, Cao Cao went to offer condolences. Yang Biao said, "I am ashamed of my foresight and still cherish the love of an old ox licking the calf." this is the origin of"the old ox licking the calf".
A native of Huayin, Hongnong. Together with Zhong Yao and others, he helped Emperor Xian of the Han Dynasty ran east. It seems that he died before or after Cao Cao welcomed the emperor to Xuchang.

A native of Yuling, Xingyang, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. Bu Xie, the Commander of Xiling, rebelled and fell to Jin. Sima Yan ordered Yang Zhao, Yang Hu and Xu Yin to lead the army for assistance, but he was defeated by Lu Kang, a general of Wu, and Yang Zhao was demoted to the common people. Yang Zhao was a famous calligrapher at that time and was good at cursive and clerical writing.

Born in Qianwei, Yizhou, he has served in Shu Han and the Western Jin Dynasty. During the Jiaozhi rebellion, he led the army to win the final victory and served as Governor of Jiaozhi. But later, Yu Si and Tao Huang of Wu attacked again and captured Jiaozhi. Yang Ji and others were captured. He died when he was escorted back to Hepu.

Born in Wuyang, Qianwei, he's an official of Shu Han. He's the author of "Jihan Fuchen Praise", and because the Shu Han did not have a sole-duty historian, when Chen Shou wrote the Shu Book in Records of the Three Kingdoms, he often quoted and referred to this article. Later, he was dismissed because he refused to obey Jiang Wei and made a slip of the tongue after drinking.

A native of Huayin, Hongnong, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty, and the younger brother of Yang Jun. Known for his outstanding martial arts. He advised his brother Yang Jun several times, but they were not adopted. After the Upheaval of the Eight Princes, Jia Nanfeng killed Yang Jun and exterminated his family, and Yang Ji was exexuted.

Subordinate of Zhang Yang. When Cao Cao attacked Lu Bu, Zhang Yang wanted to help Lu Bu because they were acquaintances, but Yang Chou assassinated Zhang Yang and wanted to defect to Cao Cao, although he was killed by Sui Gu.

Native in Huayin, Hongnong. High rank official of Western Jin and father of Empress Yang Zhi. 
As Emperor Wu grew ill, he considered both Sima Liang and Yang Jun to be regent. But Yang Jun managed to make the emperor to appoint him alone. 
After he assumed his post, his dictatorship and cronyism caused disturbances among the court officials and imperial family. Later Jia Nanfeng secretly conspired with Sima Liang and Sima Wei to murder Yang Jun as well as massacred his clan.
Native in Chenggu County. His accounts can be found in the Chronicles of Huayang. The story of her teaching daughter-in-law is included in the History of Later Han.
A fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms", he is the general of Han Xuan, the governor of Changsha. He fought against Guan Yu, but was killed by him in just one round.

The first of these is the first of the two. Yang Yan died early, before her death, worried about Emperor Wu Jin's favorite concubine Hu Gui woman for the queen, and further influence the Prince of the Secretary, so recommended his sister Yang Zhi into the palace. After the death of Yang Yan, Xianning two years, Emperor Wu Jin established Yang Zhi as the queen.

Born in Qi County, Taiyuan. Cao Wei official. 
At first, he served as First Secretary under Cao Cao and later was appointed as Inspector of Yangzhou because of Cao Cao's trust. 
He was insightful. In the Battle of Fancheng, he forsaw that Cao Ren would be in danger because he was alone to defend the city and the freshet. And when Xiangyang was in crisis, he warned Pei Qian that he should hurry to send troops to the battlefield. 
Later, he was promoted to the Inspector of Liangzhou, but died en route to assuming his new offices. Cao Pi paid his condolences.

The confident Sun Hao. 
He was the magistrate of Wucheng and befriended Sun Hao, Marquis of Wucheng of the time. 
After Emperor Sun Xiu died, Wan Yu, Puyang Xing, Zhang Bu and others helped Sun Hao claim the throne. Though mediocre in talent, he became Sun Hao's only confident because of this. 
Later Sun Hao launched a military campaign, but a snowstorm on the way stopped his advance. So Wan Yu and Ding Feng secretly made arrangements to retreat without informing the emperor, who held grudge ever since. Later, Wan Yu was bestowed poisonous wine, but he luckily survived. However, knowing the emperor's intention, he became depressed and died.

Native in Langya. Taoist in Three Kingdoms period. Grandfather of Ge Hong, who is the author of Baopuzi. 
Together with Zhang Daoling, Xu Xun and Sa Shou, they were known as the Great Four Celestial Masters. 
Someone said Ge Xuan learned from Zuo Ci, while the others said he learned Lingbao Scripture from Xu Laile.

Native in Jianning, Nanzhong. He served Shu, Wei, Jin successively. In the Rebellion of Jiaozhi, he was tasked to support Lu Xing and defeated Wu forces several times, thus being appointed as the Governor of Jiuzhen. During the invasion of Yu Si and Tao Huang, Dong Yuan and Yang Ji led troops to defend. But Dong Yuan died before the war ended.
Born in Lintao, Longxi, granddaughter of Dong Zhuo. When Wang Yun killed Dong Zhuo, she wasn't spared either.
Native in Linzhao, Longxi, the daughter of Dong Zhuo. Her name doesn't exist in the official history records, Dong Yi is a fictional one.

Native in Dingtao, Jiyin, counselor of Cao Wei. 
He previously serverd under Yuan Shao and Zhang Yang, but eventually followed Cao Cao. 
Together with Cheng Yu, Guo Jia, Liu Ye, Jiang Ji and others, Chen Shou called them the unconventional mastermind. 
He helped Cao Cao trick Yang Feng to lead the emperor to Xuchang, which make Cao Cao successfully implement the strategy. 
When Liu Bei took shelter under Cao Cao, he and Guo Jia claimed Liu Bei would rebel sooner or later. This means he is a shrewd judge of character. 
He also advised Cao Cao to restore the five rank of nobility, which laid the foundation for House Cao to usurp the throne. 
During the service under Cao Pi, he offered many suggestions on the south campaign and none of them missed.
A eunuch of the Jin Dynasty. He was a member of the inner circle of Empress Jia Nanfeng of Emperor Hui of Jin Dynasty, and was eventually killed by Sima Lun.

Born in Yiyang, Jingzhou. An official of Shu. 
He was a clerk under Zhuge Liang and later was promoted to First Secretary. 
After Zhuge Liang died, Dong Jue was appionted as the Book of Documents and later as the Prefect of the Masters of Writing. During the coup, he was promoted to Senior General Who Assists the State in hope to remove Jiang Wei's military power, but Jiang Wei stayed in Tazhong and never returned. After the fall of Shu, he and Liu Chan surrendered.

High-ranking official in late period of Wu. 
Accounts about him are scarce in history records. He was ordered by Sun Chen to help Sun Liang claim the throne. Favored by Sun Hao, he was appointed as Prefect of the Palace Writers and later promoted to Education Supervisor.
Longxi Lintao people, Dong Zhuo's nephew. Wang Yun killed Dong Zhuo, was killed by Huangfu Song in the dock.

Born in Yuyao, Kuaiji. Wu Official. Son of Yu Fan. 
He was born when Yu Fan was exiled to Jiaozhou. After his father died, his family was freed from exile and so Yu Si returned. 
When Sun Chen wanted to deposed the emperor Sun Liang and replaced him with Sun Xiu, he summoned the court officials for a meeting before Sun Xiu arrives, but such action was opposed by Yu Si. After Sun Xiu ascended the throne, he appointed Yu Si as Central Regular Mounted Attendants. 
Later together with Xue Ying and Tao Huang, they attacked Jiaozhi and regained some of the lost territory. For his success in the campaign against Fu Yan, he was promoted to Inspector of Jiaozhou and enfeoffed as the Marquis of Yuyao.

Born in Yuyao, Kuaiji. Wu official. Son of Yufan. 
When the Jin forces invaded Wu, Yu Zhong refused to surrender and committed suicide after the fall of city. Someone also said he was killed by the Jin army.

Born in Yuyao, Kuaiji. Wu official. Son of Yu Fan's brother. There are only some accounts about him on the Yu Xian stele unearthed in Xuehu Village of Yuyao. He was the Garrison Commander of Wu and abandoned the official life after the fall of Wu.

He was a native of Zhuo County in Jinan, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. He had a reputation for being a noble and virtuous man who did not flatter the rich and powerful. However, during the pacification of the rebellion of Qiang Hu, he did not save Zhou Di, which led to his death in battle. He was eventually killed by Sima Lun, the king of Zhao, during the Eight Kings' Rebellion.

Born in Xiangling, Pingyang. The sister of Empress Jia Nanfeng. Originally, Jia Chong wanted Jia Wu to marry the crown prince, but she was too young, so Jia Nanfeng is chosen instead. She and her sister plotted to muder Sima Yu. In the Upheaval of the Eight Princes, Sima Lun executed Jia Nanfeng and Jia Wu died of caning.

Born in Xiangling, Pingyang, she's the queen of Emperor Hui of Jin Dynasty. She is famous for her ugly appearance and jealousy. Her dictatorship is also one of the causes of the Upheaval of the Eight Princes. He was killed by Sima Lun in the upheaval. However, when compiling history in ancient China, it was unfair to blame women for the disaster and subjugation of the country. If Emperor Wu of Jin had not enfeoffed his clan in front, would there be a result that the princes' power would be out of control? Although Jia Nanfeng was jealous and lacked virtue, he also promoted Zhang Hua and others who were born in a poor family but talented, which was very different from the atmosphere of paying attention to family status at that time. The time of Jia Nanfeng's reign was known as "peace and stable", which was also a rare prosperous period in the Western Jin Dynasty. The Western Jin's decline and perish wasn't the fault of single person.
A native of Xiangling, Pingyang, the eldest daughter of Jia Chong and his first wife Li Wan. Also known as Bao. Married Sima You.

A native of Xiangling, Pingyang, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty, He's the nephew of Jia Chong. During the dictatorship of Jia Nanfeng, in order to establish followers, he served as Jia Mo's regular attendant, and Zhang Hua and Pei Wei served as assistants. During this period, Jin was peaceful and stable. Jia Mo stated the gains and losses for Jia Nanfeng for several times, but Jia Nanfeng didn't listen to his advice and opposed his alienation and suspicion. Jia Mo was depressed and frustrated, and died of worry and anger.

In The Romance of the Three Kingdoms, he's the lieut. general of Gongsun Yuan in Liaodong. Before Gongsun Yuan rebelled against Cao Wei, Jia Fan remonstrated: "Sima Yi is good at using troops, and even Zhuge Liang of Shu can't win, not to mention the Lord?" To persuade Gongsun Yuan not to send the troops. After hearing this, Gongsun Yuan was furious and publicly executed Jia Fan. Sima Yi learned of this after defeating Gongsun Yuan, and praised Jia Fan for his integrity, built a tomb for him, and knighted descendants.
A native of Xiangling, Pingyang, the son of Jia Chong. He died early at the age of three.
A native of Xiangling, Pingyang, the second daughter of Jia Chong and the first wife Li Wan. Also known as Yu.

A native of Xiangling, Pingyang, Jia Chong's grandson. His surname was originally Han, and his biological father is Han Shou. Jia Chong's wife Guo Huai asks Emperor Wu of Jin to let Han Mi succeed as a grandson. Jia Mi was talented and learned. The imperial court discussed the establishment of the Jin Dynasty, and finally adopted Jia Mi's theory. However, he was conceited, arrogant and extravagant. When Sima Lun killed Jia Nanfeng, Jia Mi was also killed.

An official in Cao Wei and Western Jin Dynasty. He once participated in calming the rebellion launched by Zhuge Dan in Shouchun. Later the You Xianwang of Xiongnu rebelled on the frontier, Lu Fan was also ordered to fight, and finally defeated Liu Meng. Liu Meng was killed by his subordinate Li Ke.

A subordinate of Gongsun Zan. After Gongsun Zan killed Liu Yu, Liu Yu's former tribe Xianyu Fu and others recommended Yan Rou as Mounts Supervisor of Wuhuan. He fought with Zou Dan in the north of Luhe River and killed more than 4000 people such as Zou Dan.

A native of Wucheng, Wu County. When Sun Ce went to Jiangdong, Zou Ta, Qian Tong, Wang Sheng and others set up an army to cooperate Yan Baihu. They were enemies with Sun Ce, but they were defeated and captured. Together with Qian Tong, they were beheaded by Sun. His family was exterminated. In the romance of the Three Kingdoms, he was Yan Baihu's subordinate, who was shot by Taishi Ci after he ascended the city walls.

His name is unknown in history. In The Romance of the Three Kingdoms, he is called Zou. The name of Zou Yuan is a fiction. When Zhang Xiu surrendered, Cao Cao took Zou Yuan as his concubine. Zhang Xiu was dissatisfied, rebelled and defeated Cao Cao.

Once led Liu Bei to fight with the Yellow Turban Army, and then together with Huangfu Song, he conquered Han Sui and Bian Zhang. In "The Romance", he was a subordinate of Liu Yan, the Governor of Youzhou. the Yellow Turban army was powerful at the time. He suggested to Liu Yan to recruit local troops as a volunteer army. Liu Bei, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei responded to the recruitment at this time. Later, together with Liu Bei and others, they crusaded against the Yellow Turban army and ended the siege of Qingzhou.

Liu Bei's subordinates. After Cao Pi usurped the Han Dynasty, it was rumored that Emperor Xian had been killed. Therefore, Liu Bei wanted to ascend the throne and inherit the Han Dynasty. Liu Ba and Yong Mao wrote a letter to persuade Liu Bei not to be emperor. Therefore, Liu Bei secretly hated Yong Mao and executed him. However, there are many contradictions in the records of this matter in historical books.

A native of Lujiang, Yangzhou. Originally a subordinate of Yuan Shu, he took refuge in Liu Bei who had owned the four counties of Jingnan after the Battle of Red Cliff, But he was soon attacked and killed by Xiahou Yuan. It is said that Lei Xu and Lei Bo are the same person.

A native of Chengdu, Shu County, he has served in Shu Han and Western Jin Dynasty. In the Jin Dynasty, he was recommended by Luo Xian and recruited by Sima Yan, Emperor Wu of Jin. In the Chronicles of Huayang, it is said that both Shou Liang and Chen Shou have written Zhuge Liang Anthology. Their emphasis on content is quite different, but now they have been lost.

Born in Linyuan, Wuling, he was an Shuhan official. After the Battle of Red Cliff, he was recruited by Liu Bei to serve as an official. Zhuge Liang called him "the wise talent of Chu" together with Pang Tong. However, he was arrogant, regarded others as nothing, and repeatedly criticized Liu Bei and his officials. During his tenure as the Governor of Ba County, he was regarded foolish and abominable; he had fled without a fight; he even cut off others' head and put it on the side of Liu Bei's coffin. In the end, Zhuge Liang said that he "defamed the former Emperor and officials." He wrote to Liu Chan to abolish him as a common people and exile him to Wenshan.
A fictional character, daughter of Liao Hua.

Born in Changyi, Shanyang, a general of Cao Wei, the grandson of Man Chong. When Cao Mao attacked Sima Zhao, Man Changwu, who was in charge of guarding the gate, refused to let him go and asked Sima Gan to change his way to Dongye Gate. Wang Xian, who joined the army at that time, was also unable to enter his door. He secretly hated him, so he slandered Sima Zhao and framed Man Changwu, resulting in Man's death by torture.

Born in Changyi, Shanyang, a general of Cao Wei, the son of Man Chong. He is well-known for his character, and he was appointed as Minister of Guards. Later, his son Man Changwu was framed, and he was implicated and demoted as a common man.
A fictional character. Did not exist in history.
Born in Wuji, Zhongshan, he's the father of Cao Pi's concubine Zhen.
Born in Wuji, Zhongshan, he's the elder brother of Cao Pi's concubine Zhen. Early death.

Born in Changguang, Donglai. Originally a pirate, he gathered more than 3000 people to rebel. After being defeated by Yue Jin and Li Dian sent by Cao Cao, he fled to the island. Cao Cao adopted the plan of He Kui and ordered Huang Zhen, the Deputy Governor, to persuade Guan Cheng to surrender.

Born in Pingyuan, he's famous for Feng Shui, divination and fortune-telling. He is not handsome, but he is very talented. He was known as a prodigy when he was young. Later, he became famous for his divination skills. He is witty, generous, loyal, filial and faithful. All his acquaintances like him. The annals of the Three Kingdoms contains his deeds of speculating on good or bad luck for Wang Ji, Zhong Yu, Liu Bin, Wuqiu Jian, He Yan and others. His divination skills have won Chen Shou's praise: "mysterious and unique skills." In "the Romance", it is also made up that Guan Yun divined the good and bad of the battle on Dingjunshan for Cao Cao, and Guan Lu predicted that Xiahou Yuan would die.

Born in Zhuxu, Beihai, a hermit in the Three Kingdoms period. When he was young, he studied with Hua Xin and Bing Yuan, and the three of them were called "Yilong." Chen Shou called him "profound, elegant and outstanding."

A native of Yongning, Kuaiji, a heroic woman. Also known as the surname Qu. Originally from Huangfu Mi's "Preceeding Biographies of Exemplary Women". She and the maidservant were killed by thieves because they did not want to be humiliated.

Born in Sheyang, Guangling. Participated in the Anti-Dong Coalition, and later served Yuan Shao. When Cao Cao attacked Lu Bu, Zhang Miao and others, he surrounded Zhang Miao's brother Zhang Chao in Yongqiu. Zhang Chao and Zang Hong are old friends, Zang Hong asks Yuan Shao to send troops to rescue him, but Yuan Shao refuses. Zang Hong resents Yuan Shao, and led the whole city rebels. After being besieged by Yuan Shao for a year, when his food was exhausted, Zang Hong killed his wife and cooked his concubines for food. In the end, he still lost to Yuan Shao and was killed after the fall of the city.

Born in Huaxian, Taishan, he's a general under Cao Cao's command. Once a subordinate to Tao Qian, and later the leader of Mount Tai bandits, he formed an alliance with Lu Bu. After Lu Bu's defeat, he returned to Cao Cao. When Cao and Yuan fought, Zang Ba led his elite troops to invade Qingzhou and contained Yuan's army, allowing Cao Cao to concentrate on the battle of Guandu. After the pacification of Zhongyuan, Zang Ba followed Cao Cao to conquer Sun Quan and became a commander. He fought with Sun Wu repeatedly without defeat.

A native of Xiangyang, Jingzhou, he served in Cao Wei and the Western Jin Dynasty. "A New Account of Tales in the World" refers to Kua Jun as the son of Kua Liang, and is related to Emperor Wu of Jin by marriage. He was once the Governor of Nanyang.

Born in Zhonglu, Nanjun, his wife is the daughter of Zhuge Gui and Zhuge Liang's elder sister. However, this theory can only be seen in the Old Records of Xiangyang, which is difficult to distinguish between true and false. He was appointed as the Governor of Fangling. After Liu Bei's pacification of Hanzhong, when he became the King of Hanzhong, he ordered Meng Da to attack Fangling, and was killed by Meng Da.

Born in Wenxi, Hedong, he served in Cao Wei and Western Jin Dynasty. He's the son of Pei Qian. Senior General Cao Shuang appointed him as the emperor's close attendant. After Cao Shuang was killed, he changed to serve Sima. Yu Zhuge took part in military affairs in putting down the rebellion of Zhuge Dan in Shouchun, and have rendered great service. After Cao Mao was killed for resisting Sima Zhao, Pei Xiu was responsible for revising the bureaucratic establishment, which enabled Sima's clan to be knighted in large numbers. When Sima Zhao selected his successor, he firmly supported Sima Yan, so he became the Engineering Supervisor of the Jin Dynasty. He made outstanding contributions to ancient Chinese cartography, compiled 18 pieces of Yugong Regional Map, and initiated the "six aspects of Cartography".

Born in Wenxi, Hedong, he has served as an official in Wei and Western Jin Dynasty. He knows people. He has commented on Zhong Hui, Xiahou Xuan, Shan Tao, Fu Peng and others. He stayed aloof from the worldly success, solved several dangerous situations in his official career, and he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace.

The native of Wenxi, Hedong, he's an official of Wei, served the house of Cao for three generations. He took refuge at Jingzhou, but because he knew that Liu Biao was not an conquerer, he went to Changsha and finally served Cao Cao. During the riots of Wuwan barbarians in Dai County, Pei Qian proposed not to send troops to suppress them. During his term as the Governor of the county, the barbarians kept themselves in peace. After that, Cao Pi and Cao Rui also relied heavily on Pei Qian and served in important official positions such as Chief Imperial Secretariat and Imperial Court Grandee.

The native of Wenxi, Hedong, he's a Western Jin official, and son of Pei Xiu. He was a confidant of Sima Yan, Emperor Wu of Jin Dynasty. He was killed by Sima Lun, King of Zhao, during the the Upheaval of the Eight Princes. He's a well-known philosopher, contrary to Wang Bi and other metaphysics which advocates "no-centeredness".

He was originally a Jiangxia soldier. In the third year of Zhongping, he gathered people to rebel, killed Qin Jie, Governor of Nanyang, and successively captured six counties. Finally, he was attacked by Wang Min, the then-Inspector of Jingzhou, and Yang Xu, who succeeded Wang as the Governor of Nanyang.

A native of Changling, Jingzhao, he's an official in Eastern Han Dynasty. His real name is Zhao Jia. Because he and his cousin Zhao Xi satirized the Central Accendant Tang Heng's brother Tang Yu several times, his entire family was killed. He changed his name to escape. Later, he was recruited as the Inspector of Bingzhou, and was dismissed because he was involved in the second party forbiddance incident. Later, although he became an official again, there was great chaos at the end of the Han Dynasty. Finally, when he was sent to Liu Biao as an envoy by Emperor Xian, he stayed in Jingzhou because of his age. Zhao Qi is a well-known Confucian scholar, once wrote an annotation to Mencius, from which Mencius was called "the Second Saint".

The fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms", he's Dong Zhuo's general. Guarding the Si Shui Pass with Hua Xiong, and later fighting with Sun Jian's general Cheng Pu. He was killed by Cheng Pu.

Born in Tianshui County, he's a Cao Wei official, and Wang Yi's husband. When Ma Chao rioted for the second time, many counties in Longyou responded and joined after hearing the news. Later, Yang Fu, Zhao Ang and others saw Ma Chao's vigilance gradually go away. When Ma Chao left the city, they closed the city gate, refused Ma Chao outside the city, and held on for more than a month until Xiahou Yuan led the army to the city, and Ma Chao withdrew. But Zhao Yue was killed by Ma Chao. During this period, Zhao Ang and Wang Yi had nine tricks, which made great contributions to suppressing the rebellion of Ma Chao.
Born in Tianshui County, she's the daughter of Zhao Ang and Wang Yi. There is no detailed record in official history.
From "Shishuo Xinyu", she's a native of Yingchuan, and a well-known talented woman in Wu at that time. She has a lot of talent, and once wrote a note for "Biographies of Exemplary Women".

Originated from "Biographies of Exemplary Women". Born in Fulu, Jiuquan, she is the daughter of Zhao An, and mother of Pang Yu, a Cao Wei general. She was also called Pang E, a well-known heroic woman at that time. His father Zhao An was killed by Li Shou, and his three younger brothers also died of illness. Zhao E still insisted on avenging his father, and surrendered after successfully assassinating Li Shou.

He and Ma Xiang gathered people to rebel in Mianzhu, Yizhou. They called themselves the Yellow Turban Army. They killed Xi Jian, the Inspector of Yizhou. After that, they successively captured three counties such as Ba and Qianwei, Ma Xiang was usurped the name of the emperor again. Later he was conquered by Liu Yan and Jia Long.

Originated from "Biographies of Exemplary Women". Born in Zizhong, Qianwei, she's the wife of Sheng Dao. Sheng Dao gathered a crowd to raise an uprising. After the defeat, Zhao Yuanjiang was tortured and died for leaving behind a cover for Sheng Dao and her son to escape.
Originated from "Ling Fei Jing", she's a female alchemist in the late Eastern Han Dynasty. She achieved wisdom and passed away.

Born in Tianshui County, she's Sima Yan's concubine, and the cousin of Queen Yang Yan. Later, he attached to Jia Nanfeng and committed many injustices. Zhao Can, Jia Wu and Jia Nanfeng conspired to frame Prince Sima Yun. When Sima Lun, King of Zhao, killed Jia Nanfeng, he was together.
A fictional character, daughter of Zhao Yun.

A native of Luoyang, an official of Wu, he's one of the "Eight Wonders" of Wu. He's good at the Nine Halls arithmetic, and he is very accurate in all calculations. It's said that Sun Quan once asked him for skills, but Zhao Da kept it secret, so he was negligent and neglected by Sun Quan, and he was failed to hold an important official position all his life.
Subordinate of Yuan Shao. During the Battle of Guandu, he escorted the grain with Chunyu Qiong and others. Cao Jun was killed when Cao force attacked Wuchao granary at night.

A native of Xixian, Tianshui, he's one of the Eight Commandants of Xiyuan. After the heroes rose, Chun Yuqiong, one of the Eight Commandants, turned to Yuan Shao. After Yuan Shao was defeated, they turned to Cao Cao. In addition, under Liu Bei's command, there were also people with the same name and surname who participated in the battle of Yiling, which has not been recorded since.

A native of Yangdi, Yingchuan, he was a Cao Wei official and served four generations of Cao family. He's known for his fortitude. After Cao Cao welcomes the Emperor Xian, Zhao Yan believes that this is the one who can pacify the world, and he went in office. With good resourcefulness and good political achievements, he made a lot of credit for Cao Cao from the time when Cao and Yuan fought against each other. Later, when Guan Yu attacked Fancheng, it was because of his strategy that Cao Ren was determined and succeeded in holding on.

A native of Xiangyang, Jingzhou, he's a general of Shu Han. Once served as the Governor of Ba County, he went with Liu Bei during the battle of Yiling and survived. He became the General of the Right.

The son of Liu Bei and the younger brother of Liu Chan. Liu Yong has always been at odds with the eunuch Huang Hao. Therefore, Huang Hao slandered Liu Chan and framed Liu Yong, so that Liu Yong could not appear before Liu Chan for more than ten years.

From Lingling, Liu Xian originally served under Liu Biao before joining Cao Wei. During the conflict of Cao and Yuan, Liu Xian, along with Han Song and Kuai Yue, advised Liu Biao to be decisive about choosing a side. Later, he visited Cao Cao as an envoy for Liu Biao. Cao Cao criticized Liu Biao but Liu Xian refuted with reason. Cao Cao was left speechless but he was impressed by Liu Xian's talent. After Liu Cong surrendered to Cao, Liu Xian was recruited by Cao Cao as Prefect of the Masters of Writing.

A native of Peiguo, Yuzhou, one of the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove. Liu Ling was dissatisfied with Sima's regime. In order to avoid persecution, he was addicted to alcohol. He was often drunk, acted licentiously, and despised principals. He once wrote "Ode to Virtue of Wine", which reposes the idea of advocating metaphysics and avoiding the affairs of human life with wine.

From Handan, Guangping, Liu Shao was an official of Cao Wei and a relative of the royals of Han. Highly knowledgeable, he, along with Wang Xiang, Huan Fan, Wei Dan, Miao Xi and the others, were ordered to write Imperial Mirror, the first category book in China, which contained 40 volumes, 1,000 chapters, and more than 8 million words. However, this publication had been lost.

Emperor Xian of Han Dynasty. Dong Zhuo abolished Liu Bian, the young emperor of Han, and made Liu Xie the emperor. After that, Liu Xie remained in the hands of various powerful officials until he was welcomed to Xudu by Cao Cao. Although Liu Xie tried to bring down Cao Cao with a secret edict, he failed because of leak of words. After Cao Cao's death, under Cao Pi's coercion, he abdicated the throne and was granted Duke of Shanyang.
A native of Zhuojun, Youzhou, he's a clansman of Shu Han, and the great-grandson of Liu Bei. There is no record of his life deeds in history.

He was a native of Fangcheng in Zhuo County, a member of the Han clan and an official of Cao Wei. He was an official of the Cao Wei dynasty. He was a magnificent writer and good at writing diatribes, and many of the imperial edicts of the Cao fathers and sons came from his hand. 
When Sun Quan's secret letter was seized by a Wei border general, Liu Fang altered the words in the letter to divide the two countries. 
Before Cao Hiei's death, he wanted to use Cao Zhao to assist him in his administration, but Liu Fang and Sun Zhi, who were at odds with Xiahou Xian and Cao Zhao, were keen on recruiting Sima Yi as a minister of trust, which was the cause of the Wei family's downfall.
A native of Luo County, Changsha, he was a general of Shu Han and the son of Liu Feng. After the fall of the Shu Han Dynasty, he moved to Hedong during the reign of Cao Hanjin, the Emperor of Wei.
A general of Wu, mainly stationed in Jinzhou. He once participated in the battle of Yiling, and also fought against Zhang He and Sima Yi, but defeated by them.
A native of Zhuojun, Youzhou, he's a clansman of Shu Han, and the great-grandson of Liu Bei. There is no record of his life deeds in history.

A native of Gaoping, Shanyang, he's the son of Liu Biao, younger brother of Liu Qi and Liu Cong. After Liu Cong surrendered to Cao, he became an official of Cao and served as the Governor of Dong'an County.
Found in the record of "Xunyue Epitaph" unearthed in Yanshi, Henan. She is the daughter of Liu Yi, and the wife of Xun Yue, also knows as Liu Jianxun.

Originated from "Biographies of Exemplary Women". Born in Xiapi, she's the daughter of Liu Fang, wife to Hua Mu from Danyang. After her husband died, she cut her ears with a knife and disfigured her face. She determined not to remarry.
Daughter of Liu Biao. No official history records her name, Liu Zhu is a fictional character in this title.

Born in Zhuo County, Youzhou, he's the son of Liu Chan. After the subjugation of Shu, he moved to Luoyang with Liu Chan. At the end of the Western Jin Dynasty, the Yongjia chaos caused his descendants died out.

A native of Jingzhou, a general of Shuhan. He had been under Liu Bei's command before he entered Shu. After Yizhou pacificated, he was appointed as the Governor of Jiangyang. He recommended Jiang Wan to Zhuge Liang. He became an Overseer-General of the Rear.

A native of Muping, Donglai, an official of the Eastern Wu Dynasty, son of Liu Yao. He was a beautiful man of his generation and was favored by Sun Quan, who later asked for his son Sun Ba to marry Liu Ji's daughter. 
When Yu Fan offended Sun Quan at a banquet, Sun Quan, in a drunken rage, wanted to kill Yu Fan, but only Liu Ji dared to dissuade Sun Quan. After Sun Quan sobered up, he was happy and respected Liu Ji more and more.
Second daughter of Emperor Huan, and the Yingyin Princess of Han.

A native of Pingyuan, an official of Wu. He is good at divination, especially astrology, and is one of the "Eight Wonders" of Wu. In order to avoid the chaos of war, he took refuge in Jiangdong. He was made an aide by Sun Quan's brother sun Fu. He predicted that Bian Hong would kill Sun Yi, the Governor of Danyang.
The daughter of Emperor Xian of the Han Dynasty. After Cao Pi usurped the Han throne, he canonized Liu Man as the princess of Changle County.
Son of Liu Bei, and married with the daughter of Ma Chao.

Native of Chengde, Huainan, he's the son of Liu Ye. He's eloquent and good at arguing. He was once a follower of Cao Shuang. When Cao Shuang was killed, he was saved from death because of his father's meritorious service. However, when Wu Qiujian rebelled, he relapsed and angered Sima Shi, and was eventually killed.

A native of Gaotang, Pingyuan, he served successively in Wei and the Western Jin Dynasty. He's educated and knowledgeable, especially good at "Spring and Autumn." Before the battle of the Wei to subjugate Shu, he had foreseen the victory and defeat of the battle, and even asserted that Zhong Hui and Deng Ai "will break Shu, and neither will be returned." After Jin Dynasty replaced Wei, he served in many prominent positions.

Born in Weichang, Zhongshan, he's a general in the two Jin Dynasties. When he was young, he met with Zu Ti, and the allusion of "Rise upon Hearing the Chicken Crow" came from the two. In the last years of the Western Jin Dynasty, the Upheaval of the Eight Princes met the turmoil of barbarians, and the royal family of Jin went southward. Liu Kun fought against the barbarians in Jinyang in the north. However, his military and political talents were insufficient, and he did not make good use of people or accept others' advice, which ended in failure. Liu Kun is also good at rhythm and poetry, both of which are famous at the time.

A native of Lu, Yuzhou, an official of Shu Han. Liu Bei met him when he was in Yuzhou, and Liu Bei treated him very courteously. He has no real talent, but he was good at talking, so he is at odds with many people. Later, he ordered the soldiers to lynch because he suspected that his wife Hu had an affair with Liu Chan. He was sued by Hu and was sentenced to prison, and eventually executed.
Eldest daughter of Emperor Huan, and the Yang'an Princess of Han. Her husband is general Fu Wan.
A native of Ningyang, Dongping, one of the Seven Scholars of Jian'an. Cao Pi praised him for "the goodness of his five character poetry is a wonder of the time."

From Tan, Donghai, Liu Yu was a relative of the royals of Han who once served as Inspector of You Province. 
With a kind personality, his governance was humane and benevolent, which gained him a good reputation among both tribal and Han people. He was also loyal to the Han emperorship. When Dong Zhuo became authoritative, Yuan Shu and the others tried to support Liu Yu as the next emperor but Liu Yu rejected them sternly. 
Originally Gongsun Zan's superior, Liu Yu turned against him as Gongsun Zan abused military power and connived his army in harassing his subjects. However, Liu Yu was betrayed by his subordinate, Gongsun Ji, and lost to Gongsun Zan. In the end, Gongsun Zan framed him for planning a rebellion and killed him.

Liu Pi was a leader of the Yellow Turban Rebellion. After Zhang Jiao and his brother died, Liu Pi and the others led their people to Runan and became bandits. He later submitted to Cao Cao but soon defected from Cao to Yuan Shu. He then tried to submit to Sun Jian. During the Battle of Guandu, he had contacts with Liu Bei as well. In the end, he was conquered by Cao Ren, who was sent by Cao Cao. However, his year of death was inconsistent in official records.

He was the son of Liu Fu, an official of Cao Wei. During Cao Pi's reign, he became a local governor and a magistrate with a track record of governance. Later, he became the general of the northern part of the town and supervised the area in the north of the river, built a large weir in the hostile ditch, and promoted farming so that the area around Thistle could have three catches a year.

A native of Guangling County, he's an official in the Western Jin Dynasty. After the Jin Dynasty subjugated Wu, the generals fought for merit. Emperor Wu of Jin sent him to investigate his merit as the basis for reward, but he was considered to be unreasonable and was demoted to the Governor of Jinzhao. During the the Upheaval of the Eight Princes and Sima Lun's dictatorship, he was framed and killed for being upright and mourning for Zhang Hua. According to the "Criminal Law History", Liu Song suggested resuming corporal punishment and rule with severe punishment.

Born in Anzhong, Nanyang, he's a Cao Wei official. His teacher Sima Hui and his elder brother Liu Wangzhi worked for Liu Biao. After Liu Biao killed Liu Wang, Liu Yi defected to Cao Cao, which was greatly appreciated by Cao Cao and Cao Pi. Later, because his brother Liu Wei had a good relationship with Wei Feng, when Wei Feng rebelled, Liu Wei also participated. Liu Yi was implicated. But Liu Yi had persuaded Liu Wei to alienate Wei Feng before, so he was pardoned by Cao Cao.
A fictional character, daughter of Liu Yao.

A native of Yexian, Donglai, he has served in Wei and Western Jin Dynasty. Fair and upright, he's a good critic, and once wrote to suggest that Emperor Wu of Jin abolish the nine-grade system. However, because of his strictness and uprightness, he offended the nobles and was not able to serve in prominent positions.
A fictional character, daughter of Liu Bei.

From Gaoping, Shanyang, Liu Pan was the nephew of Liu Biao. Famed for his bravery, he invaded the counties in Yang Province multiple times but was defeated by Taishi Ci. To defend against Liu Pan, Sun Quan stationed Taishi Ci to guard the province. 
After Liu Biao took over Changsha, he ordered Liu Pan and Huang Zhong to guard You County together. No document of him was found afterwards. 
In the Romance of Three Kingdoms, he was recommended by Huang Zhong to Liu Bei and served as the defense general of Changsha.

Born in Jingling, Jiangxia, he's Liu Yan's eldest son, and Liu Zhang's brother. When Ma Teng fought against Li Jue, Liu Fan was Ma Teng's internal contact, but his deeds were revealed. He and his brother Liu Dan was beheaded together.

A fictional character in the Romance of Three Kingdoms and not the Cao Wei official of the same name in official records. 
In the Romance, Liu Xian was the son of Liu Du, the Administrator of Lingling Commandery. He fought Liu Bei's army along with Xing Dao Rong. Liu Xian schemed a night ambush but his plan was seen through by Zhuge Liang, leading to him being defeated and captured by Zhang Fei. After Zhuge Liang released Liu Xian, he returned to his city to convince his father to surrender.

Officer of Yuan Shu. Minister of Lujiang. After Yuan Shu's death, he rescued his wife and children but was defeated by Sun Ce, leading him to join Cao Cao. He then would drink and be friendly with Cao Pi, letting Cao Cao look the other way when he abused his power. Eventually, his abuses caught up to him and he was executed.

A native of Weichang, Zhongshan, he's an official in the Western Jin Dynasty, and the father of Liu Kun. He has a clear reputation, but due to the Upheaval of the Eight Princes and the turmoil of barbarians in the late Western Jin Dynasty, Liu Fan suffered many times. Finally, because his son Liu Kun was greedy and killed Linghu Sheng by mistake, Linghu Sheng's son Linghu Ni betrayed Liu Kun and acted as a guide for the Han Zhao army. They attacked Jinyang, killed Liu Fan and his wife.

From Zhuo Commandery, You Province, Liu Chen was a Shu Han royal and the son of Liu Shan. He was a man of dignity. In Wei's conquest of Shu, while Liu Shan was planning to surrender to Deng Ai, Liu Chen reprimanded his father, "If we compromise, there will surely be a disaster. If you, me, and all the officials risk everything for a fight, even if we die, we will be redeemed when we meet the former emepror." 
But Liu Shan insisted on surrendering. Griefed and indignant, Liu Chen committed suicide for his kingdom.

Born in Zichuan, Zibo, he was a famous mathematician in Wei and Jin Dynasties. He once wrote notes for "The Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art", and wrote books such as "Haidao Suanjing", which has a profound influence on the development of arithmetic in later generations.

A native of Weichang, Zhongshan, he's an official of the Western Jin Dynasty, the son of Liu Fan, and the brother of Liu Kun. He's talented and famous. However, due to the Upheaval of the Eight Princes in the last years of the Western Jin Dynasty, his official career was not good. He died about before the turmoil of barbarians and Han Zhao conquered Luoyang.

From Zhuo Commandery, You Province, Liu Xuan was a prince of Shu Han and the eldest son of Liu Shan. Fond of horse-riding and archery, he was a wasteful man who was killed by a rebel during Zhong Hui's rebellion.

Liu Fu, a native of Xiang, Pei State, was Cao Cao's subordinate. As he convinced Yuan Shu's officers, Qi Ji and Qin Yi, to surrender, he was appointed Inspector of Yang Province. 
During his tenure, he subdued local bandit forces, promoting agriculture and education, leading to the prosperity of the area. He also ordered the construction of Hefei City and the stockpiling of military supplies. 
One of the reasons Sun Quan failed when he attacked Hefei was definietely Liu Fu's contribution. 
In the Romance of Three Kingdoms, to vilify Cao Cao, it claimed that Liu Fu described certain lines from Short Song Style as inauspicious and was therefore stabbed and killed by Cao Cao.

A Wu official. He first married Sun Quan's second daughter, but she died early. Later he married his third daughter, Sun Lu, as his second wife. Once foloowed Lv Dai to fight the rebellion. He became the Chariot Horse General.
A native of Changsha County. At the time of the Han Ling Emperor, because of his attachment to the eunuch, he was appointed as engineering supervisor.

From the famous han music bureau poem "The Peacock Flies Southeast", it is said that she was a native of Lujiang County and the wife of Jiao Zhongqing. In the poems, she is said to be good at weaving, able to play Konghou, recite poems and books, and is a beautiful woman with excellent talents and appearance. But she was not tolerated by Jiao's mother and Jiao Zhongqing was orderd to divorce his wife. Later Liu Lanzhi's brother forced her to remarry. On the day of remarriage, both Liu Lanzhi and Jiao Zhongqing committed suicide.

Staff officer of Yuan Shao. Fended off Cao Cao in a castle with his uncle. When his friend Xin Pi called for surrender, his enraged uncle executed all of his family members in the castle. This shocked Shen Rong into betraying his uncle, and he let Cao Cao's troops in.

Yuan Shu's subordinate. When Cao Cao personally led an army to attack Yuan Shu, Yuan Shu fled in a hurry, leaving Qiao Rui, Li Feng, Liang Gang and Le Jiu behind. All four generals were executed after their defeat.

From Weiguo, Yangping, Yue Chen was a military general of Wei and the son of Yue Jin. 
He was brave like his father. When Wen Qin started a rebellion, Yue Chen led his troops after Wen Qin. Zhuge Dan therefore was apprehensive of Yue Chen. He also doubted Yue Chen for sowing discord between him and Sima Zhao and killed him immediately after his revolt. 
In the Romance of Three Kingdoms, he served as the vice vanguard of Cao Zhen during Zhuge Liang's northern expeditions. When Sima Yi and Zhuge Liang had a battle of formations, Yue Chen, Dai Ling, and Zhang Hu were captured in the Eight Diagrams formation and only released after their face were painted with ink. In the end, he still died in the hands of Zhuge Dan.

From Yiyang, Jing Province, Fan Jian was a official of Shu Han. 
Once an envoy to Eastern Wu, Fan Jian was said to be less knowledgeable but better in nature than Zong Yu by Zhuge Ke, a great politcian of Eastern Wu. 
Upon his return, he served as a Palace Attendant. In the last year of Shu Han, as the then Prefect of the Masters of Writing Dong Jue was promoted to Grand General, Fan Jian was appointed Prefect of the Masters of Writing. Fan Jian loathed the power-thirsty eunuch Huang Hao. Though he couldn't stop him, he didn't befriend him either. 
After the fall of Shu Han, Fan Jian surrendered along with Liu Shan and was recruited by Emperor Wu of Jin, Sima Yan. He promoted Zhuge Liang's ways of ruling to the emperor diligently and sought redress for Deng Ai.

Wife of Fuwan, Emperess Han Xian Fushou's mother. After Dong Cheng and others failed in their plot to kill Cao Cao, Empress Fu wrote to his father Fu Wan, asking Fu Wan to kill Cao Cao, but Fu Wan did not dare to agree. After the incident was revealed, Empress Fu was abolished and killed, more than a hundred people in his clan was killed too. Fan Ying and others were exiled to Zhuojun.

Fan Neng was a major general under Liu Yao, Inspector of Yang Province, who was ordered to guard Heng River against Yuan Shu. 
Yuan Shu sent Wu Jing and Sun Ben to battle his forces but the two fell into a stalemate. In the next year, Sun Ce went down to Jiangdong, settled commanderies such as Kuaiji, before turning around to attack Liu Yao. He then met up with Wu Jing and Sun Ben, who were his relatives, to defect from Yuan Shu. 
Sun Ce greatly defeated Fan Neng twice. In another battle, Sun Ce was shot in the thigh so he acted weak to trick the enemies, set up an ambush with Wu Jing, and slayed Fan Neng on the battlefield.
A native of Qi, Pei county, Eastern Wu official. Was sentenced to exile to Guangzhou because of outspoken remonstrance and angered Sun Hao.

A native of Bohai Nanpi, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. He has friends with Shi Chong, Pan Yue, Zuo Si and others, and is one of the twenty-four friends of Jingu. During the Eight Kings Rebellion, Sima Lun killed Shi Chong, Pan Yue, Ouyang Jian, Du Bin and others. Before his death, Ouyang Jian wrote "Dying Poems". Ouyang Jian also wrote "Lin Zhong Shi", the full text is concise, and its purpose is very different from the theory of contemporary metaphysics.

A native of Beihai, Ju County and an official of Sun Wu. Teng Yin and Sun Lin failed to fight for power and were killed, and Teng Mu was implicated and moved to the border county. It was not until Sun Xiu killed Sun Lin that he was able to return to the court. When Sun Hao was named Wuchenghou, he married Teng Fanglan, Teng Mu's daughter, as his concubine. After Sun Hao took the throne, his actions became more tyrannical. Courtier asked Tengmu to persuade Sun Hao. Sun Hao resented Teng Mu and moved Teng Mu to Cangwu County. Teng Mu died of fear on the way.

Born in Beihai, Ju County, daughter of Teng Mu. When Sun Hao was named Wu Chenghou, he married Teng Fanglan as his concubine. Later falling out of favor, father Muye was also moved to Cangwu, where he died of fear on the way. After Wu's death, he moved to Luoyang with Sun Hao.

From Ju County, Beihai, Teng Yin was a politician of Eastern Wu. 
Due to the chaos in the central region, his father, Teng Zhou, went south to submit to Liu Yao and later served under Sun Wu. Since young, Teng Yin acted dignified and decent-looking. Diligent and fair, he gained a high reputation while serving as a local administrator. 
He was summoned to assist Sun Liang in Sun Quan's will but wasn't compatible with Sun Jun, a powerful official of the royals. After Sun Chen seized power, Teng Yin was stationed to Wuchang. When Lu Ju was planning to overthrow Sun Chen, he contacted Teng Yin. After Sun Chen learned about it, he falsely accused Teng Yin of rebelling, forcing Teng Yin to revolt with his soldiers. In the end, he was unfortunately defeated and executed by Sun Chen.

A native of Nanyang, Xi'e, an official of Sun Wu and the Western Jin Dynasty. Sun Hao was the Inspector of Guangzhou at that time, and he had a good governance record, and had pacified the Guo Ma Rebellion.
A fictional character, daughter of Teng Yin.
There are few relevant records in the official history. Its name can be found in "Nvhong Yu Zhi" and "Shi Yi Ji". It is one of the four beauties of Sun Liang's imperial harem.

A native of Zhongmu, Xingyang, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. The famous beautiful man, namely Pan An. He met with Shi Chong, Zuo Si, and was one of the twenty-four friends of Jingu. In his early years, he disliked Sun Xiu, and humiliated him a lot. Later, during the Upheaval of the Eight Princes, Simalun came to power, and Sun Xiu was his favored minister. Sun Xiu framed Shi Chong and Pan Yue for rebellion. In the end, he and Shi Chong were killed, implicated three generation.

Wife of Sun Quan and mother of Sun Liang. The year after she gave birth to Sun Liang, the Crown Prince, she was made Sun Quan's Empress. Eventually, when taking care of her husband took its toll, she was strangled by court ladies while asleep.
Leader of the Shanyue. Eventually, Lu Xun raised an army of volunteers, but Pan Lin quickly surrendered and became his subordinate.
The Eunuch Jian Shuo's Mounts Supervisor. He had an acquaintance with the general He Jin, and when Jian Shuo conspired to kill He Jin, Pan Yin secretly informed He Jin and let He Jin escape.

A literary man from Wei and one of the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove. He married Cao Cao's great-granddaughter, revered nature, and, following the Qingtan movement, avoided common society. He was sentenced to death with his friend when he sided with him in a quarrel over refusing to back Shan Tao's appointment as minister. A master Qin player, people declared the melody he played before his execution would die along with him, since he had taught it to no one.

Cai Zhong was a fictional character in the Romance of Three Kingdoms from the same clan as Cai Mao. After Cao Cao fell for the discord scheme and killed Cai Mao, he sent Cai Zhong and his brother Cai He as spies in Eastern Wu but they were disclosed by Zhou Yu, who went along and let Cao Cao believe Huang Gai had made a false surrendered. He was slain by Gan Ning before the Battle of Red Cliffs.
No official history records her name, Cai Yue is a fictional character in this title.

A native of Peiguo in Yuzhou, a subordinate of Cao Cao. His real name is Cai Yang. During the battle between Cao and Yuan, Yuan Shao ordered Liu Bei to lead his troops to Runan to unite with Gong Du, Liu Pi and other Yellow Turbans, gathering thousands of people to harass Cao's rear. Cao Cao sent Cai Yang to attack, but Gong Du broke it, and Cai Yang was killed.
A fictional character, daughter of Cai Mao.

A native of Jincheng County, originally a subordinate of Han Sui. After the Battle of Tongguan, Han Sui lost to Jincheng Qiangzhong, and was later killed by his Xiping, Jincheng generals Quyan, Jiang Shi. And cut off his head sent to Cao Cao. Another way of saying that Han Sui died of illness.

A native of Jiujiang Shouchun, an official of Dong Wu, the son of Jiang Qin. After Jiang Qin's death, the eldest son Jiang Yi inherited the military power and his title, fought with Cao Wei, and died in battle. Jiang Xiu led the army, and Jiang Xiu was removed from office for crimes.

The favorite concubine of Emperor Sima Yu, the prince of Emperor Jin Hui. When Ja Nanfeng murdered Sima Yu, she framed that Sima Yu had conspired and killed Jin Hui Emperor, and deposed Sima Yu as a civilian, and even framed his mother Xie Jiu and concubine Jiang Jun as accomplices and killed with a Staff.

Jiang Ban served under Cao Wei and Western Jin. Originally Zhuge Dan's close general who scored battle exploits. 
When Zhuge Dan defected from Wei, Jiang Ban and Jiao Yi advised Zhuge Dan to attack with all forces while the soldiers were still loyal to him and that he could surely broke through the siege instead of being trapped. However, Zhuge Dan rejected, even attempting to kill Jiang Ban and Jiao Yi. The two took the chance to surrender to Wei instead. 
Jiang Ban also battled in Jin's conquest of Wu and greatly defeated the Danyang elites led by Sun Wu general Shen Ying.

A native of Jiujiang Shouchun, an official of Dong Wu, Jiang Qin's eldest son. After Jiang Qin's death, Jiang Yi assumed the military power and his title. During the battle of Yiling, he led the troops against Liu Bei, and he was transferred back to the southern county. At last he was killed in battle with Wei.

From Xiang Town, Lingling, Jiang Bin was an official of Shu Han and the eldest son of Jiang Wan. When Zhong Hui invaded Shu, Jiang Bin and him exchanged letters as he wished to inquire about the location of Jiang Wan's tomb so he could pay his respects. After the fall of Shu, Jiang Bin surrendered to Zhong Hui in Fucheng and the latter treated him as a friend. Later Jiang Bin got involved in Zhong Hui's rebellion and died on the battlefield.

Originally an area commander at Wuxing, Shu Han, Jiang Shu was transferred to Hanzhong after failing to fulfill his duties, which he held grudges for. In the Conquest of Shu by Wei, Jiang Shu tricked Fu Qian, the defense general of Yangping Pass, into battle while he surrendered to Wei himself and attacked Fu Qian instead, which led to the latter's death and the fall of Yangping Pass. The Wei army was able to enter the territory and invaded Jiange.

From Pinge, Chu State, Jiang Ji was an official in Cao Wei. Proficient in handling both civil and military affairs, in Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms, he was said to be an equal to Guo Jia and Cheng Yu. 
Jiang Ji submitted many admonitions on military and political affairs, always hitting the nail on the head, therefore winning the trust of three generations of the Cao family and became the backbone of Cao Wei ministers. 
In the Incidents at Gao Ping Tombs, Jiang Ji suggested Cao Shuang to surrender in a letter but after the latter surrendered, he was killed by Sima Yi. Ashamed that he failed Cao Shuang, Jiang Ji later died of grief.

Chief secretary of Shu and son of Jiang Wan. Following the fall of Chengdu, when Jiang Wei was still resisting, he was sent to deliver the order for him to surrender. He then returned to Chengdu to inform Deng Ai that Jiang Wei had surrendered to Zong Hui.

A native of Hedong Anyi, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. A well-known calligrapher, author of "Si Ti Shu Shi", has in-depth research and analysis on the four types of Zhuan, Li, Xing, and Cao, as well as major masters. It is one of the earliest calligraphy theories in the world. During the Upheaval of the Eight Princes, he was killed by Jian Nanfeng and Sima Wei, the king of Chu.

A native of Xiangyi, Chenliu. 
When Cao Cao first arrived in Chenliu, Wei Zi said to others, "This is the man who will level the world. 
Cao Cao also felt that Wei Zi was different from others and often discussed important matters with him, and Wei Zi even financed Cao Cao's army with his family's property. 
Later, Wei Zi followed Cao Cao in his war against Dong and was killed in the Battle of Zhuyang.

Dongwu generals. Sun Quan was superstitious in his later years, and feeling that the population of Dongwu was scarce, he sent generals Wei Wen and Zhuge Zhi to seek out Yizhou and Bozhou. Most people died due to the long distance and the disease. In the end, they could not find Danzhou, and only brought back thousands of Yizhou people. Sun Quan believed that Wei Wen and Zhuge had violated the edict, put them into jial and killed.

Wei retainer during the Later Han. After he was appointed by Xiahou Dun, he was made the Secondary Marquis by Cao Cao due to his father's merits. When Cao Pi took the throne, he would be made secretary general. He was given important roles during Cao Rui's rule, and advised in many campaigns, including Zhuge Liang's northern expedition, and the Wu invasion of Hefei. He was later promoted to Chief and Senior Minister.

A native of Hedong Anyi, Cao Wei official. Because of his insight into the situation in Guanzhong, Cao Cao adopted his suggestions and gradually restored Guanzhong's prosperity. Later, he and Wang Can presided over the formulation of the Wei State's ceremony system, and advocated the establishment of a doctor of law to teach laws, enforce in accordance with the law, and reduce corvee. Wei Ji is also a master of calligraphy, who is good at Zhuan and Li.

A native of Han Jia, Yan Dao, Shuhan official. In history, it is said that the scholarship is extensive, and he became the official of state and county. At the end of the Shu Han Dynasty, the official to Book of Documents. During the Zhonghui Rebellion, he died in the rebellion army.

From Anyi, Hedong, Wei Guan served under Cao Wei and Western Jin. 
In the Conquest of Shu by Wei, he served as the military governor in the army. When Zhong Hui and Deng Ai had a power dispute, Zhong Hui worked with Wei Guan to arrest Deng Ai and had him sent to Luoyang. 
Later, upon learning Zhong Hui's plan to rebel in Chengdu, Wei Guan contacted all the generals who didn't wish to participate in the coup. He sent an official letter to all generals, announcing Zhong Hui's defection, leading to the latter's arrest before he could start a rebellion. 
However, worried that Deng Ai would seek revenge on him after he cleared his reputation, Wei Guan took the chance to kill Deng Ai in chaos. 
In the end, he died in the chaos of the eight princes.

From Langya, Xu Province, Zhuge Jun was an official of Shu Han and the younger brother of Zhuge Jin and Zhuge Liang. As there was no historian official in Shu Han, his life was merely documented. The only thing known about him was that he followed Zhuge Liang to serve under Liu Bei and was promoted to ‪Changshui Lieutenant.

From Langya, Xu Province, Zhuge Shang was an official of Shu Han and the grandson of Zhuge Liang. In the Conquest of Shu by Wei, Deng Ai successfully invaded Shu, Zhuge Zhan retreated to Mianzhu then died in action. The fall of Shu was certain but Zhuge Shang refused to surrender to Wei even until the end and died on the battlefield.

The daughter of Zhuge Liang. Whether there is a real person is quite controversial. Zhuge Liang believed that his daughter would be able to become the immortal in the future, so he named her Zhuge Guo. It is mentioned in the "Tong Jian of Ancient Gods and Immortals" that Zhuge Liang taught her Qixiangg Beidou, and it is rumored that Zhuge Guo went to the southwest of Chengdu, Chaozhen Taoist temple to avoid misfortune and practice, and eventually became an immortal.

Dongwu generals. Sun Quan was superstitious in his later years, and feeling that the population of Dongwu was scarce, he sent generals Wei Wen and Zhuge Zhi to seek out Yizhou and Bozhou. Most people died due to the long distance and the disease. In the end, they could not find Danzhou, and only brought back thousands of Yizhou people. Sun Quan believed that Wei Wen and Zhuge had violated the edict, put them into jial and killed.
A fictional character, daughter of Zhuge Liang.
Concubine of Emperor Jin Wu, and the daughter of Zhuge Chong.

From Langya, Xu Province, Zhuge Qiao was an official of Shu Han. Originally Zhuge Jin's second son and the younger brother of Zhuge Ke, he was later adopted by Zhuge Liang. 
He once followed Zhuge Liang to Hanzhong and participated in military affairs. After Zhuge Ke and his family were killed in Eastern Wu, the son of Zhuge Qiao, Zhuge Pan, returned to Zhuge Jin's family to continue the lineage.
A fictional character, daughter of Zhuge Jin.

From Langya, Xu Province, Zhuge Xu served under Cao Wei and Western Jin. He participated in the suppression of Guanqiu Jian's rebellion. 
In the Conquest of Shu by Wei, he was ordered to intercept Jiang Wei at Yinping Bridge but was tricked by Jiang Wei into leaving the spot. Later, when Zhuge Xu was framed into an arrest by Zhong Hui and sent to the capital, his army was also incorporated by Zhong Hui. 
After Jin replaced Wei, he was promoted to Minister of Ceremonies, one of the nine ministers. His granddaughter, Zhuge Wan, was married to Emperor Wu of Jin.

From Langya, Xu Province, Zhuge Jing was the youngest son of Zhuge Dan who served under Cao Wei and Eastern Wu. He was upright, talented, and famed. 
After Zhuge Dan was killed after failing to revolt against the powerful official Sima Zhao, Zhuge Jing submitted to Eastern Wu. 
After Jin eliminated Wu, though Zhuge Jing was an old acquaintance of Emperor Wu of Jin, as the emperor was responsible of his father's death, he avoided him for the rest of his life, turning down all positions offered.

A Wu bureaucrat and younger brother of Zhuge Ke and Qiao. After his father's death, he inherited his army and worked to keep peace. Tolerant, likeable, and always out to have fun, he was beloved by soldiers and officials alike. When his brother was assassinated by Sun Jun and he was surrounded by the enemy army, he took his own life with poison.

Zhuge Zhan was Zhuge Liang's eldest son. 
Zhuge Liang had him late and was ill. He died on an expedition before he could raise him to adulthood, during which Zhuge Liang wrote to his brother, Jin, "Zhan is 8 and very clever. I am worried his precociousness means he won't achieve great things." He was right. 
Sheltered by his father's reputation, Zhuge Zhan was loved by the people of Shu to the point that he was "overly praised." 
When Wei sent Deng Ai and Zhong Hui to invade Shu, Zhuge Zhan missed the chance to fight back and retreated to Mianzhu Pass. 
With no chance of winning and Deng Ai already sending an envoy to convince him to surrender, Zhuge Zhan defended Shu with his son Zhuge Shang until the end. 
Though intellectually unequal to his father, he was surely as loyal.

Officer of Shu. When Liu Bei entered Shu, he joined him as Jing Assistant Officer. He then became Zhuti Governor when Liu Bei conquered Yi province, and was assigned to supervise foreign tribes in Nanchang to the south. He was respected for fending off larger forces with smaller numbers.
A fictional character, daughter of Deng Ai.

A native of Yiyang, Xinye, Shuhan official, son of Deng Zhi. When Wei defeated Shu, Liu Chan ordered Deng Liang, Zhang Shao, Qiao Zhou and others to bring the seal and surrender to Deng Ai. After the Jin Dynasty replace the Wei Dynasty, he became the Governor of Guanghan.

From Jiyang, Yiyang, Deng Zhong was Deng Ai's son. 
He followed Deng Ai to guard the west territory and repelled the Shu army multiple times. 
Later, Deng Zhong and his father participated in the conquest of Shu. The two passed Yinping Path to ambush Mianzhu Pass. Deng Zhong and Shi Zuan were ordered to battle. They were first stopped by Zhuge Zhan but Deng Ai ordered to execute anyone who retreated. The two had no option but to defeat the Shu army. 
After invading Chengdu, Deng Ai was framed into arrest by Zhong Hui and Deng Zhong was arrested as well. The two were killed on the way back to the capital.

Deng Mao was a fictional character in the Romance of Three Kingdoms. He was a Yellow Turban general who led 50, 000 soldiers with Marshal Cheng Yuan Zhi to invade Liu Bei's hometown, Zhuo Commandery. 
They fought Liu, Guan, and Zhang at the foot of Mt. Daxing. Deng Mao struck first but was stabbed and killed by Zhang Fei.

General Sun Ce, brother-in-law of Lu Meng. Lu Meng relied on Deng Dang at the beginning, and secretly followed Deng Dang several times to crusade against the Shanyue. After Dengdang's subordinates repeatedly insulted Lu Meng, Lu Meng killed him in anger, and then confessed his crime, so he was favored by Sun Ce. After Deng Dang died, Lu Meng inherited his military power.

A native of Zhangling, Jingzhou, under Liu Biao. His name may be Deng Xi. 
After Cao Cao welcomed Emperor Xu, Liu Biao sent an envoy to pay tribute to the Han court, but he still had dealings with Yuan Shao. Deng Yi had advised Liu Biao on this matter, but Liu Biao did not comply, so Deng Yi resigned from his post, claiming to be sick. 
Only after Cao Cao went down to Jingzhou did he serve again. His subsequent experiences are unknown.

A native of Nanyang, Xinye, Cao Wei official. Power minister Cao Shuang partisan. At the time of Emperor Ming of Wei dynasty, he was deposed because of theFuhua case. After the death of Emperor Ming, Cao Shuang was reactivated when he took power. Because of Cao Shuang's favor, he became more indulgent and defied the laws and regulations. After Gao Pingling's rebellion, he and Cao Shuang were both killed.

A native of Gaomi, Beihai, Cao Wei official. Grandson of Zheng Xuan, a great master of Confucian classics. Once taught Cao Mao "Shangshu" with Sakong Zhengchong. After being questioned by Sima Shi, he was poisoned. Or it said Sima Zhao.

A native of Nanyang, Xinye, the mother of Deng Zhi. His name can be found in the Taoist classic "Zhen Gao" compiled by Tao Hongjing in the Southern Liang Dynasties. In addition, "Zhen Gao" has plagiarized the "the Sutra of Forty-two Sections".

A native of Kaifeng, Xingyang, an official of Cao Wei and Western Jin Dynasty. He was baseborn, eager to learn and talented, and was promoted by Cao Pi. Once taught Cao Mao "Shangshu" with Zheng Xiaotong, the servant. When Cao Huan demised, Zheng Chong entered and offered a letter of abdication to Sima Yan.

A native of Kaifeng, Xingyang, an official of Cao Wei and Western Jin Dynasty. Xun You once praised him for being knowledgeable and able to distinguish others. Served as local governor of many places, all have governance achievements, and the officials and the people are pleased to subdue. Cao Huan was blind due to illness during his reign and repeatedly begged to retire and was not approved. Until the Jin Dynasty replaced the Wei Dynasty, he was still recommended by scholars at the time and Sima Yan paid attention to him, and he was invited to serve as Engineering Supervisor many times.
