Staff officer of Wei. He fled to Huainan to avoid strife and was well-received by Yuan Shu, but he sought safety with the Yu Zhang Governor when he prophesied Yuan Shu's fall. He later joined Cao Cao and had a career of governorships. Passionate about agriculture, irrigation, and law, he was beloved by the people. Cao Pi highly regarded his irrigation works, and he was made Court Architect in Cao Rui's age.

A native of Kaifeng, Xingyang, he was the son of Zheng Mao, an official of Wei Dynasty and the Western Jin Dynasty. He was knowledgeable as his father. He was once instructed to "assess the old texts and delete the foulness" of the books in the court. Until the Jin Dynasty replaced the Wei Dynasty, he was appreciated by Emperor Wu of Jin and appointed him as a eunuch, often following him.

A native of Fufeng, Mei County, he was appointed to the Cao Wei Dynasty and the Western Jin Dynasty. In his early years, guarded the Western Frontiers for Cao Wei and resisted the Northern Expedition of the Shu Han. When Gao Pingling rebellion, he urged Cao Shuang to fight against the Sima clan as a supporter. If he surrendered, he would surely be killed. But Cao Shuang refused to listen, and was eventually killed, and Lu Zhi was implicated and sentenced to death. However, he was so persistent that he was appreciated by Sima Yi and reactivated after he was exonerated. During Zhuge Dan's rebellion, Lu Zhi took the lead in the army and made great achievements in pacifying the rebellion.
A fictional character, daughter of Lu Su.
Staff officer of Wu, and the son of Lu Su. He and Xue Ying led an army to attack Jin, but was defeated by Wang Hun, the general of Jin.

Yuan Shu's subordinate. When Cao Cao personally led an army to attack Yuan Shu, Yuan Shu fled in a hurry, leaving Qiao Rui, Li Feng, Liang Gang and Le Jiu behind. All four generals were executed after their defeat.

A native of Fanyang, Zhuo, an official of Cao Wei and Western Jin Dynasty, and the grandson of Lu Zhi. Noble and unsullied, fond of classics. Was confiscated by Cao Shuang as auxiliary, and was implicated and dismissed from office during the Gao Pingling rebellion. Later, it was gradually reused by the Sima family, once became Shangshu Buye, managing secret.

Staff officer of Wei. Though Lu Yu lost his father and brother at a young age, he took good care of his sister-in-law and nephew through the chaos, his knowledge and grace well-praised. He became Ji Province Registrar under Cao Pi, moving to presided over many counties after Cao Pi's succession. Lu Yu then became a personnel officer in Cao Rui's age and nominated those of talent. He was spurned by Cao Shuang later, but was the one to judge him when Sima Yi took power.

Mu Shun was a fictional character in the Romance of Three Kingdoms and a general under Zhang Yang. When the coalition against Dong was stopped by Lu Bu at HuLao Gate, Mu Shun challenged Lu Bu but was slain easily by Lu Bu.

A native of Wu county, Wucheng. At the end of the Eastern Han Dynasty, the world was in chaos, Qian Tong gathered together more than 10, 000 people. Later it was broken by Sun Ce, and Qian Tong was also killed.

From Nan Commandery, Jing Province, Yan Yu was a official of Shu Han. He had meritorious deeds and was a diligent man. His reputation was only slightly lower than that of Ma Zhong. Though he fawned over Huang Hao, who was favored by Liu Shan, he didn't conduct any immoral deeds. 
In the Conquest of Shu by Wei, he led the troops to aid Chengdu. No document of him was found later. 
In the Romance of Three Kingdoms, he was defamed as an incompetent snob. When Huang Hao suggested to Liu Shan to replace Jiang Wei with Yan Yu, Yan Yu refused out of cowardliness as he heard Deng Ai excelled at military affairs.

From Jincheng, Liangzhou, Yan Xing was originally Han Sui's general who submitted to Cao Cao after the Battle of Tong Gate. He then changed his name to Yan Yan. 
He was a minor general under Han Sui. When Han Sui battled Ma Teng, Yan Xing fought Ma Chao and almost killed him. 
After Ma Teng assumed a position in the palace, Han Sui sent Yan Xing as an envoy to Cao Cao. When he returned, he advised Han Sui to submit to Cao Cao but was ignored. 
In the Battle of Tong Gate, to stop Yan Xing from surrendering to Cao, Han Sui married his daughter to him but failed to change his mind. In the end, Yan Xing still went to submit to Cao Cao.

Shuhan official, former Brazilian Governor. After the defeat of Battle of Yiling, Yan Zhi issued five thousand troops to Liu Bei. It is mentioned in the "Second Northern Expedition Memorial" that he died before the second Northern Expedition.

Yan Rou was a general of Cao Wei who first served under Yuan Shao before serving under Cao Cao. 
When young, he was abducted by the Wuhuan and Xianbei tribes. He later earned the trust of Xianbei people. With their help, he became Wuhuan Marshal and fought Gongsun Zan. After the Battle of Guandu, he surrendered to Cao Cao, who treated him like a son. 
Yan Rou was friendly with the tribes. The Xianbei people submitted to his ruling, with Xianbei leaders Bu Dugen and Ke Bineng sending their sons as hostages and even helping quell revolts.

Yan Xiang was Yuan Shu's subordinate. 
When Yuan Shu planned to hold the Imperial Seal and declare himself an emperor, Yan Xiang tried to stop him with the example of King Wen of Zhou, who held 2/3 of the country but still submitted to his ruler. But Yuan Shu quoted a prophecy "The one to replace Han is the one on the right path." He emphasized that his curtesy name "Gonglu" meant "on the right path" which stated that he was the one and still declared himself an emperor.

Later Han official. Liang Province Aide-de-camp. When Jicheng was surrounded by Ma Chao, he left the castle in secret to seek help from Xiahou Yuan, but he was captured by Ma Chao. Ma Chao demanded that he tell the besieged castle that no reinforcements would be coming, but he was killed because he gave the defenders encouragement, saying reinforcements were on their way instead.

From Zhijiang, Nan Commandery, Huo Yi served under Shu Han and Western Jin and was the son of Huo Jun. In the Romance, he was falsely named Huo Ge. 
He was a major general in the late Shu. When Liu Shan surrendered to Wei, Huo Yi was Administrator of Jianning. When he learned the fall of the kingdom, he put on plain clothes, looked west to the old capital, and cried for 3 days. 
Later, in Jiaozhi Chaos, Huo Yi led his troops to aid Lu Xing. After Lu Xing was killed by a subordinate, Huo Yi led Dong Yuan, Mao Jiong, Meng Gan and others joined the battle again, securing three commanderies, Jiaozhi, Rinan, and Jiuzhen.

A native of Kuaiji, Wushang, the father of Luo Tong. At the end of the Eastern Han Dynasty, he was appointed as Chen Guoxiang. Yuan Shu wanted to take grain from Chen, but Luo Jun rejected and sent Zhang Kai to kill Luo Jun and Liu Chong.

From Wushang, Kuaiji, Luo Tong was a politician of Eastern Wu. As Chancellor of Wucheng, he performed well and was scouted by Sun Quan. 
After Ling Tong passed, Luo Tong succeeded his position. He scored an exploit when he followed Lu Xun to fight the Shu army in the Battle of Yiling. He also repelled Cao Ren in the third Battle of Ruxukou. He was later promoted to Area Commander of Ruxu. 
Besides his military and political achievements, he was also respected for his reasonable and honest admonitions.

Bao San Niang was not found in official records but only in local tales and folklores. The opera Biography of Hua Guan Suo from Ming Dynasty was the most notable one. 
Comprehensive Records of Sichuan wrote, "Bao was Guan Suo's wife. She lived in Bao's family house in Kui Province." 
However, the interesting thing was that Guan Suo was also not found in official records like the Records of the Three Kingdoms. 
Legend has it that after Bao San Niang married to Guan Suo, the two followed Zhuge Liang south to conquer Meng Huo and scored merits in the battle to quell Nanzhong. 
Yanxing Year 1 of Shu, Zhong Hui led a great army to attack Shu. The two were ordered to guard Jiameng Pass and both died in action for their kingdom.

Bao Long was a fictional character in the Romance of Three Kingdoms and a subordinate under Zhao Fan, Administrator of Guiyang. He used to be a hunter who once shot and killed two fierce tigers. When Zhao Yun attacked Guiyang, Zhao Fan originally wanted to surrender but Bao Long talked him out of it and led the troops to resist Zhao Yun with Chen Ying. He was defeated and captured. 
After Zhao Fan submitted, he wished to marry his widowed sister-in-law, Fan, to Zhao Yun but was rejected. Out of doubt, he started a revolt. Bao Long and Chen Ying made a false surrender but Zhao Yun disclosed the scheme, slain the two, and captured Zhao Fan.

Staff officer of Wei. Son of Bai Shin. His father's achievements earning him an invitation from Cao Cao, he was appointed Crown Prince's Attendant when Cao Pi became prince. Virtuous, he treated Cao Pi fairly, but was disliked due to his scoldings. After Cao Pi's ascension, though he received a high post, he was sent away after warning against Cao Pi's attack on Wu. Then, after committing a minor infraction, he was sentenced to death despite protestations of the court.

Once served as one of the eight Commandant of the West Park, he earned merits in the crusading Yellow Turban Army of Yuzhou. However, Huangwan reported him, and he was sent to prison for embezzlement official property and tens of millions money.

Younger brother of Bao Xin. He followed his brother into the coalition against Dong Zhuo. Bao Xin. Angry that Sun Jian had taken all the glory, he secretly ordered Bao Tao to attack Sishua, but Bao Tao was slain there by Hua Xiong.

A native of Runan, Nandun, an official of Cao Wei and the Western Jin Dynasty. Good at discussing, known for talents. After the Jin Dynasty replaced Wei Dynasty, due to his proficiency in Confucianism, he was ordered to work with Grand Commandant Xun yi to write new etiquette .
Nanyang county Examiner. The defender of Wancheng, Hou Yin, rebelled and communicated with Guan Yu. He wanted to hold the Governor Dongli Gun, but Yingyu fought to cover Dongli Gun to death.

A native of Runan, Nandun, Cao Wei official. He is knowledgeable and literary, and good at writting. When Cao Shuang monopolized power, he violated many laws, and Ying Qu wrote a poem to express satire.

From Yingchuan, Xi Zhi Cai was an adviser under Cao Cao. Recommended to Cao Cao by Xun Yu, Xi Zhi Cai was greatly valued by Cao Cao but he died young. Cao Cao therefore lamented, "Ever since Zhi Cai died, I have no one to form strategies with." and asked Xun Yu for a successor of Zhi Cai. Xun Yu later recommended Guo Jia.

Dai Yuan was the subordinate of Sheng Xian, the former Governor of Wu county, who was killed by Sun Quan. He and Gui Lan fled into the mountain, waiting for an opportunity to take revenge. Later, they were pardoned by Sun Yi, the Governor of Dan Yang. They instigated Bian Hong to kill Sun Yi and then killed Bian Hong. He also killed Sun He, who came to ask for guilt, and planned to surrender to Cao Cao. Finally, the two were killed by Sun Yi's wife Xu and Sun Yi's former subordinates Xu Yuan, Sun Gao and Fu Ying.

Cao Wei officials. Jointly persuaded Cao Pi to become the emperor. He was sentenced to a severe sentence for repeatedly admonishing Cao Pi not to hunt, and was pardoned and reinstated later. During Zhuge Liang's Fourth Northern Expedition, he accompanied Sima Yi to fight against the Shu army and was ordered to guard Shanggui.

A native of Chenliu, Waihuang, official to the prime minister of Dongwu. Before Sun Xiu passed away, entrusted his son to Puyang Xing, but Wan Yu tried his best to recommend Sun Hao to Puyang Xing and Zhang Bu, so changed Sun Hao as emperor. Not long after Sun Hao ascended the throne, his tyrannical nature was exposed . Puyang Xing and Zhang Bu complained privately about regretting the establishment of Sun Hao. They were delated, so they were put to death by Sun Hao and implicated their relatives.

From Qu County, Donghai, Mi Zhen was Mi Zhu's sister and Liu Bei's wife. When Xu Province was ambushed by Lu Bu, Liu Bei was at his worst but he got help from Mi Zhu, who even married his sister to Liu Bei. 
Later, when Cao Cao attacked Xu Province, Lady Mi and Guan Yu were both captured. No mention of her was found in official records. 
In the Romance of Three Kingdoms, Guan Yu escorted Liu Bei's wife back to him alone. In the end, in the Battle of Changban, she entrusted her son to Zhao Yun and committed suicide by jumping into a well so she wouldn't burden him.

Born in Yingchuan. He first served under Liu Biao with Du Xi, Zhao Yan and others, and later served under Cao Cao. He was well-known in Ru and Ying areas for his literary talent and eloquence. He also wrote The Conquest of Tianshan, describing Zhang Liao's battle against Chen Lan and Mei Cheng.

A native of Lanling, Donghai. Cao Wei official. He was talented and left numerous masterpieces. He served House Cao for four generations until Cao Fang. And the highest appointment was Superintendent of the Imperial Court.

He was an official of Cao Wei. He was a loyal and capable official of the world. 
When Chen Gong welcomed Lu Bu into Yan, Xue Ti helped Cheng Yu and Xun Yu to defend Jancheng County, Fan County and Dong'a County without losing. After that, he participated in the battle of Hefei and fought with Sima Yi against Shu. 
He also participated in the battle of Hefei and the fight against Shu with Sima Yi. Although Xue Ti's administration was mainly based on Confucianism, he was also compatible with the strengths of various schools of thought.

From Zhuyi, Pei Commandery, Xue Xu was a Eastern Wu general, Xue Zong's eldest son, and Xue Ying's elder brother. 
As an envoy to Shu Han, he foresaw the fall of Shu Han and commented, "The ruler doesn't know his mistakes. The officials only try to not get into trouble." and "Small birds can't see the upcoming disaster." 
In Jiaozhi Chaos, he led the troops to a grand victory against Jin generals, Mao Jiong, Yang Ji, Meng Gan, Cuan Neng, and Li Song and regain Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen, Rinan which were occupied by Jin forces.

From Zhuyi, Pei Commandery, Xue Ying was a Eastern Wu general, Xue Zong's second son, and Xue Xu's younger brother. He was uncorrupt, diligent, and loyal. 
During Sun Liang's rule, Xue Ying, Zhou Zhao, Liang Guang, and Hua He were ordered to assist the historian Wei Zhao in writing the Book of Wu. 
Later, Wei Zhao was executed by Sun Hao and Xue Ying became in charge of the writing of historical records.
He was a native of Xiang County in Peiguo. He joined Chen Gong and Zhang Miao to welcome Lu Bu into Yan, but was defeated by Cao's army and Xue Lan was killed by Cao Cao.

A native of Changshan County. Concubine of Cao Pi, also known as Xue Yelai. In Record of Gleanings, the story of Red Tears was about her. And she was regarded as the Goddess of Needlework. There are also other interesting tales about her.
Concubine of Emperor Hui Sima Zhong, mother of Prince Sima Yu. Jia Nanfeng falsely accuse Sima Yu of conspiracy of rebellion, Xie Jiu was implicated and killed together with Sima Yu.

A military general of Eastern Wu. After Lu Xun defeated Guan Yu and captured Jingzhou, Xie Jing and Li Yi led 3, 000 troops to attack Shu and defeated Zhan Yan, Deng Fu and Guo Mu, and captured Chen Feng. Later, with Lu Xun, he defeated Wen Bu and Deng Kai.

He was a native of Wan County, Nanyang, and an official of the Eastern Wu Dynasty. He was a guest of Prince Sun Deng in the East Palace and later became the governor of Yuzhang, where he was praised by the officials and the people for his good performance.

The fictional character in "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms". The subordinate of Xiahou Dun. During the Battle of Changbano, he and his brother Zhong Jin were killed by Zhao Yun, who just got the Blue Steel Sword.

A native of Changshe in the original river, wife of Wang Hun. Ancestor was a famous minister of Cao Wei, Zhong Yao. He was a clever and elegant person, a good reader of records, good in appearance and manners, good in poetry and literature, and had a collection of works. 
There are also anecdotes about her ability to look at people.

From Changshe, Yingchuan, Zhong Yu was Zhong Yao's son and Zhong Hui's elder brother. He was quick-witted like his father. He was insightful about the world situation as well as military affairs. He once advised Sima Zhao not to allow Zhong Hui to seize great power, whose children were therefore able to remain safe during Zhong Hui's rebellion.

A fictional character in the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, he was a member of Cao's army under Xiahou Dun. During the battle of Chang Ban Po, he and his brother Zhong Gen blocked Zhao Yun and they were killed by Zhao Yun who had just won the Green Submarine Sword.

Huiji Shanyin people, the general of the Eastern Wu. Zhong Li is a compound surname. He had the style of an elder and was a wise and brave man. He was good at dealing with the southern barbarians such as Shan Yue and Wu Squab, and was ordered to pacify them several times.

Qingzhou Linzi people, Cao Wei officials, fraudulent surrender to the Eastern Wu. He was quite talented and skillful in arguing. 
He was instructed by Emperor Ming of Wei to rebel against Wei and join Wu. During his stay in Wu, he won the trust of important officials such as Quan Zong, Zhu Zai and Hao Pu. 
Later, Yinfan tried to separate from the rulers and ministers of Dongwu, but was arrested for his failed rebellion and refused to give up his henchmen until he was executed.

Han Zhong was a subordinate of Zhang Mancheng, a Yellow Turban marshal in the Nanyang region. After Zhang Mancheng and Zhao Hong were subdued by Zhu Jun, General of the Household Who Suppresses Rebels, and Qin Jie, Administrator of Nanyang, the Yellow Turban forces in Nanyang supported Han Zhong as the leader for the resistance forces in Wancheng. He was in the end tricked, defeated, and killed by Zhu Jun.

Han Yin was an official under Yuan Shu. 
After Yuan Shu declared himself an emperor, he was attacked by other warlords. When Han Yin visited Xu Province as an envoy, he wished to see Yuan Shu's son marry Lu Bu's daughter in the hopes to strengthen the allay between Yuan and Lu so Yuan Shu could have Lu Bu's support. 
However, this matter was interfered by Chen Gui. Lu Bu rejected the marriage and retrieved his daughter while Han Yin was arrested and sent to Xuchang by Lu Bu. He was then executed in public by Cao Cao.

Han Juzi was a subordinate under Yuan Shao. In the Battle of Guandu, he was ordered to escort food supplies with Chunyu. Later, Xu You surrendered to Cao and suggested they attacked the supply warehouses in Wuchao, Han Juzi was defeated and killed.

A native of Nanyang Juyang, an official of Cao Wei. He is famous for his patience and revenge for his father and brother. He was recruited several times by the Eastern Han court, Yuan Shu and Liu Biao, but refused to serve, and finally reluctantly accepted because Liu Biao held a grudge against him. 
Later, he served Cao Cao and was praised for improving the smelting method.

He was originally a general of Wu, but later joined Cao Wei. His father, Han Dang, was one of the twelve tiger vassals of Jiangdong, and after his death, he inherited his titles and troops. 
He was appointed by Sun Quan to be the governor of Wuchang, but Sun Quan did not pursue him because of his merits. Later on, he was a thief and defected to Cao Wei. 
After his defeat, he was killed by Zhuge Ke and his head was sent to Sun Quan's soul.

Born in Wuyang, Yingchuan. Dong Zhuo once appointed him as Grand Herald. During the Campaign against Dong Zhuo, he was tasked by Dong Zhuo to enlist Guandong Coalition and was spared because of his virtues. Later in the Rebellion of Li Jue and Guo Si, they held Emperor Xian and officials as hostages, Han Rong was also among them.

Famous assassin in the Three Kingdoms period. Kebineng plotted to rebel and invaded Bingzhou several times, so the Inspector of Youzhou Wang Xiong sent Han Long to assassinate Kebineng. After his success, no one had never heard about him again.
A fictional character, daughter of Han Fu.

Palace Assistance of Eastern Han. When Dong Zhuo seized cotrol of capital, he was arbitrary and wanted to establish authority. So when Rao Longzong presented himself before Dong Zhuo with his sword on, he was executed.

Officer of Wu. After attaining Yuzhang's Merit Officer post on Yu Fan's recommendation, Nie You joined Gu Tan and Gu Cheng in Zhuge Ke's good graces. He later became a general and put down the rebellions at Zhu Ya and Dan Er before becoming the governor of Danyang. In 253, Zhuge Ke was killed by Sun Jun, and since they were on poor terms, Nie You's post moved to Yulin, where he died a quiet death.

Born in Xiapi. With 3000 people under command, he claimed himself emperor. Instigated by Tao Qian, he tried to invade the counties around Taishan. But Tao Qian betrayed, he killed Que Xuan and took his men.

Wei You was Liu Yu's subordinate. Gongsun Zan was Liu Yu's subordinate but the two had conflicted ideas about policies on the tribal people. Gongsun Zan supported forceful actions while Liu Yu wished to handle it with kindness. However, Gongsun Zan repeatedly disobeyed Liu Yu, who worried that he would rebel in the future and wished to eliminate him first. He sought advice from Wei You, who said, "You're the ruler now who need the help of your subordinates." Zan was competent in civil and military affairs. Though he had his flaws, it'd be best if you tolerate them. After Wei You died of illness, Liu Yu led his troops to attack Gongsun Zan but he lost and escaped to Juyong.

Born in Fanyi, Ren City. Cao Wei and Jin official. He was maverick and fond of wine. Good at equestrian skill and archery. Later he was favored by Sima Yan and Sima Zhao. During the period of Jin Dynasty, he was appointed as Education Supervisor.
She was born in Fan Yi, Rencheng, and is said to be the daughter of Wei Shu. She was honored by Shangqing and Maoshan as the founder of the mountain, with the title of South Mountain Zixu Yuanjun.

The Shiyu claimed Wei Feng from Pei but Wang Chang's Admonition to Son recorded that he was from Jiyin. Talented and famed, he acquainted himself with many other officials. However, there were also people like Fu Xun, Liu Ye, and Zheng Mao who thought Wei Feng seemed treacherous. 
While Cao Cao conquered Hanzhong in person, Wei Feng took the chance to plot a revolt to seize Yecheng with Chen Yi, the Minister of the Guards of Changle. But Chen Yi felt fearful and informed Cao Pi of it instead. Cao Pi executed Wei Feng, along with dozens of his associates. Annals of the Later Han even claimed thousands were executed along with him.

The general of Dong Wu. When he and his military guards Shi Shuo noticed that the vassal, Sun Qiun, was mobilizing his troops and using his armament, they were afraid of a rebellion, so they informed Sun Huo and enabled him to eliminate Sun Qiun

He was a native of Shangyu, Huiji, and an official of the Eastern Wu Dynasty. He was a straightforward and uncompromising person who did not conform to the wishes of his superiors, thus angering Sun Ce, who wanted to kill him in anger. Later, he was persuaded by Madam Wu, Sun Ce's mother, to stay alive.
The leader of Shanyue. He and Li Huan were entrenched in the areas of Luling and Nanhai. So Sun Quan ordered Liu Zuan and Tang Zi to root them out.

From Xiangyang, Jing Province, Luo Xian was a military general of the late Shu Han. 
When young, he studied under the great scholar Qiao Zhou and became famed for his talent. 
When Shu fell, though he had received Liu Shan's letter of surrender, he insisted on resisting Sun Wu forces, who took the chance to invade Badong. He retreated while fighting all the way to Baidicheng before being besieged by Wu forces and surrendering to Wei. 
After Sima Yan usurped Wei, Luo Xian recommended many offsprings of Shu officials to him, Chen Shou included.

Shi Chong, the wealthy man of Western Jin, found Xuan Feng when she was young. When she grew up, the gorgeous appearance and good literacy made her the most beloved of Shi Chong. After she was over 30, other young concubines were jealous of her and defamed her. So she was in disgrace with Shi Chong and was sent to live with other servants. After Shi Chong was killed in the Upheaval of the Eight Princes, she was spared because of being a maidservant.

From Xichong, Baxi, Qiao Zhou was an official of Shu Han and a great scholar. Chen Shou, Luo Xian, Wen Li, Li Mi, and Du Zhen were all his pupils. 
Showing disapproval of Jiang Wei's meritless northern expeditions which cost lives and great fortune, he wrote Chou Guo Lun to state the cons of Jiang Wei's northern expeditions. In the Conquest of Shu by Wei, he advised the last emperor Liu Shan to open the city gates and surrendered, and was therefore given the title of a marquis.
The subordinate of Sun Yi. Since Sun Yi reproached him, he had held grudges. Dai Yuan and Gui Lan deluded Bian Hong into killing Sun Yi and killed him afterwards.

Born in Jin City, Liangzhou. He and Han Sui were former Han officials, but they were kidnapped by Liangzhou rebels Beigong Boyu, Li Wenhou, Song Yang and Wang Guo. After the two joined the rebels, they gradually became warlords, so they had to change names because they were wanted by the court. 
Later Han Sui killed Beigong Boyu and Li Wenhou, and Bian Zhang was also killed by Han Sui. Someone also said that Bian Zhang died of illness.

From Xie County, Hedong, Guan Tong was a general of Shu Han, Guan Xing's son, and Guan Yu's grandson. 
He married a princess but her name was unmentioned in historical records. He served as an officer in Huben Division. As Guan Tong was heirless, he named his concubine's son, Guan Yi, as his successor.

From Taiyuan, Bing Province, Guan Jing was Chief Clerk under Gongsun Zan. 
When Gongsun Zan was surrounded by Yuan Shao's army in Yijing, Gongsun Zan tried to ally with the generals in Heishan to repel Yuan's army from behind. But Guan Jing thought that, as their army already had a low morale, guarding where they were until Yuan's army retreated on their own was the better way, which Gongsun Zan followed. 
The Yuan army later broke through the city's defense and Gongsun Zan committed suicide by self-immolation. Regretful that he stopped Gongsun Zan from sending out his army, Guan Jing lamented, "I heard when you put someone in danger, you must suffer with them. How can I live on my own then!" He charged into Yuan Shao's army alone and died.
The name of the artist is found in "Xi Nang Yu" and "Gleanings", and is one of the four beauties of Sun Liang's harem.
He was a native of Xiping, Liangzhou, and sent the head of Han Sui to Cao Cao with Jiang Shi. He was defeated and killed by Su Ze, a Wei general.

Born in Xiangyang, Jinzhou. Heir of Pang Shanmin and Pang Degong, brother of Pang Tong. The name of Pang Xiu is fictional. He and his father were famous scholars in Jin and Xiang areas. And his wife was the elder sister of Zhuge Liang. Later, he served as official of Cao Wei.

He was a native of Xiangyang, Jingzhou, an official of the Shu Han Dynasty, and the son of Pang Tong. He was a straightforward man, who had a problem with the latter's favorite minister, Chen Gion, and was therefore suppressed by Chen Gion and was never reappointed in his life.

A native of Xiangyang, Jingzhou, brother of Pang Tong. When Liu Bei launched the Battle of Yiling, he accompanied the general of Shu Han to the north of the river to prevent the attack of Wei army. But because of Liu Bei's defeat, Huang Quan's retreat was cut off and he was left alone, so he had to surrender to Cao Wei.

Born in Nan'an , Liangzhou. Shu official and brother of Pang De. During the Battle of Xiangfan, because Pang Rou served under Liu Bei, Pang De was questioned by the surrendered of Cao Wei. When Pang De was captured, Guan Yu tried to persuade him to surrender for Pang Rou.

Officer of Wei. Pang Yu was praised as a righteous warrior after crying without worry for Handang Shang, killed by the rebelling Zhang Meng while he was magistrate of Poqiang. He later served the Jiuqan Governor and desperately escaped the castle to seek reinforcements when a rebellion occurred. He was later recruited by Cao Cao and became a marquis in Cao Pi's age.
Born in Xiangyang, Jinzhou. Son of Pang Shanmin and nephew of Zhuge Liang. He once was the Governor of Zangke, but chose to resign and returned to his hometown.

A native of Xiangyang, Jingzhou. Famouse scholar and hermit in Jing and Xiang area. Uncle of Pang Tong. He was a shrewd judge of character. The pseudonym of Sima Hui, Zhuge Liang, Pang Tong and others all came from him. He refused to serve in court and led a seclusive life in Lumen Mountain.
A fictional character, daughter of Yan Baihu.

A fictional character in the Romance of Three Kingdoms, Yan Zheng was the subordinate of Zhang Bao, the Yellow Turban Digong General. 
When Zhang Bao was attacked by Zhu Jun and Liu Bei's allied army in Yangcheng, Yan Zheng saw no way to win so he decapitated Zhang Bao and surrendered to Zhu Jun.

Born in Jingzhao, Sili. He was ordered to lead a punitive expedition against Yuan Shu, who died of illness when he arrived. He was appointed as the Inspector of Yangzhou. When Sun Ce attacked Jiangdong, Yan Xiang was killed by Sun Ce's subordinate Li Shu.

Yan Gang was a military general under Gongsun Zan. 
In the Battle of Jieqiao, Yan Gang led the Baima volunteer militia as the vanguard to attack Yuan Shao's forces. Seeing that Yuan Shao didn't have many soldiers, Gongsun Zan ordered the cavalry to attack by force. But they were defeated by the food soldiers and archers led by Yuan Shao's subordinate, Qu Yi. Yan Gang was killed by Yuan's army in this battle.

Du Youdao's wife, born in Jingzhao, Sili. Zhenshu is knowledgeable and a shrewd judge of character. She had foreseen that He Yan and Deng Shao would be rooted out by Sima Yi. She also asserted that Fu Xian and Du Yu would achieve greatness.

From Wuchen, Wu Commandery, Yan Yu was the younger brother of Yan Baihu. 
When Sun Ce came down to Jiangdong, Yan Baihu failed to defeat the enemy forces so sent Yan Yu to Sun Ce for a truce. Sun Ce slain Yan Yu, who was famed for his strength and bravery. Yan Baihu and his men were all shocked and panicked after they heard the news.
Originally the Governor of Hanzhong. The Shepherd of Yizhou ordered Zhang Lu and Zhang Xiu to attack Hanzhong. After the fall of Hanzhong, Su Gu was killed by Zhang Xiu.

A Wei bureaucrat. Governor of Jiuquan, Anding, and Wudu, Su Ze boasted a fearsome name. Cao Cao found him while mobilizing and appointed him governor of Jincheng. He worked to revitalize his fatigued people after the war and worked with the Qiang. After Cao Cao's death, he subjugated the rebellious Qu Yan and stabilized Western Liang. However, he was later hated by Cao Pi and died on the way to an assignment.

Su Fei was a military general under Liu Biao. Friendly with Gan Ning, he knew Gan Ning was a talent and recommended him to Huang Zu several times but Huang Zu refused to recruit Gan Ning as he used to be a pirate. 
Later, when Gan Ning wished to submit to Sun Quan, he was worried he would be killed by Huang Zu. He was able to make his escape thanks to Su Fei. 
Later, Sun Quan ordered Gan Ning to attack Jiangxia and specified that he killed Huang Zu and Su Fei. For the old favor's sake, Gan Ning vouched for Su Fei with his own life and Su Fei was therefore spared.

Born in Wugong, Fufeng. During the reign of Emperor Jin of Wu, he was the Imperial Court Grandee. Later, he served as the Inspector of Liangzhou, and was defeated during the rebellion of Tufa Shujineng.
Cao Wei officials. Guan Jun was ordered by Cao Pi to supervise and correct Cao Zhi's behaviors. His reports had caused Cao Zhi to be demoted from Prince of Dong'e to Marquis of Anxiang.

He fought with the army several times and was promoted to general because of his success in battle. Later, he and his brother, Gu Tan, followed Prince Sun He during the dispute between the two palaces and were attacked and framed by King Sun Ba's party members, including Quan Zong, and they were both exiled to Jiaoshu.

He was a native of Wu County, Wu County, Wu County, and an official of the Eastern Wu Dynasty, son of Gu Yong. When he was young, he was very famous, and his reputation exceeded that of Lu Xun. He was also praised by Pang Tong for his great talent in carrying weight and reaching far. He had the ability to know people and many of his recommendations were successful.

Born in Wu County, an official of Wu and the younger brother of Gu Yong. During the Rebellion of Jiaozhi, he was ordered to suppress the insurgency and regain the lost ground. But because of his failures, Yulin and Jiuzhen were also taken by Jin. Gu Rong had to flee to Hepu.

Grandson of Wu Prime Minister Gu Yong, son of Gu Shao, and brother to Gu Cheng. He was friends with the Crown Prince, Sun Deng, and none could match his unparalleled knowledge. He became Minister of Ceremonies after Gu Yong's death. He then advised Sun Quan, who doted on Sun Ba while ignoring Prince Sun He, to prioritize his heir. This soured Gu Tan's relationship with Sun Ba, ending in him being exiled out of spite. He wrote 20 books in rage and died after 2 years of exile.
A fictional character, daughter of Gong Jing.

The fictional character in The Romance of the Three Kingdoms. The Governor of Qingzhou. After being besieged by the Yellow Turban, he asked Liu Yan for help. With the help of Liu Bei, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei, they repelled the Yellow Turban Army together.
Shu official. Friend of Zhang Yi and Yao Ni. During Zhuge Liang's Southern Campaign, he was killed by Li Qiucheng. Later the murderer was captured and executed by Zhang Ni.

Born in Guangxin, Cangwu. The younger brother of Shi Xie. He was the Governor of Jiuzhen. Later, Wu plotted to nibble up Jiaozhou with new county policy, Shi Hui, the son of Shi Xie, was angry about it and rebelled, but eventually he was defeated and killed. So Shi Cheng surrendered and was deposed as common civilian. Later he was executed for some other reason.
Born in Kuaiji, Yangzhou. The Traveling alchemist active in Wu area. He was skilled in all kinds of divine arts, especially in stealth. Rumor had it that Sun Qun invited him and treated with respect.
Subordinate of Gongsun Kang, the Governor of Liaodong. He was in charge of Daifang. He once led troops to attack small state of Han and Ye.

Wei governor of Wuwei. Father of Guanqiu Jian and Guanqiu Xiu. After subjugating the Qiang, he governed Wuwei, and his fame reached Su Ze. When Zhang Jin and Huang Hua revolted in response to Qu Yan, Su Ze sought his help and they worked together to defeat Zhang Jin.
He was subordinate of Cao Cao. But when Lu Bu came to Yanzhou, he and Xu Xi betrayed Cao Cao. And after Lu Bu's defeat, he joined Zang Ba, the Mount Tai Bandit.

Native in Taiyuan County. Upright and outspoken. When Li Jue breahed Luoyang and captured Wang Yun, Wang Hong was in charge of You Fufeng and Song Yi was in charge of Zuo Fengyi. Li Jue was afraid of their resistance, so he issued an edict, ordering them to come to court. Wang Hong intended to raise armies, but in Song Yi's opinion, the edict was infrangible. So upon arrival in capital, they were both arrested and executed.

A native of Jinyang, Taiyuan, he served Cao Wei and Western Jin Dynasty. 
Cao Mao intended to root out Sima Zhao, so he discussed about it with Wang Shen, Wang Jing and Wang Ye. But Wang Jing persuaded him to wait for a good opportunity. While Wang Shen and Wang Ye suggested they reported to Sima Zhao about Cao Mao, but Wang Jing refused. So the other two reported on their own. After Sima Zhao learned the fact, he executed Wang Jing and Cao Mao.

A native of Linyi, Langya. Senior official of the Western Jin Dynasty. Father of Wang Huifeng, the concubine of Prince Sima Yu. 
After the Rebellion of the Eight Princes, the Central Plains withered and the people's livelihood declined. Though in the high ranks of official, Wang Yan never cared about it and only thought about his own safety. Before the Disaster of Yongjia, he was held captive by Shi Le. 
During their conversation, Wang Yan asserted that he scarcely handle political affairs. Shi Le said angrily: As the high rank official in the court, how can you say so! Such misconduct is your crime. And he decided to execute Wang Yan. 
Also, there's one idiom that originate from him.

A native of Jinyang, Taiyuan, a general of the Western Jin Dynasty. He was in charge of Qingzhou and Youzhou area. After the Upheaval of the Eight Princes, he intended to claim himself warlord and introduced foreign tribesmen, which sowed the seed of the Upheaval of the Five Barbarians. 
Later, he attempted to claim the emperor title and fell foul of Duan tribe. Eventually he was defeated by Shi Le.

Born in Linyi, Langye. Jin official. Brother of Wang Dao, the first Imperial Chancellor of Eastern Jin. After the Jin Royal Family evacuated to souther region, he and Wang Dao helped Sima Rui ascend the throne. 
Later, he plotted to rebel and ursurped power. In history, it is called the Rebellion of Wang Dun. But soon died of illness.
Born in Linyi, Langye. Cao Wei official. When Kebineng rebelled, Wang Xiong sent Han Long to assassinate him.

A native of Wuling, he served in the Cao Wei Dynasty and the Western Jin Dynasty. 
Sima Zhao has the power, but Wei Shao Emperor Cao Mao intends to eliminate it and summons Wang Shen, Wang Jing, and Wang Ye to discuss. Wang Jing persuaded him to hold off for a good opportunity because the young emperor had no power or anyone to use. While Wang Shen and Wang Ye suggested they reported to Sima Zhao about Cao Mao, but Wang Jing refused. So the other two reported on their own. After Sima Zhao learned the fact, he executed Wang Jing and Cao Mao.

Born in Donghai. An alchemist in late Han Dynasty. Regarded as Immortal at that time. During the reign of Emperor Ming, he ascended on the Pingdu Mountain in Fengdu. In "The Legend of the Immortals", he had a conversation with Magu, this was also the source of "the vicissitudes of life".

A native of Linyi, Langya, an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. Served as the governor of Jingzhou, brilliant and talented, but because of this Wang Dun was jealous of him. And Wang Dun sent Lu Rong to kill him.

Staff officer of Wei. When Cao Shuang fell from grace and Sima Yi took over, Linghu Yu plotted with his uncle Wang Ling to oust Cao Fang and put Cao Biao on the throne. He died of illness before acting, and this revealed the plan. Wang Ling and the Linghu family were killed.

From Wen County, Henei, Sima Zhou was the son of Sima Yi. When Cao Mao wished to overthrow Sima Zhou and became an emperor himself, Sima Zhou and Jia Chong led their troops together to besiege Cao Mao. After Jin replaced Wei, Sima Zhou led one of the armies to participate in the conquest of Wu.

A native of Wen County. Son of Emperor Wu and the younger brother of Emperor Hui. One of the princes during the Rebellion of Eight Princes. 
He participated in the killing of Sima Lun, the Prince of Zhao. But he was imperious and usurped powers. First he was defeated by Sima Teng and Wang Jun in conjunction with Wuwan Jiezhu, and finally imprisoned by Sima Xiao. After Sima Xiao died, his subordinate Liu Yu was worried that Sima Ying had long-standing prestige and might become a disaster. He issued a fake edict and killed Sima Ying.

Native in Linzi. His sister Zuo Fen was the concubine of Emperor Wu of Jin. Zuo Si was famous for Rhapsody of Three Capitals. 
Together with Shi Chong, Ouyang Jianand Pan Yue, they are all "Twenty-Four Friends of the Golden Valley." His poems and essays are different from the atmosphere of the time, and they are mostly allegorical works with a strong Jian'an style.

He was the Governor of Nanjun. Accounts about him are scarce. At odds with Duan Yan, so Yang Ding conspired with Zhong Ji and Zuo Ling to falsely accuse him of plot of rebellion. When Dong Cheng ordered his henchmen to assassinate Empress Fu, the killer was stopped by Zuo Ling. 
In The Romance of the Three Kingdoms, he was the adherents of Li Jue. During the conflict between Guo and Li, Guo Bang detained the officials and Li Yu threatened Emperor Xian, Zuo Ling and Jia Xu jointly imprisoned Emperor Xian's carriage.

Born in Waihuang, Chenliu. Together with Xun Shuang and Zheng Xuan, they were talented but never served in court. Shentu Pan did not serve as an official for his whole life and led a hermit life. The great scholar Cai Yong appreciated his talents and said his morality is better than himself.

Born in Mianzhu, Guanghan. He learned augury from Yang Hou and achieved greatness. He was equally famous as Dong Fu. In Qin Mi's comment, Dong Fu praises trivial kindness and criticized trivial vice. While Re An never forgets others' kindness and is lenient on mistakes.
He was a native of Wu Fang in Runan. When Dong Zhuo was in power, he assassinated Dong Zhuo, but was killed. Also, he may be the same person as Wu Qiong.

Born in Wufang, Ru'nan. During the dictatorship of Dong Zhuo, Yuan Shao and Dong Zhuo were at odds. Dong Zhuo wanted to kill Yuan Shao, but Wu Qiong, He Yong and others persuaded him to change his mind. 
He also conspired with Xun You, Zheng Tai, He Yong and others to assassinate Dong Zhuo, but was reported. 
He was executed by Dong Zhuo because he and Zhou Yan suggested that Dong Zhuo seal the discords as state ministers and governors. 
In addition, perhaps he was the same person as Wu Fu.

A fierce general under the command of Lu Bu, known for his courage. He was with Lu Bu when he attacked Zhang Yan. When Cao Cao pacified Lu Bu, he was captured by Cao Cao's army and was never recorded again. 
He was called one of the eight generals of Lu Bu in The Romance of the Three Kingdoms, and was shot and killed by Le Jin.

From Shangyu, Kuaiji, Zhu Jun was a famed general in the late Eastern Han. He once quelled the rebellion of Wuhu tribe in Jiaozhi and was therefore summoned to the palace. 
In the Yellow Turban Uprising, Huangfu Song and him were ordered to conquer the Yellow Turban army. They achieved a great victory against Yellow Turban leaders such as Po Cai, Zhao Hong, Han Zhong, and Xia Sun. 
He later led an army against Dong to save the Han royals but was defeated by Li Jue and Guo Si.

A native of Nancheng, Taishan, the father of the second empress of Hui Emperor Yang Xianrong. During the Rebellion of the Eight Kings, Sima Ying and Sima Yong sent troops to attack Sima Yi on the grounds that "Yang Xuanzhi and Huangfu Shang relied on their favor for disaster". Yang Xuanzhi died in fear.

A native of Liangfu, Taishan, he's a Wei official. The history books have little ink on him. He's only known as the father of Sima Shi's wife Yang Huiyu and the famous general Yang Hu, and his wife Kong and Cai are the daughters of Kong Rong and Cai Yong respectively.

A Later Han Dynasty marshal, brother-in-law of He Jin, and half-sibling to the Empress He. When Empress He exiled Empress Dowager Dong and her family took power, Zhang Rang sent bribes, and he was made one of the Ten Attendants. When He Jin attempted to eliminate the Ten Attendants, he was stopped. He Jin would later be assassinated by the Ten Attendants, and was killed by Wu Kuang, who supposedly assisted in the assassination.

He was a general of He Jin's army in Chenliu, Yanzhou. After the eunuchs killed He Jin, Wu Kuang thought that the death of He Jin was due to the collusion between He Miao and the eunuchs, so he joined hands with Dong Min, Dong Zhuo's brother, to kill He Miao.

A native of Fenning, Yuzhang, he's a famous alchemist and filial son in Jin Dynasty. In "Twenty Four Filial Piety", Wu Meng is in the story of wanton mosquitoes full of blood. Both him and his daughter Wu Cailuan were regarded as Immortals by later generations.

A native of Changyuan, Chenliu, she's the wife of Liu Bei and the sister of Wu Yi. She was originally the wife of Liu Mao, the son of Liu Yan, and after Liu Bei entered Shu and Mrs. Sun returned to Wu, Liu Bei accepted the advice of Yizhou officials such as Fa Zheng, and took Wu as his wife. Later, Liu Bei became the Monarch of Shu and Wu Xian was made queen.

A native of Guangling, Yangzhou. Under the tutelage of the famous doctor Hua Tuo in the last years of the Eastern Han Dynasty, according to Hua Tuo's health maintenance method, he lived more than 90 years, still had smart ears and eyes, and strong teeth. Wu Pu also compiled several medical books, but all of them have lost.

Liu Yu's subordinate. After Gongsun Zan defeated Liu Yu, he falsely accused Liu Yu of intending to pretend to be the monarch and beheaded him. Wei Dun waited for the opportunity to seize Liu's head and buried him.

A native of Badi, he's Li Te's younger brother, and Li Xiong's uncle. Li Te, the leader of the Badi tribe in Shu County, revolted against the Western Jin Dynasty, and Li Liu also followed his brother. The two attached to Zhao Bing first, but turned against each other because Zhao Bing killed their brother Li Xing, and stood on their own after the defeat of Zhao Bing. Later Li Te's son Li Xiong proclaimed himself the King of Chengdu and the Emperor of Cheng Han.

A native of Ru'nan, Yuzhou. Originally a subordinate of Sun Ce, he was ordered to intercept and kill Yan Xiang, the Inspector of Yangzhou appointed by Cao Cao. After Sun Ce's death, Li Shu refused to accept the assignment of Sun Quan. Sun Quan sent Sun He and Xu Kun to attack Li Shu, besieged him for many days, and slaughtered the city after capture. Li Shu was beheaded.

A native of Li , Guanghan, he's an official of Shuhan. Once he joined others in a statement to persuade Liu Bei to become the emperor, and went to go for an expedition with Liu Bei in the battle of Yiling. He died shortly after he was defeated and returned to Yongan.

A native of Ru'nan, Yuzhou, he was Zhou Jun's concubine, and Zhou Wei's mother. There are many contradictions regarding its records. It is rumored that Li Luoxiu was willing to be his concubine, so that the family can be named prominent. However, some historical data claimed that Li Luoxiu was in fact the principal wife, and the birth year of his son Zhou Kai is also inconsistent with the time when he was admitted as a concubine.

A native of Shu, Yizhou, also known as Li Yiqi. He's recorded in the Biography of Immortals compiled by Ge Hong. He is a alchemist who can predict good and bad luck. Before the battle of Yiling, he predicted that Liu Bei would be defeated and die in Baidi Fortress.

A native of Li County, Guanghan, he's an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. He's famous for execute Zhang Hong first and report later. He joined the army to participate in the warfare to destroy Wu. After Wu subjugated, he served as the Governor of Yunnan. After he quelled Mao Xu, Li Meng, and Li Rui rebellion, he was promoted to the Inspector of Ningzhou. However, due to the famine in Ningzhou, a disease broke out and the local barbarian people rebelled. Li Yi was surrounded by Ningzhou for several years without the help of court, and eventually died of illness. His daughter Li Xiu inherited Li Yi's ambitions and continued to hold in Ningzhou.

A native to Tongdan, Shangdang, He's an official in Cao Wei and Western Jing dynasty. He was designated as a subordinate by Sima Yi, and was re-used by Emperor Wu of Jin Dynasty after the fall of Wei and rise of Jin Dynasty. He was the Royal Preceptor of Prince and Vice Director of Imperial Secretariat.

A Wu bureaucrat. From a military family, Yang Dao saw his talent and nominated him to Sun Quan. There, he fiercely denounced Lu Yi, earning him the position as Zhuge Ke's Major. He became Danyang Governor at his request after his master's death. Sun Xiu was there at the time, and ignoring his wife's urgings, Li Heng took him to task for his blunders. He nearly joined Wei out of fear when Sun Xiu took the throne, but apologized and was forgiven at his wife's urging.

A native of Li County, Guanghan, he's an official of Shuhan. He was talkative and liked to talk nonsense. Later, after Zhuge Liang's death he criticized Zhuge Liang for "Rely on an elite army alone, just like wolves and tigers staring at other things," suggested that Zhuge Liang was arrogant and domineering, the monarch Liu Chan was angry and ordered him to be executed.

Wife of Qin Yilu, Lu Bu's officer, mother of Qin Lang, and Cao Cao's concubine. She ended up divorcing Qin Yilu after Yuan Shu made him marry another woman while he was away from home in Xiapi. When Lu Bu died in Xiapi, Guan Yu asked Cao Cao for her hand in marriage. Cao Cao, however, took her as his concubine when captivated by her beauty. Qin Lang, her son by Qin Yilu, grew up with great influence in Cao Cao's imperial court from all of the affection he received.

A native of Weishi, Chenliu, he's one of the Seven Scholars of Jian'an, and the father of Ruan Ji. Cao Pi called him and Chen Lin together, saying that the two "none under heaven to equal them in the articles." In addition, Ruan Yuan's poetic and prose phonological attainments are also quite good. His "Driving Out of Beiguo Gate" faithfully reflects contemporary society.
A native of Kuaiji, Yangzhou. He served as the Governor of Jiujiang, and struggled with Sun Jian for Yuzhou. Later, he was defeated by Sun Ben. Since then, there has been no record of him.

A native of Xunyang, Lujiang, he's a famous general in Jin Dynasty. He has successively conquered the rebellion of Hua Yi, Du Chen and Du Zeng. After the Jin Dynasty moved eastward, as the power official, Wang Dun had a desire to revolt, but he did not dare to act rashly because of Zhou Fang and Zu Ti. After Zhou and Zu died, Wang Dun immediately set up a rebellion.

A native of Shu County, Lujiang, he's a Commander of Wu, Zhou Yu's eldest son, and Sun Luban's husband. Sun Quan wanted to reuse Zhou Xun, but Zhou Xun died early. Later, Sun Luban remarried Quan Cong.

A native of Langzhong, Baxi, he's the father of Zhou Qun. he's good at divination. People quoted the "Spring and Autumn Annals" that "The Han Dynasty will be replaced by Dang-tu-gao" and asked Zhou Shu, Zhou Shu replied: "Dang-tu-gao is Wei."

At the time of the Ling Emperor, Beigong Boyu, Bian Zhang and Han Sui and Hu rebelled in the north and attacked Sanfu. The imperial court sent Engineering Supervisor Zhang Wen to lead yuan Pang, Dong Zhuo and Zhou Shen to fight against the rebels. At that time, Sun Jian was Zhou Shen's subordinate, and he had made plans for him, but Zhou Shen did not adopt it, which led to the defeat of the army.

A native of Ancheng, Runan, he's an official of the Jin Dynasty, and the son of Zhou Jun. He's upright and loyal. When Wang Dun rebellion started, he persuaded the Emperor Yuan to let go of Wang Dun's little brother Wang Dao. Later, he was executed by Wang Dun for bluntly reprimanding Wang Dun. Wang Dao had the opportunity to intercede for Zhou Wei, but in the end he was afraid of Wang Dun and did not speak. After learning about Zhou Wei's past favor, he was overwhelmed with sorrow, and told his sons: "Although I didn't kill Boren, Boren died by me. In the gloom, I disappointed this good friend!"

He was a native of Runan, Yuzhou, and an official of Cao Wei. He once traveled with Zhuge Liang to study in the state of Jingzhou. During his second trip to Qishan, Zhuge Liang also mentioned in his correspondence with Sima Yi that he hoped Sima Yi would ask Du Xun to greet Meng Jian on his behalf.

Hou Yin and Wei Kai joined Guan Yu to the south. During the Nanyang rebellion, Zong Ziqing served as the Examiner of Nanyang and advised Hou Yin to release Dongli Gun, the governor of Nanyang. Later, Zong Ziqing escaped at night, gathered the remaining soldiers with Dongli Gun, and met Cao Ren to attack Hou Yin.

Hou Yin and Wei Kai joined Guan Yu to the south. During the Nanyang rebellion, Zong Ziqing served as the Examiner of Nanyang and advised Hou Yin to release Dongli Gun, the governor of Nanyang. Later, Zong Ziqing escaped at night, gathered the remaining soldiers with Dongli Gun, and met Cao Ren to attack Hou Yin. In the battle of Xiangfan, Dongli Gun joined the war together with Yu Jin. He was defeated and captured by Guan Yu. After Guan was defeated and killed by Wu, he was captured by Wu and was able to return to Wei.

He's a native of Shandong and lived in Sanfu. During the late Han Dynasty and the Three Kingdoms period, he was a hermit and alchemist who knew the ephemeris, divination and birds. When Sanfu was in chaos, he first went south into Hanzhong. After Liu Bei occupied Hanzhong, Mr. Qingniu went to Shu. After that, his whereabouts were unknown.

It was made up by the novel, which is taken from the Taoist title of "Nanhua Zhenren" given to Zhuangzi. Zhuangzi was honored as a Nanhua immortal, which can be traced back to the key points of "Taiji immortal applying Lingbao, fasting and dignified rites in the late Eastern Jin Dynasty". In the first episode of "The Romance of the Three Kingdoms", the person who presented Zhang Jiao's "Tai Ping Yao Shu" called himself the Immortal Nanhua. Although the title is used in Romance, most of them think that it is not an allusion to Zhuang Zhou.

Subordinate of the governor of Liaodong, Gongsun Du. One of Gongsun Du's appointed government servants. It is said Liu Yi was the person who informed him about the unrest at Zhongyuan. He was later re-stationed only to be expelled by Zhang Liao's subjugation under orders from Cao Cao.
A native of Jiangdu, Guangling, one of the "Eight Wonders" of Wu, he is good at calligraphy, especially cursive script.

A native of Fenggao, Taishan, he discounts wealth and treasures righteousness, and is one of the "Eight Chefs" at the end of the Han Dynasty. When the Anti-Dong Coalition was established, Han Rong, Yin Xiu, Hu Wuban, Wu Xiu, Wang Gui and others were ordered by Dong Zhuo to recruit the generals of Guandong. All of them were captured and exexuted except for Han Rong.

A native of Waihuang, Chenliu, he studied with Ma Rong the Confucian scholar, and is a master of the Five Classics, especially the Book of Documents and Yi Jing. He is poor. The idiom "Zeng Chen Fu Yu"(dust has covered kitchen utensils and fish has spawned in cooking vessels because of long disuse) comes from Fan Ran.

A native of Waihuang, Chenliu, he's the eldest son of Fan Can, a loyal minister of Cao Wei. After the fall of Wei and rise of Jin Dynasty. , Fan Can is speechless, living in the caravan, not walking on the ground, to show his loyalty to Wei. His son Fan Qiao did not go to be an official because of him.

Born in Qiao County, Pei State, she's the biological mother of Sima Rui, the founding monarch of the Eastern Jin Dynasty, and a descendant of Xiahou Yuan. It is said that Sima Rui was born by Xia Hou Guangji in an affair with a small official surnamed Niu, which fulfilled the prophecy of "the cow succeeds the horse."
Once a subordinate of Zhang Yan. After Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shang and captured Yecheng, he surrendered to Cao with Zhang Yan.
Once a subordinate of Cao Cao, Chen Gong and others responded to the betrayal of Cao with Mao Hui when Lv Bu entered Yan. After Lu Bu's defeat, the two turned to Mount Tai Bandit Zang Ba.

Born in Ju County, Beihai, he's one of the Seven Scholars of Jian'an. He is good at poetry, and his poems are wonderful. His seven character poetry is unique in contemporary times, and is as famous as Chen Lin, who is good at five character poetry.

Born in Dixian, Fanyang, he was a famous general in the northern expedition of the Eastern Jin Dynasty. The term "rise upon hearing the chicken crow" is an anecdote between him and Liu Kun. During the disaster of Yongjia, he wrote to Sima Rui, asking for the northern expedition, but Sima Rui focused on consolidating the throne and did it perfunctorily. Later, Zu Ti recruited soldiers, forged weapons, crossed the river and made a northern expedition. After several defeats, Zu Ti recovered most of the land south of the Yellow River from Shile of Hou Zhao. Shile was afraid of Zu Ti and dared not invade the south. He even presented predentials for good trade and temporary peace in border. However, emperor Yuan appointed Dai Yuan, a civilian who was not familiar with military affairs, as the general of the western expedition to keep Zu Ti in check, and allowed Wang Dun and Liu Kai to oppose each other in the court. Zu Ti could not resist the enemy outside, but civil strife was about to start, so he became angry and died in Yongqiu.

Officer of Lu Bu. When Lu Bu was forced into defense by Cao Cao, Qin Yilu ran to Yuan Shu seeking reinforcements, but was deceived into marrying into the imperial bloodline. He surrendered to Cao Cao after Lu Bu's death, but his new master took his wife. When Liu Bei rose against Cao Cao, Zhang Fei visited Qin Yilu and called him a fool for following the man who stole his wife. This tipped him to joining Liu Bei, but he changed his mind and was killed.

Born in Yunzhong, Xinxing, he's an official of Cao Wei, stepson of Cao Cao, born to Qin Yilu. Won the favor of Emperor Ming of Wei, he was ordered to quell the rebellion of Kebineng and Budugen of Xianbei; later he led his army to support Sima Yi to fight against Zhuge Liang's Northern Expedition. When Emperor Ming was seriously ill, he initially wanted to use Cao Yu, Xia Houxian, Cao Shuang, Cao Zhao, and Qin Lang to serve together, but was eventually persuaded by Liu Fang and Sun Zi to turn to Cao Shuang and Sima Yi. Qin Lang was removed from office, and then there was no record in the history books.

Born in Yingyang, Yingchuan, he's a historian and Confucian at the end of Han Dynasty. Emperor Xian of the Han Dynasty ordered Xun Yue to imitate Zuo Zhuan's style, abbreviate "Han Shu", and compile "Han Ji". People at the time praised the "Han Ji" for "detailed appointments, beauty in discussion," and "saving appointments, easy to learn, and easy to use".

Born in Yingyin, Yingchuan, he have served in the Wei and the Western Jin Dynasty. Talented, tuned, and knowledgeable, he was responsible for editing and editing ancient tomb bamboo slips into the "Book of Tombs". He is good at trying to figure out what the king wants, so Sima Yan is very pleased. He also relied on Jia Chong, the power minister, and helped Jia Nanfeng and Emperor Hui to rise to power, so he became prominent for a while.

From Yingyin, Yingchuan, Xun Chen was Xun Yu's brother. He first served under Han Fu. Later, he advised Han Fu to make Yuan Shao Governor of Ji Province and was therefore summoned by Yuan Shao as an adviser. After the Battle of Guandu, he was not mentioned again in historical records.

He was a native of Yan Shi in Henan Province, the son of Yu Jian and the father of Yu Zheng. After Liu Bei entered Shu, he joined Liu Bei and was assigned as Meng Da's subordinate. After Meng Da rebelled against Shu, he followed Meng Da to Cao Wei and became the official secretary of Cao Wei.
A native of Langzhong, Baxi, he was originally a subordinate of Liu Zhang and later belonged to Liu Bei. It is said to be talented in history, slightly inferior to Yao Zhou.

Officer of Wei and Jin. When Sima Yan sought warriors to subjugate Wu, Ma Long was recruited from Ji. When Jufashu Jineng of the Xianbei started a revolt in the Liang Province, he rode out himself and defeated them with unpredictable tactics. He became the Xiping Governor, defeating foreign tribes and winning renown. Though he was toppled by Yan Shu's slander, he quickly regained his position and reigned peacefully over Longyou until he died.

A native of Langzhong, Baxi, he's an official of the Han Dynasty. He's talented, and have a fine style of writing. He was originally an Examiner worked under Zhang Fei. Zhang Fei recommended Ma Qi to Liu Bei, and he was heavily relied on. After Zhuge Liang's death, Ma Qi was appointed as Imperial Secretariat, and the position of Imperial Chancellor of Shu Han was demolished. Chief Imperial Secretariat is the substantive decision-maker, and the Imperial Secretariat ministry was the core of the political decree.
Born in Taiyuan, Bingzhou. Shang Yao and others gathered in Daling to rebel and were attacked by Xiahou Yuan and Xu Huang.

He is the son of Cui Lie, a native of Anping, Boling. Friendly with Zhuge Liang, Xu Shu. Zhuge Liang cultivated Long Mu and lived in seclusion, and when his fame was not obvious, he often compared himself to Guan Zhong and Le Yi, and only Cui Zhouping and Xu Shu recognized his talent.

Born in Anping, Boling, he's the son of Cui Lie, and the brother of Cui Zhouping. At the time of the Emperor Ling, his father bought an official as Education Supervisor, and was widely criticized. Cui Jun said bluntly: "Critics just think copper coin smells bad." This is the origin of the term"copper smell". Later, Cui Jun responded against Dong Zhuo, so Cui Lie was captured and jailed. Shortly after Dong Zhuo's death, Li Zhe attacked Chang'an, Dong died in the chaos. Cui Jun has always wanted to avenge his father, but unfortunately he died of illness.

A native of Yanling, Yingchuan, he's the elder brother of Yu Wenjun, a power official in the Eastern Jin Dynasty, and the brother of Empress Yu Wenjun. Su Jun rebellion was triggered because he tried to recruit Su Jun, the internal history minister of Liyang, into the court in order to keep his power in check. After the death of Shile of Hou Zhao, Yu Liang wanted to take the opportunity to make a northern expedition, but he was defeated by the Shihu force. After the defeat of the northern expedition, Yu Liang fell ill and died.

A native of Yanling, Yingchuan, he had been an official in Wei and Western Jin Dynasty, and he was the elder brother of Yu Chun. Diligent and successful, he once explained the problems of "Book of Documents" for Cao Mao; and served Emperor Wu of Jin to explain "Classic of Poetry" for him. Unlike the prevailing atmosphere of old-fashioned talks and flashy competition at the time, Yu Jun respected Confucianism and advocated the conformity of name and reality. In addition, he has the talent of judgment.

A native of Yanling, Yingchuan, he had been an official in Wei and Western Jin Dynasty, and he was the little brother of Yu Jun. Similar to his brother Yu Jun, he's knowledgeable and talented, neither advocating flashy, nor old-fashioned talks. He was at odds with the powerful minister Jia Chong. Jia Chong once ridiculed Yu Chun and was heckled by Yu Chun about killing Cao Mao.

Born in Yanling, Yingchuan, he was an official of the Western Jin Dynasty and the son of Yu Jun. Very different from his father, he likes metaphysics and idle talk, his style is flashy and mediocre. 
During the Yongjia rebellion, he was captured by Shile of Hou Zhao and killed soon after.

Born in Yiyang Counrt, he's a barbarian who's naturalized by Han people. He set off the Zhang Chang Rebellion during the Emperor Hui of the Western Jin Dynasty. At the time of the Eight Kings Rebellion, Li Liu rebelled in Yizhou, Zhang Chang took the opportunity to gather people in the name of recruiting soldiers in order to separate the regime. Later, he greeted Qiu Shen. Assuming that he was the heir of Han Dynasty, he changed Qiu's name to Liu Ni, set him as the Son of Heaven, and determined Shenfeng as the era name. Zhang Chang's influence has reached its peak since then. Later, he was defeated by Tao Kan, a general of Jin Dynasty. Zhang Chang was beheaded and his head was passed to the Capital.

Born in Nanzheng in Hanzhong. Guarding the border area, he served as the Prefect and Governor of Zangke, Fufeng, Guiyang, Liangzhou and other places. He awed and subdued the barbarians. At that time, he was called "Crouching Tiger".

Younger brother to the governor of Chenliu Zhang Miao in the Later Han. Governor of Guangling. He joins the anti-Dong Zhuo coalition along with his brother. In 194, when Cao Cao is attacking Tao Qian, he plots with his brother and Chen Gong, invites Lu Bu to be their leader and causes an uprising. However, they are beaten by Cao Cao's fierce attack and he kills himself.

Yanzhou Dongping people. When Zhang Miao and Chen Gong rebelled against Cao Cao and welcomed Lv Bu, they took Bi Chen's family as the hostages, so Cao Cao let Bi Chen leave. Although Bi Chen once said that he had no second thoughts, he still turned to Lv Bu's command. After the defeat of Lv Bu, Cao Jun captured Bi Chen. Cao Cao thought, "Those who are filial to their parents will be loyal to his monarch. This is the man I'm looking for!" Not only did he not hold him accountable, he also hired him as the Xiang of Lu.

He was born in Runan, Henan Province. He was an Alchemist in the Western Jin Dynasty. It is said that the alchemist, who learned Taoism from Wu Meng or Chen's mother, ascended during Emperor Xiao Wu era in the Eastern Jin Dynasty. Later generations respected him as the founding father of Jingming Taoism and Lushan sect, and called them Heaven Masters, together with Zhang Daoling, Ge Xuan and Sa Shoujian.

When Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang engaged in a power struggle, they both wanted to recruit the famed politician Cui Yan, who refused by claiming he was ill. He was imprisoned for it and was spared after Yin Kui and Chen Lin saved him. 
Later, when Cao Cao greatly defeated Yuan Shang in Yecheng, Yuan Shang sent Yin Kui and Chen Lin to surrender but Cao Cao refused. Yin Kui's name was not seen in official records after that.
Born in Songzi, Lujiang, he's a Commander of Dong Wu, and the son of Chen Wu. He has the legacy of his father, and he is good at training soldiers.

Born in Moling, Danyang, he's a Commander of Dong Wu. Served as the Inspector of Jiaozhou, he promoted education in the local area, so that the foreigners were attached to it and the culture was greatly expanded.

A native of Niyang in the north, he's an official of the Western Jin Dynasty, the son of Fu Xuan. He always offended powerful people and was impeached repeatedly because he was strong and loyal and dared to admonish. The allusion of "Liao Que Guan Chi" comes from letters of Yang Ji and Fu Xian.

A native of Lingzhou, Beidi County, and a loyal minister of the Eastern Han Dynasty. Together with Huangfu Song, he defeated Zhang Jiao and killed Bu Si, Zhang Bo, Liang Zhongning and other Yellow Turban generals. However, because of he wrote to Ling Emperor asking to eradicate the eunuch, he was hated by Zhao Zhong, one of the Ten Accendants, and was framed by Zhao, failed to be confered nobility. At that time, the Western Qiang in Liangzhou made a riot, and Zhao Zhonghe was jealous of Fu Xie's dignitaries and released him as Hanyang Governor. After Fu Xie took office, he showed compassion for the people, and even the rebellious Qiang people surrendered. Then Han Sui rebelled and besieged Fu Xie in Han Yang. Han Sui led the Qiang people to beg Fu Xie to surrender one after another because they were grateful for Fu Xie's kindness and could not bear to fight with him. His son Fu Gan also advised him to give up, but Fu Xie refused and died in the war. Fu Xie was loyal and brave, but he could not be entrusted. It was regrettable that he finally gave up his life.
Gongsun Zan's subordinate. The history books only mentioned that he joined forces with Liu Bei and Tao Qian against Cao Cao and Yuan Shao, but he was still defeated by the Cao-Yuan coalition.

Dai is the subordinate of Sheng Xian, the former Governor of Wu, who was killed by Sun Quan. He and Gui Lan fled into the mountain, waiting for an opportunity to take revenge. Later, they were pardoned by Sun Yi, the Governor of Dan Yang. They instructed Bian Hong to kill Sun Yi and silenced Bian Hong. He also killed Sun He, who came to ask for guilt, and planned to surrender to Cao Cao. Finally, the two were killed by Sun Yi's wife Xu and Sun Yi's former subordinates Xu Yuan, Sun Gao and Fu Ying.

Wei officer. Son of You Yan. His father had a fondness of Zhang Ji, leading the man to recommend You Chu to be governor of Hanxing after Cao Cao seized power. He later moved to Longxi. When Zhuge Liang attacked Longyou and Tianshui and Nan'an surrendered, only Longxi held strong and fended off the Shu army. This won You Chu great esteem with Cao Rui, and he spent the rest of his life enjoying games and music.

He was born in Pinyang, Zuopingyi, the father of You Chu. He was the friend of Zhang Ji, recognized him very much, and entrusted his son to Zhang. Later, because of disagreement with Hu Zhen, he was killed by Hu during the Li-Guo insurrection.

From the famous Han Yuefu poem "The Peacock Flies to the Southeast", it is said that he was a small official in Lujiang County and married Liu Lanzhi as his wife. Liu Lanzhi was not tolerated by Jiao's mother and ordered Jiao Zhongqing to divorce his wife. Later Liu Lanzhi's brother forced her to remarry. On the day of remarriage, Liu Lanzhi and Jiao Zhongqing committed suicide.

Born in Dayang, Hedong, he was a hermit at the end of Han Dynasty and the Three Kingdoms era. He had a loose appearance and rarely communicates with people. He often feeds on white stones, and has a life span of more than 170 years. At that time, people thought that he's an immortal.

A fictional character in The Romance of the Three Kingdoms. When Liu Bei attacked Shu, Liu Zhang, Zhang Ren, Leng Bao, and Deng Xian, subordinates of Liu Zhang, went to Jinping Mountain to ask Immortal Zixu about good or bad luck. Immortal Zixu hinted that Pang Tong was going to die, and the four of them could not escape the same destiny.
The history books only mention that Yang Yi is a confidant of Gongsun Du. Gongsun Du once discussed with Liu Yi and Yang Yi about self-reliance as king.

General under Liu Biao, governor of Zhang, and son of Huang Zu. When Liu Xun sought Huang Zu's help after his defeat to Sun Ce, Huang She led a navy to reinforce Xun, but Xun had already been defeated. He later led thousands of soldiers to attack Sun Quan Army's Chaisang, but was defeated by a mere 200 men led by Xu Sheng. He then disappeared after the death of Huang Zu. He was friends with Mi Heng, and they would sometimes travel together.

Officer of Dong Zhuo. He served Wang Yun after Dong Zhuo's death, but his frustrations with Wang Yun's attitude pushed him to defect to Li Meng. When Li Meng came to blows with Guo Si, he joined the latter. He escorted Emperor Xian in his escape from Chang'an and was welcomed by Duan Wei, whom he hated. He attempted to slander the man, but ended up attacked and chased off to the Jing Province.

A native of Yuling, Xingyang, he's a Commander of Cao Wei. A confidant of Cao Rui of the Wei Ming emperor, he led the army in the central government, took charge of the imperial army, supervised and unified the generals, and presided over the election of military officers. When Gongsun Yuan rebelled in Liaodong, Yang Ji recommended the Ming emperor to acknowledge Tian Yu as the general. Tian Yu did not fail his mission and returned with victory. Since then, Yang Ji also put forward suggestions on the conquer of Shu.

A native of Huayin, Hongnong, he was an official of the Western Jin Dynasty, and the son of Yang Xiu. "The Three Kingdoms" stated: "Xiao, Yang Xiu's son, together with Zhun, son of Xiao, are well-known in the Jin Dynasty." Xu's father Yang Xiu was killed for involving in the dispute between Cao Zhi and Cao Pi, and Xu was never reused during the Cao Wei period.

A Later Han Confucian scholar. He studied Confucianism at various schools, after which he learned prophecy from following Yang Hou. He was enlisted by He Jin and became an honored member of the Imperial Court. When Liu Yan plots to become the regional governor of Jiao Province to avoid the disorder occurring in the center, it was he who advised him that the aura of the Son of Heaven was in Yi Province. Hearing this, Liu Yan asked to become regional governor of Yi, instead. Dong Fu then followed Liu Yan into Yi.

A native of Houguan, Kuaiji. Together with Hua Tuo and Zhang Zhongjing, they were called "three miracle doctors of Jian'an". Later generations regarded them as gods, and they were listed in the "Biography of Immortals" compiled by Ge Hong in the Eastern Jin Dynasty. In addition, the origin of the allusion of "Warm spring in apricot forest" originated from Dong Feng.

A native of Chenliu, Yanzhou, he was an official of Cao Wei at the end of the Han Dynasty, served as the Tuntian Chief Commandant and Cai Yan's third husband. After Wen Ji returned to Han, Cao acted as a mediator and married Cai Yan to Dong Si. Later, when Dong Si broke the law and executed according to the law, Cai Yan bowed his head and pleaded guilty for Dong Si, Cao Cao was moved and ordered Dong Si to be exempted from the crime.
Wang Cheng was famous. He despised Wang Dun in his words. He was hated by Wang Dun, so he sent Muscleman Lu Rong to kill Wang Cheng.

A native to Changyi, Shanyang, he was an official of the Western Jin Dynasty, and the grandson of Man Chong. During the Rebellion of the Eight Kings, Shangguan Si took the prince Sima Tan into Luoyang and ransacked the city. Man Fen, Zhou Fu and others wanted to assassinate Shangguan Si. The incident was vented. Only Zhou Fu escaped, and Man Fen and the others were killed.

Officer of Yuan Tan. Guan Tong ignored family and sided with Yuan Tan in the many uprisings that occurred in the discord between him and Yuan Shang. Cao Cao took advantage of the conflict, forcing many officers to surrender, and killing Yuan Tan. However, Guan Tong continued to resist him under orders from the governor of Lean. Following that, Wang Xiu, who had already succumbed to Cao Cao, arranged for his surrender, and he was given a pardon for his loyalty.

A native of Bobai, Baizhou, she's the concubine of Shi chongchong, a rich man in the Western Jin Dynasty. According to The Book of Jin, Lvzhu is "beautiful, good at playing flute." fter the rebellion of the eight kings, when Sima Lun was in power, his confidant Sun Xiu coveted the beauty of Lvzhu and asked Shi Chong for her, which was rejected by Shi Chong. Sun Xiu then falsely accused Shi Chong of conspiring against Sima Yun, led troops to attack Shi Chong's Jinguyuan residence, and Lvzhu committed suicide for Shi Chong.

It is recorded in unofficial history novels. It is said that he was a swordsmith of Shu Han Dynasty. He once casted three thousand swords for Zhuge Liang in Xiegu. All of them are mystical weapons. In addition, the ox-cart may came from his hands.

A native of Changling, Jingzhao, he once involved in Party Forbiddance incident. Because of the Yellow Turban rebellion, the dynasty was in chaos, and he was recruited as Court Counselor again. During the dictatorship of Li Jue, Ma Riden was appointed as the envoy and Zhao Qi as the deputy envoy to coordinate the dynasty. After Emperor Xian went east to Luoyang, he sent Liu Biao to send troops to Luoyang to help build the palace and deliver supplies. After Zhao Qi became old and ill, he stayed in Jinzhou.

A native to Baxi, Yizhou, he was formerly a subordinate of Liu Yan and Liu Zhang. Seeing that Liu Zhang was mediocre and cowardly, he took the opportunity to join forces with local houses to set up troops. Shu, Guanghan, Qianwei and other counties responded. Finally they were defeated by the Dongzhou Troops, and their subordinates Pang Le and Li Yi rebelled at that time, killed Zhao Wei.

Born in Zhuo County, he was the imperial clan of Shuhan, son of Liuchan. After the subjugation of Shu, he moved to Luoyang with Liu Chan. After the death of prince Liu Xuan in Zhong Hui rebellion, he became the heir. After the death of Liu Chan, he succeeded the Gong of Anle County. He was arrogant, tyrannical and obscene. He Pan wrote remonstrations together with Wang Chong, Governor of Shangyong, and Zhang Yin, Governor of Fuling.

A native of Zhuojun, Youzhou, Shuhan clan, son of Liu Chan. he was the imperial clan of Shuhan, son of Liuchan. After the subjugation of Shu, he moved to Luoyang with Liu Chan. After the death of prince Liu Xuan in Zhong Hui rebellion, he was supposed to be the heir, but because Liu Chan loved Liu Xun, he ignored opposition and made Liu Xun the heir.

Liu Gui was Liu Zhang's general. When Liu Bei attacked Shu, Liu Gui guarded Fucheng with Deng Xian, Leng Bao, and Zhang Ren. Upon defeat, they retreated Mianzhu. However, Li Yan and Fei Guan, who were guarding Mianzhu, defected and Liu Gui took shelter in Luocheng, where Liu Xun, the son of Liu Zhang, was. After a year of resistance, Luocheng was invaded.

A native of Gaoping, Shanyang, he was an official of the Western Jin Dynasty. Once a criminal, he was redeemed by Sima Jun with 500 pieces of cloth, and then he was appointed Zhonglang. It was well told by people at that time. Later, because of his knowledge of classics and history and good at writing articles, he was designated as the Zhongshuzi of the crown prince to explain the Scriptures for the prince.

A native of Jingling, Jiangxia, he was the son of Liu Zhang. After Liu Zhang surrendered to Liu Bei, he was moved to Jingzhou. After Guan Yu was defeated, Jingzhou was captured by Wu, and Liu Zhang, Liu Chan and his sons seeked refuge to Wu. Liu Chan successively served as the Inspector of Yizhou and Yushi Zhongcheng. When Yong Kai rebelled against Shu, he also served as Jiaozhou governor. He was obviously not incompetent.

A native of Pengcheng, Xuzhou, he studied under the tutelage of the famous doctor Hua Tuo in the late Eastern Han Dynasty, and was good at acupuncture and moxibustion. Hua Tuo taught him the secret recipe of "Green Sticky Powder", which is beneficial to people. Fan E has followed his words and lived more than a hundred years old.

A native of Qiantang, Wujun, he was an official of Wu. He was appointed Governor of Linhai, and was meritorius in governance. Yao Xin, He Shao and several other important officials at the end of Wu was also his close friends. Wu refused to be an official after the subjugation of Wu. His family is studious and has more than 7000 books.

He's once a subordinate of Cao Cao. Hou Yin and Wei Kai joined Guan Yu in Nanyang and rebelled. They once held Dongligun, Governor of Nanyang. After that, Zong Ziqing persuaded Hou Yin to release Dongligun. Zong Ziqing escaped at night, gathered the remnants with Dongligun, and joined Cao Ren to attack Hou Yin and Wei Kai. After the city was captured, he and Hou Yin were both executed.

A subordinate of Gongsun Yuan. After Gongsun Yuan rebelled against Cao and was defeated by Sima Yi, he first sent Wang Jian and Liu Fu to make peace with Sima Yi. Sima Yi beheaded the envoy. Gongsun Yuan then sent Wei Yan to surrender again, but Sima Yi still refused.

Born in Langya, Xuzhou, he was Zhuge Ke's eldest son. Because he was involved in the dispute between the two palaces, and he was the partisan of Sun Ba. Sun Quan ordered Zhuge Ke to teach his son even more, and Zhuge Ke killed him.

Born in Gaomi, Beihai, he's a scholar of Eastern Han dynasty and a famous Confucian. He was known as a prodigy when he was young, and Du Mi, the Chancellor of Beihai, highly regarded him and recommended him to Taixue. He also studied under Ma Rong together with Lu Zhi, and then traveled to various states. He involved in Party Forbiddance incident and was imprisoned.
